r819.riskReason: Common Sense Media has strong child privacy protections and does not sell data, but the commonsensemedia.org domain does share personal information with advertising partners for platform-targeted ads, uses web beacons and third-party cookies, and lacks explicit FERPA compliance language, which warrants medium risk for K-12 school use.
r819.parentSummary: Common Sense Media collects personal information such as name, email, username, device data, and usage activity when users register accounts, with membership optional for basic browsing. The platform explicitly supports COPPA, does not sell personal data, and states that any advertising is limited to its own platform and not shared with third-party advertisers; children under 13 are having their accounts discontinued as of October 2025, with the minimum age moving to 13. Parents should be aware that the main commonsensemedia.org site does share data with advertising partners for platform-based ad delivery and uses third-party cookies and web beacons, and while a subprocessor list is published, FERPA compliance is not explicitly stated.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy has an effective date (December 3, 2024) and a former version is archived, but the policy does not explicitly commit to advance notification before changes take effect — it states changes are effective upon posting.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and its FAQ provide a detailed enumeration of data types collected including name, email, username, device identifiers, IP address, usage data, location, school information, and payment data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected: through registration forms, cookies, web beacons, automatic device logging, Single Sign-On services, and third-party sources.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly assert that users own their data; it describes CSM's rights to use personal information broadly, and while the Education/CSP ToS states customer data ownership, the main consumer privacy policy is ambiguous on this point.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users and parents can delete accounts and postings via the My Account section, by clicking delete on reviews, or by contacting privacy@commonsense.org through the Privacy Requests Portal.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained while there is a legitimate business need and deleted/anonymized when no longer needed, but does not specify a concrete retention period in days or months.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'reasonable administrative, organizational, technical, and physical measures' to protect personal information and mentions a Data Incident Response Plan, but does not list specific technical controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is not explicitly detailed in the privacy policy; the cookie policy references secure connections for necessary cookies, but no explicit statement about end-to-end or at-rest encryption is made.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Single Sign-On (SSO) via Google and other providers is supported, and the platform's use of SSO satisfies this criterion as a secure authentication alternative.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: SSO/LTI integration is explicitly supported, satisfying the MFA/SSO requirement for secure account access.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A detailed Cookie Policy exists that lists cookie categories (Necessary, Analytics, Advertising), their purposes, and how to disable non-essential ones; logged-in children and teens have non-necessary cookies turned off.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: A publicly available Subprocessor List names specific third-party service providers used for school products and the main website, including Google Classroom integration.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Subprocessor List groups processors by service category rather than specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of targeted advertising and non-necessary cookies via the Cookie Policy controls; Common Sense states it does not share data for profit and does not engage in third-party advertising outside its own platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states that third-party service providers are restricted from using personal information beyond providing services to CSM, and are required to meet equivalent data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Subprocessor List notes updates will be provided as needed, but does not guarantee advance notice to users before new third-party processors are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Advertising and marketing activities are stated to be exclusively related to Common Sense's own services on commonsensemedia.org; no third-party ads are shown on education or other CSM domains, but platform-based ads do exist on the main site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: While no third-party targeted advertising is confirmed, the main commonsensemedia.org site does share personal information with advertising partners to personalize and improve ad delivery, creating partial targeting concern.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising partners can receive personal information on commonsensemedia.org for ad delivery; opt-out is available per applicable law but tracking exists and the opt-out mechanism is not prominently described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy acknowledges use of web beacons and similar tracking technologies linked to the Cookie Policy; advertising cookies are used on the main media site though non-necessary cookies are disabled for logged-in minors.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Applicable law opt-out rights for targeted advertising are acknowledged, a Privacy Requests Portal is provided, and users can manage cookie preferences — constituting a clear, if multi-step, opt-out process.

dataSharedWith: Service providers (email delivery, database hosting, database management, security vendors)
Successor entities in merger or acquisition (with opt-out rights for student data)
r1034.riskReason: DeltaMath explicitly prohibits targeted advertising and the sale of student data, operates under FERPA as a school official, delegates COPPA consent to schools, and applies SSL/TLS encryption plus encryption at rest for student PII.
r1034.parentSummary: DeltaMath collects student names, email addresses, assignment responses, usage behavior, and technical data (IP address, device info) solely to deliver its math practice service. It explicitly states it does not sell student data or permit targeted advertising, and it processes student data under FERPA as a school official with consent managed through the school. Parents of children under 13 should confirm their school has provided appropriate COPPA consent, and parents can request data deletion by contacting support@deltamath.com.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Material policy changes are announced via a banner on the website and the Effective Date is updated, but no advance pre-notification period is stated and no publicly accessible revision history is maintained.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy comprehensively lists all categories of data collected, including registration data, student assignment data, and automatically collected technical/usage data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically explains that data is collected through registration forms, student assignment interaction, and automatically via log files, web beacons, browser cookies, and device identifiers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states student data is treated as confidential and used only to provide the service, but does not explicitly declare that users own their data; ownership language is absent.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Deletion is available by contacting support@deltamath.com, but there is no self-service in-account deletion option for students; the process requires an email request, making it limited/manual.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: A specific retention period is not stated in the public privacy policy for school accounts; the Children's Privacy Policy notes a 2-year post-subscription retention for DeltaMath for Home, but school-context retention is only described vaguely as 'as long as needed to provide the Service.'
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy and associated Data Security and Privacy Plan describe specific measures including SSL/TLS encryption in transit, encryption at rest, salted password hashing with key stretching, and access controls limited to authorized accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: DeltaMath explicitly uses SSL/TLS for data in motion and encrypts all student PII at rest and at the application level, as confirmed in the Data Security and Privacy Plan.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service place password confidentiality responsibility on users and note DeltaMath may require password changes if a password is deemed insecure, but no explicit minimum password strength requirements or enforcement rules are described in the public policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Google SSO is offered as a login option, which satisfies single sign-on support, but there is no explicit mention of multi-factor authentication as an available or required option.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies and web beacons and lists examples of the data they collect, but does not provide a complete categorized cookie inventory (e.g., functional vs. analytics) with individual cookie names and purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third-party categories (service providers, affiliates, legal authorities) are named broadly, but specific vendor company names are not disclosed in the public privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared with service providers generally (e.g., email delivery, database hosting, security) without specifying which data elements go to which vendor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: DeltaMath explicitly states it does not share personal information with third parties for advertising or marketing, and student data sale is prohibited, effectively eliminating the need for an advertising opt-out.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that service providers 'do not have the right to use your personal information we share with them beyond what is necessary to assist us,' and affiliates must agree to consistent use standards, indicating contractual obligations are in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy notes changes will be communicated via a website banner and Effective Date update, but does not specifically commit to notifying users when the list of third-party service providers changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states 'Targeted advertising is not permitted on DeltaMath' and there is no indication of any ads being displayed to school users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: DeltaMath explicitly prohibits targeted advertising and states it does not sell or rent personal information to third parties for advertising or marketing purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is present; the no-targeted-advertising policy effectively means no third-party tracking for advertising purposes occurs on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Web beacons and cookies are acknowledged as tracking technologies used for usage data collection, but the policy does not fully clarify whether any of these serve any ad-adjacent analytics purposes beyond core service operation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because DeltaMath does not share data with advertisers or permit targeted advertising, no opt-out mechanism is necessary, and the policy's explicit prohibition constitutes the strongest possible protection on this dimension.

r1035.riskReason: Follett Software expressly commits to FERPA and COPPA compliance and does not sell student data, but the broader Follett Software privacy policy and cookie policy permit third-party advertising tracking and web beacons on its websites, specific data retention periods are not disclosed, and third-party advertisers are described only in general categories rather than named individually, creating partial transparency gaps.
r1035.parentSummary: Destiny Discover, operated by Follett School Solutions, collects student names, login credentials, usage activity, and library resource access history to provide library management services; student data is owned by the school district, not Follett, and is not used for advertising or sold to third parties. Follett has achieved SOC-2 Type 2 certification and expressly commits to FERPA and COPPA compliance, with parental consent required via the school for students under 13. However, the broader Follett privacy policy and cookie statements describe third-party advertising trackers and web beacons used on Follett's marketing websites, and the policies do not specify a precise data retention period, which parents should be aware of.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it 'may be revised from time to time' and that Follett will 'make reasonable efforts to notify affected individuals,' but no formal advance notification timeline or revision history archive is specified.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates several data categories (name, email, usage data, IP address, cookies, web beacons), but a comprehensive list specific to the Destiny Discover K-12 product — including all student library activity data — is not provided in a single consolidated table.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy describes general methods of data collection (cookies, web beacons, embedded scripts, direct user input) but does not specifically detail the technical mechanisms used within Destiny Discover itself beyond high-level descriptions.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy explicitly states that 'Follett Software does not own or control Student Data, which belongs to the student and/or the Customer,' clearly establishing school/student ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may submit deletion requests via email to privacy@follettsoftware.com, but deletion is conditional on jurisdiction, legal obligations, and identity verification, meaning full deletion is not guaranteed in all circumstances.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy references that data is retained to comply with 'legal obligations' and that policies for storage/retention/disposition exist, but no specific retention period (e.g., 90 days, 1 year) is stated in the publicly available privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Follett has achieved SOC-2 Type 2 certification, TX-RAMP Level 2 certification, and 1EdTech Data Privacy Certification, and references 'commercially reasonable security measures' including physical, electronic, and procedural safeguards.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The EU privacy policy references encryption of sensitive information (e.g., credit card tokenization) and Azure-based infrastructure with encryption, but the main U.S. privacy policy does not explicitly confirm end-to-end encryption for all student data in transit and at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Destiny supports SSO and LTI-based access, which delegates authentication to the school's identity provider and effectively enforces institutional password and security policies without requiring separate Destiny credentials.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Destiny Discover supports SSO via SAML and LTI, enabling schools to apply MFA through their existing identity providers, which meets this requirement for the intended K-12 school deployment model.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The cookie policy lists categories of cookies (strictly necessary, performance/analytics, functionality, advertising) and describes third-party cookies, but does not provide a named, itemized table of every specific cookie with its purpose and duration.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third parties are described in broad functional categories (analytics providers, ad agencies, authorized subcontractors) rather than by specific named companies, providing only a general disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by category of third party and purpose rather than specifying exactly what data is shared with each individual vendor, resulting in partial but not full transparency.

complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that service providers 'have no independent rights' in personal information and are not authorized to use data except to perform services on Follett's behalf, indicating contractual responsibility is asserted.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may be revised and that reasonable efforts to notify users will be made, but there is no explicit commitment to provide advance notice specifically when third-party data sharing arrangements change.

complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Follett explicitly states student data is not used for advertising purposes and is not sold, but the broader corporate cookie and privacy policies describe interest-based targeted advertising on marketing websites, which are not clearly segregated from the K-12 product environment in the published policies.

complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy acknowledges web beacons and embedded scripts are used for tracking user navigation and email engagement, and the cookie policy confirms these may serve advertising purposes on Follett websites, though their use within the Destiny Discover product itself is not separately clarified.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out of data sharing with advertisers is available via NAI and DAA opt-out programs referenced in the cookie policy, and a 'Do Not Sell' opt-out link is mentioned in state privacy disclosures, but the process is not clearly described as simple or in-platform.

r820.riskReason: Dexcom Follow collects highly sensitive protected health data (real-time glucose levels) from children as young as 2 via parent/guardian accounts, discloses data to advertising networks and data brokers, and has no explicit COPPA compliance statement or K-12/FERPA-specific protections, making it unsuitable as a school-managed EdTech platform without significant legal review.
r820.parentSummary: Dexcom Follow is a medical CGM remote-monitoring app that collects sensitive health data including real-time glucose readings, health conditions, and device/usage information; children under 18 must be managed through a parent or guardian account. While Dexcom maintains HIPAA compliance and ISO 27001 security certification for health data, the platform also discloses certain non-HIPAA-covered data (such as website identifiers and cookies) to advertising networks, data analytics providers, and data brokers for interest-based advertising purposes. This platform is designed as a medical device companion app, not an educational tool, and schools considering its use should be aware that it is not built for FERPA compliance and carries elevated data-sharing risk given the sensitivity of the health data involved.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Dexcom states significant policy changes will be notified via prominent website notice or email, but changes take effect upon posting without advance notice, and a revision history is not publicly maintained.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy provides a high-level summary table of data categories collected, but specific data fields for the Dexcom Follow app are not individually enumerated and users are told to contact Dexcom for specifics on third-party joint-use data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes collection through device/app use, account creation, and optional integrations, but does not provide a granular, Follow-app-specific breakdown of each collection method.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Use grant Dexcom a broad license to use User Data and state Dexcom may retain personal information after account termination as permitted by law, making data ownership ambiguous rather than clearly vesting in the user.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users have a documented right to request deletion of personal data via Dexcom's OneTrust privacy portal or by email, and this right is referenced in both the privacy policy and the US State Privacy Rights disclosure.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy includes a 'How Long Your Personal Data Will Be Kept' section, but the disclosed retention standard is vague ('as long as required or permitted by applicable law') rather than citing a specific retention period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Dexcom's ISMS is certified under ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and the Trust Center documents specific security program pillars including confidentiality, integrity, and availability controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The platform transmits health data over secure connections (implied by HIPAA compliance and ISO 27001 certification), and the App Store listing confirms encrypted data transmission as part of healthcare-grade security standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Dexcom requires account creation and mandates that accounts only be created by users 18 or older, implying some account security controls, but password strength requirements are not explicitly described in public-facing policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The policy does not explicitly mention multi-factor authentication as an available or required option for Dexcom Follow app accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Dexcom maintains a dedicated Cookie Policy that categorizes cookies into functional, performance, and targeting types with purposes described, and provides an opt-out toggle for the sale of personal information via cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The US State Privacy Rights disclosure lists broad categories of third parties (advertising networks, data analytics providers, social networks, data brokers) but does not name specific vendor companies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared per third-party category is grouped broadly rather than specifying which exact data elements go to which named third party, making it difficult to assess exposure for any individual data type.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: California residents and some other state residents can opt out of the sale/sharing of personal data via a 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link, but this opt-out is state-law-dependent and not universally available to all users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states data is shared 'in accordance with applicable privacy and data protection laws' and references contractual obligations with service providers in the context of consumer health data, but no universal vendor agreement standard is explicitly described for all third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Significant policy changes trigger notification via website notice or email, but updates to the specific list of third parties do not independently trigger user notification and may be reflected only upon policy update.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Dexcom's cookie policy and US State Privacy Rights disclosure confirm that targeting cookies are set by advertising partners to build user interest profiles and show relevant ads on other sites.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Dexcom explicitly acknowledges disclosing personal data to advertising networks for cross-contextual behavioral advertising on its non-HIPAA-covered, educational webpages.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: An opt-out toggle for the sale of personal information (including ad-related cookies) is available per CCPA for California residents, and browser privacy controls are honored, but a universal opt-out mechanism for all users is not clearly provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Dexcom's cookie policy identifies targeting cookies set by third-party advertising partners that are used to build interest profiles and serve ads across other sites, confirming third-party tracking for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out mechanism exists for California residents via the 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' link and the cookie consent toggle, but the process for non-California users to opt out of advertiser data sharing is not clearly described.

r282.riskReason: Econ Lowdown is operated by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (a government entity with no ad-driven model), offers a FERPA compliance document, and explicitly states no data sale or targeted advertising; however, the platform has announced retirement as of December 31, 2025 with migration to FRE.org, its privacy policy is a general St. Louis Fed research site policy not specifically tailored to K-12 student users, no dedicated Terms of Service for Econ Lowdown exists, the policy reserves the right to change without notice, Google Analytics cookies are used without granular opt-out, COPPA compliance is stated as a commitment but lacks detail on parental consent mechanisms, and data retention periods are not specifically stated.
r282.parentSummary: Econ Lowdown, run by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, collects basic registration information (name, email, student codes) and course progress data to support classroom use; it explicitly states it does not sell personal data and does not display targeted advertisements. The platform uses Google Analytics for aggregate site analysis and employs outside contractors who are required to keep data secure and use it only on behalf of the Federal Reserve. Parents and eligible students can request review, correction, or deletion of voluntarily submitted personal information by emailing the site, though specific data retention periods and a detailed COPPA parental consent process are not clearly documented in the publicly available policy.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The St. Louis Fed online privacy notice explicitly states 'We reserve the right to change this policy at any time without notice,' meaning no advance notification or revision history is provided to users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists some categories of data collected (personal info voluntarily submitted, cookies, aggregate analytics) but does not provide a comprehensive, itemized list specific to Econ Lowdown student and teacher accounts.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states data is collected when users register, subscribe, answer surveys, or use the site, but does not specifically enumerate all collection mechanisms (e.g., LTI data pass-through, Canvas integration) used by the Econ Lowdown platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly address who owns user-submitted data; it states the Federal Reserve 'will be free to use any ideas, concepts... embodied in the Content for any purpose,' which creates ambiguity around content ownership for submitted educational work.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users who have voluntarily submitted personal information may request review, update, correction, or deletion via email to the Federal Reserve, but no self-service deletion mechanism or specific timeframe for processing such requests is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not specify any data retention periods for student or instructor account information, course progress records, or assessment data collected through the Econ Lowdown platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states security measures include 'technical and procedural steps to protect your data from misuse, access or disclosure, loss, alteration or destruction,' but does not specify what those measures are (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, audit logs).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of encryption (e.g., TLS/SSL for data in transit, encryption at rest) is made in the privacy policy; the site does appear to use HTTPS in practice, but this is not documented in the policy itself.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform requires account registration with a password, and an email confirmation process is mentioned, but no explicit password strength requirements or enforcement policies are described in the available documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform supports LTI integration with Canvas (a form of SSO), which partially satisfies MFA/SSO requirements for LTI users; however, direct Econ Lowdown account holders have no documented MFA option.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions session cookies for logged-in users, Google Analytics cookies, and possible third-party contractor cookies, but does not provide a full list of all cookies with individual names, purposes, and durations as would be expected in a complete cookie policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Google Analytics as a third-party service used for aggregate website analysis and references outside contractors for mailing list administration, but does not name all third-party vendors or services used specifically by the Econ Lowdown platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: While Google Analytics is identified as receiving aggregate, non-PII data, and contractors are said to receive data needed for their services, the policy does not specify what specific data fields are shared with each named or unnamed third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy does not provide a direct opt-out mechanism for Google Analytics data collection or contractor data sharing; users wishing to opt out of Google Analytics would need to use external browser tools, which is not addressed in the policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy explicitly states that outside contractors 'are required to keep information obtained through our website secure and confidential' and 'use personal information obtained through our website only on behalf of the Federal Reserve,' meeting the vendor agreement requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states the Federal Reserve reserves the right to change the policy at any time without notice, meaning users would not be specifically notified when third-party relationships or data-sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, as a non-commercial government entity, does not display advertisements on the Econ Lowdown platform, and the policy states collected data is 'for Federal Reserve use only.'
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy states the site does not rent, sell, or share personal information with nonaffiliated companies for commercial purposes, and there is no evidence of targeted advertising based on user data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google Analytics is used for aggregate site analysis, which may involve cookies set by Google; while the policy references Google's own privacy policy for opt-out options, no direct in-platform opt-out mechanism is provided to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy references Google Analytics cookies and mentions possible third-party contractor cookies but does not enumerate web beacons or pixel tracking; usage appears limited to analytics rather than advertising, though this is not fully explicit.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or commercial data sharing with advertisers takes place, and the policy states data is 'for Federal Reserve use only' and not sold or shared with nonaffiliated companies, there is no advertising data sharing to opt out of.

complianceNotes.SECQ4: Edia supports SSO via Google (and Clever per third-party listings), which provides federated identity management; no standalone MFA is described, but SSO availability meets the standard for K-12 contexts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy names two types of cookies — necessary/session cookies and Google Tracking cookies for analytics — but does not provide a comprehensive cookie list with individual purposes, and no cookie opt-out mechanism is described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references categories of third parties (service providers, Stripe, Google Analytics, district colleagues, law enforcement) but does not publish a named list of all current third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared is described by category of third party rather than specifying exactly which data elements are shared with each named vendor, making it a grouped rather than per-vendor disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No explicit opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing (e.g., Google Analytics) is provided; users can request deletion but cannot selectively opt out of specific third-party integrations while continuing to use the platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states third parties are prohibited from using personal information for purposes beyond delivering Edia's services, and Edia commits to maintaining current data sharing terms even if vendor relationships change.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy commits to maintaining data sharing terms with third parties through vendor changes but does not explicitly commit to notifying users when new third-party relationships are added or existing ones change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states that targeted advertising is not permitted on the site, representing a strong, unambiguous commitment against ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Targeted advertising is explicitly prohibited, and the policy states personal information will not be used for third-party advertising or marketing purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google Analytics tracking cookies are used for behavioral analytics on the platform, which may involve third-party data collection by Google; no opt-out from Google Analytics is described in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Google Tracking cookies are disclosed as being used for analytics and user behavior analysis, but the policy does not clarify whether Google's use of this data may include ad-related profiling beyond Edia's control.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No explicit opt-out mechanism for data sharing with analytics providers like Google is provided; the only recourse described is a full data deletion request rather than a granular opt-out.

r286.minAge: Under 13 with parental consent (school may act as parental agent under COPPA)
r286.riskReason: Edpuzzle holds iKeepSafe FERPA/COPPA/SOPIPA certification, is a Student Privacy Pledge signatory, does not sell student data or serve targeted ads, and limits data use strictly to educational service delivery.
r286.parentSummary: Edpuzzle collects student names, email addresses, video viewing history, and quiz responses to enable teachers to assign and track video lessons; this data is used solely for educational purposes and is never sold or used for advertising. The platform is COPPA and FERPA compliant, with schools acting as the parental consent agent for students under 13, and student accounts are automatically deleted after 18 months of inactivity. Parents who wish to delete their child's account or review their data must submit a request through their child's school or teacher.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Edpuzzle states it will notify users of policy changes via email and/or a general announcement on its website, but no publicly accessible version history or changelog for the policies is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy Policy and COPPA Direct Notice to Educational Institutions enumerate specific categories of data collected, including PII, usage data, IP addresses, cookies, viewing history, and quiz responses.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Edpuzzle clearly describes multiple collection methods: account registration, teacher-assigned class codes, LMS/SSO integration, cookies, and automatic collection of usage/device data.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Per the iKeepSafe profile and FERPA commitments, Edpuzzle explicitly states users retain possession and control of their own generated content, aligning with user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Teacher and administrator accounts can self-delete, but student account deletion requires a formal request through the school or teacher, meaning direct student/parent deletion is not available without an intermediary.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Edpuzzle states student data is retained only while the account is active and automatically deleted after 18 months of inactivity, with disaster-recovery backups retained for up to an additional 3 months.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Edpuzzle's Data Privacy and Security Plan documents specific security measures including encryption at rest (AES-CBC), password protection, role-based access controls, annual employee privacy training, and an Incident Response Plan.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Edpuzzle encrypts data at rest using AES (CBC mode) and data is hosted on Amazon Web Services; data in transit encryption (TLS) is industry-standard and referenced in district DPA agreements.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Edpuzzle supports SSO/LTI login via Google, Microsoft, and LMS integrations, which delegates password strength enforcement to those providers; the platform itself also supports password-based login with reset mechanisms.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Edpuzzle supports SSO through Google and Microsoft and LTI integration with LMS platforms, providing federated authentication that satisfies the MFA/SSO requirement for institutional users.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Edpuzzle mentions the use of cookies and similar technologies (IP addresses, cookies, etc.) in its policies, but a fully enumerated cookie list with individual purposes is not prominently published in a dedicated cookie policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Edpuzzle's iKeepSafe profile and Privacy Policy specifically name each third-party service provider (HubSpot, Mixpanel, OpenAI, Stripe, Zendesk, MongoDB, etc.) and their respective functions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The iKeepSafe profile and supplemental DSPS documents describe the specific function each third party performs, allowing reasonable inference of what data categories each receives to fulfill that function.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Edpuzzle explicitly states it does not sell, trade, or loan student PII to any third party including marketers, and data sharing with service providers is limited to what is necessary for service delivery with no opt-out required.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Edpuzzle's documentation states it has agreements in place with all third parties with access to student PII, requiring them to use data only for authorized service purposes and maintain confidentiality and security.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Edpuzzle's policy change notification process (email and/or website announcement) would cover third-party changes, but there is no explicit commitment to proactively notify users specifically when the third-party vendor list changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Edpuzzle's Privacy Policy, COPPA notice, and Common Sense Media evaluation all confirm that no personalized or third-party advertising is displayed to users on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Edpuzzle explicitly prohibits the use of PII for targeted advertising or other commercial uses, and Common Sense Media confirms no data profiles are created for personalized advertisements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Common Sense Media's evaluation confirms user information is not used to track and target advertisements on third-party websites or services, and third-party data collection for their own ad purposes is not permitted.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While cookies and usage tracking are used for functional and analytics purposes (e.g., Mixpanel, NewRelic), these are for service improvement, not for advertising; no ad-related web beacons are disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because Edpuzzle does not engage in advertising or share data with advertisers, no opt-out of advertiser data sharing is necessary, and this is clearly documented in policy.

dataCollected: Content created by teacher (word lists, quizzes, pairs)
r287.riskReason: Educandy explicitly states it does not collect student personal data, and students need no account, but the privacy policy lacks COPPA/FERPA declarations, minimum age requirements, specific third-party disclosures, and advance notification of policy changes, creating meaningful compliance gaps for U.S. K-12 deployments.
r287.parentSummary: Educandy collects personal information (username, email, password) only from teachers who create accounts; students access games via a shared code with no account or personal data required. The platform uses HTTPS encryption and states it does not sell data, but the privacy policy does not reference COPPA or FERPA compliance, does not specify a minimum age, and provides only vague descriptions of how teacher data may be used or retained, leaving some important protections unaddressed for U.S. schools.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service state modifications are effective immediately upon posting and users are expected to review the agreement periodically, with no advance notification process or revision history provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy states that teacher sign-up data (username, email) is collected and that student personal data is not collected, but does not enumerate all data types such as IP addresses, device info, or behavioral/usage analytics explicitly.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy references that data is collected when users sign up and through cookies, but does not specifically detail all collection mechanisms such as server logs, analytics tools, or app-based collection.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service assert that all materials on the site are owned and copyrighted by Educandy, with no explicit statement that user-submitted content or personal data remains user-owned.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Account deletion is possible by submitting a support ticket, but it is a manual process requiring staff involvement rather than a self-service option, with no stated timeframe for completion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy states data is kept 'only for as long as is necessary and in accordance with UK law' but does not provide a specific retention period or timeframe.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy states physical, electronic, and operational procedures are in place to safeguard data, but does not specify what those measures are beyond HTTPS encryption.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states that HTTPS encryption is used when data is transmitted from the user's computer to the server, indicating encryption in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Access is by username and password but no mention is made of password strength requirements or enforcement; Microsoft SSO is available for app purchases but not for core account login.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication is mentioned, and the standard login relies solely on username and password with no SSO or MFA option stated for the web platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy describes cookies and states they are used for navigation, preferences, and measuring site visits, but does not provide a full list of individual cookies and their specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy does not name any specific third-party service providers, analytics platforms, or data processors used by Educandy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown is provided of what specific data is shared with any third party; the only disclosure is that personal information may be shared if legally required.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can unsubscribe from marketing emails via an unsubscribe link, but no broader opt-out mechanism for any other form of data sharing is described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy contains no statement that third-party recipients of data are bound by data processing agreements or required to follow equivalent privacy protections.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no stated process for notifying users when third-party data relationships change; the ToS permits immediate modifications without advance notice.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No advertising of any kind is mentioned or apparent on the platform; the service is subscription and free-tier based with no indication of ad display.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no mention of targeted advertising, behavioral profiling, or use of user data for ad purposes anywhere in the privacy policy or terms.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is mentioned or indicated; cookies are described as functional and analytics-only with no link to advertising networks.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies are described in general terms for navigation and site analytics, but a complete list of all tracking technologies (e.g., pixels, SDKs) is not provided, leaving some ambiguity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or data sharing with advertisers is stated, an opt-out is not applicable; the absence of such practices effectively meets this criterion.

r288.riskReason: Educaplay is a Spain-based platform that explicitly uses third-party cookies for personalized advertising, does not specify a minimum age, contains no stated COPPA or FERPA compliance, and serves content to all ages including K-12 students without documented child-specific data protections.
r288.parentSummary: Educaplay collects account information (name, email, password) and usage/behavioral data including cookies for analytics and personalized advertising. The platform is operated by a Spanish company primarily governed by GDPR rather than US COPPA or FERPA, and it has no publicly documented minimum age requirement or parental consent process for students under 13. While Educaplay does offer a 'ticket' system allowing students to participate in activities without registering an account, the free tier displays third-party advertising and uses cookies tied to browsing behavior, which raises significant concerns for K-12 school use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy references updates may occur but does not clearly describe an advance notification process or maintain a publicly accessible revision history, resulting in only partial compliance.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy references collection of account data, usage data, and cookies but does not provide a fully exhaustive enumerated list of every data type collected, leaving some ambiguity.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy references collection via forms, cookies, and third-party logins, providing a general but not fully specific description of how each data type is collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; ownership and licensing terms for user-created content are referenced in platform terms but data ownership for personal information is not clearly assigned to the user.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their accounts, but the policy does not provide clear detail on whether all associated personal data is fully and promptly deleted upon account closure, making this only partial.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period or even a general retention statement is identifiable from publicly accessible policy summaries, leaving this requirement unmet.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy references data protection measures in general terms consistent with GDPR obligations, but specific technical or organizational security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls) are not enumerated.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS (standard encryption in transit) but the privacy policy does not explicitly state encryption at rest or detail encryption practices, yielding only partial credit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Account creation requires a password but no evidence of enforced strong password policies (e.g., minimum length, complexity requirements) was found in publicly accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Educaplay supports Google, Facebook, and Microsoft SSO login options which can provide MFA at the identity provider level, but the platform itself does not appear to natively enforce or offer MFA, resulting in partial compliance.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Educaplay acknowledges use of both own and third-party cookies including for advertising purposes and provides a cookie consent banner, but a fully detailed cookie list with individual purposes and retention periods was not identified in public-facing documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The platform broadly references use of third-party cookies and SSO providers (Google, Facebook, Microsoft) but does not publish a comprehensive named list of all third-party data processors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No documentation was found specifying exactly which data categories are shared with each named third party, failing to meet this requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: A cookie consent mechanism with a 'Set up' option is present allowing some cookie opt-out, but no clear comprehensive opt-out from all third-party data sharing is documented.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No publicly available statement was found confirming that third-party vendors are contractually bound to data protection standards equivalent to Educaplay's own policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No policy language was found committing to notify users when third-party sharing arrangements change, leaving this requirement unmet.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The free tier of Educaplay explicitly includes advertising (the Advanced paid plan is marketed as 'no publicity'), meaning ads are displayed to free-tier users including students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Educaplay's own site pages reference cookies used to 'personalize the advertising you see based on your browsing habits,' confirming behavioral/targeted advertising is employed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party cookies for advertising are confirmed in use with no clear opt-out mechanism specifically for ad tracking found beyond the general cookie consent banner.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Educaplay uses third-party cookies tied to advertising, and the cookie consent description suggests tracking for ad personalization purposes occurs across browsing sessions.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear, dedicated opt-out process for data sharing specifically with advertisers was identified; the general cookie settings panel provides limited control but does not constitute a full advertiser data-sharing opt-out.

dataCollected: Quiz, homework, and assessment answers and results
Google Classroom class roster and course info (if integrated)
dataSharedWith: Back-office SaaS tools (Finance, HR, Marketing, Customer Support)
CRM and marketing platform (for teacher communications)
r289.riskReason: Education Perfect expressly prohibits use of student data for advertising or commercial purposes, does not share student data with third parties, is ISO 27001 certified, and explicitly acknowledges COPPA compliance, though FERPA compliance is not formally stated and cookie use on the marketing site and vague data retention language introduce minor residual concerns.
r289.parentSummary: Education Perfect collects student names, school email addresses, login activity, and academic performance data solely to operate its learning platform. Student data is not shared with third-party systems, is never used for advertising or behavioral targeting, and schools retain control over student data with the ability to request deletion at any time. The platform is ISO 27001 certified and acknowledges COPPA obligations for children under 13, though the privacy policy does not explicitly reference FERPA compliance.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states material changes will be communicated via prominent in-service notice or email, and the policy is versioned with a date (last updated April 2025), but the consumer Terms of Use notes changes can take effect immediately upon posting without guaranteed advance notice, creating inconsistency.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and security risk assessment page enumerate specific categories of data collected including name, email, school ID, student ID, IP address, device info, login times, lesson time, quiz answers, results, and assignment completion data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically explains data is collected automatically on website visit, via school enrollment provisioning, via Google Classroom integration, and through optional profile configuration.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The standard terms explicitly state that schools and users retain ownership of their generated content, and the GDPR DPA designates the school as the data controller with Education Perfect acting as a processor on the school's instructions.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The security and risk assessment page states schools can request removal of user data from the system at any time, satisfying the full deletion right for school-administered accounts.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy states data is retained while a user is active or for as long as there is a legitimate interest, and the security page specifies automatic anonymization after 3 years of inactivity, but no specific retention period in days or months is stated for active users.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Education Perfect discloses ISO 27001 certification, AWS cloud hosting, role-based access controls, annual employee privacy and security training, and a detailed internal privacy compliance manual as specific security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The platform uses HTTPS and AWS infrastructure implying encryption in transit and at rest, but the privacy policy does not explicitly state encryption standards or confirm end-to-end encryption, making this only partially documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Account registration requires a password and email, but the privacy policy and terms do not specify password complexity or strength enforcement requirements, only stating an account and password are required.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Google Classroom SSO integration is supported for provisioning, but there is no explicit mention of MFA availability for teacher or administrator accounts in the publicly available policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies including functional and analytics/advertising cookies on the marketing website, and notes a Do Not Track non-response policy, but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies by name, type, and purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The third-party data processing page lists categories of third-party tools (CRM, billing, payments, support, onboarding) but does not name every specific vendor by company name across all categories.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The third-party page describes the purpose for each tool category but groups data sharing by function rather than specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each individual third-party vendor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Student data is explicitly stated as not shared with any third-party systems, and marketing opt-out is available via unsubscribe links, effectively meeting opt-out requirements for the relevant contexts.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The third-party processing page states that all third-party services are evaluated for appropriate security mechanisms and externally validated compliance such as SOC2 before use and on a regular schedule.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy states the policy link will be updated when changes are made and material changes will be communicated, but does not specifically commit to notifying users of changes to the list of third-party sub-processors.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Education Perfect explicitly states student data is not collected for advertising or behavioral targeting, and the only data collection tools are on the separate marketing website not accessible to students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The student data privacy policy explicitly states no student data is used for advertising, behavioral targeting, or any other commercial purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Student data is confirmed as not shared with any third-party systems, meaning no third-party ad tracking occurs within the learning platform used by students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While no advertising tracking is used within the student platform, the marketing website uses analytics and advertising cookies, and the privacy policy does not fully enumerate all tracking technologies used there.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Marketing communications include an unsubscribe option in all emails, and the privacy policy confirms users can opt out of marketing at any time by clicking the unsubscribe link or contacting Education Perfect.

dataSharedWith: Third parties receiving aggregate non-identifiable data
r290.riskReason: While Educreations explicitly prohibits selling or advertising-targeting student data and acknowledges COPPA obligations, its policies claim a broad perpetual and transferable license over user-uploaded content, security practices are vague, and third-party advertising use of data is not definitively ruled out for all contexts.
r290.parentSummary: Educreations collects student data including name, email, photo, audio and video recordings, school name, and usage activity, but states this information is used only to support the learning environment and is never sold or used for targeted advertising. Students under 13 must sign up with a teacher-provided class code, and consent is managed through the school acting as the parent's agent under COPPA. Parents and users can add, delete, or modify personal information at any time, though security practices and specific third-party service providers are not thoroughly detailed in the policy.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states Educreations 'may attempt to notify you when major changes are made' but does not guarantee advance notice or maintain a public revision history, making notification inconsistent.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and Common Sense evaluation confirm a detailed list of collected data types including name, email, photo, date of birth, school name, audio, video, online activity, and persistent identifiers.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy describes some collection methods (account creation, linked third-party services, content uploads) but does not comprehensively explain all technical data collection mechanisms such as cookies or tracking pixels.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Use state users and schools own their data, but the policy also declares that submitted personal information 'is our asset and will become part of our normal business records,' creating a contradictory ownership claim.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states users may add, delete, or modify personal information at any time, and GDPR users can demand deletion, satisfying the deletion requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state any specific or general data retention period for personal or student data after account closure or request.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy does not list specific security measures; Common Sense's evaluation noted the policies 'do not provide details on the confidentiality, security, or integrity of a student's personal information.'
complianceNotes.SECQ2: SSL/HTTPS encryption is present on the login page and site, but the privacy policy itself does not explicitly describe encryption practices for data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy and terms do not mention any password strength requirements or enforcement for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: While Clever Instant Login and Google sign-in are referenced in app store notes, the privacy policy and terms do not explicitly describe or require MFA or SSO for account security.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy does not include a dedicated cookie policy, list specific cookies, or explain the purpose of any cookies or tracking technologies used on the site.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references sharing with 'companies and organizations' under confidentiality agreements and mentions Facebook, Google, and Dropbox as third-party integrations, but does not name specific service provider vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing with affiliated companies and service providers without specifying which data elements are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can delete or modify their personal information and may opt out via account settings, but there is no explicit, standalone opt-out mechanism described specifically for third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that data may be shared with companies 'that have agreed not to disclose it to others,' indicating a general contractual requirement, but does not detail vendor agreement specifics.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states Educreations may update the Privacy Policy at its sole discretion and does not commit to notifying users specifically when third-party sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Educreations explicitly states it does not display ads to students, and the blog confirms the company's position that ads do not belong in educational products used by students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states student information 'is never used or disclosed for third-party advertising, or behaviorally-targeted advertising.'
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: While student data is stated to not be used for targeted advertising, Common Sense's evaluation found it unclear whether third-party tracking services operate on the platform for any purpose.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy does not address web beacons or other tracking technologies, leaving it unclear whether any such methods are employed beyond functional site operation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There is no clearly described opt-out mechanism for data sharing with any advertisers, though the explicit prohibition on student data use for advertising partially mitigates the concern.

r291.riskReason: edX is primarily designed for adult learners (min age 13), collects extensive personal and behavioral data, engages in third-party targeted advertising via cookies and pixel tracking, retains course data in archived research packages even after account deletion, and does not explicitly address COPPA or FERPA compliance for K-12 institutional use.
r291.parentSummary: edX collects personal information such as your child's name, email, date of birth, course activity, and browsing behavior, and shares this with partner universities, 2U (its parent company), service providers, and advertising partners. While edX provides an account deletion option, course data may be retained in encrypted research archives even after deletion and cannot always be fully removed. edX is not designed for K-12 use, does not explicitly claim COPPA or FERPA compliance, and uses third-party advertising cookies that track users across the web — making it a high-risk platform for school deployment without a dedicated data processing agreement.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service state that material revisions will be effective 30 days after posting or notice to existing users, but a full revision history is not publicly maintained or linked.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, usage data, course performance, cookies, proctoring data), but the enumeration is not exhaustive and some data types are described only in general terms.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically describes how data is collected — directly from users at registration and during course participation, automatically via cookies and tracking technologies, and from third parties such as social media platforms.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy does not clearly state that users own their data; edX retains course data in encrypted research archives even after deletion requests, and data may be transferred to successors in a sale or acquisition.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request account deletion via an in-account button, but deletion is limited: course data is archived for research purposes and historical activity logs are not immediately purged, representing only partial deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained as long as the account is active or as needed for legal/financial obligations, but no specific retention periods (in days or years) are stated, making the retention period vague.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy references maintaining 'reasonable security practices' and the edX research data guide references disk encryption and firewalls, but the main consumer-facing privacy policy does not list specific security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: edX's data security documentation references encrypted research data packages and disk encryption for stored learner data, but the main privacy policy does not explicitly confirm end-to-end or in-transit encryption for all user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service and Privacy Policy do not mention any password strength enforcement requirements or policies, and there is no reference to SSO or similar mechanisms as a default.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: There is no mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) availability or requirement in either the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy, and no reference to LTI or SSO integration for institutional accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: edX provides a dedicated Cookie Policy page (https://www.edx.org/edx-privacy-policy/cookies) that categorizes cookies by type (functional, performance, targeting/advertising) and identifies their purposes, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy identifies broad categories of third parties (service providers, 2U affiliates, payment processors, proctoring vendors, advertising partners) but does not name specific third-party companies beyond 2U.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared with third parties by category of recipient but does not specify exactly which data fields are shared with each individual third party, providing only a generalized disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of interest-based advertising via DAA/EDAA/NAI tools referenced in the Cookie Policy, and can manage cookie preferences, but opt-out from all third-party data sharing is not clearly available.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that service providers are 'prohibited from using or sharing your information for any other purposes' and are required to maintain 'reasonable security practices,' constituting a general contractual obligation but without detailed specifics.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Terms of Service indicate edX may update policies and recommends users check periodically, but there is no stated commitment to proactively notify users specifically when third-party partners or data sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Cookie Policy explicitly states that edX uses targeting and advertising cookies to 'collect information about browser habits to target advertising' and provide user visit data to advertising agencies, confirming ads are displayed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The Cookie Policy confirms that edX and its advertising partners use tracking technologies to serve interest-based (targeted) advertisements to users based on browsing behavior across the internet.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising tracking is confirmed, but users can opt out via DAA, EDAA, and NAI opt-out tools referenced in the Cookie Policy, providing a limited but available opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The Cookie Policy explicitly references pixel tags, HTML5 storage objects, web beacons, and third-party cookies used for targeting and advertising purposes, confirming use of web beacons/tracking methods for ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The Cookie Policy references DAA/EDAA/NAI opt-out tools and the ability to disable non-essential cookies, but the process is described externally and is not a simple, direct in-platform opt-out, making it only partially clear.

dataCollected: Rostering data from student information systems
r292.riskReason: eDynamic Learning explicitly states it will never sell student data, conduct targeted advertising to students, or build marketing profiles, and explicitly claims COPPA and FERPA compliance with school-directed consent mechanisms.
r292.parentSummary: eDynamic Learning collects student data such as name, email, date of birth, and course/usage data primarily through school rostering and direct platform use, and uses it solely for educational purposes. The platform explicitly commits to never selling student data, never conducting targeted advertising toward students, and never building marketing profiles. Third-party sub-processors (such as AWS and Google) are named on a dedicated Trusted Partners page, and all are contractually required to meet eDynamic's privacy and security standards.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states material changes will be posted and users are encouraged to check back periodically, but advance notification before changes take effect is not guaranteed and no formal revision history is maintained.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates categories of data collected including personal information input by customers (name, email, date of birth), usage data, course/assessment data, and rostering data from student information systems.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes three methods of data collection: customer-provided rostering/SIS transfer, data generated directly by student/educator use of the service, and data generated from general service usage.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy explicitly states 'We will never claim ownership of Student Data,' clearly assigning data ownership to the user/institution rather than the company.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy states that upon request, school customers can review and delete student personal information, but individual student/parent deletion rights are directed back to the school rather than directly to eDynamic, limiting direct deletion access.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained 'only for as long as reasonably necessary' to fulfill the purpose and comply with legal obligations, but no specific retention periods (e.g., 90 days, 1 year) are provided, making this a general rather than specific retention statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references security measures and requires service providers to comply with 'appropriate security measures,' encourages federated identity management (SAML), and has breach notification procedures, but does not list specific technical security controls (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, penetration testing).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy does not explicitly state that data is encrypted in transit or at rest; while AWS is used for hosting (which typically includes encryption), this is not stated directly in eDynamic's own policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy encourages use of federated identity management or 'strong and unique passwords' but does not confirm that strong passwords are technically enforced on the platform itself.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The policy encourages use of secure federated identity management technologies such as SAML (which supports SSO), but MFA is not explicitly mentioned as available or required.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The website acknowledges both necessary/functional cookies and non-necessary cookies (analytics, ads, embedded content), but does not provide a full cookie inventory with named cookies, purposes, and durations in the privacy policy itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: A dedicated Trusted Partners page at edynamiclearning.com/trusted-partners/ names all sub-processors specifically, including AWS, Google, Salesforce, Agilix, Cloudflare, and over a dozen others with links to their privacy policies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Trusted Partners page lists sub-processors with their general function (e.g., 'Customer Support,' 'Marketing Tooling,' 'LMS') but does not specify exactly which personal data fields are shared with each third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy provides California residents a process to opt out via email, and states that student data is never shared for advertising, but there is no general opt-out mechanism for non-California users regarding subprocessor data sharing for operational purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states that third parties with access to personal information are 'subject to stringent privacy and security contractual requirements' including deletion, de-identification, and prohibitions on unauthorized collection and use.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not mention any process for notifying users when sub-processors are added, removed, or changed on the Trusted Partners list.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states 'We will never conduct targeted advertising to Student Users,' and no advertising is displayed to students within the educational platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states student data will never be used for targeted advertising and marketing profiles of student users will never be built.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy commits to never sharing student data with third parties for targeted advertising purposes, effectively prohibiting third-party tracking of students for ad purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While the website uses non-necessary cookies for analytics and embedded content on its marketing site, the policy explicitly prohibits use of tracking for advertising directed at student users of the educational service.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out is needed for student data sharing with advertisers because the policy categorically prohibits such sharing; Nevada opt-out is addressed and stated as not applicable since data uses do not constitute sales.

r293.riskReason: No publicly accessible Terms of Service or Privacy Policy could be located at https://www.elearning.com, making it impossible to verify any data collection, sharing, or protection practices required for K-12 compliance.

The absence of these foundational legal documents is itself a serious red flag for any K-12 school considering this platform. Schools and parents should not allow student use of any platform that does not publish clear, accessible privacy and data use policies.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Terms of Service or Privacy Policy was found at elearning.com, so no policy change notification process can be evaluated.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: No Privacy Policy was discoverable at elearning.com, so there is no listing of data collected from users.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Without a Privacy Policy, there is no disclosure of how data is collected from users or students.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: No policy document was found to determine data ownership rights for users or students.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No policy was located that addresses user or student rights to request data deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No Privacy Policy exists at elearning.com to state any data retention period or schedule.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No documentation of security measures, technical controls, or data protection practices was found.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No information about encryption practices in transit or at rest was discoverable for this platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Without any terms or policy, there is no information about password standards or enforcement.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No information about multi-factor authentication or SSO support was found in any accessible policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy or disclosure of cookie usage and purpose was found at elearning.com.
