r294.riskReason: ELEGOO is a consumer e-commerce and hardware platform that requires users to be at least 18 years old, has no COPPA or FERPA compliance provisions, collects extensive personal and device data, partners with third-party advertisers for personalized tracking, and has no student data protections making it wholly unsuitable for K-12 use.
r294.parentSummary: ELEGOO collects a broad range of personal data including names, email addresses, billing details, device identifiers, location data, and browsing behavior, and shares this data with third-party advertisers, payment processors, and partner services for marketing and operational purposes. The platform requires users to be at least 18 years old and has no COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance provisions, making it inappropriate for use by K-12 students. There are no student-specific data protections, and third-party advertising trackers including cookies and tracking pixels are used across the platform.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it is updated periodically and instructs users to review it regularly, but does not provide advance notification of changes or a revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy provides a reasonably detailed enumeration of data collected including account info, device data, location, Wi-Fi, payment information, and usage data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy explains data is collected via account registration, platform use, cookies, mobile applications, Google APIs, and third-party service providers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is not explicitly assigned to the user; the policy focuses on how ELEGOO uses and shares data without clearly affirming user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can withdraw consent and opt out of certain data uses, but there is no clear, straightforward account or data deletion mechanism described for general users.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes collected, but does not specify exact retention periods for most data categories.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references general commitments to protecting privacy but does not enumerate specific technical security measures on the main website privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is referenced in associated app-specific privacy documents (TLS), but the main website privacy policy does not explicitly confirm encryption of user data in transit or at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy places responsibility for password confidentiality on the user but does not state that ELEGOO enforces strong password requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and tracking pixels broadly and references opt-out tools, but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies used with their specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names some third parties (Amazon, PayPal, Google APIs, advertising providers) but does not provide a complete named list of all third-party data recipients.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by category of recipient rather than specifying exactly what data is shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications and use the DAA WebChoices tool for ad tracking, but opt-out from all third-party data sharing is not clearly available.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states partners may have their own privacy policies and that some data is subject to third-party terms, but does not clearly state that all third parties are contractually bound to ELEGOO's data standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not state that users will be notified when third-party data sharing arrangements change; it only advises users to review the policy periodically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states that ELEGOO partners with third-party advertisers and uses cookies and technologies to deliver personalized advertising on third-party platforms.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms targeted/personalized advertising is conducted via third-party advertising partners using user data and tracking technologies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The DAA WebChoices opt-out tool is mentioned as a way to globally opt out of third-party tracking cookies, but ELEGOO disclaims responsibility for its effectiveness.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms use of tracking pixels, cookies, and third-party advertising network trackers over which ELEGOO states it has no control.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of marketing emails and use third-party opt-out tools for ad tracking, but no clear, direct, platform-level opt-out from all advertiser data sharing is provided.

r295.riskReason: Ella Learning collects substantial student identity data including date of birth, grades, and school schedule, and while it prohibits use of student data for advertising, it lacks explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance statements, has no stated data retention period, and its cookie policy does not enumerate all cookies with their purposes.
r295.parentSummary: Ella Learning collects student identity information such as name, school name, date of birth, grades, and schedule, as well as technical data like IP addresses and browser information, to provide its educational services under agreement with schools. The platform explicitly states it will not use student data for advertising or share it with third parties for marketing purposes, and security measures including access controls and periodic risk assessments are in place. However, the privacy policy does not specify a data retention period, does not explicitly reference COPPA or FERPA compliance, and data may be shared with service vendors like Google and AWS or transferred in the event of a business merger or acquisition.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service state that advance notice will be provided and governing body consent obtained before implementing amended terms, but there is no mention of a publicly accessible revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates specific categories of data collected including Student Identity Data, Parent Identity Data, Teacher Identity Data, Contact Data, Technical Data, Profile Data, Usage Data, Communications Data, and De-identified Data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy states data is collected through use of the Properties (website and mobile apps) and through account creation and service interaction, but does not specifically describe the technical mechanisms of collection such as forms, automatic logging, or cookies in the main policy body.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy does not clearly assert that users or schools own the data; data ownership and control language is vague, referencing obligations to a 'Governing Body' but not explicitly stating that students or schools retain ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy does not include a self-service deletion mechanism; users would need to contact the platform, and there is no stated timeline or process for honoring deletion requests.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not specify any data retention period or retention schedule for student or user data, leaving this entirely unaddressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy states appropriate security measures are in place, access is limited to those with a business need, and periodic risk assessments are conducted, but does not enumerate specific technical security controls such as encryption standards or firewall protections.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy does not mention encryption of data in transit or at rest, and no encryption standard or protocol is referenced anywhere in the available documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Neither the Terms of Service nor the Privacy Policy mentions password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: There is no mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration in the available policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A separate Cookie Policy page exists at ellalearn.com/cookie-policy/ and mentions cookies are used for preferences, account settings, and service improvement, but does not enumerate all cookies by name or provide a full cookie inventory with individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy names Google (for email) and Amazon Web Services (for hosting/storage) as vendor examples but uses 'including but not limited to' language, indicating the list is not exhaustive.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy policy groups data shared with vendors generally without specifying which data elements are shared with each named third party such as Google or AWS.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The privacy policy does not provide any opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing; there is no process described for users to opt out of data being shared with service vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states that third-party vendors 'will only process your personal data on our instructions and they are subject to a duty of confidentiality,' indicating contractual obligations are imposed on processors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not state that users will be notified of changes to third-party vendor relationships or if new third parties are added to data processing activities.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states that student identity, teacher, parent, profile, and contact data will not be used to advertise or market products and services.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly prohibits using student data for advertising or marketing purposes and states personal data will not be shared with third parties for marketing, indicating no targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy's prohibition on using student data for advertising and marketing implies no third-party tracking for advertising purposes, though this is not stated explicitly in the context of tracking technologies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The Cookie Policy references cookies being used for preferences and service improvement but does not clearly confirm or deny whether any cookies or web beacons are used for advertising tracking purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since the policy explicitly prohibits use of data for advertising and marketing and states no sharing with third parties for marketing, there is effectively no advertising data sharing to opt out of, which satisfies this criterion.

dataSharedWith: Other registered users for educational purposes (with consent)
r296.riskReason: Ellii acknowledges COPPA and FERPA obligations and allows student accounts under 13 with parental/guardian setup, but the privacy policy explicitly states it may change without notice, uses Google Analytics (transmitting IP data to US servers), provides only general security statements without specific measures listed, and lacks specific data retention periods or detailed per-third-party data disclosure.
r296.parentSummary: Ellii collects personal information including names, email addresses, school names, ages, and usage data from registered users, including students whose accounts are created by teachers or guardians. The platform acknowledges FERPA and COPPA and states it will not sell personal data, but it shares usage data with Google Analytics and discloses information to service providers and payment processors. Parents should be aware that the privacy policy can change without advance notice and that data retention periods are not specifically defined.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states it may be changed 'without any notice or liability' to the user, with no advance notification or revision history provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists specific categories of personal data collected including name, email, postal address, educational information, school name, age, group contact information, interests of children, usage data, and IP address.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes that data is collected through account registration forms, subscriptions, user correspondence, service requests, and Google Analytics cookies.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy is unclear on data ownership; it describes data use by Red River Press but does not explicitly affirm that users own their data, creating ambiguity.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy explicitly states users may request deletion of some or all personal information by contacting the company, satisfying the deletion requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period or general retention timeframe is stated in the privacy policy; the policy is silent on how long data is kept after account closure or inactivity.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references security safeguards and breach notification obligations in general terms but does not list specific security measures such as encryption standards, firewalls, or access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is mentioned only in the context of payment/credit card protection in the Terms of Use; no statement on broader data encryption at rest or in transit is provided.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy and terms do not mention password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords, nor is SSO or MFA referenced as an alternative.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is found in the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Google Analytics and payment processors PayPal, Stripe, and Recurly by name, but other service providers and partners are described only in general terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Specific data shared with each third party is not individually itemized; the policy groups disclosures broadly rather than specifying what data goes to each named or unnamed third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can unsubscribe from marketing communications, but no clear opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing (e.g., Google Analytics) is described within the policy itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states data is shared with service providers 'as is reasonably necessary' but does not explicitly require third parties to be bound by a data processing agreement or equivalent vendor obligation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may be changed at any time without notice, and does not specifically commit to notifying users of changes to third-party sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The platform is a subscription-based educational service; no evidence of display advertising targeting logged-in users is found in the policies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising directed at users within the platform is mentioned or indicated in the policies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google Analytics is used and transmits IP addresses and usage data to Google servers in the US; no explicit opt-out mechanism for this tracking is described within the Ellii policy itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Google Analytics cookies are used and described, but no comprehensive cookie inventory with purposes for all cookie types is provided; tracking methods beyond Google Analytics are not detailed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can unsubscribe from marketing emails, but no clear opt-out process specifically for data sharing with analytics/advertising-related third parties is described in the policy.

dataSharedWith: Third-party service providers for business operations
r297.riskReason: Originator/Endless Apps explicitly states it does not seek to collect PII from children under 13, and states no behavioral advertising, but the privacy policy is outdated (copyright 2013), third-party service providers are named only in a separate Cubric-specific policy rather than the main Endless Apps policy, and no FERPA certification or formal third-party COPPA Safe Harbor verification (e.g., kidSAFE, iKeepSafe) was found for the Endless Apps suite specifically.
r297.parentSummary: Endless Apps (by Originator Inc.) are designed for young children ages 2–6 and explicitly state they do not seek to collect personally identifiable information directly from children under 13; any such data collected inadvertently will be deleted upon parental request. The apps are advertised as 100% free of advertisements and do not use child data for behavioral or targeted advertising. However, the main privacy policy appears outdated (last copyright notice is 2013), does not name specific third-party service providers used, and no independent FERPA or formal COPPA Safe Harbor certification was found for the Endless Apps suite, which may concern schools requiring verified compliance documentation.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The TOS states Originator may update it by posting a new version on the website, but the main privacy policy bears a 2013 copyright date with no advance notification commitment and no visible revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists some data categories (name, email, device information, usage data) but uses vague language ('depending on the information and/or services you request') and does not comprehensively enumerate all data types collected across all Endless apps.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected when users request information or services and through app usage, but does not specifically describe the technical collection mechanisms (e.g., SDK tracking, automatic device logs) in sufficient detail.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly assert user ownership of data; it describes data use by the company and mentions potential asset transfers in mergers, implying Originator retains control over collected data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy states inadvertently collected child PII will be deleted at parental request via contact email, but does not describe a self-service deletion mechanism or process for adults' own data deletion; contact-based deletion only partially meets this standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The main privacy policy contains no stated data retention period or schedule; no specific timeframe or retention policy is articulated for how long user data is held.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states only that 'despite our best efforts, no security measures are completely impenetrable' without listing any specific security measures implemented to protect user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption is made in the main privacy policy; the children's policy for Cubric references trusted infrastructure providers (AWS, Azure) but encryption is not explicitly confirmed for the Endless Apps suite.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The TOS requires users to be 13 or older to register, and the apps are primarily used without account creation by young children; no account is required for core app use, which meets this criterion for the child-user context.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No user account creation is required for core gameplay in the Endless apps; purchases are handled via Apple App Store or Google Play Store authentication, which provides platform-level SSO, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The main privacy policy does not contain a cookie policy or enumerate specific cookies and their purposes; no cookie disclosure is present on the endlessapps/originatorkids main policy page.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The main Endless Apps privacy policy does not name specific third-party service providers; third-party names (AWS, Unity, Google, AppsFlyer, Zendesk, Azure, Amplitude, Saucelabs) appear only in the separate Cubric children's privacy policy, not in the primary Endless Apps policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Cubric children's policy names third-party providers but does not specify exactly what data is shared with each individual vendor; the main Endless Apps policy provides no per-vendor data breakdown.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The children's policy explicitly states child personal information is not shared with anyone outside Originator and is not used for behavioral or targeted advertising, effectively providing a no-sharing guarantee that satisfies opt-out requirements.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The children's policy states third-party providers are not allowed to use children's information for their own needs or share it with anyone else, but the main policy provides only a general statement without contractual specifics.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Neither the main privacy policy nor the TOS includes a process for notifying users of changes to third-party vendor relationships; policy updates are indicated only by a new posting on the website with no advance notice.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Endless Learning Academy School Edition and other Endless apps explicitly state they are 100% free of advertisements, satisfying this criterion.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The children's policy explicitly states child personal data is not used for behavioral or targeted advertising, clearly meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy confirms no third-party tracking for advertising purposes for child users; third-party vendors listed are infrastructure/analytics providers with explicit restrictions against using data for their own purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While no advertising tracking is confirmed, the use of analytics vendors such as Amplitude and AppsFlyer involves tracking technologies whose full scope is not detailed in the main Endless Apps privacy policy, leaving some ambiguity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising data sharing occurs with child users per the policy, there is no applicable opt-out needed; the policy's prohibition on behavioral advertising effectively satisfies this criterion.

r298.riskReason: Engineering Tomorrow's website lacks a discoverable, substantive Privacy Policy entirely, and the Terms of Use page returns only general nonprofit mission content with no meaningful data governance disclosures, leaving all K-12 data privacy compliance questions completely unanswered.
r298.parentSummary: Engineering Tomorrow (engineeringtomorrow.org) is a nonprofit offering free virtual engineering labs to high school students, but its website does not publish an accessible Privacy Policy document. The Terms of Use page exists in URL form but renders only general organizational content, with no information about what data is collected, how it is used, or what protections are in place for students. Until a comprehensive privacy policy is published, parents and schools have no basis to evaluate whether student data is being handled appropriately.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No privacy policy is publicly accessible on the site, so no policy change notification process or revision history can be evaluated.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: No privacy policy was found that lists any categories of data collected from users or students.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: There is no documentation anywhere on the site explaining how data is collected (e.g., forms, cookies, third-party tools).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: No policy exists that addresses data ownership; it is entirely silent on whether users or the organization owns submitted data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No mechanism or policy language addressing user data deletion rights was found anywhere on the platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or retention policy of any kind is disclosed on the site.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No security measures, safeguards, or data protection practices are described anywhere on the site.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption, SSL, or any data-in-transit or data-at-rest protection is made anywhere on the site.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The site does not appear to require user accounts for accessing content, and no password policy is stated; the absence of account documentation leaves this unresolved.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI integration is found anywhere on the site.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: There is no cookie policy, cookie banner, or disclosure of cookie usage on the platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No third-party vendors, service providers, or data-sharing partners are named or disclosed anywhere.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Without any third-party disclosure, there is no information about what specific data is shared with any third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described anywhere on the site.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor agreements, data processing agreements, or third-party contractual obligations are mentioned on the site.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no process described for notifying users of changes to third-party data-sharing relationships.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No advertising policy exists; it is unknown whether ads are displayed within the platform's digital tools.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The absence of any advertising or privacy policy means targeted advertising practices are completely undisclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure exists regarding third-party tracking technologies or ad-related trackers being used on the site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No disclosure of web beacons, pixel tags, or other tracking methods is made anywhere on the site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out mechanism for data sharing with advertisers is described, nor is advertising even acknowledged.

dataCollected: User-generated content (messages, photos, videos, lesson plans)
r299.riskReason: Epic does not sell student data and states COPPA/FERPA compliance for its School Plus tier, but its consumer-facing policy confirms third-party partners collect data for targeted advertising purposes, parental consent processes are unclear, and the platform lacks formal COPPA Safe Harbor certification.
r299.parentSummary: Epic collects personal identifiers, payment information, device and usage data, location information, and reading history from children under 13, and shares this data with service providers for operational purposes such as hosting, payment processing, and customer support. While Epic states it does not sell or rent data, its privacy policy confirms that third-party partners may collect data for targeted advertising, which is a notable concern for K-12 use. The platform claims COPPA and FERPA alignment—especially through its paid Epic School Plus tier—but lacks formal Safe Harbor certification and has unclear parental consent withdrawal processes.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Epic's policies indicate updates may occur but the process for advance notification and maintaining a full revision history is not clearly described in publicly available policy language.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy specifies categories of personal information collected including identifiers, payment information, device and usage data, location information, and reading/usage analytics.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected when users register and use the service, but does not provide a fully detailed breakdown of each specific collection mechanism (e.g., forms, cookies, SDKs) for every data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Common Sense Media's evaluation confirms users retain ownership of their data, though Epic claims a limited-scope copyright license to user-generated content.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Processes for authorized users to delete data are available, and children's personal information is deleted if collected without parental consent, satisfying the deletion requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is deleted when no longer necessary, but does not specify a precise retention period (e.g., 90 days, 1 year) for most data categories, making this only a general retention statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references data security practices and access controls but does not enumerate specific technical security measures (e.g., AES-256, SOC 2) in its publicly available privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Data in transit is confirmed encrypted (HTTPS), but whether data at rest is encrypted is unclear per Common Sense Media's evaluation, resulting in only partial credit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Account creation requires a username and password but the policy does not specify enforcement of strong password standards; SSO is noted as a forthcoming feature for Epic School Plus but is not yet universally available.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Multi-factor authentication is not mentioned in Epic's consumer privacy policy; SSO for district accounts is described as a planned future feature, not a current standard offering.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions use of cookies and tracking technologies but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies with their individual purposes, only a general description of cookie usage.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names broad categories of service providers (hosting, payment, customer support) but does not enumerate specific third-party company names used for data processing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Purposes for sharing with third-party service providers are indicated at a grouped level, but specific data elements shared with each individual third party are not disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications, but the ability to opt out of data sharing with third-party advertising partners is unclear, per Common Sense Media's evaluation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not clearly state that all third-party service providers are contractually bound to the same data privacy and security standards as Epic itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no explicit statement in the publicly available policy that users will be notified if third-party data-sharing partners change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Common Sense Media confirms that third-party partners collect data for targeted advertising purposes, meaning ads or ad-related tracking extend beyond the platform itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms Epic and third-party partners collect data for targeted advertising, indicating user data is used for targeting beyond first-party contextual ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: User information is confirmed to be used to track and target advertisements on third-party websites and services, with no clear opt-out mechanism disclosed in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy acknowledges use of cookies, web beacons, and similar tracking technologies, and Common Sense Media confirms these are used in connection with third-party advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Whether users can clearly opt out of data sharing with advertisers is listed as unclear by Common Sense Media, and no explicit opt-out process for advertising data sharing is described in the publicly available policy.

dataCollected: Optional third-party test scores (NWEA Map Growth, Renaissance Star)
Student choices and inputs for AI-enabled activities
r300.riskReason: eSpark explicitly prohibits selling student data, displays no ads to students, claims COPPA/FERPA/SOPIPA compliance, stores data on AWS within the US, and restricts data use to educational purposes only.
r300.parentSummary: eSpark collects limited student information — including names, school IDs, grade levels, and learning activity data — provided by teachers or school officials (never directly from students) solely to deliver personalized educational content. The platform explicitly commits to never selling student data, never showing ads to students, and storing all data securely on AWS servers in the United States. Parents may request to review, correct, or delete their child's data by contacting eSpark, though the policy notes that deleted data may persist in backup copies.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use state changes are effective upon posting with no advance notification requirement, though the Privacy Policy is date-stamped (updated January 2, 2025); no formal revision history is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy Policy specifically enumerates collected data including student names, school IDs, grade levels, teachers, class enrollment, usage data, activity data, placement/progress data, optional third-party test scores, and AI interaction inputs.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly explains data is collected via teacher-initiated rostering through integrations (Google Classroom, Clever) or manual entry, and that students never provide data directly.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy explicitly states that information provided by a school district is owned by the school district or the student, not eSpark, which only has permission to use it to provide services.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents may request deletion of their child's data, but the policy warns that removed information may persist in backup copies indefinitely, limiting the effectiveness of deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not specify a concrete data retention period; it implies data is retained while the student is active in the program but does not state a defined timeframe after account closure.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states data is hosted on AWS with servers in the United States and mentions breach notification procedures, but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or audits.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy references secure data hosting on AWS and mentions 'securely collected' data but does not explicitly state encryption in transit or at rest is used for student data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Students cannot create their own accounts; teachers roster students via integrations (Google Classroom, Clever) or manually, meaning student access is controlled by SSO/rostering systems rather than individual passwords.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Student accounts are managed entirely through teacher rostering and SSO integrations (Google Classroom, Clever), eliminating the need for student-level password or MFA management.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Privacy Policy mentions use of cookies and analytics services but does not provide a comprehensive cookie inventory with specific names, types, and purposes for each cookie used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy broadly references sharing with 'technology companies for web hosting and analytics' and names AWS for hosting and Google Classroom/Clever for rostering, but does not provide a comprehensive named list of all third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared with third parties generally (hosting, analytics, rostering) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy states eSpark will never sell or share student data without consent, and students receive no ads; there is effectively no third-party ad sharing to opt out of, meeting this criterion.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that in cases of business transfer, the new provider must agree to 'data privacy standards no less stringent than our own,' but does not reference formal supplier/vendor data processing agreements for all third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Terms of Use state changes are effective upon posting without advance notice, and the Privacy Policy does not specifically commit to notifying users when third-party service providers change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states students will never receive any advertisements from eSpark while using the service.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly prohibits using personal information to send marketing messages to students, and no targeted advertising is conducted within the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party tracking for advertising purposes is disclosed or permitted within the student-facing platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No advertising-related web beacons or tracking methods are described; any tracking appears limited to functional/analytics use for service improvement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or data sharing with advertisers occurs on the student platform, there is nothing to opt out of; this criterion is fully satisfied by design.

r301.riskReason: Etymonline uses Google DART advertising cookies and Google Analytics to track and serve targeted ads to all visitors including students under 16, with no COPPA or FERPA compliance statements and no meaningful parental consent mechanism.
r301.parentSummary: Etymonline collects usage data, IP addresses, browser information, and uses Google DART cookies to serve interest-based ads to all users. The site states it does not address anyone under 16 and does not knowingly collect data from children under 16, but it lacks formal COPPA or FERPA compliance frameworks, and third-party advertising tracking (Google AdSense/DART) is active for all visitors. Parents should be aware that if a student uses this site, their browsing behavior may be tracked by Google's advertising network with limited opt-out options.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service states a revision date will appear at the bottom of the page and encourages users to check periodically, but there is no advance notification process — users are bound by changes simply by continuing to use the service.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists log file data (IP address, browser type, ISP, timestamps, referring/exit pages, clicks) and usage data, but does not comprehensively enumerate all categories of personal data that may be collected via account creation or third-party tools.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected via log files, cookies (including DART cookies), Google Analytics, and Firebase, providing reasonably specific collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service states that the service and its content 'are and will remain the exclusive property of Etymonline,' and there is no statement affirming that users own their own data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The Terms of Service states that to terminate an account a user may 'simply discontinue using the Service,' which does not constitute a meaningful data deletion mechanism; no formal deletion request process is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as necessary for stated purposes and legal obligations, but does not specify a concrete retention period in days or months, making this a vague general statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy mentions 'appropriate data collection, storage and processing practices and security measures' but does not enumerate specific technical security controls beyond SSL/encryption.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states that sensitive data exchange 'happens over a SSL secured communication channel and is encrypted and protected with digital signatures.'
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform does not require account creation for basic use and there is no mention of password strength enforcement or requirements anywhere in the Terms or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration; account creation is optional and MFA is not referenced.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies generally and names DART advertising cookies and Google Analytics cookies specifically, but does not provide a full enumerated cookie list with purposes for each cookie type.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google is named as a third-party vendor using DART cookies and providing Analytics/Firebase services, but other potential third-party service providers are referenced only generically without being named.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states Google Analytics receives usage/traffic data and Google AdSense uses DART cookies for ad targeting, but data shared with unnamed 'third-party service providers' is not broken down by party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of DART cookies via the Google ad and content network Privacy Policy URL provided, and Firebase features can be adjusted via device settings, but opt-out for other third parties is not addressed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states third-party service providers 'are obligated not to disclose or use it for any other purpose,' indicating a general contractual obligation, but no specifics about vendor agreements or audits are provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not include any provision notifying users when third-party vendors change or when new third parties are added to the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly confirms that Google DART cookies are used to 'serve ads to site visitors based upon their visit to etymonline.com and other sites on the internet,' and the site displays ads to non-premium users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Google DART cookies are confirmed to serve interest-based and behavioral targeted advertising to all users including students, with no age-gating or school-use exemption.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Users can opt out of DART cookies by visiting the Google ad network Privacy Policy URL provided in the policy, but the opt-out process is indirect and relies entirely on Google's own tools.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms use of DART cookies (web beacons/tracking for ads) to serve ads based on cross-site browsing behavior, which constitutes confirmed ad-tracking beyond functional use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An indirect opt-out path is referenced via Google's ad network privacy policy URL, but no clear, platform-native opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described.

dataCollected: Usage data (log data, actions taken in app)
Device information (device type, OS, hardware identifiers, IMEI, SIM number)
Third-party account data (e.g., via Google login)
dataSharedWith: Service providers (credit card processors, customer management systems)
Affiliates and subsidiaries (Bending Spoons S.p.A., Evernote do Brasil)
r302.riskReason: Evernote Scannable is governed by the general Evernote privacy policy, which permits targeted advertising, collects extensive personal and device data, does not explicitly address COPPA or FERPA compliance, lacks a minimum age requirement, and allows data transfer to third parties and advertisers — making it unsuitable for K-12 use without significant additional contractual protections.
r302.parentSummary: Evernote Scannable operates under Evernote's broader privacy policy, which collects a wide range of data including email, device identifiers, IP address, usage logs, scanned content, and optionally location data. This data is shared with service providers, analytics partners, and advertising networks, and users may be subject to targeted advertising. While Evernote states it does not sell personal data, it does not explicitly claim COPPA or FERPA compliance, does not state a minimum age for Scannable specifically, and allows for data transfer in the event of a merger or acquisition — raising serious concerns for use with K-12 students.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it may be amended as new features or legal requirements arise and to check back periodically, but does not guarantee advance notification to users before changes take effect.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy clearly enumerates categories of data collected including email, billing information, usage data, IP address, location, device identifiers, and scanned content.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes data collected directly from users, automatically through app usage and cookies, and from third-party login services such as Google.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy implies user ownership through data export rights ('Third Law of Data Protection') but does not unambiguously assert that users own their data, creating partial clarity.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion of content, but data is not automatically deleted upon account cancellation and deletion requests are evaluated on a case-by-case basis for suspended accounts.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states specific retention periods: up to 3 years for service/support data and up to 5 years for legal compliance data from last interaction or subscription expiry.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Security Overview policy states Evernote encrypts data in transit and at rest, conducts regular security audits, enforces strict access controls, and has an incident response plan.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The Security Overview confirms encryption of user data both in transit and in storage, meeting the encryption standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Evernote offers two-factor authentication but does not explicitly enforce strong password requirements; password strength enforcement is not clearly stated in the policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Evernote offers optional two-factor authentication (2FA) for accounts, which satisfies the MFA availability requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy references a Cookie Notice for details on cookies and opt-out but does not enumerate all cookies with their specific purposes within the main privacy policy text.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references broad categories of third parties such as service providers, analytics vendors, and ad partners but does not name specific third-party companies in the main policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups third-party data sharing by category (e.g., service providers, analytics) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each specific third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The Cookie Notice provides some opt-out for ad targeting and retargeting, but opt-out is limited and not available for all third-party sharing (e.g., service providers).
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states service providers must agree to 'strict data protection requirements,' but does not make a blanket claim that all third parties are contractually bound to equivalent privacy standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not commit to notifying users specifically when third-party partners change; it only states the policy itself may be amended without advance notice guarantees.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Terms of Service explicitly state that Evernote may display advertisements and promotions paid for by third parties in connection with its service, including targeted ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy confirms that data may be used to show personalized/targeted advertising, including through third-party ad networks, which is not appropriate for K-12 student users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The Cookie Notice provides some opt-out mechanisms for ad targeting and retargeting, but third-party tracking for advertising purposes is confirmed, with only a limited opt-out path.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies and similar tracking technologies are used to support advertising and analytics, with opt-out described in the Cookie Notice, but tracking methods are not fully enumerated in the main policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The region-specific privacy policy and Cookie Notice provide some opt-out options for ad targeting, but the opt-out process is not straightforward or clearly described in the primary policy document.

dataSharedWith: Unknown additional parties (per older policy language)
r303.riskReason: Examity collects highly sensitive biometric and identity data including facial images, keystroke patterns, and government IDs from students, and prior policy language indicated data transmission security could not be guaranteed and data could be transferred to unspecified third parties.
r303.parentSummary: Examity is an online exam proctoring service that collects extensive personal and biometric data from test-takers, including name, government-issued photo ID, webcam recordings, screen activity, and keystroke patterns. The platform claims FERPA compliance and uses encrypted servers with SOC 2 Type II certification, but its primary market is higher education and professional certification—not K-12—and it lacks explicit COPPA protections or a minimum age policy. Parents should be aware that prior versions of Examity's privacy policy acknowledged it could not guarantee data security and reserved the right to share data with unspecified third parties.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Examity's privacy and security page shows dated policy updates (e.g., June 1, 2023) indicating some versioning, but there is no documented advance-notification process or publicly accessible revision history for users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Examity lists core data types such as name, ID, digital signature, webcam/audio, and payment info, but older policy language referenced collecting addresses, biometric records, and passwords without complete enumeration in current public-facing documents.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Examity clearly states it collects data via browser extension, webcam, screen sharing, and challenge questions during proctoring sessions, meeting the requirement for specificity on collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Examity positions itself as a 'data processor' acting on behalf of institutional 'controllers,' implying user data ownership, but does not explicitly state that users own their data in its public-facing policies.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No public-facing deletion request process or user-initiated data deletion mechanism is described in Examity's available policy documents for individual test-takers.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Examity states exam data is typically available for 60 days then destroyed, extended to 1 year if a red flag is raised, with some programs having unique retention periods—a general but stated retention framework.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Examity specifies use of SSAE-16 certified data centers, role-based authorization, PCI compliance, SOC 2 Type II certification, and database-wide encryption both at transmission and at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Examity explicitly states it uses database-wide encryption for data security both at transmission and at rest, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Examity recommends using a different password for each exam and term but does not state it enforces strong password complexity requirements; SSO/LTI integration is available as an alternative.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Examity supports LTI 1.3 and SSO integration, and uses multi-factor candidate identity verification during exam sessions, meeting the intent of this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Examity mentions necessary and non-necessary cookies but does not provide a full named cookie list with purposes; only a general description of functional vs. tailoring cookies is disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Examity references a payment processing service and institutional administrators as recipients of data but does not name specific third-party vendors or provide a complete third-party list publicly.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Examity does not specify what particular data elements are shared with each third-party category; sharing disclosures are grouped and vague.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out process for third-party data sharing is described in Examity's public-facing materials; test-takers must consent to data collection to use the service.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Examity states data passed to payment processors is done 'securely' and references confidentiality obligations generally, but does not detail contractual requirements imposed on all third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Examity does not disclose a process for notifying users when third-party data-sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Examity is a proctoring service with no evident advertising displayed to users; the platform is not ad-supported.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no evidence Examity engages in targeted advertising directed at students or test-takers based on their personal data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Non-necessary cookies described as providing a 'tailored experience' suggest possible third-party tracking exists, but no detail or opt-out mechanism is clearly described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Examity mentions non-necessary cookies without clarifying if they involve third-party web beacons or tracking pixels, leaving tracking methods partially unclear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Examity does not provide a described or accessible opt-out mechanism for any data sharing with advertising or analytics partners.

r304.riskReason: ExamView officially reached end-of-life on June 30, 2024, meaning no further security patches, updates, or technical support are provided, creating significant ongoing security and compliance risks for any K-12 schools still using the platform.
r304.parentSummary: ExamView, operated by Echo360 (formerly Turning Technologies), collects educator and student account data including names, school information, email addresses, and usage/interaction data during test-taking sessions. The platform states it does not knowingly collect data from children under 13 without parental or organizational consent, and it claims FERPA and COPPA compliance. However, ExamView reached its official end-of-life on June 30, 2024, meaning it no longer receives security updates or support, which poses a heightened risk to any student data processed through the platform.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The EULA and Privacy Policy exist on echo360.com but no clear advance notification process or revision history is documented for ExamView users specifically, especially given its end-of-life status.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The EULA and Privacy Policy list some data types (account info, usage/statistical interaction data, device/browser data) but do not provide a comprehensive, exhaustive enumeration of all student data collected during assessments.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Data collection methods are described in general terms (automatic reporting, account registration, software use) but lack specific detail about how student assessment response data is collected and transmitted.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The EULA explicitly states that 'Statistical Viewer Usage Data is owned by Echo360,' indicating the vendor claims ownership of key interaction data rather than users, which is a significant concern for K-12 compliance.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The Privacy Policy references user rights and data requests but routes students and parents through the educational institution rather than providing a direct, clear deletion mechanism; no specific deletion timeline is stated.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Neither the ExamView EULA nor the Echo360 Privacy Policy as applied to ExamView specifies a concrete data retention period for student assessment or account data; retention language is vague and conditional.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The EULA states Echo360 will 'apply reasonable measures' and references industry standards, and the corporate responsibility page mentions SOC 2 and AWS infrastructure, but specific security measures for ExamView are not enumerated in the policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is not explicitly mentioned in the ExamView EULA or Privacy Policy; the corporate responsibility page references AWS infrastructure implying encryption, but no direct encryption commitment is stated for ExamView data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The EULA requires account credentials and states users must protect them, and the platform requires account activation, but no explicit strong password enforcement policy or requirements are documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The Echo360 platform is LTI 1.3 certified, which supports SSO and secure credential exchange for educational institutions, meeting this requirement for institution-managed deployments.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Neither the ExamView-specific EULA nor the Echo360 Privacy Policy provides a detailed cookie policy listing all cookies with their specific purposes; cookie usage is not addressed in ExamView's governing documents.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy mentions vendor and partner relationships and third-party service providers in general terms but does not name specific third parties used in the delivery of ExamView services.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with each category of third party is provided; sharing practices are described only in aggregate and general terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in the ExamView EULA or Echo360 Privacy Policy for student users; institutional administrators have no documented opt-out process either.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Privacy Policy includes a general statement about managing vendor relationships but does not explicitly require third-party sub-processors to adhere to the same privacy standards through named contractual obligations.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no stated process for notifying users or institutions when third-party relationships or data-sharing arrangements change; the policy may be updated without specific advance notice to ExamView users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Echo360 privacy policy references managing advertising on third-party sites, suggesting some advertising activity exists, though ExamView's classroom use context makes direct in-app ads unlikely; this is insufficiently clarified.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No explicit prohibition on targeted advertising directed at student users of ExamView is stated in the EULA; while Echo360 claims COPPA compliance broadly, a specific no-targeted-ads pledge for students is absent from policy documents.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No information is provided about third-party tracking for advertising purposes, nor is any opt-out mechanism described; the policy's reference to advertising on third-party sites suggests tracking may occur.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The use of web beacons, tracking pixels, or similar technologies is not addressed in the ExamView EULA or associated Privacy Policy, leaving the scope of tracking methods entirely unclear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described anywhere in the ExamView or Echo360 governing documents available to K-12 users or their institutions.

dataSharedWith: Third-party service providers and subprocessors (named in subprocessor list)
Cloud integration partners (Dropbox, Box, Microsoft, Google Drive)
r305.riskReason: Explain Everything (owned by Promethean) explicitly states FERPA alignment and prohibits selling personal data, but is not certified under any FTC-approved COPPA safe harbor program, allows subprocessor changes without advance notice, and provides only a general (not specific) cookie disclosure with limited detail on tracking technologies used.
r305.parentSummary: Explain Everything, operated by Promethean, collects account-related data such as name, email, and usage information to provide its whiteboard and collaborative learning service; student data is not sold to third parties and is used solely for educational purposes. The platform states alignment with FERPA and uses SSL encryption to protect data, and schools or teachers can request deletion of student data within 30 days. However, the service is not certified under any FTC-approved COPPA safe harbor program, and Promethean reserves the right to change third-party subprocessors without advance notice to users, which is a notable concern for K-12 deployments.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states Promethean may attempt to notify users of major changes but requires users to periodically review the policy themselves; a full revision history is not publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists specific categories of personal data collected including name, email, phone number, mailing address, IP address, usage data, and device identifiers.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy explains data is collected via direct user input, automatic device/browser logging, cookies, and third-party API integrations such as Google Drive and Dropbox.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Promethean describes itself as Data Controller for account registration data and notes schools act as data controllers for student data, but ownership language regarding user-created content is not fully explicit.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can cancel accounts at any time and student data must be deleted within 30 days of a school or teacher request, with a dedicated contact email provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy references deletion due to inactivity and a 30-day student data deletion window upon request, but does not state a specific general data retention period for non-student accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states Promethean uses 'reasonable security measures' and has protections against loss, misuse, and alteration, but does not enumerate specific technical or organizational security controls beyond SSL encryption.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states that SSL or similar encryption technologies are applied when users enter information into the product or online service.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not describe password strength requirements or enforcement; SSO via Google EDU is available for school deployments, which partially addresses this concern.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: SSO and Google EDU account login are supported for school plans, but no explicit MFA policy is described for standard account login.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions use of cookies and similar technologies with general purposes (preferences, login persistence), but does not provide a full categorized list of all cookies used with specific purposes for each.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: A dedicated List of Data Subprocessors page exists at explaineverything.com/privacy-policy/data-subprocessors/ naming specific third-party service providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The subprocessors list names parties but does not clearly specify which particular data fields are shared with each individual subprocessor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can contact Promethean to manage data and schools have administrative controls, but there is no clearly described self-service opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that Promethean requires third parties, agents, or contractors to execute a data processing agreement governing the processing of personal information.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Promethean explicitly reserves the right to add, remove, or change subprocessors at any time without advance notice to users, only providing an updated list upon written request.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Promethean explicitly states it will not sell personal information to third parties for marketing purposes, and no advertising is displayed within the educational platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly prohibits selling personal information for marketing and there is no evidence of behavioral targeting of students or teachers within the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy references use of third-party analytical software and cookies for usage analytics, but does not fully clarify whether any third-party ad tracking pixels are present or offer a clear opt-out.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies and similar technologies are mentioned for functional and improvement purposes, but the policy does not explicitly enumerate whether web beacons or tracking pixels are used or absent.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can contact Promethean at privacy@prometheanworld.com to exercise data rights, but a clear, self-service opt-out from any form of data sharing with analytics or advertising partners is not prominently described.

dataCollected: Teacher feedback and grades on recordings
dataSharedWith: AI/ML service providers (e.g., ChatGPT/OpenAI) for product development
Agents and contractors for promotional campaigns
Third parties who may license anonymized/de-identified voice recordings
r306.riskReason: While Extempore explicitly states it does not sell student data and acknowledges COPPA/FERPA, it reserves the right to share student content including audio/video recordings with AI providers like ChatGPT and to license anonymized voice recordings to third parties, which presents notable risks for a K-12 environment collecting biometric-adjacent data from minors.
r306.parentSummary: Extempore collects students' names, email addresses, and audio/video recordings submitted as part of coursework, storing data on secure servers (including Amazon Web Services). The platform states it does not sell student data and allows parents to request deletion by emailing support; however, it may share student content with AI service providers like ChatGPT for product development and can license de-identified voice recordings to third parties, which parents should be aware of before approving use in their child's classroom.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states changes may be posted on the policy page and users are notified via the privacy policy page, but there is no advance notification process or versioned revision history explicitly documented.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy explicitly lists the two categories of data collected from all users including children: account credentials (username, password, email) and content generated (uploaded audio/video files in response to coursework).
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states data is collected directly from users upon registration and through use of the mobile application, and server logs track site activity including IP addresses.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Ownership of student content is ambiguous; the TOS states Deeloh owns all rights to the Services and Deeloh Content, while subscriber content ownership is referenced but the policy also allows Deeloh to retain and use de-identified content after deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents can request deletion by emailing support@extemporeapp.com, and teachers can delete all student recordings by archiving a class; however, deletion may render the account unusable and cached/backup copies may persist for a reasonable period.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained until account termination and deleted upon request, but no specific retention period (e.g., number of days or years) is stated, making this vague rather than a defined timeframe.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states 'appropriate security measures' are implemented but does not enumerate specific technical controls such as encryption standards, access controls, or audit procedures beyond a general assurance.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of encryption (e.g., SSL/TLS or at-rest encryption) is stated in the Extemporeapp privacy policy; only a general statement that 'appropriate security measures' are in place is provided.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The TOS references a password recovery feature and advises users to alert Deeloh of security risks, but there is no stated policy enforcing strong password requirements such as complexity or length minimums.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration options is made anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies are used for session management and preferences, but does not enumerate all cookie types, their purposes, or provide a comprehensive cookie inventory as expected for full compliance.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Amazon Web Services, Apple, Google, and references 'third party providers of AI and machine learning services such as ChatGPT' by category but does not provide a complete list of all named third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups third parties broadly (e.g., agents/contractors, AI providers, licensees of voice recordings) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Students can email privacy@extemporeapp.com to opt out, but the policy notes opting out will render the account unusable, providing a technically available but highly restrictive opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states third parties who receive subscriber content must do so 'pursuant to a written agreement' and affiliates must 'preserve the confidentiality' of personal information, constituting a general contractual requirement but without specific data protection standards enumerated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not include any provision notifying users when third-party vendors are added, removed, or changed; users are only told to periodically check the policy page.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy and TOS do not describe any advertising displayed within the platform, and the FERPA help article explicitly states student data is not used for marketing purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is described or permitted within the platform; the policy explicitly states student and teacher data are not used for marketing purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party behavioral tracking for advertising purposes is disclosed; the privacy policy states third-party analytics services collect data anonymously and in aggregate only.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies described are limited to functional/session purposes (saving passwords and preferences) with no mention of advertising beacons or tracking pixels within the app platform itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising or data sharing with advertisers takes place, no opt-out is necessary; the policy confirms student data is not shared for marketing or advertising purposes.

dataSharedWith: Third-party vendors for web hosting and applications
r307.riskReason: Fact Monster is explicitly child-directed but displays targeted/behavioral advertising via Playwire LLC, collects data through third-party tracking services, and creates data profiles for ad targeting on a site intended for children under 13, raising serious COPPA and K-12 safety concerns.
r307.parentSummary: Fact Monster collects cookies and usage data from all visitors, including children, and uses a third-party ad network (Playwire LLC) that may collect and use aggregated data for advertising purposes. While the site states it will not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 without parental consent, behavioral and targeted advertising is still displayed to child visitors via third-party tracking. Parents should be aware that third-party ad trackers operate on this child-directed site and data profiles may be created for ad targeting purposes.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use states changes are effective immediately upon notice, but does not guarantee advance notification or provide a revision history archive.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy mentions cookies, usage data, and personal information generally but does not provide a comprehensive itemized list of every data type collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy references automated means (cookies and similar technologies) and voluntary submission but provides only a general description of how data is collected.

The platform self-declares compliance with both COPPA and FERPA, states it does not sell personal data, and uses SSL encryption plus restricted access controls to protect information. However, multiple third-party analytics services (Google Analytics, Bing Analytics, Google Tag Manager) are active on the platform, and data retention timelines are only described vaguely as 'only as necessary,' which parents and administrators should be aware of when evaluating the tool.

r310.riskReason: Fanschool explicitly prohibits selling student data and targeted advertising, uses TLS encryption, has a Data Protection Officer, acknowledges COPPA and FERPA, and offers school-controlled deletion of student data.
r310.parentSummary: Fanschool collects basic account information (name, username, email, IP address, and content posted) to operate its student blogging and portfolio platform, and uses it solely for educational purposes under teacher and school control. The platform does not sell student data, does not serve targeted ads, and encrypts traffic via TLS; schools and parents may request deletion of student data at any time by emailing privacy@fan.school. Third-party sharing is limited to infrastructure service providers and school-authorized applications, with those parties contractually restricted from using data for other purposes.

r311.riskReason: FBI-SOS is a federal government program that explicitly does not collect student names or identifying information, assigns students anonymous numbers for exams, collects only minimal teacher registration data, serves no advertising, and operates under federal privacy law including the Privacy Act.
r311.parentSummary: FBI-SOS (Cyber Surf Island) is a free, federal government-run cybersafety program for grades 3–8. The FBI explicitly states it does not collect student names, ages, or other identifying information — students are identified only by number during exams. Teachers must register with their name, school, and email for class participation, but no student personal data is collected or retained, and no advertising is present on the platform.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The FBI privacy policy does not include an explicit advance-notification process or revision history for policy changes; it is a static government policy page without versioning.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The FBI privacy policy lists automatically collected technical data (IP address, domain, browser/OS) and teacher registration data, but the SOS-specific data handling (student numeric identifiers, exam scores) is only described in news/FAQ pages rather than a dedicated SOS privacy policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected automatically when visiting the site and voluntarily when teachers register, but lacks a fully detailed, SOS-specific breakdown of collection mechanisms.

complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy references the Federal Records Act and National Archives retention schedules as governing data retention, which is a general legal framework statement but does not specify a concrete retention period for teacher or usage data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states the FBI uses 'commercially reasonable tools and techniques' to protect against unauthorized access and restricts access to those who need it, but does not enumerate specific technical security measures for the SOS platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site operates on a .gov HTTPS domain, meaning TLS/SSL encryption is enforced throughout by federal government standards, satisfying encryption requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Students do not require accounts; teacher registration is managed through a secure government system, and no password complexity requirements are publicly documented, but the no-account-required design for students satisfies this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Students require no account to use the platform; teacher registration uses a secure government system without publicly documented MFA, but the no-account-required approach for students satisfies the spirit of this control.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy describes session cookies, persistent cookies (for navigation and surveys), and third-party video cookies by general purpose, but does not provide a complete enumerated cookie inventory with names and detailed purposes.

complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy implies contractors act on the FBI's behalf and are subject to applicable law, but does not explicitly state third parties must comply with a vendor data protection agreement.

complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is present; the site is a .gov platform and federal policy explicitly prohibits use of data for commercial advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Only functional tracking (session cookies, navigation statistics) is used; no web beacons or advertising tracking methods are employed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There are no advertisers and no data sharing with advertisers; the opt-out question is fully satisfied by the absence of any advertising infrastructure.

r312.parentSummary: FBLA collects personally identifiable information from student members including name, address, email, phone number, grade, age, and date of birth, and requires verifiable parental consent before collecting data from children under 13. Data is shared with service providers such as Impexium for membership database management, as well as mailing, event registration, and consulting vendors, and FBLA states it may also share member information with affiliated advertisers for targeted advertising. SSL encryption is used for sensitive transactions and parents can request deletion of their child's data at any time, but the policy does not specify exact data retention periods and does not include advance notification of policy changes.
