r340.riskReason: Common Sense Privacy rates GCFGlobal with a 'Warning' due to concerns about personal information shared for third-party marketing, personalized advertising display, and third-party data collection for their own purposes, which conflicts with some of the more privacy-protective claims in the legacy Terms of Use.
r340.parentSummary: GCFGlobal collects minimal personal information (name and email for registered accounts) and uses Google Analytics with anonymized IP addresses for site improvement; most content is freely accessible without an account. However, the newer Privacy Notice (effective October 2024) acknowledges sharing data with subsidiaries for marketing purposes and with service providers, and a Common Sense Privacy evaluation flagged concerns about personalized advertising and third-party data collection. The platform does not explicitly address COPPA, FERPA, or student data sale prohibitions in its publicly available policies.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Privacy Notice states changes will be posted on the page with an effective date, but the Terms of Service indicate GCF may revise terms at any time without notice, with no formal advance notification process described.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The legacy Terms of Use lists name, email, session cookies, and Google Analytics data, and the Privacy Notice references personal information collection, but neither document provides a fully comprehensive enumerated list of all data types collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The Terms of Use describes cookies and Google Analytics as collection mechanisms and the Privacy Notice broadly references data collection as users use the site, but neither document comprehensively explains all data collection methods (e.g., form submissions, behavioral tracking).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Privacy Notice states GCF is the Data Controller making decisions on processing, and users retain rights to their submitted content per the Terms of Use, but ownership of collected personal data is not explicitly assigned to users.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The Terms of Service allows users to close their account at any time, and the Privacy Notice references rights to erasure subject to legal obligations, but no clear self-service deletion process or timeline is described for all data types.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Neither the Terms of Service nor the Privacy Notice states a specific data retention period or general retention timeframe for user personal data; the topic is not substantively addressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Privacy Notice states GCF 'implements and maintains reasonable security measures' but does not specify what those measures are (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, audits).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of encryption is found in the publicly available Terms of Service or Privacy Notice; the site uses HTTPS but no encryption commitment is stated in policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Neither the Terms of Service nor the Privacy Notice mentions password strength requirements or enforcement; no SSO is described for general users.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication is found in any publicly available policy document; no SSO or LTI integration is described for K-12 use.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The legacy Terms of Use describes session cookies, local progress cookies, and Google Analytics cookies with revocation options, but the newer Privacy Notice and cookie policy (Spanish-language) reference marketing cookies and third-party tracking cookies without a complete English-language enumeration of all cookies and their purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Notice identifies GCF subsidiaries, service providers, and Google Analytics as parties with whom data may be shared, but does not name specific third-party service providers beyond Google Analytics.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Privacy Notice groups data sharing by category (subsidiaries, service providers) without specifying which data elements are shared with each third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can revoke Google Analytics cookies at any time per the Terms of Use, and marketing consent to subsidiaries can be withdrawn via a Contact Us form, but opt-out processes for other third-party sharing are not clearly described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Privacy Notice states service providers assist in providing the website under a legitimate interest basis but does not explicitly state that third parties are contractually required to follow GCF's data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No policy language notifies users of changes to third-party service providers or data-sharing arrangements; the Terms of Service allows changes without notice.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Common Sense Privacy flagged that personalized advertising is displayed on GCFGlobal, though the legacy Terms of Use does not mention advertising; there is a conflict between policy documents and third-party evaluation findings.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Common Sense Privacy's evaluation found that user information is used to track and target advertisements on third-party websites, and that it is unclear whether data profiles are created for personalized advertisements, indicating possible third-party targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Common Sense Privacy flagged third-party data collection for advertisers' own purposes and user tracking for ad targeting on external sites, with no clear opt-out mechanism described in GCFGlobal's own policies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The Spanish-language cookie policy references marketing cookies that track online activity and share data with advertisers, and Common Sense Privacy identified tracking practices, but GCFGlobal's English policies do not clearly disclose web beacons or ad tracking technologies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described in GCFGlobal's English-language privacy documents; users can revoke Google Analytics cookies but broader advertiser data-sharing opt-out is not addressed.

dataSharedWith: Third-party service providers for log data
r341.riskReason: GDevelop blocks accounts from children under 13 and offers anonymous Education plan accounts, but the standard platform collects email and analytics data via unspecified third parties, lacks explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance declarations, no data retention period is stated, and specific third-party analytics partners are not named in the policy.
r341.parentSummary: GDevelop collects email addresses and device/usage analytics data when students create accounts, and recommends that teachers use the paid Education plan which provides fully anonymous accounts without student emails. The platform states it does not knowingly collect data from children under 13 and will delete such data if discovered, but it uses unspecified third-party analytics and log services that may access user data. No explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance certification is claimed, and data retention periods and specific third-party vendor names are not disclosed in the policy.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states users will be notified by email of material changes, but no revision history or changelog is published on the policy page.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists email, IP address, device name, OS version, app configuration, timestamps, and analytics statistics, but uses broad language such as 'and other statistics' that leaves the full scope unclear.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected directly from users (e.g., email at account creation) and passively via third-party analytics tools, but does not detail specific collection mechanisms such as form fields, SDKs, or tracking scripts.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; it only states data is used to provide and improve the service, leaving ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: GDPR data portability and deletion rights are mentioned for EEA users, and the policy notes accounts with PII will be removed for under-13s, but there is no clear, universal self-service account or data deletion mechanism described for all users.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not specify any data retention period or general retention statement for any category of data collected.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy does not describe specific security measures such as encryption, access controls, or security audits; it only states data is stored in a database of the service.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption in transit or at rest is made anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not mention password strength requirements, enforcement of strong passwords, or availability of SSO for standard accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in either the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions that cookies are used for account sessions and that third-party code may use cookies, and notes users can accept or refuse them, but does not provide a full list of cookies by name or specific purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Only Google Play Services is named as a third-party provider; other analytics and log data providers are referenced generically via external links without naming them in the policy text.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify which data elements are shared with each individual third-party provider; it only states third parties may access personal information to perform tasks on GDevelop's behalf.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described beyond the ability to refuse cookies via browser settings, which does not cover all sharing scenarios.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states third parties are 'obligated not to disclose or use the information for any other purpose,' indicating a general contractual obligation, but no specific vendor agreement terms or DPA references are provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention any process for notifying users if third-party service providers change or if new third parties are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy does not address whether advertisements are displayed to users within the platform, leaving ad practices unaddressed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy makes no statement about targeted or behavioral advertising, neither confirming nor prohibiting it for standard (non-Education plan) users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party analytics providers that may use tracking technologies are referenced but not named, and no opt-out from their tracking is described in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy acknowledges third-party libraries and cookies but does not clarify whether web beacons, pixels, or other tracking methods are used or for what purpose.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No process for opting out of data sharing with advertisers or analytics partners is described; users are only told they can refuse cookies at a browser level.

r342.riskReason: GemKids explicitly targets children ages 9–12 (grades 4–6) yet the governing Terms of Use bar users under 13, with no COPPA-specific children's privacy protections, no parental consent mechanism, and broad cookie/tracking technologies deployed on a child-directed platform.
r342.parentSummary: GemKids is a free earth science and gemology education website operated by GIA (Gemological Institute of America) and designed for students in grades 4–6 (ages 9–12). GIA's privacy notice discloses collection of device and usage data including IP addresses, cookies, web beacons, and browsing behavior via analytics service providers, yet the site's Terms of Use state users must be at least 13 — a direct conflict with the platform's stated child audience. No dedicated COPPA children's privacy protections, parental consent mechanism, or child-specific data handling commitments are visible in the governing policies, which is a significant concern for K-12 deployment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: GIA's privacy notice states material changes will be communicated via email or prominent site notice and the notice is versioned (v. 6.2, last updated May 5, 2025), but no advance notification timeline or full revision history is publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy notice lists several categories of data collected (device info, IP address, usage data, cookies) but does not provide a fully exhaustive enumerated list specific to the GemKids subdomain or children users.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy notice specifically explains that data is collected through cookies, pixels, log files, web beacons, Flash LSOs, and analytics service providers, providing a clear description of collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy notice does not assert user ownership of data; GIA positions itself as the data controller and does not expressly state that users retain ownership, leaving data ownership ambiguous or effectively assigned to GIA.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy notice references a right to request deletion of personal data via a GIA Privacy Rights Request Form, but this is a request-based process and not a direct self-service deletion tool, representing only a limited deletion pathway.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy notice does not state a specific data retention period in days or years; it references retaining data as necessary for stated purposes and legal compliance, which is a vague general statement without specifics.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy notice references 'reasonable measures' for security but does not enumerate specific technical controls such as encryption standards, access controls, or penetration testing, amounting to only a general security statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The GemKids site uses HTTPS (standard web encryption), but the privacy policy does not explicitly mention encryption of stored data or data in transit beyond what is implied by HTTPS, making encryption coverage only partially addressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No user account is required to access the primary GemKids educational content, so there is no password enforcement issue for general student use; educator access to GemKit resources may require registration but no specific password policy is stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No user account is required for the core GemKids student-facing content, effectively eliminating the MFA risk for students; educator tools that may require registration do not explicitly offer MFA but the no-account model for students meets the spirit of this control.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: GIA provides a separate Cookie Notice (gia.edu/cookie-notice) describing cookie types including session and persistent cookies, but it does not enumerate each individual cookie name and purpose in a granular table, and it references third-party analytics cookies only broadly.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy notice references sharing with 'analytics service providers' and 'social media platforms' in broad categories but does not name specific third-party vendors (e.g., Google Analytics) in the GemKids-specific context, providing only a broad generalization.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy notice does not specify which data elements are shared with each named or category of third party; it groups data sharing disclosures broadly without mapping specific data types to specific recipients.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications via unsubscribe links or emailing privacy@gia.edu, and Google Analytics opt-out is mentioned in related notices, but no streamlined child/parent opt-out from all third-party data sharing is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy notice states service providers are only permitted to use data for specified purposes, implying contractual obligations, but does not explicitly describe a vendor management program or supplier agreement framework for third-party compliance.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy notice states users will be notified of material changes but does not specifically address whether users will be notified when third-party sharing arrangements change, leaving this partially addressed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The GemKids website does not appear to display third-party advertisements to students, and GIA describes itself as a nonprofit educational resource, but the privacy notice does not explicitly state that no ads are served on the GemKids subdomain.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No evidence of targeted behavioral advertising on the GemKids platform was found, and GIA does not appear to engage in ad targeting of children; however, the privacy notice does not explicitly prohibit targeted advertising, leaving this only partially confirmed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party analytics providers (such as Google Analytics, referenced in related GIA privacy notices) may collect usage data via cookies and tracking technologies on the site, with opt-out available via browser tools or Google's opt-out plugin, but not with a simple in-site control.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy notice explicitly discloses the use of web beacons, clear GIFs, Flash LSOs, and pixel tags alongside cookies for tracking user activity, and these are combined with personal data, meaning tracking methods beyond functional cookies are confirmed and in use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can contact privacy@gia.edu or use the GIA Privacy Rights Request Form to exercise data rights including opt-outs, and marketing unsubscribe options exist, but a clear, child/parent-specific opt-out from data sharing with analytics and social media partners is not prominently provided.

dataSharedWith: Ad networks (third-party ad servers, ad agencies, ad technology vendors, research firms)
r343.riskReason: The platform explicitly allows targeted advertising using user profile data including age and gender via third-party ad networks, contains no COPPA or FERPA language, no minimum age requirement, and no data deletion rights for users — making it wholly unsuitable for K-12 deployment.
r343.parentSummary: Gen-Z Media (gzmshows.com) collects IP addresses, cookies, email addresses, and behavioral/usage data from users, and expressly reserves the right to serve targeted advertisements — including via third-party ad networks — based on user profile categories such as gender and age. The platform does not mention COPPA, FERPA, or any parental consent mechanisms, and provides no minimum age requirement, no data deletion process, and no data retention timeline. Parents should be aware that this platform was not designed for K-12 educational use and poses significant privacy risks for minors.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy (dated May 2020) provides no advance notification process for policy changes and no revision history is published.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Some data types are listed (email, IP address, cookies, usage data, click data) but the policy does not comprehensively enumerate all data collected — for example, inferred profile attributes used for ad targeting are only vaguely described.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general description of collection methods (browser interaction, user submission, cookies) but does not specifically enumerate all data collection points or mechanisms.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not state that users own their data; it implies company control by stating user information may be transferred as a business asset in mergers or acquisitions.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No data deletion rights or process for users are described anywhere in the policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is specified for any category of data collected.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy makes no mention of any specific security measures or protocols used to protect user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No encryption is mentioned anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of use.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No password strength requirements or enforcement mechanisms are described.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO is made anywhere in the policy or terms.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are mentioned generally with a note that browsers can disable them, but individual cookie purposes are not listed and third-party cookie use is explicitly disclaimed as outside the policy's scope.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third-party categories are described broadly (ad networks, agents, payment processors) but no specific named third parties are identified.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by category of third party rather than specifying exactly what data is shared with each type of party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is provided; the policy only states users will be notified for certain sharing scenarios but provides no mechanism to prevent ad-network targeting.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states agents may not use shared Personal Information beyond what is necessary to assist, providing a general contractual constraint, but no equivalent binding requirement is described for ad networks.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention any process to notify users if third-party sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states targeted ads may be served through the platform via third-party ad networks, confirming ads are displayed to all users including potential minors.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Ads are confirmed to be targeted based on user profile categories (gender, age), usage patterns, and activity on third-party services — constituting confirmed user-level targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party ad networks are explicitly permitted, with no opt-out mechanism described and no controls provided to prevent tracking of users by those networks.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Third-party ad networks using tracking technologies are acknowledged, but no specific tracking methods (e.g., web beacons, pixels) are disclosed and the policy disclaims responsibility for third-party cookie use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out mechanism for data sharing with advertisers or ad networks is provided anywhere in the policy.

r344.riskReason: Genius is a general consumer entertainment platform with no K-12 or FERPA safeguards, uses third-party advertising and tracking, lacks explicit COPPA protections or parental consent mechanisms, and has no student data policies.
r344.parentSummary: Genius.com is a song lyrics and annotation platform that collects personal information including name, email, usage data, and persistent identifiers, and shares data with third-party advertisers and analytics providers. The platform has no specific protections for students or children and is not designed for K-12 educational use. There are no stated FERPA or COPPA compliance measures, and the site displays targeted advertising, making it inappropriate for school use without careful administrator review.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Genius privacy policy does not describe an advance notification process for policy changes or maintain a publicly accessible revision history; users are simply expected to check the policy periodically.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy references collection of registration data, usage data, cookies, and user content, but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of all data types collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy makes a general statement that data is collected through use of the service and registration, but does not specifically describe all collection mechanisms such as tracking pixels, SDKs, or third-party scripts.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly state that users own their data; Genius claims broad rights over user-submitted content and collected information, indicating the company effectively claims data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Account deletion may be possible but the policy does not clearly articulate a full user-initiated data deletion process; deletion of all collected data is not explicitly guaranteed.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated in the accessible policy; there is no clear timeline for when data is deleted or archived after account termination.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references security practices in general terms but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or security audits.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS (passing a basic encryption test for data in transit), but the policy does not explicitly describe encryption for data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not describe any password strength requirements or enforcement mechanisms for user account passwords.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the accessible policy or product description.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy references use of cookies and similar tracking technologies generally but does not provide a detailed cookie table listing each cookie, its purpose, and its duration.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references sharing with third parties such as advertisers and service providers in general categories but does not name specific third-party companies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify which particular data fields are shared with each category of third party; disclosures are grouped and vague.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No clear or easy opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in the policy; users cannot readily opt out of third-party advertising data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not state that third-party vendors are contractually required to maintain data privacy standards equivalent to Genius's own policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not commit to notifying users when new third-party data sharing relationships are established or when existing ones change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Genius displays advertising including third-party targeted advertisements to users, which is confirmed by the platform's ad-supported business model.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The platform uses behavioral and interest-based targeting for advertising, using persistent identifiers and usage data to profile users for ad delivery.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party ad networks and tracking technologies operate on the site and collect data for targeted advertising with no straightforward opt-out disclosed within the policy itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The platform uses cookies, web beacons, and similar tracking technologies for advertising purposes without providing a clear disclosure of all tracking methods employed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear, accessible opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described in the policy; users are not given a simple mechanism to stop their data from being used for ad targeting.

r345.riskReason: Genius Scan explicitly states its services are not directed at children, does not specify a minimum age, lacks COPPA/FERPA compliance language, and an optional AI feature sends document text to OpenAI — posing risk if students scan sensitive materials.
r345.parentSummary: Genius Scan is a document scanner app that, by default, stores all scans locally on the device and does not transmit data to third parties unless users opt in to cloud sync or export features. If a cloud account is created or the optional AI document-naming feature is used, document content may be processed externally — including by OpenAI for up to 30 days. The app collects anonymous usage and crash analytics but explicitly states it does not show third-party ads and does not sell user data; however, it does not make any COPPA or FERPA compliance claims, and its policy states the service is not directed at children.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy posts changes on its page with a dated revision history (e.g., Feb 18, 2025; Dec 11, 2024), but there is no stated process for advance notification to users prior to changes taking effect.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy clearly lists all categories of data collected: anonymous usage identifiers, analytics, crash logs, name/email (support), document content (if cloud/AI opted in), location (optional), and billing data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how each data type is collected — on-device by default, via opt-in for cloud/AI features, and passively for analytics/crash reporting.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service explicitly state that the terms 'don't give us any rights to your data except for the limited rights that enable us to offer the Service,' indicating user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their account and documents, but cloud-stored documents are only 'flagged for deletion' and permanently deleted after an unspecified 'reasonable delay,' creating a partial deletion gap.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Specific retention periods are stated: analytics data is kept for 2 years, crash data for 1 year, and cloud documents are retained while the subscription is active or until deleted.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references HTTPS transmission and encrypted storage at rest for cloud users, and document password encryption (RC4 128-bit) for exports, but does not comprehensively list server-side security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Documents are transmitted via HTTPS and stored encrypted at rest on Genius Cloud servers, and PDF exports can be password-encrypted; encryption is addressed for both transit and storage.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service instruct users to 'use a strong password' but this is advisory language rather than a technically enforced requirement; no mention of password complexity enforcement.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) or SSO/LTI support in the privacy policy or terms of service for any account tier.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy identifies TelemetryDeck (cookieless, privacy-friendly analytics) and Sentry for crash reporting; TelemetryDeck explicitly does not use cookies, so cookie exposure is minimal and functionally described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Specific third parties are named: TelemetryDeck (analytics), Sentry (crash reporting), OpenAI (optional AI naming), Stripe (billing), Apple/Google (subscription status), and user-chosen cloud services.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared with each third party at a high level but does not provide a precise per-third-party data field breakdown (e.g., exactly what crash data fields Sentry receives).
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Third-party cloud service exports are fully opt-in and user-controlled; the OpenAI naming feature is described as optional; however, analytics collection via TelemetryDeck does not appear to have an explicit in-app opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy references that third-party services govern data under their own policies, but does not explicitly state that all sub-processors are contractually bound to data protection obligations matching Genius Scan's own standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy notes changes will be posted on the privacy policy page with dated revision logs, but does not commit to proactively notifying users when specific third-party processors change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states Genius Scan does not show third-party ads, and the free plan is confirmed to be entirely ad-free.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising of any kind is conducted; the policy removed prior mention of banner ads and confirms no third-party advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is present; analytics are handled by TelemetryDeck which is cookieless and does not track users across services.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No ad-related web beacons or cross-site tracking methods are used; only functional analytics (TelemetryDeck) and crash reporting (Sentry) are in place.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising or data sharing with advertisers occurs, there is nothing to opt out of — this requirement is met by design.

r346.riskReason: GeoGuessr collects PII, uses third-party tracking for targeted advertising, shares data with marketing partners, builds ad profiles, and has no COPPA or FERPA provisions for K-12 student use.

The platform states it does not sell personal data but does permit third-party data collection for marketing profiling. There are no COPPA protections, no FERPA compliance provisions, and no school or district agreement process, making this platform unsuitable for use with K-12 students without significant caution.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states material changes will be communicated via email, and the current policy is always available on the website, but there is no explicit revision history or versioning.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists categories of PII collected including account data, game data, device/browser data, cookies, and payment data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy explains data is collected directly from users, automatically via cookies and tracking technologies, and from third-party login providers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy grants GeoGuessr AB broad rights to process user data and does not clearly affirm user ownership; intellectual property of platform content is claimed by GeoGuessr.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete profile images via account settings, and GDPR/CCPA rights to erasure are referenced, but full self-service account deletion process is not clearly outlined.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: A general data retention statement exists (data kept as long as necessary), but no specific retention timeframes are provided for different data categories.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references GDPR compliance and data processor agreements but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as encryption standards or access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS, implying transport encryption, but the privacy policy does not explicitly state encryption is used for data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy and terms make no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of MFA is made in the policies; SSO via Google, Facebook, and Apple is supported but MFA is not described as available or enforced.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy describes functional, analytics, and marketing cookies separately, with consent-based controls offered to users on first visit and adjustable via profile settings.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Specific third-party service providers are named, including Google, Facebook, Apple, Paddle, Canny, and Freshdesk.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared by purpose category (e.g., login, payments, analytics) but does not specify exactly which data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can adjust marketing cookie preferences in their profile, and Global Privacy Control signals are honored per the shop opt-out page, but the opt-out path for all third-party sharing is not straightforward.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that data processors (suppliers) may only use personal data per GeoGuessr's instructions, indicating contractual limits, but independent service providers are noted as separate data controllers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states material changes will be communicated by email, which implies notification of third-party changes, but this is not explicitly guaranteed for all third-party relationship changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: GeoGuessr uses third-party cookies to show personalized ads and collects data from other websites to build user audiences for targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states user data is used to create audience profiles and display targeted advertisements, confirming active user-level targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking for advertising is confirmed and enabled by default unless users opt out; data collected by third-party ad cookies is used across the web.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms use of third-party cookies and marketing trackers that collect cross-site behavioral data, and these are used to build advertising profiles.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out mechanism exists via cookie preferences and Global Privacy Control support, but the process involves multiple steps and is not a simple, clearly labeled single opt-out.

r347.riskReason: The platform is discontinued with no active technical support since July 2020, its privacy policy is outdated (last copyrighted 2014 by McGraw-Hill Education), and it lacks explicit COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance statements, data retention periods, deletion rights, security disclosures, or cookie policy — creating significant unmitigated compliance gaps for K-12 use.
r347.parentSummary: Geometer's Sketchpad is a legacy desktop math software that was officially discontinued by McGraw-Hill in 2019, with all digital and technical support ending July 2020. The software collects license validation data (including MAC addresses and IP addresses for school licenses) and the companion website may collect voluntarily submitted email addresses, which it states it does not sell or share with third parties. However, the privacy policy has not been updated since at least 2014, there are no explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance statements, and there is no information about data deletion rights, retention periods, or modern security practices — making it a poor choice for current K-12 classroom deployment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy is undated beyond a 2014 copyright notice and contains no stated process for notifying users of policy changes or maintaining a revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The license agreement identifies specific data types collected (License Name, Authorization Code, MAC address, IP address, computer hardware info) but the website privacy policy only vaguely references 'routine information' and 'personal information from forms' without a comprehensive enumeration.

complianceNotes.DCQ4: Neither the privacy policy nor the license agreement provides any process or mechanism for users or schools to request deletion of collected data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated in either the privacy policy or the license agreement; the documents are silent on how long collected data is retained.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Neither the privacy policy nor the license agreement describes any specific technical or organizational security measures used to protect collected data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption of data in transit or at rest is made anywhere in the available policy or license documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The software uses a License Name and Authorization Code system for access, but no strong password policy or enforcement is described; there is no SSO integration mentioned.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI integration is mentioned in any available documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The website privacy policy makes no mention of cookies, tracking technologies, or their purposes; there is no cookie policy of any kind.

complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party or internal data sharing is described in any available documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The license agreement does not include any language requiring downstream parties to comply with a data protection agreement or privacy standards equivalent to the vendor's own obligations.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No process for notifying users or schools of changes to third-party data sharing arrangements is described anywhere in the available documentation.

r348.riskReason: Geometry Dash collects advertising identifiers and shares data with third-party ad SDK operators for targeted advertising, lacks a clear minimum age requirement or COPPA-compliant parental consent mechanism, and the official geometrydash.com website renders no substantive privacy policy or terms of service content — making it inappropriate for K-12 school deployment.
r348.parentSummary: Geometry Dash, developed by RobTop Games, collects advertising identifiers (Apple IDFA and Google Advertiser ID), device data, general location, usage analytics, and social network identifiers, and integrates third-party SDKs that may use this data to target advertisements at users. The official website (geometrydash.com) does not display a readable Privacy Policy or Terms of Service — the policy located at robtopgames.com is outdated (last updated May 2022), does not specify a minimum age, and does not include a COPPA-compliant verifiable parental consent process. Parents and educators should be aware that the game displays advertising, shares data with multiple third-party operators for ad targeting, and lacks the student data protections required for K-12 use under COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The RobTop privacy policy states updates will be made periodically and continued use constitutes acceptance, but no advance notification process or revision history is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists advertising identifiers, device info, usage data, general location, social identifiers, and messages, but does not comprehensively enumerate all data categories in a structured list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states that data is collected through SDKs, cookies, and service usage, but does not specifically detail the collection mechanism for each data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not address user data ownership; RobTop implies control over collected data without granting users ownership rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy allows users to contact RobTop to delete data for themselves or a child under 13, but no self-service deletion tool or defined process is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not specify any retention period for any category of data collected.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The RobTop privacy policy contains no description of specific security measures, safeguards, or data protection practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption in transit or at rest is made anywhere in the policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not address password requirements; no SSO or account-free enforcement is described for the web platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies are used for record-keeping and tracking but does not enumerate specific cookies or their individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references third-party SDK operators and mentions categories (advertising, analytics, game services, social networks) but does not name specific vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by category of third party but does not specify which data fields are shared with each named or unnamed vendor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An opt-out for interest-based advertising is described via mobile device settings (iOS/Android), but no opt-out is provided for non-advertising data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states third-party operators are allowed to use data only for limited purposes, implying contractual constraints, but no explicit vendor agreement or DPA is referenced.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may be updated to add additional third-party operators with no commitment to notify users of such changes in advance.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Third-party advertising SDKs are integrated and the policy confirms ads are served to users, including in the free Geometry Dash Lite app.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states third-party operators may use collected data to target advertisements, confirming user-level ad targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: An opt-out for interest-based advertising is available via mobile device settings, but it is device-level only, indirect, and not clearly communicated in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Advertising identifiers (IDFA and Google Advertiser ID) and cookies are used for tracking, confirming ad-purpose tracking with no functional-only limitation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The opt-out process references OS-level device settings rather than providing a clear in-product or policy-linked opt-out mechanism for data sharing with advertisers.

r349.riskReason: No publicly accessible Privacy Policy or Terms of Service could be located on getintoenergy.com, leaving all data collection, sharing, security, and student protection practices entirely undisclosed and unverifiable for K-12 compliance purposes.
r349.parentSummary: Get Into Energy (getintoenergy.com), operated by the Center for Energy Workforce Development (CEWD), does not appear to publish a publicly accessible Privacy Policy or Terms of Service on its main domain. Because no policy documents could be found, parents and schools cannot determine what data is collected from students, how it is used, or what protections are in place. Schools should contact CEWD directly to request privacy documentation before allowing student use of this platform.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Privacy Policy was found on getintoenergy.com, so no policy change notification process or revision history can be assessed.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: No Privacy Policy is publicly accessible on getintoenergy.com, so data collection practices are entirely undisclosed.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Without a Privacy Policy, there is no statement of how data is collected from users on the platform.

complianceNotes.DCQ4: No information about user data deletion rights or processes is available anywhere on the platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or policy statement of any kind could be located on the site.

r350.parentSummary: Get Into Theatre collects personal information including name, address, email, and sensitive demographic data such as race/ethnicity and disability status from users aged 11 and older. This data is used to provide services and to support advertising, including sharing a hashed version of users' email addresses with third-party ad partners for audience matching and serving remarketing ads via Google. There is no COPPA or FERPA compliance statement, no explicit parental consent mechanism for minors, and policy updates are posted without advance notice.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states updates will be posted on the website with no advance notification to users and no revision history provided; users are told to 'check back regularly.'
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several data types (name, address, email, phone, demographic/sensitive data, cookies, usage data) but does not comprehensively enumerate all data collected, particularly around behavioral and tracking data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that data is collected at registration and through website use, but does not specifically detail all collection mechanisms (e.g., cookies, analytics, third-party tracking) in one place.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly state that users own their data; data ownership is implicitly claimed by the platform as the data controller, with no user ownership language present.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can contact the Data Protection Officer to request data changes, and a GDPR Subject Access Request process exists, but a straightforward self-service full deletion option is not clearly described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data will be removed from systems when no longer needed but gives only a vague general retention statement with no specific retention periods defined.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy makes no mention of specific security measures, encryption, or technical/organizational controls used to protect personal data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption in transit or at rest is made anywhere in the privacy policy or terms and conditions.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The terms and conditions only advise users to 'keep your password safe' with no enforcement of strong password requirements stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO is made anywhere in the policy or terms; standard username/password accounts are used.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A separate cookie policy exists and names Google Analytics and Google Display Network cookies, but 'other third party cookies' are acknowledged with a disclaimer of no control, leaving the full cookie inventory incomplete.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google Analytics, Google AdWords/Display Network, and 'carefully selected third party partners' are mentioned, but a comprehensive named list of all third-party data recipients is not provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify which data fields are shared with each named or unnamed third party; only general or grouped descriptions are given.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An opt-out for third-party advertising cookies is referenced via links to third-party platforms, but the process is cumbersome and not platform-managed; no simple platform-level opt-out exists.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor agreement, data processing agreement, or contractual obligation binding third-party partners to data protection standards is mentioned.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy reserves the right to update at any time by posting a revised version without notifying users in advance of changes to third-party sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The platform explicitly permits advertisements on the site, including banner ads and Google Display Network ads served to users, including those aged 11 and up.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The platform uses Google AdWords remarketing to target previous site visitors across the Google Display Network with personalized ads based on their past behavior.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party vendors including Google use cookies to serve ads based on past visits, and the platform acknowledges it has no control over certain third-party tracking cookies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Google AdWords remarketing and Google Display Network tracking are confirmed, and other third-party ad trackers are acknowledged but not fully disclosed, indicating ad-tracking beyond functional purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out option for third-party advertising cookies is referenced in the cookie policy with links to third-party opt-out pages, but the process is unclear, external, and not easy for a general user to complete.

r351.riskReason: Girls Who Code maintains comprehensive, age-differentiated privacy policies, voluntarily aligns with COPPA despite nonprofit exemption, prohibits behavioral advertising to minors, explicitly states student data is never sold, signs state-level DPAs, and supports full data deletion by parents and schools.
r351.parentSummary: Girls Who Code collects student information such as name, email, school details, IP address, and coding project content to provide its educational Clubs platform; children under 13 require parental or school consent to create an account, and the organization explicitly states that student personal information is never sold, rented, or used for behaviorally targeted advertising. Data is shared with named third-party service providers (e.g., AWS, Salesforce, Zoom) solely to operate the platform under strict confidentiality requirements, and GWC has signed Data Privacy Addendums with many states to support FERPA compliance. Parents and schools can request access, correction, or full deletion of a child's personal information at any time by contacting privacy@girlswhocode.com.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Clubs Privacy Policy states that upon a material change, GWC will post a prominent notice on the Clubs Service or website and notify users by email, and will prompt re-acceptance of terms at next login.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Clubs Privacy Policy provides a detailed chart listing all categories of personal information collected per user type, including account info, demographic data, IP address, coding content, and virtual event recordings.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy explicitly distinguishes between information voluntarily provided by the user, information collected automatically, and information received from third-party sources such as Teacher Facilitators and parents.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Clubs Privacy Policy and DPA framework clarify that schools and data owners retain control over student data, and GWC acts as a processor on behalf of schools, supporting user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents and students can request full deletion of personal information via privacy@girlswhocode.com or account settings, though school-directed Education Records may be retained per FERPA requirements after account deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: A data retention schedule and lifecycle policy are referenced and inactive Club Student Accounts are deleted after 12 months, but a specific numeric retention period (e.g., number of days) for most data types is not explicitly stated in the publicly accessible policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'security industry best practices' and encryption, and a security white paper is mentioned, but the main privacy policy does not enumerate specific technical security measures (e.g., SOC 2, penetration testing) in the public-facing document.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states encryption and other security safeguards are used to protect personal information, and IP addresses stored for minors are held in truncated or encrypted form.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy mentions Google Login (SSO) as an optional authentication method for Club Student Users, but there is no explicit statement about enforcing strong password requirements for standard username/password accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Google for Education SSO login is offered as an optional method, providing an SSO pathway, but multi-factor authentication is not explicitly mentioned or required for all account types.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Cookies Policy at girlswhocode.com/website-cookies-policy lists and categorizes all cookies by type (essential, functionality, analytics/performance) and names specific third-party tools including Google Analytics and Hotjar.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: GWC publishes a dedicated Third-Party Service Providers page for Clubs (girlswhocode.com/clubs-third-party-service-providers) that names specific vendors including AWS, Salesforce, Zoom, Zendesk, Cloudflare, and others.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The third-party service provider pages list specific data types shared with each named vendor, including identifiers, contact info, technical data, and engagement metrics per provider.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Parents of Outside School Learner Users can choose not to allow disclosure to certain third parties, but the opt-out process for school-connected student accounts is limited and mediated through the school district.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that third-party service providers process information solely on GWC's behalf following GWC's instructions, Privacy Policy, and strict confidentiality and security requirements, and GWC has signed state DPAs.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The third-party provider list notes it 'may be updated over time' and GWC will strive to keep it current, but there is no explicit commitment to notify individual users when specific third-party vendors are added or changed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Clubs Privacy Policy explicitly states that no behaviorally targeted advertising is displayed to Club Student Users, Outside School Minor Users, or Outside School Club Child Users by GWC or any third party.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Student personal information is never used for behaviorally targeted advertising; only contextually relevant educational content (not using personal data) may be presented to users over 13 for non-commercial educational purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy prohibits third-party behavioral advertising and tracking for ad purposes for all student/minor user types, and the Online Tracking Technologies Policy is referenced for additional opt-out details.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Pixel tags and web beacons are defined in the key terms and referenced in the privacy policy as potential tracking methods used by GWC or third-party service providers, though their use for student accounts appears limited to functional/analytics purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Parents of Outside School Learner Users can opt out of disclosure to certain third parties at any time, and the Children's Privacy Policy outlines the process for contacting GWC to restrict data sharing.

r352.riskReason: GoFan's parent company PlayOn Sports was fined $1.1 million by the California Privacy Protection Agency in March 2026 for forcing students to accept tracking and data sharing with advertisers as a condition of accessing school event tickets, failing to honor opt-out signals, and maintaining a privacy policy that falsely stated it did not sell user data.
r352.parentSummary: GoFan collects personal information including name, email, payment data, device identifiers, and browsing behavior using cookies and tracking technologies such as Meta Pixel, sharing this data with advertising, social media, and analytics partners. The platform was fined $1.1 million in 2026 for requiring students to agree to data tracking before they could redeem tickets to school events — with no real opt-out option — constituting coercive data collection targeting a captive student audience. While GoFan states it seeks parental consent before collecting data from children under 13 and uses Stripe and Firebase for secure payment and login handling, its broader advertising data practices raise serious privacy concerns for K-12 school use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use states a date at the top and mentions email or pop-up notification of changes, but enforcement findings cited an outdated privacy policy not updated annually, indicating incomplete revision management.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (personal info, device data, cookies, tracking technologies, payment data), but the full enumeration is not exhaustive and was found by regulators to be inaccurate or misleading in places.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy and FAQ specifically describe collection methods including first- and third-party cookies, persistent trackers, Meta Pixel, Firebase login, and Stripe payment processing.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly affirm user ownership of data; the company retains and commercializes user data for advertising and business operations, with no explicit grant of data ownership to users.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The Terms of Use allow account closure and GoFan Market states data is retained until deletion is requested, but the broader PlayOn privacy policy does not clearly outline a straightforward deletion process for all data types.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy and terms do not state a specific data retention period; no retention timeline is disclosed for personal, behavioral, or advertising data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The FAQ mentions Stripe for PCI-compliant payment processing and Firebase for encrypted login, but broader security measures for non-payment personal data and advertising data are not specifically described.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Login data is explicitly stated to be encrypted via Google Firebase, and payment data is tokenized through Stripe, providing meaningful encryption coverage for key data types.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Use advise users not to share passwords and to maintain account confidentiality, but no specific enforcement of strong password requirements is mentioned.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is mentioned in the consumer-facing policies or FAQ; accounts are managed with standard username/password credentials.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The website discloses use of first- and third-party cookies and trackers including Meta Pixel in its consent banner, but a full enumerated cookie list with individual purposes is not provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy names broad categories of third parties (advertising, social media, analytics partners, co-branded partners, affiliates) but does not provide a specific named list of all third-party vendors receiving personal data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing broadly across advertising, analytics, and social media partners without specifying which data types are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Regulators found that GoFan failed to provide an effective opt-out mechanism — directing users to third-party NAI/DAA tools instead of offering a direct opt-out — and the enforcement order required this to be corrected.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The School Terms of Use reference service providers being permitted to process customer data as necessary for GoFan services, but no binding data protection agreement obligations are explicitly stated for advertising or analytics partners.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not commit to notifying users when third-party data sharing relationships change; no process for user notification of third-party changes is described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Regulators confirmed that GoFan displayed targeted advertisements to ticketholders and used tracking technologies specifically for advertising purposes, including running targeted advertising campaigns on its ticketing platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The California Privacy Protection Agency confirmed GoFan used tracking technologies and user data for targeted advertising, including profiling users across sessions via cookies and persistent identifiers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: GoFan deployed Meta Pixel and other third-party tracking technologies for advertising and shared user data with advertising and social media partners, with no effective opt-out mechanism available during the cited violation period.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: GoFan confirmed use of Meta Pixel, persistent trackers, and first- and third-party cookies for advertising purposes, constituting targeted ad tracking with no functional opt-out, as found by regulators.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The CPPA enforcement action found that GoFan failed to provide consumers with an effective method to opt out of the sale and sharing of their personal information with advertisers, and the privacy policy falsely stated data was not sold.

r353.riskReason: Godot Engine is an open-source game development tool with no dedicated K-12 or COPPA compliance posture; the privacy policy explicitly states it does not currently target children under 13, makes user contributions and forum posts publicly visible, does not specify data retention periods, and lacks a standalone Terms of Service, making it unsuitable as a managed EdTech platform without additional controls.
r353.parentSummary: Godot Engine collects personal data such as your name, email, and physical address when you sign up for community services (forum, chat, asset library, mailing lists), and publicly logs contributions to forums, IRC channels, and source repositories. The platform is not designed for children under 13 and does not claim COPPA or FERPA compliance; it acknowledges COPPA obligations only as a future contingency. SSL encryption and partner confidentiality agreements are in place, but data retention periods are unspecified and no formal Terms of Service document exists on the main godotengine.org domain.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No standalone Terms of Service exists on godotengine.org, and the privacy policy does not describe an advance-notification process or maintain a public revision history for policy changes.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of personal data (name, address, email, contributions, cookies) but uses 'may include (but are not limited to)' language, meaning the list is illustrative rather than exhaustive.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes contexts in which data is collected (account sign-up, conventions, platform use) but does not provide a specific, systematic breakdown of each collection method per data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; it claims a 'legitimate business interest' in maintaining a public record of contributions, creating ambiguity around ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: GDPR-based rights including deletion are mentioned and users can email privacy@godotengine.org, but the process for non-EU users is not clearly defined and no self-service deletion mechanism is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific or general data retention period is stated anywhere in the privacy policy for any category of data collected.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy mentions SSL encryption and partner confidentiality agreements but does not list specific technical security measures such as access controls, audits, or intrusion detection.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states the website uses SSL/TLS technology to encrypt personal data transmitted on the site.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy makes no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement policies for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are acknowledged and users are directed to browser-level controls, but no detailed cookie list with names, purposes, or durations is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third-party sharing is described in broad categories (partners, TuxFamily, law enforcement) without naming specific vendor organizations beyond TuxFamily.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing purposes broadly without specifying which data types are shared with each individual third-party partner.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described; users are only told to contact the project via email with no guaranteed outcome.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states partners enter into confidentiality agreements requiring care to prevent loss or misuse, which is a general rather than specific vendor compliance statement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not describe any process for notifying users when third-party data-sharing relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Godot Engine privacy policy contains no mention of advertisements being displayed to users of the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no indication of any behavioral or interest-based targeted advertising within the Godot Engine ecosystem.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party advertising tracking is described or implied in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacons or ad-tracking technologies are mentioned or used according to the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or data sharing with advertisers occurs, no opt-out is needed and the platform fully meets this criterion by default.

r354.riskReason: GoGuardian holds iKeepSafe COPPA Safe Harbor and FERPA certifications, explicitly prohibits selling or advertising with student data, uses TLS encryption and ISO 27001/SOC 2 security controls, and schools retain ownership and deletion rights over student data.
r354.parentSummary: GoGuardian Teacher collects detailed student data including browsing history, chat messages, video recordings, screenshots, and account information in order to enable classroom monitoring, content filtering, and student safety features directed by the school. GoGuardian explicitly states it does not sell student data or use it for advertising, and schools own and can request deletion of student data at any time. The platform holds independent iKeepSafe certifications for both FERPA and COPPA compliance, though parents should be aware that significant activity monitoring occurs on school-managed devices.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy indicates a 'last updated' date at the top and states changes will be applied after notification where required by law, but does not guarantee advance notice for all material changes to the Product Privacy Policy (only where legally required), making this partially compliant.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Product Privacy Policy and COPPA Disclosure Form provide an extensive and specific enumeration of all data types collected across all GoGuardian offerings, including account info, activity data, browsing history, video/chat recordings, grades, and device data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly describes how data is collected: automatically via browser extensions on school-managed devices, through school-provided account provisioning, via API integrations (e.g., Google Classroom, Gmail), and through analytics services.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: GoGuardian explicitly states that schools own and control their Personal Student Information, and that GoGuardian acts as a 'processor' on behalf of the school 'controller,' confirming school/user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Schools can request deletion of Personal Student Information at any time via privacy@goguardian.com; parents and eligible students can also request deletion through their school, and a CCPA deletion request portal exists at goguardian.com/policies/ccpa-requests.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Specific retention periods are stated: video conferencing recordings are retained 90 days, non-alert email messages 60 days, and accounts are considered terminated 365 days after license expiry, after which data is de-identified or deleted.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: GoGuardian describes a combination of technical, administrative, and physical safeguards including TLS encryption, need-to-know access controls, anti-malware, firewalls, data backups, annual security testing, and employee privacy training.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: GoGuardian uses TLS encryption across all products and websites for data in transit, and its DPA references FIPS-validated encryption technologies for systems that process, store, and transmit data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The EULA mentions password confidentiality responsibilities but does not explicitly state enforcement of strong password complexity requirements; however, the platform primarily uses SSO via Google or Microsoft school-managed accounts, which partially addresses this.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: GoGuardian Teacher is accessed via school-managed Google or Microsoft SSO accounts, which inherently provide MFA capability at the identity provider level, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A dedicated Website Cookies Notice exists at goguardian.com/policies/website-cookies-notice listing cookie types (session, persistent, analytics, advertising) and their purposes; the Product Privacy Policy also has a cookies section describing only functional/analytics cookies with no advertising cookies in the product.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Product Privacy Policy references a linked list of third-party service providers used by GoGuardian Offerings but does not name them inline in the publicly visible policy text; affiliates (Pear Deck Inc., Snapwiz Inc., Zorro Holdco) are named, but operational subprocessors are only accessible via a separate linked page.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups third-party sharing into categories (affiliates, service providers, integration partners) with general descriptions of what is shared per category, but does not provide a granular per-vendor breakdown of exactly which data fields are shared with each specific third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Schools can direct GoGuardian not to share data or can request deletion at any time; integration-based sharing is opt-in by school configuration, and California residents have a 'Do Not Sell' opt-out mechanism at goguardian.com/policies/ccpa-requests.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The DPA explicitly states that sub-processors are bound by data protection obligations equivalent to those in the DPA, and GoGuardian retains responsibility for sub-processor compliance with applicable data protection laws.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The DPA provides at least 10 days advance written notice to schools of any additions or replacements of sub-processors, and the website policy indicates the 'last updated' date when policies change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: GoGuardian explicitly states 'no advertisements of any kind are shown in any Offerings' and that third-party advertising services do not collect any Personal Student Information through the product.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: GoGuardian explicitly prohibits using Personal Student Information to target advertisements or market to students or anyone else, and confirms no behavioral targeting occurs within the product.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The Product Privacy Policy states no advertising cookies are used in the Offerings and third-party advertising services do not collect student data through the product; the website (not the product) uses advertising tracking with an opt-out available.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Within the GoGuardian Teacher product, only functional and analytics cookies/tracking are used; the policy explicitly states 'we do not use any advertising Cookies in our Offerings.'
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No advertising data sharing occurs within the GoGuardian Teacher product itself; for the public website, California residents can opt out via the 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' page, and a clear opt-out mechanism is available.

r355.riskReason: GoNoodle explicitly commits to COPPA and FERPA compliance and does not sell student data, but its privacy policy permits targeted contextual advertising and allows third-party ad networks and tracking services to collect user data across sites, posing a meaningful risk in K-12 deployments.
r355.parentSummary: GoNoodle collects personal information only from educators and parents/guardians (not directly from students), including name, email, school name, and usage/log data. The platform states it does not sell user data and does not send marketing messages to children, and parents can request deletion of their child's account at any time. However, GoNoodle acknowledges that third-party ad networks and tracking services may collect data about users across websites, and the platform may serve targeted contextual advertising to adult account holders.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states GoNoodle reserves the right to modify the Privacy Policy per outlined procedures and posts changes on the site, but no advance notification commitment or revision history/changelog is explicitly provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates specific categories of data collected from unregistered users, educators, and family account holders, including name, email, school info, zip code, IP address, log/clickstream data, and billing information.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected — directly from users at registration, automatically via cookies and web beacons, and through third-party collection tools.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; data ownership is ambiguous, with GoNoodle claiming the right to use collected information for multiple purposes including personalized ads and product development.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users and parents can request deletion of accounts and associated personal data by emailing support@gonoodle.com, and the policy states deleted accounts cannot be recovered.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The current privacy policy states data is retained while an account is active and deleted within 24 months of inactivity, providing a specific retention timeframe.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references secure cloud-based environments, server authentication, and industry-standard firewalls, but does not enumerate comprehensive or specific security measures beyond these general statements.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The GoNoodle Shop policy references SSL encryption, but the main platform privacy policy does not explicitly confirm end-to-end or at-rest encryption; Common Sense Media noted encryption status was unclear.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The TOS asks users to choose a password and maintain confidentiality, but does not specify enforcement of strong password requirements such as minimum length or complexity rules.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the publicly available Terms of Service or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: GoNoodle references a separate Cookie Notification/Policy and mentions use of cookies and web beacons generally, but the cookie policy page did not render specific cookie categories or a full cookie list in search results.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy states a Third Party List exists and is accessible, but the actual list of named third parties is not reproduced within the privacy policy itself, making specific vendor identification dependent on a separate document.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups third-party sharing into broad categories (service providers, sponsors, ad networks) without detailing which specific data elements are shared with each named or categorized party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy directs users to NAI and DAA opt-out tools for third-party ad tracking but does not provide a direct, platform-level opt-out mechanism for all third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The main privacy policy requires third-party service providers to limit use and maintain confidentiality, but the Games privacy policy explicitly notes contracts mandating such measures may not be in place with all third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states GoNoodle may update the policy and post changes on the site, but does not explicitly commit to notifying users in advance of changes to third-party relationships.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The main platform privacy policy states GoNoodle may serve targeted contextual advertising to users, though the older sandbox policy version states they do not serve targeted advertising — creating a version conflict and partial compliance.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The current (November 2025) privacy policy explicitly states GoNoodle may serve targeted contextual advertising and that third-party ad networks may track users to deliver interest-based ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party ad networks and web analytics companies are acknowledged to collect data across sites for advertising purposes, and GoNoodle explicitly states it does not honor 'Do Not Track' signals.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms the use of web beacons, cookies, and clear GIFs by both GoNoodle and third-party ad networks for tracking and advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users are directed to external opt-out tools (NAI, DAA) for third-party advertiser data use, but no clear, in-platform opt-out process for advertiser data sharing is provided.
