r356.riskReason: Google Earth is classified as an 'Additional Service' outside Google Workspace for Education Core Services, meaning it can display ads and collects data under the broader Google Privacy Policy, requiring explicit school admin enablement and parental consent for K-12 users under 18—creating compliance gaps if not properly configured.
r356.parentSummary: Google Earth collects data including your child's account information, device identifiers, location, usage activity, and cookies when used with a signed-in Google account. As an 'Additional Service' under Google Workspace for Education, Google states that personal information from K-12 users will not be used to target personalized ads, but contextual ads may still appear, and this protection only applies when the service is properly configured by a school administrator with parental consent obtained. Parents should confirm with their school that Google Earth has been appropriately enabled in the admin console with consent collected, as without this configuration the standard consumer Google Privacy Policy applies.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Google maintains a public archive of prior Privacy Policy versions with comparison tools, and posts advance notice of material changes at policies.google.com/privacy/archive.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Google's Privacy Policy broadly lists categories of data collected including account info, device/usage data, location, cookies, and content submitted—providing a reasonably comprehensive enumeration.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The Privacy Policy describes multiple collection mechanisms including direct account signup, service usage, device sensors, third-party sources, and cookies/tracking technologies.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: For Google Workspace for Education Core Services, education organizations retain ownership of their data; however, Google Earth as an Additional Service is governed by the standard consumer Privacy Policy under which ownership terms are less clearly student-centric.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Google allows users to access, modify, delete, and export their data at any time via Google Account settings and Takeout, with a documented deletion process, though backup copies may persist for up to 6 months.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Google's separate data retention policy page (policies.google.com/technologies/retention) describes retention periods by data type, including that backup copies are retained up to 6 months post-deletion.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Google's Privacy Policy and FAQ specify multiple security measures including encryption, threat detection, and fraud prevention systems, and the company states it employs world-renowned data security experts.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Google explicitly states it uses encryption to keep data private while in transit and at rest, including encrypted backup storage.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Google Workspace for Education supports SAML-based SSO, and Google accounts enforce password strength requirements; Google Earth accessed via a Workspace account inherits these controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Google Workspace offers SAML single sign-on (SSO) integration, and Google accounts support 2-step verification (MFA), satisfying this requirement for school-managed accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Google publishes a dedicated cookies policy page (policies.google.com/technologies/cookies) listing specific cookie names, durations, and purposes including security, analytics, and advertising.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy references broad categories of third parties (service providers, advertising partners, affiliates) but does not name specific third-party companies receiving data from Google Earth users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Privacy Policy groups data shared with third parties by purpose category rather than specifying which data elements are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of personalized advertising via My Ad Center and Google Account settings, but opt-out for all forms of third-party data sharing is limited and not fully comprehensive.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Google states it provides personal information to trusted businesses only under instructions and in compliance with the Privacy Policy and appropriate confidentiality measures, indicating contractual limits are in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Privacy Policy is updated periodically with an archive available, but does not include a specific process for notifying users when individual third-party service provider relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Google Earth as an Additional Service may display ads for consumer accounts; for K-12 Workspace users with proper admin configuration, ads are not personalized, but contextual ads based on content or search queries may still appear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: For properly configured K-12 Workspace accounts, Google commits that personal account information will not be used to target ads, but contextual ads (based on page content, time of day, or search queries) remain possible.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google allows specific partners to collect information from browsers or devices for advertising and measurement using their own cookies, with limited opt-out available via ad settings—making full third-party tracking opt-out incomplete.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Google uses multiple tracking technologies including cookies, pixel tags, unique device identifiers, and advertising IDs, some of which are used for advertising purposes beyond purely functional use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of personalized ads through My Ad Center (myadcenter.google.com) and ad settings, but the process is spread across multiple settings pages and not surfaced as a single clear opt-out for all data sharing with advertisers.

r357.riskReason: Google Lens operates under Google's general consumer privacy policy — not an education-specific policy — and collects broad data including images, location, search history, and device identifiers that are used to serve personalized advertising, with no COPPA or FERPA commitments specific to this product.
r357.parentSummary: Google Lens collects a wide range of data when students use it, including images they scan, search history, location, and device identifiers, all governed by Google's general consumer Privacy Policy rather than any education-specific agreement. Google states it does not sell personal data, but it does share data with advertising and analytics partners and uses activity data to personalize ads across its services. Unlike Google Workspace for Education, Google Lens has no dedicated COPPA or FERPA compliance commitments, making it unsuitable for school-issued or school-directed use with K-12 students without additional controls.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Google states it will provide prominent notice (including email) for significant policy changes, but no versioned revision history with diff tracking is publicly maintained for the general policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Google's privacy policy lists broad categories of data collected (location, device info, usage, images, identifiers), but Google Lens has no product-specific disclosure and the general policy does not exhaustively enumerate every data point captured by Lens specifically.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Google's policy specifically describes how data is collected — through direct user input, automated means (cookies, pixels, server logs), device sensors, and partner sources — satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Google states it does not claim ownership over user-generated content and users retain rights, but Google acquires a broad license to use submitted content for service operation, leaving ownership clarity partial for K-12 contexts.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Google provides My Activity, Dashboard, and Google Takeout tools allowing users to review, export, and delete data, and users can delete Lens search history entries, satisfying the deletion requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Google describes retention practices generally (e.g., anonymizing ad data after 9–18 months, deleting location from Web & App Activity after 30 days) but does not state a single unified retention period for all Lens-specific data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Google's privacy policy and Safety Center describe specific security measures including encryption, access controls, automated threat detection, and physical data center security.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Google uses HTTPS encryption for data in transit between devices and servers, and Google Lens specifically encrypts data during transmission.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Google Accounts enforce strong password requirements and support Google's SSO infrastructure; no standalone account is required to use Lens in basic mode.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Google supports optional 2-Step Verification (MFA) on Google Accounts but does not mandate it; for school deployments, Google Workspace for Education supports SSO/LTI but Lens itself is not restricted to that environment.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Google's policy mentions cookies, pixel tags, local storage, and similar technologies generally and provides an ad settings page, but does not provide a granular per-cookie list with individual purposes for Google Lens specifically.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google's privacy policy references broad categories of third parties (service providers, advertising partners, analytics partners) but does not provide a specific named list of all third-party vendors used by Google Lens.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Google groups data sharing by category of third party (e.g., service providers, ad partners) rather than specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Google provides Ads Settings and My Ad Center to opt out of personalized advertising, but opting out of all third-party data sharing (e.g., analytics, measurement partners) is not straightforward or fully available.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Google's policy states that service providers process data under Google's instructions and in compliance with its privacy policy, but this is a general contractual claim rather than a named supplier accountability framework specific to Lens.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Google's policy says it will notify users of significant changes but does not commit to notifying users specifically when new third-party vendors are added to the Lens data processing chain.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Google Lens, as a consumer Google product, is part of the Google advertising ecosystem; Google's own policy confirms activity data can be used to serve personalized ads across its services, including from Lens usage.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Google explicitly uses cross-service activity data — potentially including Lens searches — to inform personalized advertising targeting, which is confirmed in its privacy policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google allows specific advertising and measurement partners to collect data via cookies and similar technologies for ad purposes, with limited opt-out available via Ads Settings but no full block of third-party tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Google uses cookies, pixel tags, Advertising IDs, and server logs across its services including Lens for ad-related purposes, confirming tracking beyond functional necessity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Google provides an opt-out mechanism via My Ad Center and Ads Settings for personalized ads, but the process is account-level and not clearly surfaced within the Lens product itself, making it partially accessible.

r358.riskReason: Google Scholar is a general consumer product governed by Google's broad privacy policy, which includes advertising-based data collection, behavioral tracking via cookies, and third-party data sharing not specifically restricted for K-12 students, making it unsuitable as a school-assigned tool without additional institutional controls.
r358.parentSummary: Google Scholar collects data including search queries, IP addresses, device identifiers, location, and usage activity — even without a Google Account — and ties more extensive data collection to signed-in accounts. Google's general privacy policy permits use of this data to personalize advertising and shares data with advertising and analytics partners, which raises concerns for K-12 use. While Google states it does not sell personal data, its broad data collection practices and advertising ecosystem are not tailored for student audiences, and there is no dedicated COPPA or FERPA compliance framework specific to Google Scholar.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Google's Terms of Service state that material changes will receive advance notice, and an archived version history of the Privacy Policy is publicly available at policies.google.com/privacy/archive.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Google's Privacy Policy enumerates categories of data collected including activity data, device info, location, search queries, and account information, providing a reasonably comprehensive list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The Privacy Policy specifically describes collection methods including cookies, device sensors, account sign-in, user input, and automated logging of interactions with services.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Google states it does not claim ownership of user-generated content, but the policy grants Google broad licenses to use data for service improvement and advertising, making data ownership effectively ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Google offers data deletion tools via My Account and Google Takeout, but some data is retained for legal or operational purposes and deletion of certain data types has limitations or waiting periods.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Google's data retention policy page (policies.google.com/technologies/retention) describes retention periods by data type, noting some data is deleted automatically while other data is held until user deletion or indefinitely for legal reasons.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Google's Privacy Policy explicitly lists security measures including encryption in transit, Safe Browsing, Security Checkup, and automated threat detection, constituting specific security disclosures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Google explicitly states it uses encryption to keep data private while in transit, and the Scholar site uses HTTPS throughout, satisfying this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: A Google Account (required for personalized Scholar features) enforces strong password standards and supports Google's account security infrastructure; no-account usage requires no credentials at all.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Google accounts support 2-Step Verification (MFA) and Google Workspace for Education supports SSO/LTI integrations, satisfying this criterion for institutional deployments.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Google publishes a detailed cookie policy at policies.google.com/technologies/cookies listing individual cookies by name, purpose, and expiration, which fully meets this criterion.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google's Privacy Policy refers broadly to 'partners,' 'advertisers,' 'developers,' and 'trusted businesses' without naming specific third-party companies, constituting only a broad generalization.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by purpose category (advertising, analytics, legal) rather than specifying which data elements are shared with each distinct third party, making disclosure incomplete.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Google offers opt-out controls via My Ad Center and account settings for personalized advertising, but these controls are not straightforward for unauthenticated users and do not eliminate all third-party data flows.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Google's Privacy Policy states that third parties processing data on its behalf are bound by confidentiality and security agreements and must follow Google's instructions, meeting this criterion.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Google states it will notify users of significant policy changes, but does not commit to advance notification specifically for changes in third-party partners or sub-processors, creating partial coverage.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Google Scholar as a general consumer product is governed by the same ad-serving infrastructure as other Google services; Google's cookie policy confirms cookies are used for serving and personalizing ads, indicating ads may be displayed or tracked even if Scholar itself does not show visible banner ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Google's Privacy Policy and cookie documentation confirm that behavioral and interest-based ad targeting applies to signed-in users across Google services, which includes Scholar activity, constituting confirmed user targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google allows partners to collect data for advertising and measurement using their own cookies and similar technologies, but provides opt-out mechanisms via Ad Settings and the Network Advertising Initiative, resulting in partial opt-out capability.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Google's cookie policy confirms use of pixel tags, unique identifiers, local storage, and advertising cookies (e.g., NID, IDE) for ad tracking purposes across its services, including when users interact with Scholar.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Google provides opt-out tools via My Ad Center (adssettings.google.com) for personalized ad data sharing, but the process requires a Google Account and is not clearly communicated within the Scholar interface itself.

dataSharedWith: Third-party service providers (maintenance, database management, web analytics)
Advertising partners (Facebook, Google Ads — opt-in only)
OpenAI (for AI features, stated no PII sent)
Law enforcement or legal authorities (when required by law)
Corporate successors (in case of merger or acquisition)
r359.riskReason: GooseChase demonstrates strong K-12 privacy commitments including FERPA/COPPA/SOPIPA alignment, a dedicated Student Privacy Policy, signed NDPAs, and a no-sell pledge, but its general Privacy Policy permits opt-in third-party advertising cookies (Facebook, Google Ads) and web beacon tracking on the same platform used by students, creating residual risk if cookie consent controls are not properly enforced for minors.
r359.parentSummary: GooseChase collects standard account information (name, email, usage data) and allows students to participate anonymously via a Guest Account feature that stores no data online. The platform explicitly pledges never to sell student data, states compliance with FERPA, COPPA, and SOPIPA, and has signed data protection agreements with hundreds of school districts. However, parents should be aware that the general platform supports opt-in advertising cookies from Facebook and Google Ads, and the policy confirms that user information can be used to track and target ads on third-party websites, though GooseChase states no interest-based advertising is shown to children.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy indicates it may be updated without a clearly stated advance-notification process or publicly maintained revision history, though an effective date is present.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and dedicated Student Privacy Policy enumerate categories of data collected including account data, technical data, transaction data, usage data, and user-generated content.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes data collection mechanisms including account creation forms, cookies, web beacons, log files, scripts, and social media widgets.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Voluntarily provided account information is stated to 'remain the property of GooseChase Adventures Inc.,' but schools are separately noted to retain all rights to their data, creating an unclear dual-ownership situation.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users and students (or their parents/guardians) may request full deletion of personal data, with requests processed within 28 days, and students can also delete data directly from within the app.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only 'as long as necessary' but does not specify a concrete retention period in days or years, making the timeline vague for most users.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'commercially reasonable efforts,' 'technical, contractual, administrative, and physical security steps,' and NIST Cybersecurity Framework alignment for NY Ed Law 2-d contracts, but specific measures (e.g., SOC 2, penetration testing) are not detailed in the public policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Industry-standard encryption in transit and at rest is explicitly stated for NY Ed Law 2-d data; however, the Terms of Service contains a disclaimer that 'information sent or received over the Internet is generally unsecure,' creating ambiguity about encryption coverage for all users.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Users are instructed to keep passwords secure and not share them, but the policy does not explicitly enforce minimum password complexity requirements; no SSO/LTI enforcement is mentioned in the public-facing policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the publicly available Terms of Service or Privacy Policy, and account creation is required for non-guest users.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A dedicated Cookie Policy at goosechase.com/cookie-policy lists and categorizes cookies by type (strictly necessary, tracking/advertising) with opt-in controls and opt-out instructions, providing reasonable transparency.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references third-party service providers for analytics, maintenance, and advertising (Facebook, Google Ads) by name in some contexts, but a comprehensive named list of all third-party processors is not publicly available.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing broadly by purpose (functionality, analytics, advertising) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Advertising cookies require opt-in consent, and opt-out links (aboutads.info, youronlinechoices.eu) are provided; however, opt-out for non-advertising third-party service providers is not described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states contractual and organizational safeguards are in place with agents and third parties, and Common Sense Media confirmed contractual limits are placed on third-party data use.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No explicit process is stated for notifying users when third-party service providers are added, removed, or changed; the policy only states it 'may' share with third parties from time to time.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: GooseChase states no interest-based advertising is shown to children and personalized advertising is not displayed within the platform, but the general platform supports opt-in advertising cookies from Facebook and Google Ads for adult users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The platform does not display targeted ads internally and states no data profiles are created for personalized ads, but Common Sense Media confirmed user information can be used to track and target ads on other third-party websites via opt-in advertising cookies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party ad tracking (Facebook, Google Ads) is opt-in with a cookie consent mechanism and opt-out links provided, but the policy acknowledges these third parties may collect cross-site behavioral data even with limited controls.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy and Cookie Policy acknowledge the use of web beacons and tracking pixels (including Facebook Pixel) on the website, though these are described as opt-in for advertising purposes; the functional scope of beacons is not fully separated from advertising use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Opt-out from advertising cookies is available via an in-platform toggle and external opt-out links (aboutads.info, youronlinechoices.eu), but the process is not prominently surfaced and relies on third-party opt-out infrastructure.

dataCollected: Communication-related data (partial/truncated IP address via telecom provider)
Usage-related data (commencement and duration of usage)
dataSharedWith: None (per software privacy policy — no personal data collected from app)
r360.riskReason: GoTalk NOW (by Attainment Company) explicitly states it does not collect any personal data from its applications, operates as a local iOS app without requiring user accounts, and Apple's App Store listing confirms the developer does not collect any data from this app.
r360.parentSummary: GoTalk NOW is an iPad-based AAC (Augmentative and Alternative Communication) app published by Attainment Company that explicitly states it does not collect personal data such as names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, or full IP addresses from the application. No user account is required to use the app, and data such as communication books is stored locally or backed up via Dropbox/iTunes at the user's discretion. While the software privacy policy is relatively brief, the no-data-collection stance and offline-first design represent a low privacy risk for students.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The software privacy policy states changes will be announced 'in due time' and users should check regularly, but no advance notification mechanism or revision history is explicitly promised.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy clearly states no personal data (names, addresses, phone numbers, email, full IP addresses) is collected from the application, meeting the standard by explicitly declaring minimal/no data collection.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy provides a general statement that communication and usage-related data are generated automatically by telecom providers but does not detail how Attainment itself collects anything, leaving the method partially described.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Because the policy states no personal data is collected from the app and data is stored locally on device, user/school ownership of content is implicit, though not explicitly stated in ownership terms.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The software privacy policy does not address any deletion process or user rights to delete data, since the app is local-only and no server-side data is acknowledged; no deletion mechanism is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated in the software privacy policy, consistent with claiming no data is collected, but this leaves retention practices unaddressed for any incidental data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The software privacy policy contains no specific security measures for the GoTalk NOW app itself; the Attainment Commitment to Security page (for HUB products) references SOC2 and encryption but is not clearly linked to the GoTalk NOW standalone app.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The GoTalk NOW software privacy policy does not mention encryption; the Commitment to Security page notes transit encryption for online services but GoTalk NOW is a local app with no confirmed encryption policy specific to it.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account is required to use GoTalk NOW, so password requirements are moot; the no-account design effectively meets this criterion by eliminating credential risk entirely.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: GoTalk NOW requires no user account or login, meaning MFA is not applicable and there is no authentication risk associated with the app itself.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The software privacy policy makes no mention of cookies; as a native iOS app, cookies are not directly applicable, but the policy does not address any equivalent tracking mechanisms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The software privacy policy states no personal data is collected and no third parties are named as recipients, effectively disclosing there is no sharing; this meets the criterion by confirming absence of third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Since no personal data is collected or shared per the policy, there is nothing to disclose per third party, meeting this criterion by confirming no data sharing takes place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No third-party data sharing occurs per the policy, so no opt-out is needed; the criterion is met by design through the no-data-collection stance.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The software privacy policy does not mention any vendor agreements or contractual obligations with third parties regarding data protection, leaving this dimension unaddressed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes will be announced 'in due time' but does not specify a process for notifying users of third-party changes specifically; since no third parties are used, this is partially met by default.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The GoTalk NOW app is a locally-operated AAC tool with no advertising of any kind displayed to users, meeting this criterion.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is conducted or referenced in any Attainment Company policy for the GoTalk NOW app.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is present or disclosed for GoTalk NOW; the app operates offline and collects no personal data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacons, tracking pixels, or advertising-related tracking mechanisms are mentioned or employed in the GoTalk NOW app.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no data sharing with advertisers occurs, no opt-out is necessary; this criterion is met by the absence of any advertising data practices.

dataCollected: IP address (partial, via telecommunications provider only)
dataSharedWith: None (developer states no personal data is collected from the app)
r361.riskReason: Apple App Store confirms the developer does not collect any data from this app, and the developer's own Software Privacy Policy explicitly states no personal data is collected from applications, making this a low-risk, offline-first AAC tool for K-12 use.
r361.parentSummary: GoTalk NOW LITE is a free AAC (augmentative and alternative communication) iPad app developed by Attainment Company that requires no account and collects no personal data from users according to both Apple's App Store disclosure and the developer's own Software Privacy Policy. All communication books and pages are stored locally on the device, not in the cloud. While Attainment Company's broader platform (Attainment HUB) holds iKeepSafe COPPA Safe Harbor certification, no dedicated Terms of Service or explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance statement was found specifically for the GoTalk NOW LITE standalone app.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Terms of Service page was found for GoTalk NOW LITE, and the Software Privacy Policy provides no information about advance notification of changes or a revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Software Privacy Policy explicitly states no personal data (names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, or complete IP addresses) is collected from applications, which constitutes a clear declaration.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states data is not collected from the app but notes telecommunications providers may generate communication-related and usage data automatically, without specifically detailing how Attainment itself collects anything.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Because no personal data is collected by the developer, there is no data ownership dispute; all user-created content resides locally on the device.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy does not address a deletion mechanism for users, though given no data is collected server-side, this is moot; however, no formal deletion process is documented.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated in the Software Privacy Policy, as the policy is premised on no data being collected; there is no retention schedule disclosed.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Commitment to Security page on attainmentcompany.com references SOC2 compliance, incident response plans, and access controls, but these appear to apply to the broader company/HUB platform rather than specifically to the GoTalk NOW LITE standalone app.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The Commitment to Security page states service data transmitted over the internet is encrypted-in-transit, but this appears to refer to the HUB platform; the standalone app operates offline and no encryption statement is made specifically for GoTalk NOW LITE.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The app requires no account creation and no password, meaning password policy is not applicable; this effectively means users are not exposed to weak-password risks.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account or login is required to use GoTalk NOW LITE, eliminating the need for multi-factor authentication and removing that attack surface entirely.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The website privacy policy mentions traffic log cookies used on attainmentcompany.com, but no specific cookie inventory or detailed cookie policy specific to the app or its associated website is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Software Privacy Policy states no personal data is collected and therefore no third-party data sharing occurs; this effectively constitutes a disclosure that there are no third-party data recipients.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Because no data is collected from the app, there is nothing shared with third parties, satisfying this criterion by absence of data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No third-party data sharing takes place from the app, so no opt-out mechanism is required or relevant.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No third-party data sharing agreements are documented for the app specifically; while the HUB platform lists vendor agreements, no equivalent documentation exists for GoTalk NOW LITE.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no stated process for notifying users if third-party data-sharing practices change, and no Terms of Service exists that would establish such a commitment for this app.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No advertisements are displayed within GoTalk NOW LITE; it is a paid/freemium offline AAC tool with no ad network integration.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is present or disclosed; the app has no ad infrastructure.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is present in the app, as confirmed by the developer's no-data-collection declaration and Apple's App Store privacy nutrition label.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacons or ad-tracking methods are disclosed or apparent in the standalone app; all functionality is local to the device.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No data sharing with advertisers occurs, making an opt-out mechanism unnecessary; this criterion is satisfied by the absence of advertising data practices.

r362.riskReason: GoToMeeting is a business-focused video conferencing platform that lacks any COPPA-specific protections, has no stated minimum age requirement, admits to sharing website visitor data with advertising networks for targeted advertising, and provides no FERPA-specific commitments or K-12 student data protections.
r362.parentSummary: GoToMeeting collects a broad range of personal data including names, email addresses, billing information, device data, IP addresses, and session content such as recordings and transcripts. The platform is designed for business use and makes no COPPA or FERPA-specific commitments, meaning it has no dedicated protections for children's data or student educational records. Additionally, GoTo's own policies acknowledge sharing website visitor data with advertising networks for targeted/behavioral advertising, posing meaningful risks when used in a K-12 school setting.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: GoTo's policies state they may notify users of material changes via email or website posting prior to the change becoming effective, but there is no formal revision history or changelog publicly maintained.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy describes broad categories of data collected (identifiers, usage data, session content, billing data, cookies) but does not exhaustively enumerate every specific data type collected during K-12 use.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: GoTo generally states data is collected directly from users, through automated means, and via third parties, but does not provide detailed, granular explanations of each collection method in the context of education use.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service explicitly state that users retain all rights to their files, documents, recordings, chat logs, and transcripts, and that GoTo does not own or license user content.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: GoTo's Data Privacy Framework notice references rights of access, correction, and deletion via an Individual Rights Management Portal, but deletion may be subject to retention periods tied to legal obligations and agreement duration.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The Data Processing Addendum states personal data is retained 'no longer than needed for the business purpose for which it was collected,' which is a general statement without a specific retention period defined for K-12 or educational contexts.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: GoTo's security documentation details 128-bit AES encryption, TLS protocols, hashed passwords, digital code signing, and a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL) model, indicating specific security measures are in place.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: GoToMeeting uses AES-128 encryption for session data, TLS for connections, and encrypts cloud recordings and transcripts both in transit and at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: GoTo's security documentation confirms passwords are stored using cryptographic hash functions and are never transmitted in plaintext, and strong passwords are required to log in.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: GoTo offers SSO integration options for enterprise customers, but standard multi-factor authentication for all end users is not explicitly confirmed as a universal requirement in publicly available policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: GoTo mentions using first- and third-party cookies and tracking technologies in its privacy policy but does not provide a fully detailed cookie list with specific purposes for each cookie type readily accessible to all users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: GoTo references sharing data with 'sub-processors' and advertising networks but does not provide a named list of specific third parties directly in the main privacy policy; a sub-processor list is referenced as available separately.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: GoTo groups data sharing by category of recipient (sub-processors, advertising networks, government) rather than specifying exactly which data types are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: GoTo's applicant and general privacy notices reference an opt-out mechanism for sale or sharing of personal data with advertising networks, but the process is not clearly prominent or straightforward for general service users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: GoTo's Data Privacy Framework notice and DPA state that GoTo remains responsible and liable for onward transfers to sub-processors and maintains contracts restricting their access, use, and disclosure of personal data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: GoTo's legal page indicates users can subscribe to receive notification of new sub-processors, but there is no explicit policy guaranteeing advance notice to end users for all third-party relationship changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: GoTo's own policy documentation acknowledges sharing website visitor data with advertising networks for cross-context behavioral advertising and targeted advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: GoTo explicitly acknowledges in its applicant privacy notice that it has shared personal data of website visitors with advertising networks for targeted/behavioral advertising, which is a confirmed targeting practice.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: GoTo references an opt-out mechanism for the sale or sharing of personal data for advertising, including support for Global Privacy Control (GPC) signals, but the opt-out is not prominently surfaced for all user types.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: GoTo's privacy policy acknowledges use of first- and third-party cookies and tracking technologies for advertising purposes, indicating tracking beyond functional use is occurring on its websites.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out for data sharing with advertisers is referenced in GoTo's privacy documentation and the platform supports GPC signals, but the process is not clearly described or easily accessible for school administrators or parents.

dataCollected: Student identification (name, initials, ID number, or alphanumeric code)
dataSharedWith: None (student and instructor data explicitly stated as never sold, rented, or disclosed to third parties)
r363.riskReason: GoVenture states student data is never sold or shared with third parties and uses SSL/TLS encryption, but the combined Terms of Use and Privacy Policy lacks explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance declarations, has no stated data retention period, grants MediaSpark a perpetual irrevocable license over submitted personalized content, and some content is explicitly non-deletable, raising notable concerns for K-12 deployment.
r363.parentSummary: GoVenture collects instructor account information (name, email, school, country) and limited student identifiers (username, password, and a student ID which can be anonymized by the instructor). The platform explicitly states student and instructor data is never sold, rented, or disclosed to third parties, and data is encrypted both in transit and at rest. However, any personalized content students submit is licensed to MediaSpark on a perpetual, irrevocable basis, and some content cannot be deleted, which parents and schools should be aware of before use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: MediaSpark states it will provide notice of material policy changes, but there is no commitment to advance notice before changes take effect or a publicly maintained revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The student privacy page lists specific data types collected for the online version (name, email, school, country, username, password, student ID), but the broader Terms of Use policy refers vaguely to 'Personal Information' without enumerating all collected data types comprehensively.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The student privacy page describes how data is collected (account creation, subscription validation), but the general Terms of Use only states that personal information is used to customize content, improve the platform, and respond to support requests without fully detailing all collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states MediaSpark does not claim ownership of personalized content users submit, but simultaneously grants MediaSpark a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license over that content, creating an unclear and arguably unfavorable ownership situation for K-12 users.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request data deletion by contacting MediaSpark, and instructors can delete student data; however, some personalized content is explicitly stated as non-deletable at MediaSpark's sole discretion, limiting full deletion rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Neither the Terms of Use nor the student privacy page specifies any data retention period or schedule, leaving retention practices entirely unaddressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The student privacy page specifically describes SSL/TLS encryption in transit, encryption at rest in the database, hashed passwords, and servers hosted in secure US or Canadian locations.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states data is encrypted using SSL/TLS in transit and encrypted at rest when stored in the database, and passwords are hashed and encrypted.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The student privacy page mentions passwords are hashed and encrypted, but there is no explicit statement that the platform enforces strong password creation rules or complexity requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA), single sign-on (SSO), or LTI integration is made anywhere in the Terms of Use or privacy documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Terms of Use and privacy policy contain no cookie policy disclosing which cookies are used, their purposes, or any opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The student privacy page explicitly states student and instructor data is never sold, rented, or disclosed to third parties, effectively confirming no third-party data sharing occurs.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Because no data is shared with third parties according to the stated policy, there is nothing to disclose regarding what is shared with each party — the no-sharing commitment fully satisfies this criterion.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No third-party data sharing is stated to occur, so there is effectively nothing to opt out of, satisfying this requirement by virtue of the no-sharing policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not mention any contractual obligations imposed on third parties regarding data handling, and while no third-party sharing is claimed, the absence of any supplier agreement language leaves this unaddressed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no stated process for notifying users if third-party data sharing arrangements were ever to change in the future.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The student privacy page and Terms of Use contain no indication that ads are displayed to students, and the ToU explicitly prohibits using GoVenture for advertising revenue purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No evidence of targeted advertising directed at students or instructors is present in the documentation; the platform's explicit prohibition on advertising-revenue use supports this.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is disclosed or evident in the GoVenture K-12 platform documentation; tracking for advertising purposes is not mentioned.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacons or ad-tracking methods are disclosed in the policy; the only tracking mentioned is functional subscription validation and optional play-count reporting with no personal data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising or data sharing with advertisers is disclosed or indicated, there is no advertising opt-out needed; the platform effectively meets this criterion by absence of advertising practices.

dataSharedWith: Authorized third-party service providers for school purposes
r364.riskReason: GPB Learning Media has strong student-specific protections including a no-sale and no-targeted-advertising pledge, but the parent gpb.org privacy policy discloses third-party tracking pixels (Facebook) and web beacons on general audience pages, lacks a standalone Terms of Service, and does not specify a minimum age or explicit COPPA consent mechanism.
r364.parentSummary: GPB Learning Media (operated by Georgia Public Broadcasting) does not require student logins or collect student personal information for educational use, and explicitly commits to not selling student data or using it for targeted advertising. For teacher/subscriber accounts, the platform collects email addresses and school information, and uses cookies and third-party tracking pixels on general (non-educational) pages for marketing purposes. Parents and teachers can request deletion of any student data by emailing digital@gpb.org, and significant policy changes are communicated by email with 30 days notice.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states significant changes will be emailed with 30 days notice, but there is no publicly accessible revision history or version archive linked from the policy page.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists email, school information, browser data, and cookie data for registered users, and states no student data is collected for educational use, but non-personal data collection categories are described only broadly.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Data collection methods (registration form, browser, cookies) are mentioned but the description is general rather than a comprehensive itemized breakdown per data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Student Privacy Notice explicitly states that the user or student remains the owner and controller of all student data provided, meeting the ownership standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Teachers, parents, and guardians can request return, deletion, or destruction of all personally identifiable student data by emailing digital@gpb.org, constituting a full deletion mechanism.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not specify any data retention period for personal information collected from registered users; no retention schedule or timeframe is stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy specifically lists encryption, firewalls, and SSL/TLS (secure socket layer) as security measures protecting user information.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states encryption is implemented as a security measure, and SSL is named, indicating data is protected in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy mentions account passwords and urges users not to disclose them, but does not specify enforcement of strong password requirements or complexity rules.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in the available policy documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions session and persistent cookies and describes general uses, but does not provide a full enumerated list of all cookies with individual names and purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Vendors used for email services and Facebook (Meta) via pixel are named, but the full list of third-party service providers is not disclosed; only broad categories are referenced.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy notes vendors use personal information only as directed for their specific function, but does not itemize which specific data fields are shared with each named or unnamed third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can restrict third-party advertising cookies via browser settings and can opt out of Facebook pixel tracking, but a direct opt-out mechanism within the platform itself is not clearly described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states vendors use personal information only at the company's direction and in accordance with the Privacy Policy, which is a general contractual control statement but no formal DPA or supplier agreement is referenced.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy reserves the right to change without specifying a process to notify users when third-party partners change; there is no commitment to inform users of third-party roster changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy clarifies that web beacons and pixels are used only on general audience pages not intended for children or educational content, but ads may still appear on non-educational portions of the site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy uses remarketing pixels and web beacons to serve ads on third-party websites based on site visits, but states this is limited to general audience pages and not student-facing educational content.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Facebook pixel and web beacon tracking for ad purposes is disclosed on general pages; opt-out is possible via browser settings, but no simple in-platform opt-out mechanism is described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy discloses use of web beacons and pixels from Facebook for remarketing on general pages, but states these are not used on educational or children's content pages.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of third-party advertising cookies through browser settings, and the policy references Facebook's privacy policy for further opt-out, but there is no explicit, centralized platform-level opt-out workflow described.

dataSharedWith: Third-party service providers supporting business operations
r365.riskReason: GrabCAD explicitly states the service is not structured for children under 13, has no COPPA or FERPA compliance mechanisms, no parental consent process, engages third-party analytics trackers, uses persistent cookies for personalization, and retains data for marketing purposes beyond service delivery — making it unsuitable for K-12 deployment without significant additional safeguards.
r365.parentSummary: GrabCAD, operated by Stratasys, collects personal information including name, email, company details, usage data, and uploaded CAD files from users who create accounts. The platform explicitly states it is not designed for children under 13 and has no parental consent process, COPPA compliance mechanisms, or FERPA protections, making it a high-risk tool for K-12 school use. Data is shared with third-party analytics providers and may be retained for marketing purposes even after a user's relationship with the platform ends.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use state modifications are effective 10 days after posting on the site, but users are not proactively notified — they must check the site themselves, and no version history or changelog is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and 'Your Data on GrabCAD' support page together enumerate four specific data categories: personal data, user submitted data, application usage data, and printer usage data, providing a reasonably comprehensive list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy explains that data is collected directly from users at registration, passively via cookies and tracking technologies, and by third-party analytics providers on Stratasys's behalf.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: User-submitted CAD content and personal data ownership is partially addressed — the Terms state user submissions remain with the user, but the company asserts broad licensing rights over that content, and data uploaded to company Workbench accounts is classified as company-owned, not user-owned.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their account via Settings, and upon account deletion all personally identifiable data is removed from GrabCAD; content deletion is also available for Community submissions.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained as long as necessary to deliver services and for any 'rightful interest,' including post-contract marketing purposes, but does not specify a concrete retention period in days or years.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The security whitepaper references AWS infrastructure, ISO 27001 certification, and SAS-70 Type II audits, but the main privacy policy only offers a general statement that 'reasonable means' are used to protect data without listing specific measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Data is stored on AWS which supports encryption, and the security whitepaper references FIPS 140-2 and NIST 800-171 standards, but the privacy policy itself does not explicitly state that data is encrypted at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Use and privacy policy make no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement, and no SSO or passwordless login option is described.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is found in the Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, or support documentation for general community accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy describes session and persistent cookies and their general purposes (analytics, personalization, security), but does not provide a full named list of all cookies used or a dedicated cookie disclosure table.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references third parties such as 'data analytics providers' and hosting via AWS but does not name all specific third-party vendors that receive user data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups third-party data sharing broadly (analytics providers, legal compliance, business operations) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with which party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can exercise GDPR Right to Be Forgotten and request deletion from third-party tools, but no clear opt-out mechanism is provided for third-party data sharing short of account deletion.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The 'Your Data on GrabCAD' page states GrabCAD does not sell or trade data to third parties, and Right to Be Forgotten includes third-party deletion, implying some vendor accountability, but no explicit contractual obligation language is cited.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Neither the Terms of Use nor the Privacy Policy commit to notifying users when third-party data-sharing arrangements change; the terms reserve the right to modify the agreement with only 10 days' notice posted on the site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The platform is primarily a professional/engineering community and no explicit advertising program is described; however, cookies are used for personalization and analytics in ways that could support ad-adjacent targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No confirmed user-targeted advertising is disclosed, but persistent cookies and third-party analytics providers collect behavioral usage data that could be used for targeted purposes, and this is not explicitly ruled out.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party analytics providers are acknowledged as collecting data on Stratasys's behalf, including via tracking technology, but the policy does not clearly define opt-out controls for this third-party tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Persistent cookies and third-party tracking technologies are described in the privacy policy for analytics and personalization, but the specific tracking methods and any advertising beacons are not fully enumerated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can block cookies via browser settings and invoke GDPR rights including Right to Be Forgotten, but there is no dedicated, clearly labeled opt-out process specifically for data sharing with advertisers or analytics partners.

r366.minAge: Under 13 with parental consent (via Education Client)
dataSharedWith: Third-party gradebook/school record services (when designated by user)
r366.riskReason: GradeCam explicitly states it does not sell or rent user data, does not target advertising at users or students, claims COPPA and FERPA compliance, affirms user ownership of data, and uses TLS encryption in transit; residual concerns include vague data retention timelines and limited specificity on named third-party service providers.
r366.parentSummary: GradeCam collects limited personal information such as student names and assessment results on behalf of schools acting as Education Clients, using it solely to provide its grading service. The platform states it does not sell, rent, or use student data for advertising, and commits to deleting student data upon request from the school. Parents or guardians of students under 13 should know that consent is managed through the school, not collected directly from families.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service state GradeCam may modify terms at any time and a revised version is effective upon posting, but there is no stated advance notification process or revision history log for users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy Policy lists several data types (IP address, browser info, cookies, device identifiers, uploaded content, student data) but uses broad language like 'any personal information you provide' without an exhaustive enumerated list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes that data is collected via the Services, browser activity, and cookies, but does not provide a fully specific breakdown of each collection method tied to each data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service explicitly state that the user 'possesses and retains all right, title, and interest' in their data and that GradeCam acts solely as the user's agent.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The Privacy Policy states GradeCam will delete personal information if the Education Client requests it, and parents/guardians may contact GradeCam to review or correct student data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The Terms of Service note that GradeCam may retain data until erased per user request but does not specify a concrete retention period or schedule, making this vague.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Gradient security page describes a multi-faceted approach covering physical, network, web, system, application, and data security layers, but does not enumerate specific technical controls (e.g., certifications, audit standards).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The security page states all data transmitted between users and servers is encrypted using current TLS protocols, and session cookies store only encrypted authentication information.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service require users to keep passwords secure and notify GradeCam of breaches, and an account is required, but there is no stated enforcement of strong password rules (e.g., complexity requirements).
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy, and accounts require only a username and password.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Privacy Policy describes session and persistent cookies and their general purposes but does not provide a complete list of all cookies used with individual names, types, and purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy references 'authorized service providers' and the Terms reference third-party gradebook services, but no specific third-party vendors are named by company name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states data may be shared with authorized service providers and user-designated gradebook services but does not enumerate which specific data fields are shared with which category of third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The Privacy Policy states GradeCam does not share personal information unless it informs users and gives an opportunity to opt out, but the opt-out process is not clearly described or procedurally defined.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Terms of Service describe GradeCam sharing data with third parties only when the user designates it and in accordance with applicable law, implying some contractual oversight, but no explicit vendor agreement or DPA requirement is articulated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no stated process by which users would be notified if GradeCam adds new third-party service providers or changes existing ones.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Privacy Policy explicitly states GradeCam does not target advertising at users or students, indicating no ads are displayed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The Privacy Policy clearly states GradeCam does not target advertising at users or students, confirming no targeted advertising takes place.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: GradeCam states it does not sell or lease user data to third parties and does not conduct targeted advertising, indicating no third-party ad tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While GradeCam does not use tracking for ads, session cookies and device identifiers are collected for functional purposes; the policy does not fully distinguish all tracking methods in a dedicated cookie/tracking disclosure.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because GradeCam explicitly states it does not engage in advertising or sell data, there is no advertising data sharing from which users would need to opt out.

r367.riskReason: Gradescope explicitly claims FERPA compliance, SOC2 certification, and no on-site ads, but shares data with Turnitin affiliates and uses third-party advertising cookies for off-site retargeting, and the policy lacks a specific cookie list, a stated data retention period in days, and advance notification procedures for policy changes.
r367.parentSummary: Gradescope (owned by Turnitin) collects student names, email addresses, assignment submissions, and grades to support classroom grading workflows; it claims FERPA compliance and SOC2-certified encryption, and states it does not sell student data or display ads on its platform. However, student data is shared with Turnitin affiliate companies, and a third-party advertising partner may use cookies from Gradescope activity to serve targeted ads on other websites, which is a notable concern for K-12 deployments. Schools bear responsibility for obtaining parental consent for students under 13 before enrolling them in the service.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The TOS states Turnitin reserves the right to make modifications and will provide notice, but no advance notification timeline or revision history archive is clearly documented in the publicly available policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, log data, usage data, student submissions) but does not provide an exhaustive, itemized list in one consolidated location.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically describes how data is collected — directly from users at account creation, from teachers uploading rosters, automatically via log files, and through cookies — satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The TOS explicitly states 'We claim no ownership rights over User Content created by you' and students retain copyright over submitted work, clearly establishing user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Gradescope states it will delete student records upon request and the privacy policy affirms users' rights to modify, update, or delete their data, constituting full deletion support.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy states data is retained 'only as long as necessary to deliver services' and until a deletion request is made, which is a general statement rather than a specific retention period in days or years.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy specifically references SOC2-certified data centers, strong encryption, and compliance with US, EU, and Switzerland security standards as concrete security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states data is secured with 'strong encryption' in SOC2-certified data centers, meeting the encryption requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Neither the TOS nor the privacy policy mentions password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords; LTI/SSO integration is available but not described as the default or required authentication path.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: LTI/SSO integration is supported (noted in institutional use), which provides MFA capability, but native MFA is not explicitly mentioned as available or enforced for direct accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies and their general purposes (analytics, tracking site movements, demographic data) and that a third-party partner uses cookies for off-site advertising, but does not provide a detailed list of individual cookies by name and purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references third-party service providers and an advertising partner but does not name specific companies (beyond the Turnitin affiliate family); specific vendor names are not disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing broadly by category of recipient (service providers, advertising partner, affiliates) without specifying exactly which data elements are shared with each third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The privacy policy mentions users can control cookies via browser settings and references opt-out for Flash LSOs, but does not provide a clear, easy opt-out mechanism specifically for third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The TOS and privacy policy explicitly state that third-party service providers must handle and secure data 'with the same high level of protection' under contractual agreement, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy and TOS do not contain explicit provisions stating that users will be notified when Turnitin changes its third-party vendors or data-sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Gradescope states it does not serve ads on its own site, but it does partner with a third party to manage advertising on other sites using data from user activity on Gradescope, making this only a partial meet.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy acknowledges a third-party advertising partner may use cookies from Gradescope site activity to provide interest-based advertising on other websites, constituting possible third-party targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Users can limit cookie-based tracking via browser settings, but no dedicated opt-out link or mechanism for the advertising partner's cross-site tracking is explicitly provided in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy acknowledges that Turnitin and its partners use cookies and similar technologies to track users' movements and that social media widgets may set cookies, but a complete breakdown of tracking methods is not provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process for opting out of data sharing with the third-party advertising partner is described; only generic browser-level cookie controls are referenced.

dataCollected: Parent and school administrator contact information

r368.riskReason: Gradient Learning explicitly prohibits selling student data, limits use to educational purposes only, claims FERPA and voluntary COPPA compliance, requires service providers to follow strict privacy terms, and explicitly prohibits behaviorally-targeted advertising within its platform.
r368.parentSummary: Gradient Learning collects student names, grade levels, school IDs, usage data, and device information to operate its Whole Student System learning platform, and explicitly states this data is used solely for educational purposes with no advertising. The platform is operated as a nonprofit and affirms that students, parents, and schools own and control their own data, and that student personal information is never sold. Service providers such as CZI and Instructure Canvas have access to data under strict contractual privacy and security terms, and the policy provides 30-day advance notice for material policy changes.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy explicitly commits to at least 30 days advance notice for material changes, specifies which sections are modified, and allows users to request prior versions by contacting privacy@gradientlearning.org.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy provides a detailed enumerated list of data types collected including student names, grade levels, school IDs, device/network info, cookies, pixel tags, and user-submitted content.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly states data is collected in three ways: directly from users, from web server logs, and through cookies and pixel tags, with specific examples provided for each category.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy explicitly states that school staff, parents/guardians, teachers, and students own and control their personal information, and that Gradient Learning does not own student personal information.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: School officials can request deletion and authorized users have deletion rights, but the policy notes school administrators may retain access for a limited time even after a student or teacher requests deletion, indicating a constrained deletion process.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is kept only as long as necessary to provide services and references legal or school-directed retention requirements, but does not specify any concrete retention timeframe (e.g., number of days or years).
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy describes a general commitment to privacy by design and requires service providers to implement reasonable security practices, but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as encryption standards, penetration testing, or SOC certifications.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is not explicitly described in Gradient Learning's own policy text, though the platform is built on Instructure Canvas which independently confirms all data in transit and at rest are encrypted; the Gradient policy itself does not state this directly.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not mention password strength requirements or enforcement; access is mediated through school agreements and the Canvas LMS platform, which may handle authentication, but no explicit password policy is stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No explicit mention of multi-factor authentication is made in the policy; the platform relies on school-administered Canvas accounts, and SSO/LTI integration is possible through Canvas but not confirmed as required.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges use of cookies, pixel tags, and local storage, and references a separate Cookie Policy and the Instructure Canvas Cookie Notice, but does not enumerate all cookie names, types, or purposes directly within the main privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names CZI and Instructure Canvas as specific partners and broadly references service providers for document management, data hosting, and customer service, but does not provide a comprehensive named list of all third-party service providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by recipient category (school officials, legal guardians, service providers) but does not specify which exact data fields are shared with each named third party such as CZI or Canvas.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No explicit opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described for individual users; schools sign agreements governing data use, but individual parents or students are not given a clear self-service opt-out process.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy explicitly requires all service providers to comply with strict privacy and security terms and prohibits them from selling student personal information or using it for targeted advertising, demonstrating contractual accountability.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy commits to notifying users of material changes to the privacy policy with 30 days notice, but does not specifically commit to notifying users when third-party service providers are added or changed, only noting that a service provider list 'may be updated from time to time.'
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states that Gradient Learning does not place ads in its System or Platform, including no behaviorally-targeted advertising, making this a clear meets.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states personal information is not used for ad purposes including behaviorally-targeted advertising, and service providers are contractually prohibited from using data for targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy prohibits third-party tracking for advertising purposes and service providers are contractually barred from using student data for advertising; no third-party ad tracking is indicated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While the policy prohibits advertising uses of tracking technologies, it does acknowledge use of pixel tags and similar technologies for service functionality, and defers cookie detail to a separate Cookie Policy and Canvas Cookie Notice rather than fully enumerating all tracking methods in-line.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The policy clearly states data will not be used for advertising or sold for marketing purposes, and users and schools can contact Gradient Learning to exercise data rights; no advertiser data sharing is present to opt out of.
