r409.riskReason: JSTOR is a reputable nonprofit academic platform with strong security controls (SOC 2), but its use of third-party advertising cookies, social media tracking widgets, and the absence of explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance statements make it a moderate risk for K-12 deployment, especially for students under 16.
r409.parentSummary: JSTOR, operated by ITHAKA, collects personal information such as name, email, institutional affiliation, and usage data when users create accounts; anonymous browsing is possible without an account. The platform states it does not sell user data and has SOC 2-certified security measures, but it does allow third-party advertisers and social media widgets to set cookies and potentially track browsing activity. JSTOR's minimum age is 16, which means it is not designed for younger K-12 students, and it lacks explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance commitments in its public policies.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use state that ITHAKA reserves the right to modify policies, with updated versions posted online, but there is no explicit advance notification or revision history mechanism described for end users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The ITHAKA Privacy Policy provides a reasonably detailed enumeration of data collected across different use cases including account creation, JPASS purchases, institutional authentication, and AI tool usage.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The Privacy Policy specifically describes how data is collected — directly from users, through institutional access, via third-party tools, cookies, and social media widgets — with adequate specificity.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly address user data ownership; ITHAKA controls how data is used and retained, but there is no clear statement affirming that users own their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion by contacting privacy@ithaka.org, but residual copies may persist in backup systems for an unspecified period after deletion, making this only a partial fulfillment.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained as long as an account is active or as legally necessary, and references data retention policies, but does not specify concrete retention periods in days or years.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: ITHAKA explicitly states it has implemented physical, technical, and administrative safeguards and is SOC 2 compliant with annual third-party security audits.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy and platform use HTTPS and reference SOC 2 compliance, but do not explicitly describe end-to-end encryption practices for data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms and Privacy Policy make no mention of enforcing or recommending strong passwords for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI support is made in the publicly available Terms or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: ITHAKA maintains a separate Cookie Policy at ithaka.org/cookies and mentions cookie categories, but does not provide a comprehensive per-cookie list with purposes; a Cookie Settings panel is referenced for managing preferences.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy references 'service providers' and mentions OpenAI and social media platforms (Facebook, Twitter) broadly, but does not provide a full named list of all third-party data recipients.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by use case (e.g., credit card processing, social media widgets, AI tool) rather than specifying precisely which data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of personal data use by contacting privacy@ithaka.org, and third-party ad opt-outs are referenced via aboutads.info, but the process is not streamlined or clearly prominent for K-12 contexts.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Privacy Policy states that service providers 'may not use personal information except for the purpose of providing these services,' indicating contractual data use restrictions on third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Privacy Policy does not describe a process for notifying users when new third-party data-sharing relationships are established or existing ones change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: JSTOR does not display ads to logged-in users as a primary feature, but third-party advertisers may use cookies on the site, especially via social media widgets, placing this in a partial category.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The Privacy Policy acknowledges that third-party advertisers may use cookies or similar technologies to deliver advertising based on browsing activities, indicating potential third-party targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: ITHAKA states it does not control third-party advertiser cookies but directs users to opt-out resources (aboutads.info and youronlinechoices.com), providing limited but available opt-out pathways.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Social media widgets (Facebook Like, ShareThis) are acknowledged to collect IP addresses and set cookies, but the full scope of web beacon or pixel-based tracking is not comprehensively disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out is available by contacting privacy@ithaka.org or using browser-level cookie controls and linked third-party opt-out tools, but the process is indirect and not clearly labeled as an advertising data opt-out.

dataCollected: Email address (parent/guardian email for children under 13)
Device information (device model, OS, device identifiers such as IDFA and UDID)
IP address (used for approximate location only)
Usage and engagement data (log data, feature engagement)
Google account name and email (if Google Login or Google Classroom integration is used)
dataSharedWith: Google (via Google Analytics and Google Classroom integration)
r410.riskReason: JuiceMind explicitly prohibits behaviorally targeted advertising, does not sell student data, expressly claims COPPA and GDPR compliance, assists schools with FERPA obligations, limits data collection for children under 13 to a parent/guardian email, offers account-free participation, and encrypts data in transit with signed Student Data Privacy Agreements (DPAs) on record.
r410.parentSummary: JuiceMind collects minimal personal data — primarily account details such as name and email for teachers, and only a parent or guardian's email for children under 13 — along with standard technical data like device info and IP address used for service delivery. The platform explicitly prohibits behaviorally targeted advertising, does not sell student data, and provides parents the ability to review, modify, or delete their child's information by contacting info@juicemind.com. JuiceMind states compliance with COPPA and GDPR, assists schools in meeting FERPA obligations, and uses encryption in transit and access-controlled data centers to protect user data.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy and terms of service both state that all JuiceMind users will be notified of any modifications made to the Terms and Conditions on the platform, satisfying the advance notification requirement, though no formal revision history or changelog is referenced.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates specific categories of data collected including account details, device identifiers (IDFA, UDID), IP address, browser type, language, time zone, referrer, log/usage data, and data received from Google integrations, representing a reasonably complete disclosure.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly explains how data is collected — directly from users on registration, automatically through log and device data, via cookies, and from third-party integrations such as Google Login and Google Classroom — providing sufficient specificity about collection mechanisms.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; while it affirms that data is not sold and access is limited, ownership language is absent, leaving data ownership ambiguous between the user and JuiceMind.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their account or update their information at any time by contacting info@juicemind.com, and parents can specifically request deletion of their child's data, satisfying the full deletion requirement via a contact-based process.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is not kept longer than necessary to provide services, but does not specify a concrete retention period (e.g., 90 days or a defined timeframe), making the retention statement general rather than specific.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy mentions access-controlled data centers and encryption of data in transit and password data at rest, but does not enumerate a comprehensive list of specific security measures such as firewalls, penetration testing, or SOC certifications, constituting a general rather than fully specific disclosure.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy states encryption of all data in transit and encryption of user password data both in transit and at rest, but does not confirm full encryption of all stored data at rest beyond passwords, leaving a partial encryption picture.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that strong passwords are enforced at the technical level; it supports Google SSO login which provides a degree of credential security, but no direct statement about password strength requirements is made.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: JuiceMind supports Google Login/SSO which can provide MFA if configured on the Google account side, but the platform itself does not explicitly offer or require MFA, making this only a partial meet.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges the use of cookies for identifying visitors and mentions Google Analytics cookies, and advises users to adjust browser settings to refuse cookies, but does not provide a full itemized cookie list with purposes for each cookie type.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Google Analytics as a specific third-party tool used, and references employees, contractors, and affiliated organizations, but does not provide a comprehensive named list of all third-party subprocessors or integrated service vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Google Analytics is identified as receiving usage/engagement data, and Google is identified as a source of name and email via integrations, but a full breakdown of exactly which data fields are shared with each named or unnamed third party is not provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy states JuiceMind does not share personal information with anyone except to comply with law, provide services, or protect rights, and explicitly does not sell or rent data; parents can also opt out of further data collection for children by contacting the company, effectively meeting the opt-out standard.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy references that data is shared with employees, contractors, and affiliated organizations but does not include explicit contractual language requiring all third parties (e.g., Google Analytics) to adhere to JuiceMind's privacy standards or a vendor agreement framework, though the signed DPAs with schools provide some downstream assurance.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states users will be notified of modifications to the Terms and Conditions but does not specifically address whether users will be notified if new third-party data processors are added or existing ones change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states that behaviorally targeted advertising is not permitted on JuiceMind, clearly meeting the no-ads standard for a K-12 educational platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy expressly prohibits behaviorally targeted advertising, and there is no indication of any third-party ad targeting using student data, fully meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party tracking for advertising purposes is disclosed; Google Analytics is used only for aggregate usage reporting without individual identification, and targeted ad tracking is explicitly prohibited.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies are described as used only for functional purposes (identifying repeat visitors, testing features) and analytics (Google Analytics without identifying individuals), with no web beacons or ad-tracking pixels disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since JuiceMind explicitly prohibits behaviorally targeted advertising and states it does not share data with advertisers, there is no advertiser data-sharing from which users need to opt out, fully satisfying this requirement.

dataCollected: Automated usage data via service providers
r411.riskReason: The platform is operated by Infobase under a library/school subscription model with stated COPPA and FERPA commitments and no ads, but the platform's own domain (justforkidsstreamingcollection.com) has no independently published TOS or Privacy Policy, relies on Infobase's corporate-level policies which are partially outdated (last updated May 2018 in some versions), uses YouTube API services subject to Google's privacy policy outside Infobase's control, and places parental consent obligations on the subscribing institution rather than the platform itself.
r411.parentSummary: Just for Kids Streaming Collection is a kid-safe, advertisement-free streaming platform operated by Infobase and accessed through library or school subscriptions; it does not sell student data and states COPPA and FERPA compliance. Data collected includes usage data, account identifiers, and information voluntarily provided, stored in encrypted environments in the United States; parents may request review or deletion of their child's data. However, the platform uses YouTube API services governed by Google's separate privacy policy, places the burden of parental consent on the subscribing institution rather than the platform, and the specific domain (justforkidsstreamingcollection.com) does not host its own standalone TOS or Privacy Policy, which limits direct transparency for families.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Infobase's corporate privacy policy states material changes will be communicated prominently and via email to registered users, but the specific justforkidsstreamingcollection.com domain hosts no independent policy with a versioned change history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Infobase policy describes categories of data collected (voluntarily submitted info, automated usage data, account data) but does not enumerate a comprehensive, exhaustive list of every specific data type collected through this platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected via voluntary submission, automated means, and third-party service providers, but lacks granular detail on exactly how each data type is collected within the Just for Kids platform specifically.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Users retain ownership of their own data; Infobase explicitly states education records belong to the educational institution and limits its own use of such records to legitimate educational purposes only.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents are explicitly granted the right to review, direct deletion of, and refuse further collection of their child's personal information, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not specify a concrete data retention period in days or months; it references general compliance with legal obligations but does not state a specific timeframe for retaining or deleting user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy describes specific security measures including access controls, encrypted storage environments, internal security audits, SSL encryption, and continuous network monitoring.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: SSL/TLS encryption is explicitly stated for data in transit, and encrypted server environments are stated for data at rest, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Passwords are used to protect personal information and users can change them, but the policy does not specify enforcement of strong password standards such as minimum length or complexity requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform supports LTI 1.1 integration (as noted in the EduAppCenter listing), which enables SSO-based authentication through the subscribing institution, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions use of third-party services (including YouTube API/Google) that may set cookies, but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies used, their names, and their specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references affiliated Infobase companies, service providers, and YouTube/Google API services but does not name all specific third-party vendors by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy provides general statements about data sharing with service providers and affiliated companies but does not specify exactly which data elements are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users may opt out of sharing personal contact information with third parties by contacting Infobase directly, but the process is limited to written requests rather than a simple self-service opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that service providers process data on behalf of Infobase under its instructions and in compliance with the privacy policy, and FERPA obligations are explicitly acknowledged for educational partners.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes will be posted, but does not specifically commit to proactively notifying users of changes to which third-party service providers have access to their data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The platform is explicitly described as advertisement-free by Infobase and partner libraries, meeting this requirement fully.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is used; the platform is ad-free and Infobase does not describe any behavioral or interest-based ad targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is present on the platform itself; however, YouTube API services embedded on Infobase's broader website are subject to Google's data practices.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The use of YouTube API services means Google's tracking technologies may apply to some embedded content areas, creating partial uncertainty about tracking methods even though the platform itself does not serve ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since the platform is ad-free and Infobase states student data is not shared for advertising, no opt-out process is needed and this requirement is effectively met.

dataSharedWith: Cloud infrastructure providers (AWS, Google Cloud Platform)
Third-party AI LLM providers (for AI features)
r412.riskReason: Kami holds a Common Sense Privacy Verified Seal, explicitly prohibits advertising and sale of student data, is COPPA/FERPA/SOPIPA compliant, and uses encryption in transit and at rest — though specific third-party cloud and AI LLM vendors are only broadly named rather than fully enumerated with per-party data disclosures.
r412.parentSummary: Kami collects limited personal information such as email addresses and usage/engagement data solely to provide its educational document annotation service, and explicitly states it does not display ads, sell student data, or share data for marketing purposes. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest using AWS and Google Cloud Platform, and parents or schools can request full deletion of a child's data by emailing privacy@kamiapp.com. Kami is certified as COPPA, FERPA, and SOPIPA compliant and has earned a Common Sense Privacy Verified Seal, making it a strong choice for K-12 classroom use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states Kami will contact schools/districts by email before making material changes to data practices for children, but no publicly accessible revision history or changelog is provided on the policy page.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates specific categories of data collected including email, password, IP address, browser type, ISP, referring/exit pages, date/time stamps, clickstream data, and in-app engagement data such as annotations and comments.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly explains data is collected via account registration, automatic log collection, cookies/beacons/tags, and through in-app activity such as document annotations and usage interactions.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The API Terms explicitly state 'end-user data collected through your Apps is owned by the end-user,' and the general TOS indicates user files and content remain the user's property, with Kami acting as a data processor.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request full deletion of all personal data by emailing privacy@kamiapp.com, and the policy explicitly states all data will be completely removed upon such a request.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as necessary to comply with legal obligations but does not specify a concrete retention period in days or months, making the retention window vague.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy lists specific security measures including TLS encryption in transit, encryption at rest on AWS and GCP, firewall segregation between application tiers, and strict access controls, and references a published Security and Data Protection Measures document.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Kami explicitly states all data is encrypted in transit using TLS and encrypted at rest on AWS and Google Cloud Platform servers.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Account creation requires an email and password or SSO via Google or Microsoft accounts, and SSO/LTI integration is supported for institutional deployments, satisfying strong authentication requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Kami supports SSO via Google and Microsoft accounts and LTI integrations with LMS platforms, which provide institutional-grade authentication in lieu of standalone MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Kami has a dedicated, published Cookies Policy at kamiapp.com/cookies-policy that explains first-party and third-party cookie types, their purposes, and how to manage cookie settings.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy broadly names AWS and Google Cloud Platform as cloud hosting providers and references third-party AI LLM providers for AI features, but does not provide a comprehensive named list of all third-party service vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing with cloud providers and AI LLM vendors generally without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Kami explicitly states it does not sell or share data for advertising purposes and users can request full data deletion via email, and no third-party advertising opt-out mechanism is needed given no such sharing occurs.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states Kami only uses third-party services that have made the same privacy commitment, and the TOS references contractual agreements including GDPR Standard Contractual Clauses with cloud providers, placing contractual limits on third-party data use.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy commits to emailing schools/districts before material changes to data practices involving children's data, but does not explicitly state users will be proactively notified of changes to the roster of third-party service providers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Kami explicitly states 'we do not display advertising on our App or on our Website,' confirming a fully ad-free experience for all users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states Kami does not use user data to advertise or market to users, and does not create data profiles for personalized advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Kami explicitly states it does not host third-party cookies or trackers that would allow third parties to track users on the site for advertising or marketing purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Kami acknowledges using cookies, beacons, tags, and scripts for site analytics and usage trend tracking, which while not used for advertising introduces some non-functional tracking that goes beyond purely operational cookies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since Kami does not engage in data sharing with advertisers or display ads, no opt-out mechanism is necessary, and users are clearly informed of this policy in the privacy policy and student privacy pledge.

dataSharedWith: Google LLC (hosting, cloud infrastructure, Google Analytics)
Business successors (in case of acquisition or transfer)
r413.riskReason: Kanbanchi explicitly prohibits use by anyone under 16, does not claim COPPA or FERPA compliance, and allows advertising partners to set third-party targeting cookies that build behavioral profiles, making it unsuitable for K-12 deployment without significant contractual safeguards.
r413.parentSummary: Kanbanchi collects personal data including name, email, Google account info, and usage analytics, and shares it with third parties such as Google, HubSpot, Braintree, and unnamed advertising partners who may use cookies to build behavioral profiles. The platform explicitly states it is not intended for anyone under 16, which disqualifies it for most K-12 student use without additional safeguards. No COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance is claimed, and policy changes may take effect simply by continued use of the site without advance notice to users.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states changes will be posted on the site and users are deemed to have accepted them on first use after alterations, with no advance notification or version history provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy references categories of personal data collected (name, email, usage data, Google account data) but does not provide an exhaustive enumerated list of every data field collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy provides a general statement that data is collected through use of the site and Google authentication, but does not specifically enumerate all collection methods (e.g., forms, cookies, third-party SDKs) in a single clear section.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms & Conditions grant Kanbanchi a broad non-exclusive license to copy, store, distribute, and adapt customer data, making ownership ambiguous rather than clearly affirming user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states users may withdraw consent and request deletion at any time, and account deletion can be performed via the site or by contacting support.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as necessary and until account deletion, but does not specify a concrete retention period in days or months, making this vague rather than specific.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The security page lists specific measures including TLS encryption in transit, encryption at rest, weekly vulnerability scans, annual penetration tests, Google Cloud Monitoring, and employee security training.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Kanbanchi explicitly states all web application communications are encrypted with TLS and all data is encrypted at rest on Google Cloud infrastructure.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Authentication is managed entirely by Google SSO (Google or Microsoft sign-in), meaning Kanbanchi does not store passwords and Google enforces its own strong password and security policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Sign-in is handled via Google or Microsoft SSO, which inherently supports MFA through those identity providers, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A separate cookie policy exists and categorizes cookies (functional, performance, targeting), but the policy admits advertising partner cookies are used for behavioral profiling, which is a concern for K-12 contexts.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy names specific third parties including Google LLC, HubSpot Inc., and Braintree by name, but advertising partners are not individually named.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with named processors (Google, HubSpot, Braintree) is described at a general level, but what specific data fields are shared with each party is not itemized.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of Google Analytics and withdraw consent to analytics cookies via cookie settings, but opting out of all advertising partner tracking is not clearly described with a single easy process.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Google is identified as a subcontractor and data processor subject to Google's data processing terms, but equivalent contractual accountability for advertising partners and other third parties is not explicitly stated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy states changes will be posted on the site with no prior notice, meaning users will not be specifically notified of changes to third-party data sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The cookie policy and Terms & Conditions confirm that advertising partner cookies may be used to show users relevant adverts on other sites, confirming targeted advertising is present.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Advertising partner cookies are explicitly described as being used to build a profile of user interests and show relevant adverts on other sites, confirming third-party behavioral targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Users can opt out of analytics cookies via cookie settings and opt out of Google Analytics globally, but no clear opt-out mechanism for all advertising partner tracking cookies is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The platform uses third-party advertising partner cookies that uniquely identify browsers and devices for ad targeting, which constitutes tracking for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Cookie settings allow withdrawal of consent to analytics, and Google Analytics opt-out is mentioned, but a comprehensive, clear opt-out from all advertiser data sharing is not explicitly documented in one place.

r414.riskReason: KC7 explicitly claims COPPA compliance and offers parental deletion rights, but the privacy policy does not specifically name third-party vendors, lacks explicit encryption disclosures, does not respond to DNT signals, and FERPA compliance is not directly addressed despite the platform being used by K-12 schools.
r414.parentSummary: KC7 (kc7cyber.com) collects account registration information such as name, email, and username, as well as usage/game progress data and cookies when your child uses the platform. KC7 states it does not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13, and parents of children under 13 may request to review, stop use of, or delete their child's information by contacting privacy@kc7cyber.com. While the platform does not appear to sell student data, it discloses use of cookies and web beacons, and does not name specific third-party vendors it may share data with, which is worth monitoring.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy references notifying users of changes via a revised version of the notice, but there is no clear advance notification process or revision history log described.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists general categories such as account info, usage data, cookies, and device data, but does not enumerate a comprehensive, specific list of all data fields collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected when users register, participate in activities, or contact KC7, but does not detail every specific collection mechanism (e.g., exact analytics tools used).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service state all rights and interest in the game content are owned by KC7 Foundation, but the privacy policy does not explicitly clarify that users own their personal data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users and parents may request deletion of personal information via the contact page or by emailing privacy@kc7cyber.com, and parents of under-13 children are explicitly granted this right.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is kept only as long as necessary for stated purposes and deleted or anonymized when no longer needed, but no specific retention timeframe (e.g., number of days/years) is given.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states 'appropriate and reasonable technical and organizational security measures' are implemented, but does not list specific controls such as encryption standards, firewalls, or access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (at-rest or in-transit) is made in the privacy policy or terms of service despite the platform handling student data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service state users must maintain confidentiality of account information, but there is no mention of strong password requirements or enforcement mechanisms.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is found in the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and web beacons/pixels and links to a cookie notice section, but does not enumerate individual cookies by name or provide a detailed breakdown of purpose for each.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy refers to third-party service providers in general terms but does not name any specific vendors or partners.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No specific data types shared with each individual third party are disclosed; the policy groups sharing broadly under 'service providers' without detail.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can contact KC7 to exercise privacy rights, but there is no clear, easy opt-out mechanism specifically for third-party data sharing described in the policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states KC7 'makes efforts to ensure that third-party service providers also comply with COPPA requirements,' indicating some vendor accountability, but no formal agreement details are described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy notes it may be revised but does not describe a process for notifying users specifically when third-party sharing relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The platform is a nonprofit educational game with no indication of advertising being displayed to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is mentioned or indicated anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy states KC7 does not currently respond to Do-Not-Track signals, which partially limits opt-out capability, though no advertising-specific tracking is disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy discloses use of cookies, web beacons, and pixels for general service purposes, but does not clarify whether any of these are used for advertising or tracking across sites.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out mechanism for data sharing with advertisers is described, though this appears to be because no advertising relationship exists rather than an omission of a required disclosure.

dataSharedWith: Business partners and trusted affiliates (aggregated demographic data)
r415.riskReason: Key Hero serves a typing test platform commonly used by K-12 students but has no COPPA compliance statement, no minimum age requirement, no parental consent mechanism, and actively serves Google AdSense behavioral advertising (DART cookies) to all users including potential minors.
r415.parentSummary: Key Hero Typing Test (keyhero.com) collects names, email addresses, mailing addresses, and browser/device technical data from registered users, and uses Google AdSense with DART cookies to serve behavioral ads based on user browsing history. The platform does not require an account to use the basic typing test, but registered users' scores are tracked; critically, there is no stated minimum age, no COPPA compliance notice, and no parental consent process, making this platform potentially risky for use by children under 13 in a K-12 school setting.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states Key Hero will revise the updated date at the bottom of the page when changes are made, but there is no advance notification to users and no revision history available — only the most recent update date (May 20, 2022) is shown.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data types (name, email, mailing address, browser name, OS, ISP, cookies) but does not comprehensively enumerate all data collected such as typing performance metrics, IP addresses, or session data, leaving the disclosure incomplete.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy provides a general statement that data is collected when users visit, register, or engage with site activities, but does not specifically describe the technical mechanisms (e.g., forms, analytics scripts, ad trackers) used to collect each data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; it describes how data is used and shared but is silent on ownership, creating ambiguity about whether Key Hero claims rights over user-submitted content or performance data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy notes users can request account deletion by contacting Key Hero online or via email, and can remove some profile content themselves, but also states certain information may be retained for record-keeping or legal compliance, making deletion only partially available.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state any specific data retention period or even a general retention statement, leaving users with no information about how long their personal data is stored after account deletion or inactivity.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states that 'appropriate data collection, storage and processing practices and security measures' are adopted to protect against unauthorized access, but does not list any specific security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or audit procedures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy does not mention encryption of stored data or data in transit; while the site likely uses HTTPS, there is no explicit statement in the privacy policy confirming encryption is applied to user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy makes no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement; the login page uses third-party OAuth (Google) which may impose its own standards, but Key Hero's own policy is silent on this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) is made anywhere in the privacy policy or on the site's login page; OAuth login via Google is available but not required, and there is no MFA option disclosed.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions that the site may use cookies to enhance user experience and that users can disable them via browser settings, but does not list specific cookies by name, their purposes, or distinguish between functional and advertising cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Google (AdSense/DART) as a third-party advertiser and references 'business partners, trusted affiliates and advertisers' for aggregated data sharing, but does not name any other specific third-party vendors or analytics providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states that personal identification information is not sold or rented, but that aggregated demographic data may be shared with business partners and advertisers; it does not specify what data specifically is shared with Google or other named parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of Google's DART cookie by visiting Google's ad privacy page, as referenced in the policy, but there is no platform-level opt-out mechanism and no opt-out from sharing aggregated data with other business partners.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not include any statement requiring third-party recipients of data (including Google or business partners) to adhere to data protection agreements or Key Hero's privacy standards, leaving no vendor accountability framework in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states Key Hero may update it at any time at its own discretion, with users responsible for checking the page periodically; there is no commitment to notify users of changes involving third-party data-sharing practices specifically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly acknowledges that Google AdSense serves ads on the site, including behavioral ads via the DART cookie based on user visit history across the internet, which constitutes targeted third-party advertising displayed to all users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Google's DART cookie is confirmed in the policy to serve ads 'based on their visit to our Site and other sites on the Internet,' confirming cross-site behavioral targeting is active for all users, including students who may be minors.

r417.riskReason: Khan Academy is a nonprofit that explicitly does not sell student data, displays no third-party ads, encrypts data at rest and in transit, signs Data Protection Agreements with schools, and maintains documented COPPA and FERPA compliance practices.
r417.parentSummary: Khan Academy collects basic account information (name, email, date of birth, usage/learning activity) to operate its free educational service and personalize learning. The platform does not sell personal data, does not display third-party advertising, and encrypts data both at rest and in transit. For school accounts, student data is protected under FERPA and COPPA, with deletion controls available to schools or parents, making it one of the more privacy-protective EdTech platforms available.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Khan Academy posts an updated revision date and states it will notify users of material changes, but a full revision history or archived prior versions are not publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy exhaustively lists categories of personal data collected including account info, usage data, device data, location, cookies, and communications.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes three collection methods: directly from users, from third parties (parents, teachers, schools), and automatically via device/usage tracking and cookies.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Under school DPAs, the school district or student owns all right, title, and interest to student records; personal account data ownership is implied to remain with the user.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users with personal accounts can delete their accounts and associated personal information at any time through account settings; for school accounts, deletion is controlled by the school.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as needed for educational purposes and DPAs specify a 120-day disposal window upon request, but no specific general retention period (e.g., number of days/years) is stated in the main privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Khan Academy explicitly lists specific security measures including encryption at rest and in transit, TLS 1.3, AES256, SHA256 signatures, firewalls, employee training, vendor management, and an annual incident response plan exercise.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy confirms encryption of personal information both at rest (via Google Cloud Platform with an additional layer) and during transmission over the public Internet.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service mention passwords and account confidentiality, and DPAs reference strong password policies, but the main public-facing policy does not explicitly state that strong passwords are technically enforced on all account types.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Khan Academy supports SSO via Google Accounts, Clever, and ClassLink for school accounts, which satisfies the SSO/LTI standard; individual consumer accounts do not prominently advertise MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy references a Cookie Notice and states cookies, web beacons, and similar technologies are used, and users can opt out of certain third-party cookies, but a comprehensive list of all cookies with individual purposes is not prominently surfaced in the main policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy discloses broad categories of third parties (service providers, Khan Academy family companies, rostering services like Clever/ClassLink) but does not name every individual vendor or service provider.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by third-party category rather than specifying exactly what data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of non-essential third-party cookies and LEAs can opt out of data sharing with third-party researchers; no third-party advertising data sharing exists to opt out of.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: DPAs explicitly require Khan Academy to act as a school official under LEA supervision and bind vendors to data protection obligations; the main privacy policy also states service providers are contractually bound.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy states Khan Academy will notify users of material changes to the policy, but does not explicitly commit to notifying users specifically when third-party service providers change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Khan Academy explicitly states it does not display third-party advertisements on its service; sponsored content is labeled but no personal data is shared with sponsors.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Khan Academy confirms no targeted advertising is displayed to users on its platform, and no user data is used for ad targeting purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Khan Academy does not permit third parties to collect user information for targeted advertising purposes on its service, and states it does not engage in cross-site user tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Web beacons and cookies are used only for functional and analytics purposes to operate the service; no tracking for advertising purposes is confirmed by the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because Khan Academy does not share data with advertisers or display targeted ads, no opt-out of advertiser data sharing is needed; the policy is clear on this point.

r418.riskReason: Khan Academy Kids is a nonprofit platform that displays no ads, does not sell student data, self-attests COPPA and FERPA compliance, employs strong encryption and annual SOC 2 Type II audits, and minimizes child data collection to username, age, and learning activity only.
r418.parentSummary: Khan Academy Kids collects only a parent's email and the child's username, age, and learning activity data in order to operate and personalize the educational experience; it does not display any advertising, does not sell personal data, and does not share children's data with third parties for marketing purposes. The platform uses TLS 1.3 encryption in transit and AES-256 encryption at rest, undergoes annual SOC 2 Type II security audits, and self-attests compliance with COPPA and FERPA. Parents and schools retain control over student data deletion, though school-managed accounts require deletion requests to be submitted through the school or teacher.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states Khan Academy posts a revised policy with an updated revision date and makes best efforts to notify users of material changes, with revision history inferrable from the dated policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Kids privacy policy explicitly enumerates each category of data collected from parents and children, including email, username, age, IP address, approximate location, device info, and usage/learning data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically explains how data is collected — at account sign-up, through app usage, via email verification, from device telemetry, and through school rostering services.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Under the school DPA framework, the school district or student owns all right, title, and interest in student records; for home/parent accounts, data ownership leans toward the user per policy language and deletion rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents and users can request account deletion through account settings, but school-managed student accounts require deletion to be requested through the school or teacher, creating a dependency that limits direct parent deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy and deletion practices article state data is retained only as long as needed for service provision and mentions a two-year inactivity threshold, but does not specify exact retention periods for each data type in the Kids privacy policy itself.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Khan Academy's published security practices specifically list TLS 1.3, AES-256 encryption, Google Cloud Platform hosting, SOC 2 Type II annual audits, background checks, security training, least-privilege access controls, and a vulnerability disclosure program.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Khan Academy explicitly states it encrypts personal information both at rest (AES-256 on GCP with an additional encryption layer) and during transmission (TLS 1.3), constituting full encryption coverage.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service note users are responsible for password confidentiality but the Kids privacy policy does not explicitly state strong password enforcement requirements for parent accounts, only recommending confidentiality.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Khan Academy requires internal employees to use MFA to access Khan Academy resources, but the public-facing Kids app does not explicitly advertise MFA or SSO as available options for parents or teachers.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Khan Academy has a separate Cookie Notice page (khanacademy.org/about/cookie-policy), and DPA documents reference cookie and IP address collection, but the Kids-specific privacy policy does not enumerate individual cookies with full purposes inline.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references 'vendors and service providers' and 'Khan Academy family of companies' broadly; the DPA framework references a subprocessor list available on the website, but specific third-party names are not enumerated in the public Kids privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by category of recipient (vendors, affiliates, legal) rather than specifying exactly which data elements are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy explicitly states student data is not shared with third parties for their own purposes or marketing, and the DPA framework gives schools the ability to opt out of data sharing with third-party researchers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: DPA agreements explicitly require that Khan Academy employees, contractors, and third-party service providers protect student data in a manner no less stringent than the terms of the DPA, and Khan Academy undergoes SOC 2 audits to verify this.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states Khan Academy may update the subprocessor list from time to time, but does not commit to proactively notifying users of specific third-party changes before they occur.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Kids privacy policy unambiguously states no advertising is displayed on Khan Academy Kids, consistent with its nonprofit mission.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states no targeted advertising is displayed in the Kids app and that Khan Academy does not permit third parties to collect in-app data for targeted ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Khan Academy explicitly prohibits third-party tracking within the Kids app for advertising purposes, and states it does not track users across other websites or apps over time.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No ad-related web beacons or tracking methods are used within the Kids app; any tracking is limited to functional analytics for app improvement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no targeted advertising or third-party advertiser data sharing occurs within the Kids app, there is no advertiser opt-out needed; users are directed to NAI and DAA resources only for external interest-based ads about the app itself on other platforms.

r419.riskReason: Khanmigo is operated by a nonprofit with strong COPPA/FERPA self-attestation, no ads for students, no student data sold, LLMs prohibited from training on student data, and robust DPA frameworks for school deployments — though COPPA compliance is self-attested rather than third-party certified.
r419.parentSummary: Khanmigo (by Khan Academy) collects student usernames, learning activity, usage data, and AI chat transcripts to power personalized tutoring; children under 13 require parental or school consent to create an account. Khan Academy states it does not sell student data, does not allow AI partners like OpenAI to train models on student interactions, and provides parents full visibility into their child's Khanmigo chat history. Third-party cookies (including Google and historically Facebook Pixel) have been detected on the main site, though school accounts are covered by Data Protection Agreements asserting FERPA and COPPA compliance.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Khan Academy updates its privacy policy and terms, and the policy notes users will be notified of material changes, but a publicly accessible full revision history is not prominently maintained.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and DPA documentation comprehensively enumerate data types collected, including account info, usage data, IP address, location, chat content, and learning activity.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states data is collected directly from users, from schools/parents/teachers, from third-party applications, and automatically via cookies/web beacons.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: DPA agreements explicitly state that the school district and/or student owns all Student Records, with Khan Academy acting as a data processor — a strong ownership stance.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Schools can request deletion of student records upon termination, parents can delete child accounts, and account holders can request deletion, satisfying full deletion rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as needed for educational purposes and deleted upon school termination requests, but no specific numeric retention period (e.g., 90 days, 1 year) is stated in the public policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: DPA documentation lists specific security safeguards including encryption, firewalls, employee training, vendor management, strong password policies, incident response procedures, and NIST/OWASP-aligned development practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The DPA explicitly lists encryption as a security safeguard, and the platform uses HTTPS throughout; encryption at rest and in transit is referenced in security documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: DPA references strong password policies and protections as a named safeguard, and the platform supports SSO via Clever and ClassLink for school accounts, meeting this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Khan Academy supports SSO/LTI integrations through Clever and ClassLink for school district accounts, which provide federated identity and MFA capability at the institution level.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy references a Cookie Notice and mentions cookies, web beacons, and similar technologies, but the cookie policy provides general categories rather than a fully itemized list of each cookie and its specific purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references categories of third-party service providers (hosting, analytics, email, customer service) and OpenAI is known to process Khanmigo prompts, but a comprehensive named list of all third parties is not publicly available in the main policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Third-party data sharing is described in grouped categories (e.g., 'service providers' receive what they need to perform services) rather than specifying exactly which data elements are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of email communications easily, and some third-party cookie opt-outs are available, but a clear, unified opt-out mechanism for all third-party data sharing is not prominently described for general users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: DPA documentation explicitly states third-party service providers are required to enter written agreements committing to protect the security, privacy, and confidentiality of shared information.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may be updated over time, but does not clearly commit to proactively notifying users specifically when third-party sharing arrangements change.

complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Khan Academy states it does not use student data for targeted advertising, and no third-party ad targeting of student accounts is described or permitted under their stated policies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking technologies including Google cookies and a Facebook Pixel have been detected on the main khanacademy.org domain by independent researchers, though Khan Academy provides some opt-out capability for third-party cookies — this creates partial risk for non-school visitors.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy acknowledges use of cookies and web beacons, and third-party trackers (Google, Facebook Pixel) have been independently detected on the site, suggesting tracking beyond purely functional purposes on the public-facing site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of certain third-party cookies as described in the Cookie Notice, and email marketing has an unsubscribe option, but the opt-out process for all advertiser-related data sharing is not presented in a single clear location.

r420.riskReason: Kialo Edu is a nonprofit, ad-free, FERPA/COPPA-compliant platform that minimizes data collection, does not sell or share data for advertising, uses encryption at rest and in transit, and offers school-managed accounts with full deletion rights.

complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request full account deletion via their educational institution or by emailing support, and educational institution admins have dashboard access to export, modify, or delete all user data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: IP addresses are retained for 30 days, but a general retention period for other personal account data is described only as 'no longer than required or authorized' without a specific duration stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Data Security and Privacy Plan details specific security measures including encryption at rest and in transit, Zero Trust Security model, ISO certification, and breach notification within 3 days.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy and Common Sense Privacy evaluation confirm data is encrypted both in transit and at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Kialo Edu supports SSO via Google, Microsoft, and Clever, which offloads password management to enterprise identity providers with strong password enforcement.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: SSO and LTI integrations are available through Google, Microsoft, and Clever, providing institutional-grade authentication that satisfies the MFA/SSO criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy explicitly lists only strictly necessary cookies (login session management) and local storage for UI state, with no ad-tracking cookies or third-party tracking pixels used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Data Security and Privacy Plan specifically names Amazon AWS as a subcontractor that could access PII, and states an up-to-date list of subcontractors is maintained and available upon request.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Subcontractors are named (e.g., Amazon AWS) but the specific data elements shared with each subcontractor are not individually enumerated in the public policy documents.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy states no data is shared with advertisers or marketers, and in the event of a merger/sale, users are notified and given the opportunity to opt out of data transfer before it occurs.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that subcontractors must sign 'rigorous confidentiality and data protection agreements consistent with this Policy' before receiving any user data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy reserves the right to change subcontractors and commits to maintaining an updated list, but does not guarantee proactive user notification of each individual subcontractor change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy and platform documentation explicitly state that Kialo Edu is completely ad-free with no advertising displayed to any users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy states data is not used for behavioral ad targeting and no advertising exists on the platform, confirming no targeted advertising of any kind.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The privacy policy states Kialo Edu does not use any third-party tracking services, and no ad-tracking cookies or tracking pixels are deployed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Only strictly necessary functional cookies and local storage are used; no web beacons, tracking pixels, or ad-related tracking technologies are employed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because there is no advertising or data sharing with advertisers, no opt-out mechanism is required or relevant; the platform structurally eliminates this risk.

complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Cookie-based third-party tracking opt-out is limited to browser settings, and a COPPA Inquiry process exists for children's data, but no easy in-platform opt-out for general third-party data sharing is described.

complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Terms of Service and Privacy Policy do not include any provision notifying users when third-party service provider relationships change or when new third parties are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly and prominently states there is no advertising on or in any Kids Discover products, apps, or websites, and that the company does not believe in advertising to children.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Kids Discover confirms no targeted advertising is directed at children on its platform, though the privacy policy notes it may disclose adult user information to third-party advertising platforms for off-platform advertising about the service.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party cookies and web beacons are allowed and may be used by service providers for tracking; opt-out is available only via browser settings, with no in-platform opt-out mechanism provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy acknowledges use of web beacons and similar tracking technologies by both Kids Discover and third parties, but states steps are taken to avoid collection for targeted advertising when the services are believed to be used by children.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out from third-party data sharing for advertising exists for California residents via email request, and a COPPA Inquiry process is available, but there is no clear universal opt-out process described for all users.
