r423.riskReason: The site claims COPPA compliance and states personal data is not sold to third parties, but it does use Google Analytics with advertising/demographic cookies and third-party ad networks (including Google/DoubleClick) that place cookies and web beacons on the site, creating residual tracking risk for child visitors without a robust age-gate or verified parental consent mechanism.
r423.parentSummary: Kids World Travel Guide collects personal information (name, email, address) only on a voluntary basis, such as through its annual writing competition, and states that this data will not be sold or provided to third parties. However, the site does use Google Analytics and third-party advertising companies (including Google/DoubleClick) that place cookies and web beacons to collect demographic and interest data from all visitors, including children. The site claims COPPA compliance and offers opt-outs for personalized ads, but does not have a formal Terms of Service page and lacks explicit age-verification or verified parental consent processes.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states that material changes will be indicated on the site with a link to the new policy, but there is no advance notification mechanism (e.g., email notice) and no publicly visible revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists voluntary personal data (name, email, address, phone) and Google Analytics data, but does not comprehensively enumerate all data types collected by third-party ad networks operating on the site.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically explains that data is collected voluntarily (e.g., contact forms, writing competition), through Google Analytics cookies, and via third-party advertising cookies and web beacons.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states personal information is used only for internal purposes and will not be sold or provided to third parties, implying user ownership of voluntarily submitted data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion or correction of submitted personal information via the site's Contact Us page, fulfilling a basic deletion mechanism.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not state any specific or general data retention period for either voluntarily submitted personal information or analytics/cookie data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The site has an SSL certificate, and data is stored on SiteSell Inc. servers, but the policy does not list specific technical or organizational security measures beyond server storage.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Third-party sources confirm the site uses an SSL certificate for encrypted transmission, but the privacy policy itself does not explicitly mention encryption.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No user account is required to use the site, so password enforcement is not applicable; this criterion is met by the no-account-required model.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No user account or login is required for general site use, making MFA/SSO not applicable; this criterion is met by the no-account-required model.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions Google Analytics cookies, advertising cookies, and web beacons generally, but does not provide a specific enumerated list of all cookies used with their individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Google Analytics, Google/DoubleClick ad services, and SiteSell Inc. (host) as parties receiving data, but does not provide a complete named list of all third-party ad network partners.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy indicates that no personally identifiable information is shared with ad companies (only anonymized cookie/beacon data), but does not specify exactly what data Google Analytics or each ad partner receives individually.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy provides opt-out links for personalized ads across 125+ ad networks and specifically for Google personalized ads, constituting a functional opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not state that third-party advertising companies or the hosting provider are contractually bound to follow data protection standards or a vendor agreement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention that users will be notified if the roster of third-party advertising or analytics partners changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy confirms that third-party advertising companies serve ads on the website, including Google/DoubleClick ads, meaning ads are actively displayed to all visitors including children.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Google's DoubleClick cookie is used to serve ads based on visitors' activity on other sites across the web, constituting behavioral/targeted advertising directed at site visitors.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Opt-out links are provided for Google personalized ads and a network of 125+ ad networks, but third-party tracking via cookies and web beacons occurs by default before opt-out is exercised.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy explicitly acknowledges the use of web beacons and advertising cookies by third-party companies to track ad impressions, confirming tracking for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Opt-out links for personalized ads are mentioned and linked, but the opt-out process requires users to navigate to external third-party pages, making it present but not straightforward or centralized.

r424.riskReason: CBC's privacy notice states kids platforms do not feature advertising and do not track users for personalization, but third-party data sharing practices are only broadly described, CBC Kids was previously cited in a Human Rights Watch report for canvas fingerprinting and sending data to 20 ad/marketing companies, and the policies governing the broader CBC platform include personalized ad trackers and third-party data sharing that may intersect with child-directed content.
r424.parentSummary: CBC Kids (kidscbc.com/cbc.ca/kids) states it does not offer user registration, does not track children for personalization, and does not feature advertising on its dedicated children's platforms. However, the overarching CBC/Radio-Canada privacy notice acknowledges use of device identifiers, IP addresses, location data, and third-party analytics and advertising partners across its platforms; the kids-specific carve-out is stated in policy but was disputed in a 2022 Human Rights Watch investigation that identified tracking technologies on CBC Kids. Parents should be aware that while CBC claims strong child data protections, independent audits have raised concerns about third-party tracker activity on the site.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy notice states users with a CBC account will be alerted by email on important changes and that the date of the latest update is featured at the top, but no formal revision history or advance notification timeline is documented for non-account users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The CBC/Radio-Canada privacy notice lists device data, IP address, location, and behavioral/usage data collected across platforms, but the kids-specific data collection practices are only described at a high level ('no tracking for personalization') without a comprehensive itemized list for the children's platform specifically.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy broadly states that CBC uses own and third-party technology to collect device and usage data, and mentions digital markers and analytics tools, but does not specifically detail collection methods unique to the kids platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy notice does not explicitly address data ownership; it describes user rights including access and modification but does not clearly state that users own their data, leaving ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users with a CBC/Radio-Canada account are described as having rights to access and manage their data, and can delete their account to stop collection, but since kids platforms do not require accounts, there is no clear deletion mechanism for any passively collected data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy notice does not state a specific data retention period or timeframe for deletion of data collected from children or child-directed platforms; no written retention policy is surfaced for the kids platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy notice states 'multiple measures' are in place to protect personal information and references the federal Privacy Act and CBC/Radio-Canada's Personal Information policy, but does not enumerate specific technical security controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The terms of use mention IP address depersonalization when working with third-party analytics providers and imply secure data handling, but encryption is not explicitly confirmed as applied throughout the kids platform or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Since the kids platform does not require account registration, strong password enforcement is not applicable, which satisfies this criterion by design.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account creation is required on the kids platform, so MFA is not applicable; this criterion is met by the no-account architecture.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The CBC/Radio-Canada privacy notice and terms of use reference the use of digital markers, trackers, and cookies broadly, and users can modify tracking preferences, but a complete itemized list of all cookies and their purposes specific to the kids platform is not publicly documented.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy notice references 'advertising partners,' 'web analytics providers,' 'Single Sign-On providers,' and 'third-party server contractors' but does not name them specifically, providing only broad categories.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify which data elements are shared with each individual third-party category; data shared is described only in aggregate terms across the broader platform, not itemized per vendor for the kids platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can modify tracking preferences per the privacy notice, and personalized advertising trackers are stated to be deactivated on under-13 content, but a clear, easy opt-out process specific to third-party sharing on the kids platform is not explicitly documented.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The terms of use state that third-party providers operating under contract are required not to use collected data for other purposes without prior written consent and must provide equivalent data protection, representing a general contractual obligation but not a comprehensive supplier responsibility clause.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy notice states users with accounts will be notified by email of important changes, and non-account users are encouraged to check periodically; no proactive notification is guaranteed for changes to third-party sharing arrangements specifically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The CBC/Radio-Canada privacy notice explicitly states that the kids-dedicated platforms (CBC Kids, CBC Kids News) do not feature advertising and personalized advertising trackers are deactivated on under-13 content, but the policy also notes personalized ads may appear on mixed-audience platforms for 13+ youth content, creating some ambiguity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy states no targeted advertising on child-directed platforms and that personalized ad trackers are deactivated for under-13 content; however, the broader platform does use advertising targeting technology, and independent researchers have questioned whether this boundary is consistently enforced in practice.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: CBC states personalized ad trackers are deactivated on under-13 content, but the platform does use third-party trackers on broader content and Human Rights Watch previously found tracking technologies active on CBC Kids, making full compliance with no third-party ad tracking uncertain.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy notice acknowledges use of digital markers, device fingerprinting-adjacent technologies (device ID, screen characteristics), and third-party analytics, and CBC Kids was identified in a 2022 HRW report as using canvas fingerprinting; the current policy status of these methods on the kids platform is not fully clarified.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can modify tracking preferences through the privacy choices page and unsubscribe from newsletters, but a clear, specific opt-out from data sharing with advertisers on child-directed content—separate from the general tracker preference tool—is not explicitly described in the policy.

r425.riskReason: KidzType is explicitly child-directed but its privacy policy lacks verifiable parental consent mechanisms, does not specify a minimum age, uses advertising and remarketing cookies served by third-party ad networks, and fails to prohibit targeted advertising to children as required under COPPA.
r425.parentSummary: KidzType collects minimal personal information (name and email) only if users opt into certain features, and states it does not require personal data to use the site. However, the platform uses advertising cookies and third-party ad networks that track users for interest-based advertising and remarketing, which is highly problematic for a child-directed typing site. There is no verifiable parental consent process, no stated minimum age requirement, and no explicit prohibition on targeting children with behavioral ads.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states that changes will be reflected by a revised date at the bottom of the page and that notice may be provided through contact information supplied, but does not guarantee advance notification or maintain a public revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data categories (name, email, address, usage/traffic data, cookies) but does not comprehensively enumerate all data types collected, particularly advertising identifiers and social media tracking data disclosed only in the separate cookie policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy provides a general description of collection methods (forms, automatic collection, third-party sources) but lacks specifics about which automated tools or third-party providers collect data on its behalf.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; it claims a 'no logs' priority and minimal data processing, but data ownership is neither assigned to the user nor clearly claimed by the operator.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy mentions users may contact the operator regarding individual rights and personal information, but does not provide a clear, direct deletion mechanism or self-service deletion option for users.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state any specific or general data retention period, making it impossible to assess how long children's data may be held.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards' in a controlled secure environment, but does not list specific security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or security audits.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (in transit or at rest) is made in the privacy policy or terms; the policy only provides a general disclaimer that no Internet transmission can be guaranteed secure.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account creation is required to use the site, so strong password enforcement is not applicable and this criterion is satisfied by the no-account-required model.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account or login is required to use the core typing features, making MFA not applicable; this criterion is satisfied by the no-account-required model.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The cookie policy lists general cookie categories (session, persistent, analytics, advertising) but does not enumerate specific cookies by name, purpose, or duration, falling short of full transparency.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy broadly references 'trusted third parties,' affiliates, and subsidiaries, and the cookie policy mentions social media networks (Facebook, Twitter), but does not name specific advertising or analytics third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what data is shared with each individual third party; only a general statement that third parties receive only what is needed for their function is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The cookie policy indicates users can adjust browser settings to decline cookies, but there is no dedicated or easy opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing described within the platform itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states third parties must abide by policies consistent with KidzType's or agree to its privacy terms, providing a general contractual claim, but no formal data processing agreements or specific vendor accountability mechanisms are disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not state that users will be notified when third-party sharing arrangements change; updates are communicated only by revising the policy date, with no specific notice of third-party changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The cookie policy explicitly discloses advertising cookies used by KidzType and third parties to serve relevant ads and conduct remarketing, confirming that ads are displayed on this child-directed platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The cookie policy confirms use of aggregate data from third parties to show 'interest-based advertising,' constituting targeted advertising practices on a site explicitly designed for and directed at children.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party ad network cookies are used for remarketing and event tracking as described in the cookie policy, with no opt-out mechanism provided within the platform beyond generic browser-level cookie settings.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy confirms use of third-party advertising cookies for remarketing and event tracking purposes, which constitutes tracking for advertising on a child-directed platform with no clear functional-only limitation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is provided beyond the generic instruction to adjust browser cookie settings, which is insufficient for a child-directed platform under COPPA requirements.

r426.riskReason: While Kodable does not collect PII from students and claims COPPA compliance, it uses personal data and third-party tracking to display personalized retargeting ads for Kodable on external platforms, contractual limits on third-party data use are unclear, and encryption practices are not disclosed.
r426.parentSummary: Kodable does not collect personally identifiable information directly from children — only minimal identifiers like first names or nicknames are entered by teachers for class rosters. However, Kodable does collect personal data from adult users (parents and teachers), and uses that data along with third-party tracking tools to display personalized Kodable ads on other platforms. Kodable states it does not sell personal information, supports data deletion, and accepts Data Privacy Agreements from school districts, but does not clearly disclose encryption practices or binding contractual limits on third-party data use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Kodable's privacy policy indicates an effective date but Common Sense Media found no change log or past policy version is made available, making full advance notification only partially met.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Categories of personally identifiable information collected from adult users are clearly stated in the terms, including survey data and contest entries beyond what is strictly required for the product.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected directly, through third-party logins, and via usage analytics, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is not explicitly assigned to the user; the policy is silent on who owns user data, creating ambiguity especially during mergers or acquisitions where data can transfer to third parties.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The terms state that users can access, modify, or delete their personal information, and data is deleted upon account cancellation or termination.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not clearly state a specific data retention period, only noting deletion upon account cancellation, which makes the overall retention timeline vague.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references sending security alerts but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as firewalls, access controls, or audit logging.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Common Sense Media's evaluation found that the terms do not mention whether encryption is used to protect data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that strong passwords are enforced; Clever SSO integration is available but not universally required.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Kodable supports third-party login via Clever (SSO), which partially satisfies this requirement, but MFA is not explicitly mentioned for standard accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Kodable's policy mentions using tracking and analytics tools but does not provide a comprehensive cookie list with individual purposes for each cookie.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references sharing with third-party vendors, consultants, and service providers in general terms but does not name the specific third-party companies used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing broadly without detailing which specific data elements are shared with each individual third-party category.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No clear or easy opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in the publicly available policy documents.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: It is unclear from the terms whether third-party vendors are contractually required to limit their use of shared data, as noted by Common Sense Media's evaluation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not clearly state whether users will be notified of changes to the third parties Kodable shares data with.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy does not clearly state whether ads are shown within the first-party Kodable product itself, leaving this ambiguous for school-context use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Kodable's own terms confirm that personal information and third-party tracking are used to display personalized retargeting ads for Kodable on external/third-party platforms.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking is used to serve personalized ads for Kodable on other platforms, and no opt-out from this tracking is described in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The use of third-party tracking tools for retargeting is acknowledged, but specific tracking methods (e.g., pixels, beacons) are not individually listed or explained.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The policy provides no clear opt-out process for users who wish to stop their data from being shared with advertising or retargeting platforms.

r427.riskReason: While Kurzweil 3000 claims COPPA/FERPA compliance and participates in iKeepSafe Safe Harbor, the policy allows PII transfer to parent/affiliate companies and business transition successors without granular transparency, specific named third parties are not listed, cookie/tracking disclosures are vague, and no specific encryption or MFA details are documented.
r427.parentSummary: Kurzweil 3000 collects a limited set of student PII (name, student ID, grade level) plus educator and usage data solely to provide its assistive reading and learning services, and explicitly states it will not use student data for marketing or advertising. The platform claims compliance with both COPPA and FERPA, participates in the iKeepSafe Safe Harbor program, and states student data will not be shared with third parties without written district authorization. However, parents should be aware that personal information may be shared with Kurzweil's parent company (Cambium Learning) and could transfer to successors in a merger or acquisition, and the policy's cookie and third-party disclosures lack specific detail.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states changes will be posted on the Cambium Learning homepage and users notified by email for material changes, but no revision history or versioning is provided, making it only partially compliant.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Core student PII fields (first name, last name, student ID, grade, school) and usage/log data are listed, but the full scope of behavioral or document-content data collected during platform use is not comprehensively enumerated.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected as users interact with the site and via 'tracking, cookies, and log files,' but lacks specifics on exactly how each data type is collected (e.g., what triggers logging, what the cookies capture).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly assert that users or districts own student data; it restricts Kurzweil's use of data to educational purposes but permits sharing with affiliates and successors, leaving data ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Districts can request written destruction of student data upon leaving the program, but deletion is not self-service and requires a written request to Kurzweil, making it a limited/process-dependent deletion option rather than full user-controlled deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy specifies that student data is retained until a written destruction request is received from the district, and that data inactive for ten years will be destroyed with written notice—a specific, documented retention framework.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'industry standard server and network hardware and software' to prevent unauthorized access, but does not enumerate specific security measures such as firewalls, access controls, or audit logging.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (in transit or at rest) is made anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of service; encryption is neither confirmed nor described.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform supports SSO via Microsoft and Google login, which implicitly enforces strong authentication, but no explicit password policy or strength enforcement is documented in the privacy policy or terms.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform explicitly supports Microsoft SSO and Google SSO as well as ClassLink integration, meeting the standard for federated identity/SSO-based authentication in lieu of MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges the use of cookies and log files for tracking but does not provide a detailed cookie inventory, categorization (functional vs. analytics vs. advertising), or a dedicated cookie policy page.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy mentions the parent company Cambium Learning and 'affiliated companies' as data recipients but does not name any specific third-party vendors, analytics providers, or service partners.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups sharing broadly (affiliates, district-directed third parties, aggregated research partners) without specifying what data fields are shared with each category of recipient.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users cannot independently opt out of sharing with affiliated companies; the policy allows such sharing by default, with no described opt-out mechanism beyond contacting support.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy requires written authorization for district-directed third-party sharing and states that Kurzweil acts as the district's agent, but does not state that all third-party recipients are contractually bound to equivalent data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not include any provision for notifying users or districts when third-party data sharing arrangements change or new third parties are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states that student PII is not used to market products or services to students or parents, and the platform is an assistive technology tool with no ads displayed to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Kurzweil explicitly prohibits use of personally identifiable student data for direct marketing to students or parents, and there is no indication of behavioral or targeted advertising on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party advertising tracking is described or evidenced in the privacy policy; the platform does not appear to use ad tracking SDKs or networks directed at students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While advertising tracking appears absent, the policy acknowledges the use of cookies and tracking technologies without fully detailing their scope, leaving some ambiguity about whether any third-party analytics trackers are present.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or data sharing with advertisers is described, there is effectively no need for an opt-out, and the policy's prohibition on marketing use of student data serves as a blanket protection.

r428.riskReason: LanSchool Air collects sensitive student monitoring data including screen snapshots and web browsing history, delegates COPPA/FERPA compliance responsibility to schools rather than assuming it directly, uses cookies and web beacons on its platform, and shares data with a broad but not fully enumerated set of third-party service providers including Lenovo global operations.
r428.parentSummary: LanSchool Air is a classroom device management tool used by schools to monitor student devices; it collects data such as student names, email addresses, screen snapshots, web browsing URLs, and device information, which is used solely for educational management purposes and is not sold or used for advertising. Schools bear primary responsibility for obtaining parental consent under COPPA and FERPA, and parents or students wishing to access or delete data must contact their school administrator rather than LanSchool directly. The platform states it does not sell personal information or use it for behavioral advertising, and it applies encryption and access controls to protect stored data, though the specific list of third-party service providers is not fully disclosed.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states that prior versions will be made available and that material changes will be notified via website notice, in-product notification, or email before taking effect.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, device identifiers, browsing URLs, snapshots, roster data), but the enumeration is spread across multiple product-specific sections and is not consolidated into a single comprehensive list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes that data is collected via the installed agent, Google SSO, Clever integration, and product registration, but does not provide a detailed, unified explanation of all collection mechanisms in one place.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states that school-controlled data is controlled by the school and not Stoneware/Lenovo, and that Stoneware processes student data solely on the school's behalf, but Stoneware also designates itself as an 'Independent Data Controller' for other data, creating ambiguity about ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents and students can request deletion by contacting their school, and schools can request deletion from Stoneware, but deletion is indirect and may be denied if identity cannot be verified, representing a limited rather than full self-service deletion process.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as necessary for business purposes and lists several retention triggers, but does not provide specific time periods (e.g., 90 days, 1 year) for any category of data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'standard technical and organizational measures,' authentication techniques, access controls, and encryption, but does not enumerate specific security frameworks, certifications (e.g., SOC 2), or detailed controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy states encryption is used 'when necessary' during transmission and storage of sensitive information, but does not confirm end-to-end encryption or specify which data categories are always encrypted.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: LanSchool Air supports Google SSO for instructor authentication, which enforces Google's strong credential and authentication policies, meeting this requirement via SSO rather than a standalone password policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: LanSchool Air uses Google SSO/API for instructor login, which supports MFA at the Google account level, satisfying this requirement through the SSO mechanism.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges use of 'Internet cookies, tags, web beacons, analytics and related website solutions' but does not provide a full categorized list of cookies with their purposes, falling short of a complete cookie disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Clever and Google as specific integration partners, and broadly references 'Lenovo businesses,' 'data hosting,' 'analytics,' and 'marketing' suppliers, but does not provide a complete enumerated list of all third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy indicates what data is shared with Clever (roster/name/email/ID) and Google (instructor credentials for SSO), but for the broader category of Lenovo and third-party service providers, the specific data shared with each is not individually itemized.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications and submit privacy requests to restrict processing, but there is no clear, easy opt-out specifically for sharing with the broad category of third-party service providers used for hosting and analytics.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that Stoneware takes steps to ensure suppliers adhere to Stoneware's standards for privacy and security, indicating contractual responsibility is claimed over third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states material changes will be notified in advance but does not specifically commit to notifying users when individual third-party service provider relationships are added or changed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states that student personal information is collected for the use and benefit of the school and for no other commercial purpose, with no advertising displayed within the product.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states that LanSchool does not share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising and does not engage in profiling for targeted advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy confirms no sale of personal information and no sharing for behavioral advertising, and California residents have an explicit right to opt out, effectively meaning no third-party ad tracking occurs.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While the policy confirms no advertising tracking, it does acknowledge use of cookies, web beacons, and analytics tools on Stoneware websites and within LanSchool Air, which could include functional or analytics tracking whose full scope is not detailed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The policy provides a clear privacy request submission process for opting out of any sale or sharing of personal information, and users can contact privacy@lanschool.com directly, constituting a clear opt-out mechanism.

r429.riskReason: LanSchool Classic is locally hosted on school servers with no cloud transmission of student data outside the school network, no advertising, no sale of student data, and COPPA/FERPA compliance obligations are explicitly acknowledged, though the school bears primary compliance responsibility.
r429.parentSummary: LanSchool Classic is a locally hosted classroom management tool that runs only on school servers and is non-functional when a student's device leaves school grounds. It may collect student names, usernames, email addresses, browsing history, keystroke alerts, and on-screen snapshots (which are not stored and only viewable by authorized school staff). Student data is not sold or used for advertising, and the privacy policy explicitly states that the school — not Lenovo/Stoneware — controls the data and is responsible for parental consent under COPPA.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy statement explicitly states that previous versions will be made available upon changes and that material changes will be communicated via website notice, in-product notification, or email.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy clearly lists data collected through the Clever integration (name, email, school identifier, username), browsing history, snapshots, keystroke alerts, and administrator account registration data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifies how data is collected — through the Clever/SIS integration, via the locally installed agent on student devices, and through account registration — covering the primary collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy explicitly states that 'the account, information, and content associated with LanSchool are controlled by the school – not by Stoneware and Lenovo,' clearly assigning data ownership to the school.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy statement describes the right to request deletion of a minor's personal information via a privacy request submission process, satisfying the deletion right requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy references data retention in general terms tied to the agreement period but does not specify a precise numeric retention period for student data, making this only partially addressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy provides only a general statement about suppliers 'adhering to Stoneware's standards' without enumerating specific technical security measures such as encryption protocols, access controls, or audit logging.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: LanSchool Classic uses local network (LAN) communication with a proprietary protocol; encryption is not explicitly confirmed for on-premises Classic deployments, though historical issues were reportedly fixed per public sources.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not explicitly state password strength requirements; administrator accounts use passwords during registration but enforcement of complexity or strength requirements is not detailed.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The policy and EULA do not explicitly mention MFA for teacher or administrator accounts in the Classic (on-premises) product; SSO/LTI support is not described for Classic specifically.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions that 'most browsers are initially set up to accept cookies' and references cookies generally, but does not provide a full enumerated cookie list with purposes specific to the Classic product.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy identifies Clever as a named third-party integration and references categories of service providers (hosting, analytics, marketing), but does not enumerate all specific vendor names.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy describes data shared with Clever (name, email, school ID, username) specifically, but for other service providers it groups data sharing without itemizing what each specific vendor receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The Clever integration is described as optional and school-activated, providing an indirect opt-out; however, there is no clear self-service opt-out mechanism for other service provider data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that steps are taken to ensure suppliers adhere to Stoneware's privacy standards, indicating contractual controls are in place over third-party data processors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy commits to notifying users of material changes to the privacy statement overall but does not specifically address notification procedures when individual third-party subprocessors are added or changed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy statement explicitly states LanSchool does not sell personal information and does not share it for cross-context behavioral advertising, and no ads are displayed within the product.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy clearly states that student data collected through LanSchool is used solely for the benefit of the school and for no other commercial purpose, with no targeted advertising permitted.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party advertising tracking is present or disclosed; the product is a locally hosted tool without third-party ad networks, and student data is explicitly not used for behavioral advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: There is no mention of web beacons or advertising tracking pixels within the Classic product; any cookies referenced are functional/browser-level, not advertising-related.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising data sharing occurs, no opt-out mechanism is needed; the policy's explicit prohibition on selling data and behavioral advertising targeting constitutes a fully met standard.

r430.riskReason: Leap For Literacy operates a student-facing K-12 platform with classroom and student account management features but publishes no discoverable Privacy Policy or Terms of Service, leaving all data collection, sharing, retention, and compliance practices entirely undisclosed.
r430.parentSummary: Leap For Literacy (leapforliteracy.org) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit EdTech platform that engages K-12 students in literacy and kindness programs, and its FAQ indicates the platform includes student accounts, classroom management, and a Kindness Portal. However, the organization does not appear to publish any Privacy Policy or Terms of Service on its website, meaning parents and schools have no way to determine what student data is collected, how it is used, who it is shared with, or what protections are in place. Schools should exercise extreme caution and request written data privacy agreements directly from the organization before allowing student use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Privacy Policy or Terms of Service were found on the platform, so no policy change notification process or revision history can be assessed.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: No Privacy Policy exists publicly, so there is no disclosure of what data types are collected from students or users.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: With no published policy, there is no statement of any kind about how data is collected (forms, cookies, automated tracking, etc.).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: No policy exists to establish user or student ownership of data, nor to clarify whether the organization claims ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No deletion rights or process are described anywhere in publicly accessible platform documentation.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or general retention statement is published anywhere on the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No security measures of any kind are described in any publicly available platform document.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (in transit or at rest) is made in any publicly accessible document.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No password policy, strong password enforcement, or SSO/MFA requirement is disclosed in any accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in publicly accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy or disclosure of cookie usage exists in any publicly accessible document on the platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No third-party vendors, partners, or service providers are named or disclosed in any public-facing document.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: With no policy present, there is no disclosure of what data, if any, is shared with any third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described or offered in any accessible platform documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor agreement obligations or third-party data handling responsibilities are described in any public document.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No notification process for changes to third-party relationships is described anywhere on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No disclosure is made about whether ads are displayed to users or students on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No statement exists confirming or denying the use of targeted advertising on or through the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure about third-party tracking technologies for advertising purposes is made anywhere on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No information about web beacons, tracking pixels, or similar tracking methods is provided in any public document.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described or available anywhere on the platform.

dataCollected: IP address (inferred from authentication/referral URL tracking)
r431.riskReason: Learn360 (Infobase) explicitly states COPPA and FERPA compliance, prohibits sale of student data, restricts student data to educational purposes only, and requires subcontractors to follow the same data protection policies.
r431.parentSummary: Learn360 collects basic account information such as name, email, and username, as well as usage and cookie data to operate the platform and personalize educational content. Student data is explicitly stated to not be used for commercial purposes and is retained only for educational use, with parents able to review, correct, or request deletion of their child's information at any time. The platform does not sell personal data to third parties and claims compliance with both COPPA and FERPA, making it a generally low-risk choice for K-12 schools.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states material changes will be posted prominently and emailed to registered users, but there is no explicit revision history or version log made publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy describes general categories of data collected (contact info, usage data, cookies) but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of every specific data type collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that data is collected via website use, email, and in-person interactions, but does not detail specific collection mechanisms such as tracking pixels, analytics SDKs, or log files.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Use clarify that subscribers retain ownership of user-generated content but grant Infobase a broad perpetual license, and the policy is silent on explicit student data ownership language beyond educational-use restrictions.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy explicitly allows users and parents to contact Infobase at any time to access, correct, update, or request deletion of personal information, satisfying the full deletion requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states student data is retained for educational purposes but does not specify any concrete retention period or timeframe after which data is deleted or anonymized.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy lists specific security measures including SSL/encryption, physical and electronic safeguards, encrypted storage environments, access controls, and regular internal security reviews.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: SSL/TLS encryption is explicitly mentioned for data in transit, and data is stated to be stored in encrypted environments, satisfying the encryption requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy references password protection for registered accounts but does not describe enforcement of password complexity or strength requirements; SSO options (Google, Microsoft, Classlink, SAML) are also available.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform supports SSO via Google, Microsoft, Classlink, and SAML/LTI integrations, meeting the SSO/LTI standard as a substitute for MFA in educational settings.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and their general purposes (feature tracking and content customization) but does not provide a full enumerated list of cookies used with their specific names and purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references sharing with 'technical and fulfillment agents and consultants' but does not name any specific third-party vendors or service providers by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with internal agents and consultants is described only in general terms; no breakdown of exactly what data goes to which party is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can contact Infobase to opt out of personal contact information sharing and unsubscribe from communications, but the opt-out process requires a written or email request rather than a self-service mechanism.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy explicitly states all companies working for Infobase must comply with its data policies and are not permitted to sell user information to third parties or use it beyond authorized purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states Infobase will post material changes prominently before implementing them but does not specifically commit to notifying users when third-party sub-processors change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy and terms explicitly state student data is not used for commercial purposes, and no advertising is described as being served to authenticated platform users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states student data is not used for commercial intent and there is no mention of targeted advertising or behavioral profiling of users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party advertising tracking is described within the platform, and the policy states data is not shared or sold to third parties for marketing or advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies are described as being used for feature tracking and content customization, but no explicit confirmation is given that no advertising-related tracking technologies (beacons, pixels) are deployed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can contact Infobase to opt out of data sharing and promotional communications, and the policy confirms student data is not used for commercial or advertising purposes.

dataCollected: Email address (via registration or contact forms)
Resume/CV data (for job seekers who register)
dataSharedWith: Third-party advertisers/schools/recruiters (when user voluntarily submits an inquiry or application)
r432.riskReason: Learn4good.com is a general-audience platform that displays personalized Google ads and third-party advertising cookies to all users including children, allows under-18 users with only a general supervision requirement, lacks verifiable parental consent mechanisms, makes no FERPA commitment, and reserves the right to change its policy at any time without advance notice.
r432.parentSummary: Learn4Good collects cookies, device identifiers, approximate location, and usage data from all visitors including children, and serves personalized Google ads and third-party advertising cookies in many countries — though it claims to use only non-personalized, contextual ads in the EU/EEA. The site states it does not knowingly collect personal data from children under 13, prohibits under-13 registration, and offers an ad opt-out consent tickbox, but it does not require verifiable parental consent before children under 13 access the site or its games. There is no FERPA commitment, no named school-data agreement, and the privacy policy can be changed at any time without advance notice to users.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy explicitly states it may be modified at any time and without notice, with continued use constituting consent — no advance notification or versioned revision history is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists general categories (cookies, device data, geolocation, behavioral/usage data, registration data) but does not provide a comprehensive, itemized list of every data type collected across all site features.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general description of how data is collected (cookies, registration forms, contact forms, ad networks) but does not specify the technical collection mechanism for each data type individually.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not state that users own their data; Learn4Good Ltd positions itself as the data controller and there is no explicit user data ownership clause.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Registered users can request deletion of submitted personal information at any time, but general visitors have no stated deletion right for passively collected cookie/behavioral data beyond browser-level opt-out.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The jobseeker terms specify a 4-month inactivity deletion period for job accounts, but the main privacy policy provides only a vague general retention statement without specifying retention periods for other data types.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references website security monitoring and network traffic monitoring but does not list specific technical security measures (e.g., firewalls, encryption standards, access controls) for personal data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS (SSL/TLS) for transport encryption as standard, but the privacy policy does not explicitly state that data is encrypted at rest or in transit, offering only an implied partial protection.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No password strength requirements, enforcement policies, or guidance are mentioned anywhere in the terms or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI integration is mentioned; the platform uses standard username/password account registration only.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are categorized into Necessary, Functionality, and Advertising types with an opt-out mechanism described, but the policy does not provide a fully named, per-cookie disclosure listing each cookie's name and exact purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google is specifically named as a third-party ad provider, and a general reference to 'other display ad service providers' is made, but the full list of all third-party data recipients is not disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states that behavioral/visit data (excluding name, address, email, phone) is used by ad networks, but does not provide a per-third-party breakdown of exactly what data each named or unnamed party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An on-page consent tickbox opt-out from personalized and non-personalized ads is provided, but it is noted that the opt-out may not function reliably on older browsers or devices, limiting its effectiveness.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not state that third-party vendors or ad networks are contractually required to follow data protection obligations or a vendor agreement with Learn4Good.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy reserves the right to change at any time without notice, meaning third-party relationships can change with no notification obligation to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Personalized Google ads are displayed to users in most countries (non-EEA), including potentially to child users who access the general-audience site, which poses a significant K-12 concern.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Personalized ads based on past browsing behavior are served to users outside the EU/EEA/UK, which constitutes confirmed user-behavioral targeting and is not restricted for child visitors.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: An opt-out tickbox for advertising cookies is provided and users can visit aboutads.info, but the opt-out is noted as potentially unreliable on some browsers, making it only a partial control.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Third-party advertising cookies (including Google) are stored on users' devices for behavioral tracking and ad serving purposes, which is confirmed tracking for advertising — not merely functional tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An on-page opt-out mechanism exists via a consent tickbox and a link to aboutads.info, but the process is described as potentially unreliable and does not provide a clear, guaranteed opt-out pathway for all users.

dataCollected: Disability status and type (reading/perceptual disability, specific learning disability, visual disability, physical disability)
Certificate of Eligibility / proof of disability
Access times and referring website addresses
dataSharedWith: Third-party service providers necessary to deliver the Service (for users under 13, specific providers listed in policy but not named publicly in search results)
r433.riskReason: Learning Ally explicitly claims COPPA compliance and does not sell student data, but collects sensitive disability/health information from minors, retains third-party data sharing with limited specificity on named providers, does not support Do Not Track, and reserves the right to change its privacy policy without advance notice.
r433.parentSummary: Learning Ally collects personal information including name, contact details, and sensitive disability status from students in order to verify eligibility and provide audiobook services. The platform states it does not sell or rent student data and claims COPPA compliance, including allowing parents or guardians to review and delete their child's data upon request. However, the policy reserves the right to change without prior notice, does not explicitly name all third-party vendors, and collects sensitive health-related disability information which warrants careful review by schools and parents.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy explicitly states changes may be made 'at any time and without notice,' with changes effective immediately upon posting, meaning no advance notification or revision history is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Solutions Privacy Policy enumerates specific PII collected including name, contact info, disability status, IP address, browser data, usage data, and billing information.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states data is collected when users register, use the app, contact Learning Ally by phone or web, or provide eligibility documentation voluntarily.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly assert user ownership of data; it describes Learning Ally's rights to collect, store, and use PII without explicitly stating user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents, guardians, and school administrators can request review or deletion of a child's PII by contacting Learning Ally directly, satisfying a full deletion pathway.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states student PII is 'retained only to ensure the efficiency' of service delivery but does not specify a concrete retention period or timeframe.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy describes SSL encryption, password-protected secure servers, access restrictions to employees on a need-to-know basis, and use of industry-standard encryption by vendors.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: SSL/industry-standard encryption is stated for data in transit and at storage vendors, covering the primary data transmission pathways.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy mentions password-protected servers and account security but does not explicitly state strong password requirements are enforced for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The policy makes no mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration options for student accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges cookie usage and that browsers can be set to decline cookies, but does not provide a detailed list of all cookies with their specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third-party categories are described (email hosts, server hosts, payment processors) but specific vendor names are not disclosed in the publicly searchable policy text.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by third-party category rather than specifying exactly what data each named third party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of mailing lists and direct mail, but there is no clear opt-out mechanism for all third-party data sharing, particularly for service-delivery third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that third parties 'are authorized to use a User's PII only as necessary to provide these services to us, and in a manner consistent with this Policy,' establishing vendor data use restrictions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes may be made without notice and does not include a specific commitment to notify users when third-party relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy and platform are educational/nonprofit in nature with no indication of advertising being displayed to students within the service.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no indication of targeted advertising to students; Learning Ally is a nonprofit audiobook service and the policy does not mention behavioral advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy explicitly states it does not support Do Not Track signals, suggesting some level of third-party tracking without a clear opt-out for all tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy does not detail all tracking methods used; cookies are mentioned generally but web beacons or pixel tracking are not addressed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out for mailing lists is mentioned, but a clear and comprehensive opt-out process for data sharing with any advertising or analytics third parties is not described.

r434.riskReason: Learning.com's Subscriber Privacy Policy provides strong student-focused protections, but the general public-facing Privacy Policy discloses use of third-party advertising partners and interest-based advertising tracking (including Google AdWords remarketing), creating ambiguity about whether those practices could reach authenticated users or the marketing site visited by school administrators and parents.
r434.parentSummary: Learning.com EasyTech collects a minimum set of student data—primarily name, username, district ID, and school—used solely for educational purposes, with no behavioral advertising directed at students and no sale of student data to third parties. The platform explicitly states compliance with COPPA and FERPA, allows parents to request review or deletion of their child's data at any time, and automatically de-identifies all PII 90 days after contract expiration. However, the broader public-facing Privacy Policy (applicable to teachers, admins, and site visitors) does reference third-party advertising partners and interest-based ad tracking, which may concern some stakeholders even though these practices appear to be scoped to non-student marketing activities.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Subscriber Privacy Policy indicates an effective/version date but the Common Sense evaluation notes no change log or past policy version archive is available, making revision history incomplete.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Subscriber Privacy Policy enumerates specific PII categories collected (Full Name, Username, District User ID, School Attending) and distinguishes anonymous usage data, satisfying the requirement to list all data collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Both the general Privacy Policy and Subscriber Privacy Policy describe how data is collected—through direct account creation, teacher/admin import, browser cookies for sessions, and usage tracking within the platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Use indicate Learning.com acts as a school official under FERPA and that student data belongs to the institution, but the policies do not explicitly state users own their data, and Common Sense flags ownership as unclear.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents can request full deletion of a child's data in writing at any time, institutions can request immediate de-identification upon contract expiration, and all PII is automatically de-identified 90 days post-contract, satisfying full deletion allowance.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The Subscriber Privacy Policy states PII is automatically de-identified 90 days after contract expiration and inactive accounts are de-identified annually after 2 years of inactivity, providing a specific retention period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The general Privacy Policy and Common Sense evaluation confirm specific security measures including encryption in transit and at rest, access controls, firewalls, vulnerability scans, SOC 2 Type II attestation, NIST SP 800-53 alignment, and regular penetration testing.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Learning.com's terms confirm all data in transit and at rest are encrypted, and the platform has passed independent encryption validation per Common Sense's evaluation.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policies do not explicitly describe strong password enforcement requirements for student or teacher accounts; third-party SSO (Google) is supported but is not the only login method, and password strength rules are not documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Third-party SSO login (e.g., Google) is supported, which provides a federated authentication option, but the policies and Common Sense evaluation note it is unclear whether multi-factor authentication is available for native accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Subscriber Privacy Policy states PII is never stored in cookies and cookies are used only for anonymous session and user preferences, but a comprehensive cookie list with individual purpose descriptions is not published.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Subscriber Privacy Policy references third-party content providers in general terms; the general Privacy Policy mentions advertising partners and payment processors, but specific named third-party vendors are not enumerated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Subscriber Privacy Policy identifies the specific fields shared with content providers (Name, District User ID, Username, School Attending), but the general Privacy Policy groups sharing with advertising partners without per-party data specifics.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Opt-out of marketing communications is available, and interest-based advertising opt-out links are provided in the general Privacy Policy, but opt-out from third-party content provider data sharing in the subscriber context is not clearly articulated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policies state third parties with access to information are contractually required to provide the same security protections as Learning.com, and contractual limits prohibit re-identification of de-identified data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policies do not explicitly commit to notifying subscribers of changes to which third-party content providers receive student data; the general policy indicates it may be updated and users should review it periodically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Subscriber Privacy Policy explicitly states no behaviorally targeted advertisements are provided to students, and the platform does not display third-party ads within the student-facing curriculum.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The Subscriber Privacy Policy confirms student data is not used to create profiles for non-educational purposes and no targeted advertising is directed at students, meeting the no-targeting standard for the subscriber product.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The general public-facing Privacy Policy discloses that third-party advertising partners (including Google AdWords remarketing) may track users across websites; while this appears scoped to the marketing site, it is unclear whether it applies to logged-in educators or administrators.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The general Privacy Policy discloses use of web beacons/pixel tags and local storage technologies; the Subscriber Privacy Policy limits cookies to functional session use only, creating a split tracking posture that is not fully transparent in a single document.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Industry opt-out links (DAA, NAI, Google Analytics opt-out) are listed in the general Privacy Policy for interest-based advertising, but the opt-out process requires per-device/per-browser action and is not a single clear opt-out mechanism for all advertising data sharing.

r435.minAge: Not specified (encourages parental involvement for students 13 and under, but does not set a hard minimum age)
dataCollected: Membership and payment information (for premium members)
dataSharedWith: None (policy states data is not sold, rented, or shared with third parties)
r435.riskReason: LearnThat Foundation is a nonprofit that self-claims COPPA exemption and lacks a dedicated, clearly structured privacy policy covering cookies, third-party integrations, data retention periods, security details, or formal COPPA/FERPA compliance statements required for K-12 deployment.
r435.parentSummary: LearnThatWord (operated by LearnThat Foundation, a 501(c)3 nonprofit) collects user-provided information such as name, email, and learning/quiz performance data in order to personalize vocabulary coaching for each member. The platform states it does not sell, rent, or share member personal data with third parties. However, the combined Terms of Service and Privacy Policy document is minimal and does not address cookies, specific security measures, data retention timelines, or formal COPPA/FERPA compliance procedures, which may be a concern for schools seeking a fully vetted EdTech partner.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states changes may occur and periodic email reminders may be sent, but there is no formal advance notification process or revision history published on the page.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy identifies that user-submitted information and usage data are collected to personalize learning, but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of all data types collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states information is collected when entered by users on the site, but does not address automatic or passive data collection methods such as cookies or analytics.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy and FAQ both state the platform does not sell, rent, or share member data, implying data is held on behalf of the user rather than claimed as company property.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can review their data in a customer profile page, but there is no explicit statement of a full self-service deletion right; deletion would require contacting the organization.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not state any specific data retention period or general retention policy for user data after account closure or inactivity.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy does not describe any specific security measures used to protect user data, such as encryption, access controls, or audits.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The checkout page references PCI Compliance for payment processing, suggesting some encryption is in place for transactions, but no general encryption commitment is stated in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy makes no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement; no SSO or account-free access is referenced for student accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: There is no mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration options anywhere in the policy or publicly available documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy does not mention cookies, web beacons, or any tracking technologies, and there is no cookie policy or disclosure of cookie types and purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy and FAQ explicitly state that member data is never released, sold, rented, or traded to any third party, effectively disclosing no third-party sharing occurs.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Because no third-party sharing is stated to occur, there is nothing to disclose per third party, which satisfies this requirement by default.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No third-party data sharing is stated to occur, meaning no opt-out is needed; the policy itself serves as the opt-out by prohibiting such sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not reference any vendor agreements, data processing agreements, or third-party accountability obligations, leaving this area unaddressed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not describe any process for notifying users if third-party data sharing relationships were to change in the future.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: There is no mention of advertising on the platform, and the nonprofit FAQ and policy indicate data is not shared for commercial purposes, implying no ads are displayed to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is referenced anywhere in the policy or platform documentation; the nonprofit model and data-sharing prohibitions support this finding.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is disclosed or described; however, the absence of a cookie policy means third-party tracking via embedded scripts cannot be fully ruled out.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy is silent on web beacons and tracking technologies; while no ad tracking is claimed, the lack of any cookie or tracking disclosure leaves the matter unaddressed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising or data sharing with advertisers is stated to occur, there is no opt-out needed, satisfying this criterion by the platform's stated practices.
