r436.riskReason: LEGO Education's core SPIKE App collects minimal data and explicitly prohibits selling or advertising use, but the broader LEGO Group privacy policy—which governs the education platform—allows third-party marketing cookies and does not explicitly disclaim FERPA compliance or restrict commercial data use across all services.
r436.parentSummary: LEGO Education's SPIKE App collects no personally identifiable information from students beyond the IP address needed for connectivity, displays no ads, and explicitly states that data is never sold or shared with advertising third parties. However, the overarching LEGO Group privacy policy—which applies to the broader legoeducation.com website and community platform—does permit optional third-party marketing cookies for adult-facing services and collects persistent identifiers like clickstream and device data. Parents should be aware that while the classroom app itself is very privacy-friendly, creating an educator account or using the community portal is governed by a broader policy that includes more extensive data practices, and the platform does not explicitly claim FERPA compliance.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The LEGO Group privacy policy bears an effective/revision date and states policies may be updated, but the education-specific policy does not clearly commit to advance notification before changes take effect, and no changelog of past versions is readily available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The SPIKE App privacy page clearly lists the limited data collected (IP address, anonymous performance data), but the broader LEGO Group policy governing the website and community portal lists many data categories without cleanly separating what applies specifically to K-12 education contexts.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policies specifically describe how data is collected—through direct user input, cookies, pixels, web beacons, and automatic device/browser signals—satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly declare user ownership of data; LEGO Group asserts the role of data controller, and user-submitted community content is granted broad usage rights to LEGO Education, creating ownership ambiguity.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy and US state privacy law addendums explicitly provide users the right to request deletion of personal data, and users can contact the Data Protection Officer or customer service to exercise this right.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is kept only as long as needed for its purpose or legal requirement, and factors used to determine retention are listed, but no specific retention timeframes (e.g., 90 days, 2 years) are stated for education-specific data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references using 'secure systems and partners' and secure cloud storage, and the SPIKE App notes anonymized IP addresses are stored on 'secure servers,' but specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, audits) are not detailed.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The FIRST LEGO League site (a related LEGO education property) references SSL/TLS encryption, and LEGO generally uses HTTPS, but the main LEGO Education privacy policy does not explicitly state that data is encrypted at rest and in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Neither the LEGO Education privacy policy nor the terms and conditions mention strong password enforcement requirements or minimum password standards for educator accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform does not mention MFA availability, SSO, or LTI integration in its publicly available policies, representing a gap for K-12 institutional security expectations.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The cookie policy clearly categorizes cookies into Necessary, Analytic, LEGO Marketing, and Third-Party Marketing types with descriptions of each, and a separate Cookie Declaration lists specific third-party cookies, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy states data is shared with categories of third parties (IT providers, delivery services, LEGO subsidiaries, government), but does not name specific third-party vendors by company name in the education-specific policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared by category of third party rather than specifying exactly which data fields go to which partner, providing only a general disclosure rather than granular per-party mapping.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of non-essential cookies via cookie settings and may opt out of data sale/targeted advertising under applicable state laws, but the opt-out process is not prominently linked or streamlined specifically for K-12 school users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy references that LEGO subsidiaries are 'formally contracted' to process data on LEGO's behalf, implying contractual controls, but does not explicitly state that all third-party vendors are bound by data protection agreements meeting education-specific standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The terms note that the LEGO Group 'may at any time revise' terms by updating the posting without explicitly committing to notify users of third-party vendor changes, representing a gap in transparency.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The SPIKE App explicitly states no advertisements appear within the app; however, the broader LEGO Education website and community portal do not make an equivalent blanket no-ads declaration.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: LEGO states it does not sell or use personal data for targeted advertising for known users aged 13–15 without consent under applicable state laws, and the SPIKE App confirms no targeting, but the general LEGO.com ecosystem permits third-party marketing cookies with consent.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party marketing cookies that enable behavioral tracking are available on the LEGO Group's broader web properties with consent mechanisms, but the SPIKE App explicitly prohibits sharing with advertising or tracking providers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy acknowledges use of pixels, beacons, scripts, and tags by both LEGO and third-party tracking partners, which goes beyond purely functional tracking on the broader platform, though the SPIKE App itself does not engage in this.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: US state privacy law addendums explicitly provide users the right to opt out of targeted advertising and data sale, and users can exercise this right by contacting LEGO directly or adjusting cookie settings, meeting this requirement.

dataCollected: Not specified - privacy page returned only a page title with no substantive policy content
r437.riskReason: The lessonlaunchpad.com/privacy page returns only a site tagline with no readable policy content, and no Terms of Service page was found, meaning the platform has effectively no publicly accessible, substantive privacy documentation for K-12 compliance evaluation.
r437.parentSummary: Lesson Launchpad markets itself as a classroom automation tool for teachers, but its privacy policy page (lessonlaunchpad.com/privacy) returned no substantive content during review — only a site tagline. No Terms of Service page was locatable. Without accessible policy documentation, parents and school administrators cannot determine what data is collected from teachers or students, how it is used, whether it is shared with third parties, or what protections are in place. Schools should not deploy this platform with student data until complete, COPPA- and FERPA-aligned privacy documentation is published and reviewed.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Terms of Service or privacy policy with change notification procedures was found or accessible on the platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy page returned only a site tagline; no list of data collected is available to evaluate.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: No information about how data is collected could be found in any accessible policy document.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: No policy document exists that addresses data ownership by users or the company.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No accessible policy addresses user rights to delete their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or statement of any kind was found in accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No security measures are described in any accessible policy document on the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption or data-in-transit protection was found in any accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account or password policy documentation was found or accessible on the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO is present in any accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy or list of cookies used was found in any accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No third-party disclosures or vendor lists were found in any accessible policy document.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No information about what data is shared with any third party was found.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described anywhere in accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No supplier or vendor agreement language was found in any accessible policy document.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No notification process for changes to third-party relationships was found in any accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No advertising policy was found; it is unknown whether ads are displayed to users or students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising policy or prohibition was found in any accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure of third-party tracking for advertising purposes was found.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No disclosure regarding web beacons, pixels, or other tracking technologies was found.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for advertiser data sharing was found in any accessible documentation.

r438.riskReason: LessonPix is a staff-only tool that explicitly states students do not access the platform and no student PII is collected, limiting K-12 data privacy risk significantly.
r438.parentSummary: LessonPix is a teacher-facing materials creation tool; only staff accounts exist and the platform explicitly states that students do not access LessonPix and no student information is entered into the system. Staff data collected is limited to first name, last name, and email address for account creation, plus transient payment info that is not stored. Data is not shared with third parties except as necessary to process payments, and no advertising or student data selling is indicated.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms and Conditions state LessonPix may change terms at any time with no advance notice, and continued use constitutes acceptance, with no revision history provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists name, address, email, phone, and payment info, but does not explicitly enumerate usage data, cookies, or log data that may also be collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected at pages where purchases or registrations occur and through the Add-In, but does not detail the specific technical mechanisms (e.g., forms, cookies, server logs).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state who owns user data; intellectual property in site content is claimed by LessonPix Inc., leaving user data ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can access and correct PII via the Account dashboard, but no explicit account or data deletion process is described in the policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period or general retention statement is provided anywhere in the privacy policy or terms.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states LessonPix takes 'reasonable steps' to protect data and does not store credit card details, but no specific technical or organizational security measures are enumerated.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (in transit or at rest) is made anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of password strength requirements or enforcement policies is found in the privacy policy or terms.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: LessonPix has implemented email-based Two-Factor Authentication for account logins, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy is present; cookies and tracking technologies are not mentioned anywhere in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references sharing data with 'authorization vendors' for payment processing but does not name specific third-party vendors or services.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states data is shared with outside parties only to complete an order, but does not specify what data elements are shared with each vendor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described; the only sharing noted is transactional and presented as non-optional.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No statement is made that third-party vendors (e.g., payment processors) are contractually required to protect user data or follow a vendor agreement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No process is described for notifying users if third-party data-sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No advertising of any kind is referenced in the privacy policy, terms, or platform description; LessonPix is a subscription tool with no ad model.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is referenced or indicated anywhere in the platform's policies or documentation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is referenced or indicated; no advertising ecosystem is described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies and web beacons are not mentioned in the policy, leaving tracking methods unaddressed rather than confirmed for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No data sharing with advertisers is described, and no opt-out is needed given the absence of any stated advertising data use.

dataCollected: Name (only via customer support contact, not during app use)

r439.riskReason: LetterSchool explicitly claims COPPA compliance and does not collect PII directly from children under 13, but uses advertising attribution networks (Adjust) and analytics third parties (Google Analytics) without clear opt-out for schools, does not explicitly claim FERPA compliance, and places COPPA/FERPA compliance liability on schools rather than itself.
r439.parentSummary: LetterSchool collects minimal personal data — primarily parent/guardian contact information for account creation and technical/usage data via cookies and analytics — and states it does not collect any personally identifiable information directly from children under 13. The app is advertised as ad-free with no social media integration, and SSL encryption is used to protect data in transit. However, data is shared with third-party advertising attribution networks (Adjust) and analytics providers (Google Analytics), and FERPA compliance is not explicitly claimed; instead, the Terms of Use shift compliance liability for COPPA and FERPA onto the educational institution.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it will be updated from time to time and users can check for changes, but does not commit to advance notification before changes take effect.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy identifies several data categories (identity, technical/usage, transaction, aggregated data) but does not provide a fully exhaustive enumerated list of every data element collected across all contexts.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states data is collected via sign-up forms, app/website use, newsletter sign-up, cookies, automated event logs, and from third-party providers including Adjust and Google.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: LetterSchool identifies itself as the data controller, but does not explicitly affirm that users own their data; GDPR-style controller language implies company stewardship, not user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy explicitly provides the right to request erasure of personal data and responds to requests within one month, meeting the deletion right standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained 'only for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes we collected it for' but does not specify any concrete retention period in days or months.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy mentions SSL encryption and limiting access to those with a business need to know, and references breach notification procedures, but does not detail a full security framework or specific technical controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states SSL/TLS encryption is used for transmission of personal information via the app.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Use and Privacy Policy make no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in the available Terms of Use or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The website mentions necessary and non-necessary (analytics/advertising) cookies with a consent opt-out option, but does not provide a detailed named list of each cookie and its specific purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy specifically names third parties: Adjust (advertising attribution), Google (analytics and cloud), Customer.io (email), and Apple/Google (payment processing).
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Third parties are named but the specific data elements shared with each one are described only at a category level (e.g., 'Technical Data' to Adjust and Google) rather than field-by-field disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The website offers a cookie opt-out for non-necessary cookies, and California residents may request an information sharing disclosure, but there is no clear universal opt-out from third-party data sharing for all users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states third parties 'will only process your personal data on our instructions and they are subject to a duty of confidentiality,' which is a general contractual statement but does not explicitly name a vendor agreement or DPA structure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not commit to notifying users when third-party processors or sharing arrangements change; it only states users can check the policy for updates.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: LetterSchool explicitly markets the app as 'without ads' and the privacy policy does not describe any in-app advertising to children.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising to users is described and the platform is marketed as ad-free; no evidence of behavioral targeting was found.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: While no in-app ads are served, data is shared with Adjust, an advertising attribution network, for tracking install/attribution purposes, with limited opt-out available only via cookie settings on the website.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Automated event logs, cookies, and data from Adjust (an advertising attribution network) are collected, creating some ambiguity about whether tracking extends beyond purely functional purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: California residents are offered an information sharing disclosure and opt-out mechanism, but a clear, universal, easily accessible opt-out from data sharing with advertising-related parties is not prominently described for all users.

r440.riskReason: LibraryTrac collects student PII including names, barcodes, and behavioral tracking data, but its combined ToS/PP document is not publicly accessible or fully indexable, leaving critical questions about data security, third-party sharing, advertising, data retention, COPPA compliance, and deletion rights unanswered.
r440.parentSummary: LibraryTrac is a school library tracking platform that collects students' names, student ID barcodes, library visit history, reasons for visits, teacher associations, IP addresses, and cookies to help librarians generate usage statistics. The platform does have a SDPC-standard Data Privacy Agreement available for school districts, which stipulates that student data remains the property of the school (LEA) and cannot be sold, but the publicly available combined Terms of Service and Privacy Policy document is not fully readable online, leaving many specific protections around security, third-party sharing, advertising, and data retention unclear or unverified for parents. Schools considering this platform should request and review the full DPA before deployment to understand the scope of protections in place.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The ToS/PP is hosted as a PDF at librarytrac-tos-pp.pdf but there is no publicly documented process for advance notification of policy changes or a publicly visible revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Product pages and the SDPC DPA indicate collection of student names, barcodes/IDs, IP addresses, and cookie data, but a comprehensive enumerated data list is not available in a publicly readable privacy policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The platform's FAQ and feature pages partially describe how data is entered (manual name entry or barcode scanning), but the privacy policy document itself is not fully accessible online to confirm a complete description of collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The SDPC Data Privacy Agreement executed by partner districts explicitly states student data remains the property of the LEA, but this protection is contract-dependent and not clearly stated in the public-facing privacy policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The FAQ notes an archival/management section that allows adding, editing, or deleting information from the Student Log, suggesting some deletion capability exists, but the privacy policy does not clearly articulate a user or parent data deletion right.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated in any publicly accessible document; the SDPC DPA has a three-year term but that governs the agreement duration, not data retention schedules.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, audit logs) are described in any publicly accessible portion of the ToS/PP document.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption at rest or in transit is found in any publicly accessible LibraryTrac policy or documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No information about password complexity enforcement or SSO integration is mentioned in any publicly available documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is found in any publicly accessible LibraryTrac documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The SDPC DPA reference document acknowledges use of cookies and IP addresses, but no detailed cookie policy listing cookie types, purposes, or opt-out mechanisms is publicly available.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No third-party vendors or subprocessors are named in any publicly accessible policy document; the SDPC DPA references subprocessors generically but does not enumerate them.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with each third party is available in any publicly accessible document.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in any publicly accessible document.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The SDPC DPA template (when executed) requires the provider to bind subprocessors to equivalent data protection obligations, but this protection exists only within executed contracts, not the public-facing policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No process for notifying schools or users of changes in third-party subprocessors is described in any publicly accessible document.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No statement about whether advertisements are displayed is found in any publicly accessible documentation, making compliance status indeterminate.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No statement prohibiting targeted advertising is found in any publicly accessible documentation; compliance cannot be confirmed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No statement about third-party tracking for advertising purposes or any opt-out mechanism is found in publicly accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookie usage is acknowledged in the SDPC DPA reference but no policy on web beacons or tracking methods for advertising is publicly documented.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described in any publicly accessible documentation.

dataCollected: Aggregate/anonymized usage data (resources accessed per school/district)
dataSharedWith: Successor entities in merger/acquisition (under equivalent privacy standards)
Authorized school users (teachers and administrators) for usage reporting
r441.riskReason: Lightbox Learning explicitly does not collect any personally identifiable student data, prohibits third-party targeted advertising, and expressly governs its practices under COPPA, FERPA, and SOPIPA.
r441.parentSummary: Lightbox Learning does not collect any personally identifiable information about students; only anonymized, aggregate usage data at the school or district level is collected for usage reporting purposes. The platform explicitly prohibits the sale or sharing of data for marketing or advertising and states compliance with FERPA, COPPA, and SOPIPA. The primary privacy concern is that the Terms of Service do not provide advance notice before changes take effect, requiring users to periodically check the page themselves.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use state Lightbox reserves the right to change terms at any time and that continued use constitutes acceptance, with no advance notification process and no published revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy specifically enumerates all data collected, clearly distinguishing between school administrator data, aggregate usage data, and technical/device data collected via tracking technologies, and explicitly confirms no student PII is collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states data is collected through administrator registration forms, cookies, web beacons, and similar tracking technologies during service use.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly address data ownership; while it states content on the Sites is owned by Lightbox, it does not clearly assert who owns the school or usage data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: School administrators can update account information, but the policy only vaguely references account modifications and does not provide a clear, comprehensive data deletion process for all collected data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data may be retained for a 'commercially reasonable time' after account termination for backup and audit purposes but does not provide a specific retention period in days or months.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy specifically lists SSL encryption, data encryption, firewalls, physical access controls, and strict administrative and technical procedures as security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states use of industry-standard SSL encryption technology for account registration and sign-up information, as well as general data encryption.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not address password strength requirements or enforcement of strong password policies for school administrator accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The privacy policy states that access to information is limited through user/password credentials and two-factor authentication for internal employees, though it is not explicitly clear whether end-user school accounts require MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies, web beacons, and similar tracking technologies and lists their general purposes, but does not provide a named list of each individual cookie or a dedicated cookie table with specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy broadly references sharing with law enforcement, successor entities, and authorized school users, but does not name specific third-party service providers or vendors used in operating the platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by circumstance (legal, merger, service operation) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared in each scenario.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Schools can update account settings and opt out of promotional emails, but no explicit opt-out mechanism for all third-party data sharing is described; no sharing occurs for marketing purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The merger/acquisition clause requires the new owner to maintain privacy standards 'no less stringent than our own,' but there is no explicit general vendor data processing agreement requirement stated for all third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Terms of Use reserve the right to change terms at any time without advance notice, and there is no explicit commitment to notify users specifically about changes to third-party data sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states that Lightbox does not permit third-party advertising networks to collect user information for targeted advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states it will never use Student Data for targeted advertising and does not conduct targeted advertising on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy explicitly prohibits third-party advertising networks from collecting information about user activity for targeted advertising, constituting a no-tracking posture for ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While the policy explicitly prohibits third-party ad tracking, it acknowledges collecting data via cookies and web beacons for functional and analytics purposes, making the full scope of tracking methods only partially enumerated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The policy clearly states data is never sold or shared with third parties for marketing purposes, effectively making opt-out unnecessary; users can also disable cookies via browser settings.

dataSharedWith: Third parties as required by law
r442.riskReason: Lightworks collects broad personal and financial data, uses cookies for interest-based advertising, shares data with third-party partners including Google, has no stated minimum age or COPPA/FERPA compliance language, and policy change notification relies solely on users checking the page themselves.
r442.parentSummary: Lightworks (lwks.com) collects a wide range of personal information including name, email, address, age, phone number, financial data, IP address, location, and behavioral/usage data, primarily to provide services and deliver interest-based advertising. The platform shares data with Google (via YouTube API integration) and partner companies for marketing, and policy updates are not proactively communicated to users. There are no COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance statements anywhere in the policy, and no minimum age requirement is stated, making this platform unsuitable for K-12 deployment without significant additional contractual safeguards.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states changes are made by 'updating this page' and instructs users to 'check this page frequently,' with no advance notification process or revision history provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: A broad list of collected data types is provided (name, address, email, phone, age, financial info, IP, location, usage data), but the policy language is not exhaustive and uses open-ended phrasing such as 'other information about yourself.'
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy describes some collection methods (forms, phone, email, live-chat, automated website collection), but lacks specificity about data collected via the desktop application itself or third-party SDK integrations.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not address user ownership of data; it implies company control over collected data with no explicit statement that users retain ownership of their personal information.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their LWKS account via the User Portal profile page, and GDPR rights including deletion are referenced, satisfying this criterion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated anywhere in the policy; there is no mention of how long personal data is kept after account deletion or contract termination.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy only states it will 'take all steps reasonably necessary' and acknowledges internet transmission is 'not completely secure,' without listing any specific technical security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of encryption is made; the policy acknowledges it cannot guarantee security and that transmission is 'at your own risk,' indicating no confirmed encryption standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No password strength requirements or enforcement policies are mentioned anywhere in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration options is made anywhere in the reviewed policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are mentioned and described at a general level (session, preference, interest-based advertising), but no complete list of cookies with individual purposes is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references Google (YouTube API) and unnamed 'partners' and 'suppliers,' but does not provide a complete named list of all third parties with whom data is shared.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify which data elements are shared with each named or unnamed third party; data sharing is described only in aggregate terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications via unsubscribe links and can revoke Google API access, but there is no clear opt-out for all third-party data sharing broadly.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states Google API use adheres to Google API Services User Data Policy, providing a partial contractual accountability reference, but no broad vendor agreement or data processing agreement language is stated for other third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention notifying users when third-party sharing relationships change; updates are handled only by posting a revised policy page without proactive user notification.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states cookies are used 'to provide interest-based advertising' and to 'deliver relevant advertising' based on user website activity, confirming ads are displayed to logged-in users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms that advertising may be targeted based on user activity on the website, which constitutes behavioral targeting of registered (potentially student) users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Users can adjust browser settings to refuse cookies, which provides a limited technical opt-out from tracking, but there is no dedicated opt-out mechanism for third-party ad tracking specifically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms cookies are used for interest-based advertising and to 'measure effectiveness of advertising,' but does not disclose specific web beacon or pixel tracking technologies in use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An unsubscribe option for marketing emails is provided, and browser-level cookie rejection is mentioned, but there is no clear dedicated process for opting out of data sharing with advertisers specifically.

dataCollected: Profile information (job title, work history, education)
Usage data (courses viewed, completed, learning history)

r443.riskReason: LinkedIn Learning is a professional networking platform with a minimum age of 16 that is not designed for K-12 students, collects extensive personal and behavioral data, uses it for targeted advertising and AI model training by default, shares data with Microsoft and advertising partners, and makes no explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance commitments in its public-facing policies.
r443.parentSummary: LinkedIn Learning collects a wide range of personal and behavioral data including name, email, usage/learning history, device data, and inferred attributes like age and industry, and uses this data to personalize content, target advertisements, and train AI models by default unless users opt out. Data is shared with Microsoft affiliates, advertising partners, and third-party service providers, and organizational administrators (such as school admins) can view student learning activity. LinkedIn Learning is designed for professionals aged 16 and older, has no stated COPPA or FERPA compliance commitments, and is not purpose-built for K-12 use, making it a high-risk platform for deployment with minors in a school setting.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: LinkedIn notifies users of material changes to the Privacy Policy and User Agreement (effective November 3, 2025 update was announced), but explicitly carves out cases—such as new product launches or legal changes—where advance notice will not be given.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy Policy provides a detailed and extensive list of data collected including profile data, usage data, device/network data, inferred data, cookies, payment information, and data received from third parties and employers/schools.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The Privacy Policy specifically describes how data is collected: directly from users, through cookies and tracking technologies, from employers/schools, from third-party partners, and via off-platform interactions with LinkedIn plugins and ads.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The User Agreement states 'your account belongs to you,' but LinkedIn claims broad rights to use personal data for advertising, AI model training, and sharing with affiliates, making effective ownership ambiguous in practice.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The Privacy Policy explicitly states users can request erasure or deletion of all or some personal data, and provides settings to manage, correct, or restrict data processing.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The Privacy Policy references data retention in general terms and mentions a 365-day retention for lead generation form data, but does not state a comprehensive, specific retention period for all user and learning data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: LinkedIn's security page lists specific measures including TLS encryption in transit, AES encryption at rest, cryptographic password hashing, intrusion detection, firewalls, penetration testing, and threat modeling.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: LinkedIn explicitly uses TLS for data in transit and AES for data at rest, and stores only cryptographic hashes of passwords, indicating robust encryption throughout.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: LinkedIn's User Agreement advises users to use a strong password and keep it confidential, but does not state that strong passwords are technically enforced at the platform level.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: LinkedIn offers two-factor authentication (2FA) as an available security option, and enterprise/organizational deployments can use SSO, satisfying this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: LinkedIn maintains a detailed Cookie Policy and a Cookie Table listing specific cookies and their purposes, including functional, analytics, and advertising cookies used by LinkedIn and third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy broadly names Microsoft, LinkedIn Ireland, Bing, and advertising partners as recipients of data, but does not provide a comprehensive named list of all third-party service providers used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Privacy Policy groups data sharing by category of recipient (affiliates, advertisers, service providers) rather than specifying exactly what data is shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of targeted advertising and data use for AI model training via settings, but opting out of all third-party data sharing (e.g., with Microsoft affiliates) is not fully available and requires navigating multiple settings.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Privacy Policy states LinkedIn seeks contractual requirements for advertising partners regarding consent, and references controls designed to protect privacy when working with research partners, but does not provide a broad, explicit vendor agreement commitment for all third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: LinkedIn notifies users of material changes to data sharing practices through Privacy Policy updates, but explicitly reserves the right to update without advance notice in certain circumstances such as new product launches.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: LinkedIn explicitly targets ads to Members and Visitors on and off its services using profile data, usage history, cookies, device identifiers, and data from advertising partners, which is confirmed in the Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: LinkedIn confirms it uses member profile data, learning history, usage data, inferred attributes (age, industry, seniority), and advertising partner data to deliver targeted advertising to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Users can opt out of ad targeting via settings and LinkedIn states it offers controls for cookie-based ad tracking, but third-party advertising partners can still identify users through cookies when viewing or clicking ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: LinkedIn's Privacy Policy and Cookie Policy confirm the use of pixels, ad tags (LinkedIn Insight Tag), cookies, and device identifiers for advertising measurement and targeting both on and off the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: LinkedIn provides an opt-out for targeted advertising and for data used for AI model training, but the process requires navigating multiple settings pages and the opt-out is not prominently surfaced or straightforward.

Schools and parents should request the full policy documents directly from LINKtivity Learning before deploying this tool in K-12 classrooms.

r445.riskReason: Lino (linoit.com) displays advertisements to free-tier users, stores data in Japan with cross-border transfer consent buried in ToS, lacks an explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance statement, has no dedicated K-12 or student data privacy policy, and its privacy policy is hosted on a separate parent-company domain (infoteria.com) that may no longer be actively maintained.
r445.parentSummary: Lino (linoit.com) is a Japanese web-based sticky-note platform that collects account registration data (username, email, password) and all user-generated content such as notes, images, and files. Free-tier users are shown advertisements related to their posted content, and data is stored and managed in Japan or wherever Infoteria has facilities, meaning student data may be transferred internationally. The platform explicitly limits use to users aged 13 and older but provides no parental consent mechanism, no COPPA or FERPA compliance declaration, and no dedicated student data protection commitments, making it a high-risk choice for K-12 classroom use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The ToS states users will be notified of important changes via their registered email address, but no revision history or versioned policy archive is provided, and the company reserves the right to amend terms unilaterally at any time.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The ToS references that account registration requires 'identifying information and contact information,' and user-generated content is explicitly mentioned, but a comprehensive enumerated list of all data types collected is not provided in a single consolidated document.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The ToS generally indicates data is collected during registration and service use, but does not specifically describe all collection methods such as cookies, server logs, or behavioral tracking in the accessible English-language policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The ToS states Infoteria shall not use user contents for any purpose other than providing the service, implying some user ownership, but does not explicitly declare that users own their data, leaving ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete individual canvases and stickies via the interface, but there is no stated process for requesting full account and personal data deletion, and accounts inactive for 6 months may be reassigned without notice.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The ToS references a 6-month account inactivity threshold after which accounts may be invalidated, providing a vague reference to data lifecycle, but no explicit retention period for personal data or user content is stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy and ToS contain no specific description of technical security measures (e.g., encryption at rest, access controls, vulnerability management) used to protect user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site historically used HTTP (not HTTPS) for its main domain, and user reviews noted the absence of a browser security lock; no explicit encryption policy is documented, indicating a failure to confirm encryption throughout.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: There is no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords in the ToS or any help documentation; only basic password management responsibility is placed on the user.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication option is mentioned, and while OpenID/SSO login (e.g., Yahoo ID) is supported as an alternative login method, it is not framed as a security control and MFA is never discussed.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy is provided on the linoit.com or associated infoteria.com privacy pages; there is no enumeration of cookies used, their purposes, or any opt-out mechanism for non-essential cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The ToS vaguely references advertisers and the Infoteria group of companies as potential recipients of data, but does not name specific third-party vendors, analytics providers, or advertising networks by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data elements are shared with each category of third party is provided; the policy only states that personally identifiable information will not be sold to advertisers, without further granularity.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described; acceptance of the ToS (required to use the service) constitutes blanket consent to advertisements being displayed and data being transferred internationally.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The ToS does not include any contractual language requiring third-party recipients of user data to adhere to equivalent data protection standards or a vendor data processing agreement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no stated process for notifying users when third-party relationships change; the ToS allows Infoteria to amend terms at its own discretion, meaning third-party changes could occur without specific advance notice.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The ToS explicitly states that as a condition of free service use, advertisements related to user content will be displayed, confirming ads are shown to free-tier users including potential student accounts.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The ToS states that user content shall not be read to refine advertising targeting without consent, but ads are still displayed based on 'related contents,' suggesting at minimum contextual targeting tied to user-generated content.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No information is provided about whether third-party ad networks place tracking technologies (cookies, pixels, beacons) on users' devices, and no opt-out for such tracking is described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy and ToS do not address web beacons, tracking pixels, or similar ad-tech tracking methods, leaving their use entirely undisclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There is no described opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers; free users must accept advertising as a condition of service with no documented way to opt out while retaining free account access.

r446.riskReason: Literably collects sensitive biometric-adjacent audio recordings of minors and the TOS (last updated May 2019) is significantly outdated, creating gaps in transparency around current security practices, cookie usage, and third-party subprocessor details.
r446.parentSummary: Literably collects student names, audio recordings of students reading aloud, and reading performance data in order to provide literacy assessments to schools. The platform operates under a school-official model consistent with FERPA, meaning the school or district takes responsibility for obtaining appropriate consent, and Literably contractually commits to treating student data as confidential and not selling it. However, the Terms of Service have not been updated since May 2019, the privacy policy does not enumerate specific security measures or provide a detailed cookie inventory, and the third-party subprocessors used to process student audio are not individually named, which may concern privacy-conscious parents and administrators.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service indicate Literably may update the agreement and users should check periodically, but no advance notification process or versioned revision history is explicitly described; the TOS itself has not been publicly updated since May 8, 2019.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy references collection of student data and personal information including audio recordings and performance data, but does not present a comprehensive, enumerated list of every data type collected across all user roles.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The TOS states data is collected directly from students 'at the direction of' educators and institutions and via the platform's recording functionality, but the privacy policy does not fully detail all collection mechanisms (e.g., cookies, server logs, third-party SDKs).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The TOS explicitly states that as between Literably and the Educational Institution, the Educational Institution owns all right, title, and interest to all Student Data, and Literably does not claim ownership of student data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The TOS and privacy policy allow educational institutions to request deletion of student data, but the process is not clearly self-service for parents or students, and no specific timeline or procedure for individual deletion requests is documented in the publicly available policies.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not specify explicit data retention periods for different categories of data; while there is an implied retention tied to service provision, no concrete timeframes (e.g., 'data deleted within X days of account termination') are stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy references that Literably takes reasonable measures to protect data, but does not enumerate specific technical or organizational security controls such as encryption standards, access controls, or audit practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS, indicating data is encrypted in transit, but the privacy policy does not explicitly confirm encryption at rest or describe the encryption methods used for stored student audio recordings and assessment data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Account access is managed through school rostering systems and Clever SSO integration, which typically enforces institutional password policies, effectively meeting this requirement through SSO rather than standalone password enforcement.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Literably supports Clever single sign-on (SSO) for teacher and student login, which provides institutional-level authentication controls equivalent to or better than standalone MFA for the K-12 school context.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy does not provide a specific cookie policy or enumerate the cookies used on the platform with their purposes; only a general acknowledgment of data collection practices is present.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The TOS and privacy policy acknowledge use of third-party service providers and subcontractors but do not name specific third parties (e.g., cloud hosting providers, analytics services) used to process student data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policies state data is shared with third parties only as needed to provide the service, but do not itemize which specific data categories are shared with which specific third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: There is no clearly documented opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing for parents or students; control is delegated to the educational institution, with no individual-level opt-out process described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The TOS states that Literably treats student data as confidential and does not share it with third parties except as described in the agreement, implying contractual obligations are placed on service providers, meeting the spirit of this requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policies do not explicitly commit to notifying schools or users when third-party subprocessors are added or changed; the general policy update mechanism is vague and does not specifically address third-party changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: There is no indication in any Literably policy or platform documentation that advertisements are displayed to students or teachers within the platform; the service is sold directly to schools on a per-student subscription basis.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No evidence of targeted advertising practices exists in Literably's policies or public documentation; the platform's revenue model is subscription-based with no advertising component.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policies do not reference use of third-party advertising trackers or behavioral tracking for ad purposes, and the platform's school-focused, subscription-based model does not involve ad network integrations.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While the platform does not engage in advertising tracking, the privacy policy does not fully enumerate all tracking technologies (cookies, pixels, analytics scripts) used on the site, leaving some ambiguity about non-advertising data collection methods.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because Literably does not engage in advertising or share data with advertisers, no opt-out of advertiser data sharing is necessary, and this requirement is effectively met by the absence of any such data sharing practice.
