r516.parentSummary: Nitro Type collects registration information such as username, email, zip code, age, and optional full name, as well as usage and cookie/tracking data, and shares this data with third-party advertising companies that may target users across other websites and apps. Advertisements are shown to all users including children under 13 by default, and the only way to remove ads is to pay for a Gold membership — though it is unclear whether paid accounts also remove third-party tracking. Parents should be aware that the Terms of Service can be changed without notice, data sale practices are not clearly disclosed, and the platform has received a 'Warning' rating from Common Sense Media for advertising and data-sharing practices.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service explicitly state they may be updated 'without notice,' and no revision history is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Registration data types (email, zip code, age, occupation, username) are partially listed, but behavioral and tracking data collection details are vague or unclear.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected via registration forms and social login, but specific technical collection methods (cookies, trackers, analytics SDKs) are only generally described.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Users are noted to retain ownership and can access/export their data, but ownership language is not explicit or prominent in the policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can access, edit, modify, and export personal information at any time through the service, satisfying a full deletion/control standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated in the accessible policy text; the retention policy is described as unclear by independent evaluators.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states security measures exist to protect against loss, misuse, and alteration, but does not enumerate specific technical or organizational controls beyond password hashing.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Passwords are hashed with salted encryption, but broader data-in-transit and data-at-rest encryption practices are not clearly described.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Passwords require a minimum of 6 characters but there is no evidence of enforced complexity rules or strong password requirements beyond minimum length.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration for K-12 institutional login is mentioned in the policy; social login is supported but not MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy references cookies and third-party trackers generally but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies with their specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy acknowledges use of third-party advertising companies and social login providers but does not name specific advertising or analytics vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what data is shared with each individual third party; data sharing is described only at a category level.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications, and a method to opt out of some third-party tracking is mentioned, but the process is not clearly described or easy to find.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No explicit contractual obligation requiring third-party vendors to adhere to equivalent privacy standards or a data processing agreement is stated in the policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The TOS states it can be updated without notice, which implies users would not be proactively notified of changes to third-party relationships.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Advertisements are displayed to all users by default, including children under 13, and can only be removed via a paid Gold membership upgrade.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Third-party advertising companies are stated to serve ads and may target users on other websites and applications based on their data, constituting behavioral targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party trackers are present on the site and it is unclear whether the paid Gold account removes these trackers; no clear opt-out from tracking is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Numerous third-party trackers are used on the platform for advertising purposes, and it is not confirmed that removing ads via Gold membership also removes these tracking mechanisms.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of marketing email communications, but no clear process exists to opt out specifically of data sharing with advertisers or ad targeting.

dataSharedWith: Advertising companies and networks (anonymized/aggregate data only)
Third-party service providers acting on Pearson's behalf
Law enforcement or courts as required by law
r517.riskReason: NNAT3 is operated by Pearson via a password-restricted platform with stated encryption and no direct student data sales, but the policy permits sharing anonymized data with advertising networks, uses web beacons for tracking, allows policy changes without advance notice, and students/parents cannot directly request deletion from Pearson — all of which present moderate K-12 compliance concerns.
r517.parentSummary: NNAT3 is a K-12 gifted ability assessment administered through Pearson's CAP platform (view.pearsonassessments.com), which collects sensitive student data including name, date of birth, grade, ethnicity, IEP status, and assessment scores on behalf of school districts. Pearson states it does not sell personal data and uses SSL encryption to protect transmissions, but it reserves the right to share anonymized data with advertising networks and can update its privacy policy at any time without advance notice, accepting continued use as consent. Parents and students cannot request data deletion directly from Pearson — all such requests must go through the student's school or district.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Pearson reserves the right to change the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy at any time, with continued use constituting acceptance — no advance notification process or revision history is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The CAP platform policy lists broad categories of data collected (student name, DOB, gender, grade, ethnicity, IEP status, scores, IP address, device info) but the platform-specific policy PDF was not publicly accessible, leaving completeness uncertain.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected via user submission by school personnel and through cookies/web beacons, but does not comprehensively specify all automated collection mechanisms in one place.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The education agency and school district are positioned as data owners/controllers with Pearson acting as a service provider/data processor, but this is not clearly stated in plain language for parents or students.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Students and parents cannot request deletion directly from Pearson; all requests are redirected to the student's educational institution, making full user-initiated deletion only partially available.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Pearson states data is retained as long as customers require, with a general retention statement referencing customer-configurable parameters — specific retention periods are not defined, making this only a general statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Pearson explicitly states it uses operational, administrative, technical, and physical security safeguards to protect personal data, with specific mention of SSL encryption and secured data centers.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Pearson states it encrypts all transmission of sensitive data using SSL/TLS and encrypts data at rest in secured repositories, meeting encryption standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform uses password-based access restricted by education agency authorization; no explicit strong password enforcement policy is stated, but SSO via Clever is also supported, partially meeting this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: NNAT3 supports SSO through Clever Instant Login with Clever Secure Sync for roster provisioning, which provides an SSO-equivalent authentication mechanism meeting this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are mentioned and a general cookie policy exists on pearson.com, but the CAP assessment platform policy does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies with individual purposes specific to the NNAT3 platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Pearson mentions sharing with affiliated companies, subcontractors, education agencies, and advertising networks (for anonymized data), but does not name specific third-party vendors used in the NNAT3 platform context.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing broadly by recipient category (subcontractors, affiliates, advertisers for anonymized data) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An opt-out for cookie-based data sharing is available via Pearson's Cookie Preferences Management Tool, but no opt-out exists for school-directed data sharing since that is part of the contractual assessment service.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Pearson states subcontractors are obligated to protect personal data, and education agency contracts govern authorized use — but a formal, explicit vendor agreement clause binding all sub-processors is not clearly articulated in the public policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states Pearson may update the privacy policy periodically without notice and that continued use constitutes acceptance, meaning users are not proactively notified of changes to third-party sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The NNAT3 CAP platform is a password-restricted assessment tool; no advertisements are displayed within the student-facing or educator-facing platform itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is conducted within the NNAT3 platform; Pearson states it does not currently enable third-party targeted advertising cookies on the clinical assessment site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: While no targeted advertising cookies are enabled on the clinical site, Pearson's general policy acknowledges that third-party tracking technologies and anonymized data may be shared with advertising networks, creating a limited opt-out scenario.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Pearson uses web beacons and similar tracking technologies for usage tracking and marketing campaign measurement, though these are described as functional and analytical rather than ad-targeting on the assessment platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Pearson's cookie policy offers a Cookie Preferences Management Tool to opt out of non-essential cookies and data sharing with advertisers, but this mechanism is on the general Pearson site and not clearly linked from the NNAT3-specific platform.

dataSharedWith: Certifying organizations and agencies (upon earned certification)
Business transaction successors (in case of business transfer)
r518.riskReason: NOCTI explicitly references FERPA compliance and does not sell personal data, but the privacy policy and terms of service are combined on one page, no dedicated terms-of-service URL was found, specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards) are not disclosed, data is retained for up to 10 years for secondary students with only anonymization (not deletion) as the standard removal path, and third-party sharing with certifying agencies lacks granular detail.
r518.parentSummary: NOCTI collects student contact information, assessment responses, scores, and demographic data to deliver and score CTE (Career and Technical Education) assessments for secondary students. The platform states it does not sell personal information, reports scores to schools and districts under FERPA, and shares limited data with certifying agencies only when a student has earned a certification. Parents should be aware that student data is retained for up to 10 years before anonymization, and full deletion upon request is replaced with anonymization rather than permanent erasure.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The data retention policy notes changes become effective upon publication to the website without advance user notification, so while a revision process exists, advance notice to users is not guaranteed.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates specific categories of data collected including contact information, assessment-related information, transactional data, and website interaction data (IP address, cookies).
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy explains data is collected directly from users during account setup and testing, automatically via website interaction, and through ordering and fulfillment processes.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; NOCTI acts as a data processor under FERPA, which implies the school/district retains ownership, but this is not clearly articulated for individual students.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Upon written request, NOCTI will anonymize data rather than fully delete it, which constitutes limited deletion; full permanent erasure is not offered as an option.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The data retention policy explicitly states individually identifiable score-related data is retained for up to 10 years for secondary students before anonymization, which is a clear and specific retention period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states NOCTI 'has rigorous security systems and processes in place' but does not enumerate specific technical measures such as encryption standards, firewalls, or access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of end-to-end encryption or specific encryption protocols (e.g., TLS, AES) is found in the publicly available policy documents, though the platform uses HTTPS.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform uses password-protected portals with access restricted to approved personnel, but no explicit policy on enforcing strong password requirements (length, complexity) for student accounts is stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The student login portal references SSO (Single Sign On) options including state-based SSO (e.g., West Virginia Student SSO), which satisfies the SSO/LTI standard for this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A cookie policy exists and mentions cookies are used with a consent banner on first visit, but it does not enumerate all individual cookies by name and purpose as a fully detailed cookie inventory.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy broadly refers to certifying organizations and agencies, researchers, and remote proctoring providers (ProctorU mentioned elsewhere), but does not provide a comprehensive named list of all third-party service providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states certifying agencies receive only information needed for certification purposes, but does not provide a granular data-field-level breakdown of what is shared with each specific third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No clear opt-out mechanism for third-party sharing is described; sharing with certifying agencies is tied to the student's certification relationship, with no general opt-out option provided in the policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy requires certifying organizations to sign a Data Share Agreement ensuring protection of assessment-related data, which satisfies the vendor agreement requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The data retention policy states changes are effective upon posting without explicit advance notification to users about changes to third-party sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: There is no indication of advertising on the NOCTI platform; it is an assessment-focused service with no mention of ads anywhere in the policy or platform documentation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is mentioned or implied in any policy documents; personal data is explicitly stated to not be used to target or profile individuals.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy states research results do not contain identifiable personal information and are not used to target or profile individuals, indicating no third-party ad tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies are described as functional navigation aids with no mention of tracking pixels, web beacons, or advertising-related tracking technologies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or data sharing with advertisers exists on the platform, there is no need for an opt-out, and this criterion is satisfied by the absence of such practices.

r519.riskReason: The platform lacks any COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance statements, has no minimum age requirement, reserves the right to change Terms without notice, claims ownership of service rights broadly, and does not explicitly prohibit the sale or targeted use of student data.
r519.parentSummary: Notepad (usenotepad.com) collects account information such as name and email, usage data, and content you create on the platform, and shares some of this with unspecified hosting and third-party service partners. The platform does not mention COPPA or FERPA compliance, does not specify a minimum age, and its Terms of Service can be changed at any time without prior notice to users. Schools and parents should exercise significant caution before allowing students to use this platform.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service explicitly state that Notepad reserves the right to update Terms at any time without notice, and no revision history or advance notification process is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy (linked from TOS at usenotepad.com) partially describes data collected such as account information and usage data, but the full policy content was not directly accessible for comprehensive review, leaving gaps in what is fully enumerated.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The TOS references a privacy policy for data collection details but provides only a general statement about how data is collected; no specific collection mechanisms (e.g., cookies, forms, APIs) are detailed in the accessible TOS text.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The TOS states 'Notepad owns all legal rights in the Service,' which raises significant concern about data ownership; user ownership of their own data is not clearly affirmed.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No deletion rights, data portability, or account deletion process is described in the accessible TOS or privacy policy content; users have no stated mechanism to delete their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated in the accessible TOS or privacy policy; the policy is silent on how long user or student data is retained.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No specific security measures (e.g., encryption at rest, access controls, security audits) are described in the accessible TOS or privacy policy text.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (in transit or at rest) was found in the accessible portions of the TOS or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No password strength requirements or enforcement policy is mentioned in the TOS or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in any accessible policy document.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy or list of cookies with their purposes was found in the accessible TOS or privacy policy content.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The TOS vaguely references 'third parties (e.g., hosting partners)' but does not name specific third-party vendors or provide a complete list.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with each named or unnamed third party is provided in the accessible policy documents.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in the TOS or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The TOS mentions third parties are used for hosting purposes, implying a service relationship, but no explicit data processing agreement or third-party compliance obligation is stated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The TOS states changes can be made at any time without notice, meaning third-party relationships could change with no obligation to notify users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: It is not stated whether the platform displays advertisements; however, given the subscription model referenced in the TOS, advertising may not be the revenue model, but this is not explicitly confirmed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No statement is made prohibiting targeted advertising or behavioral tracking; the policy is silent on this matter, which is a red flag for K-12 use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No mention of third-party tracking technologies for advertising purposes or any opt-out mechanism is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No disclosure of web beacons, pixel tags, or other tracking methods is made in any accessible policy document.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described; the policy is entirely silent on advertiser data sharing opt-outs.

dataSharedWith: University of Cambridge internal computer security teams
Third-party embedded content providers (e.g., YouTube, Podbean)
Law enforcement / governmental authorities (when legally required)
r520.riskReason: NRICH is a low-data, free academic platform operated by the University of Cambridge with no ads and no account required for most use, but it uses Google Analytics, allows third-party social/marketing cookies via embedded content (YouTube, Podbean), does not explicitly address COPPA or FERPA compliance, provides no minimum age restriction, and its Terms and Conditions reserve the right to change policies without advance user notification.
r520.parentSummary: NRICH (nrich.maths.org) is a free, open-access math resource from the University of Cambridge that does not require students to create an account to use most of its content; it automatically logs basic server data (IP addresses, device info) and uses Google Analytics with anonymized data for site improvement. Third-party cookies from embedded providers like YouTube may be set when students interact with embedded videos, and those cookies are governed by the third parties' own privacy policies outside Cambridge's control. No advertising is displayed by NRICH itself, no student data appears to be sold, and data is retained for up to two years for server logs, but the platform does not make explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance claims, which schools should evaluate before deploying with students under 13.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms and Conditions state that the University reserves the right to change terms and that users are responsible for reviewing changes, with no advance notification process or revision history published.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists server log data, form submissions, correspondence, and Google Analytics data, but does not comprehensively enumerate all data types (e.g., cookie identifiers and third-party tracking data are only addressed in a separate cookies page).
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that data is automatically logged and collected via forms and Google Analytics, but does not specify in detail the technical mechanisms for each data type collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states that by supplying information users consent to the University holding and using it, implying University ownership/control, but does not explicitly clarify that users retain ownership of their own data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No user-facing data deletion process or right to erasure is described anywhere in the NRICH privacy policy or terms; there is no mechanism for users to request deletion of their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy explicitly states that logged server information may be kept for up to two years, satisfying the requirement for a stated retention period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy mentions server-side security logging and refers users to a cookie policy, but does not enumerate specific technical security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls) protecting personal data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site is served over HTTPS (as indicated by the policy referencing https://nrich.maths.org URLs), but no explicit statement about encryption of stored data or data in transit is made in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account is required for the vast majority of NRICH content, effectively eliminating password risk for most users; optional registration (for solution submission) is not detailed regarding password requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required for standard use of the platform, which eliminates MFA concerns for most users; no MFA details are provided for optional registered accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The cookies policy lists essential and analytics cookies and mentions social/marketing cookies from third parties (YouTube, Podbean), but does not provide a full enumerated list of every specific cookie name and its purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy names Google (Google Analytics) and University of Cambridge security teams, and the cookies page references YouTube and Podbean as third-party embedded content providers, but does not name all third-party recipients comprehensively.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared with Google as analytics data and references that third-party embedded content providers receive interaction data, but does not specify exactly what data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can disable cookies via browser settings to limit some third-party tracking, but the policy notes this may break site functionality; there is no explicit opt-out mechanism for Google Analytics or embedded third-party tracking within the site itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy does not state that third-party recipients (e.g., Google, YouTube) are contractually required to protect user data in accordance with NRICH's or Cambridge's standards; it simply refers users to consult those third parties' own policies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Terms and Conditions do not commit to notifying users of changes in third-party data-sharing arrangements; the University simply states users are responsible for reviewing changes themselves.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: NRICH does not display advertising on its platform; it is a free, open-access educational resource with no commercial advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is conducted by NRICH itself; Google Analytics data is anonymized before use, and no behavioral targeting for ads is described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party providers such as YouTube may set marketing cookies and track users when embedded content is interacted with, and the policy acknowledges this is outside Cambridge's control with limited opt-out options (browser-level cookie blocking only).
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookies policy acknowledges that social/marketing cookies from embedded third-party content (YouTube, Podbean) may be set upon user interaction, but does not detail all web beacon or pixel tracking methods that may be in use by those third parties.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There is no clear opt-out mechanism provided by NRICH for users to opt out of data sharing with third-party providers like Google or YouTube; users are directed to consult those providers' own policies independently.

r521.riskReason: The app collects highly sensitive health and biometric data — including audiological performance, GPS location, and Remote Check clinical test results — from children as young as 6 under parental consent only; it is a medical device companion app with no K-12 FERPA/SOPIPA compliance statements, no explicit prohibition on selling or repurposing student health data for commercial use, and its privacy documentation does not address school or educational deployment contexts.
r521.parentSummary: The Nucleus Smart App, developed by Cochlear Ltd, collects sensitive hearing health data including sound processor usage, hearing tracker metrics, GPS location (when a device is lost), and clinical Remote Check test results that are transmitted to the Cochlear Cloud and shared with your child's clinician. Children under the specified age threshold require a parent or guardian to create their Cochlear Account and provide consent. While Cochlear states it does not sell personal information and implements technical and organizational security measures, the privacy policy does not explicitly address K-12 educational contexts, FERPA, or SOPIPA, and data may be shared with Cochlear Group affiliates, analytics providers, and third parties in the event of a corporate transaction.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Cochlear's Terms of Use reserve the right to update policies by posting a revised version on their websites, but do not commit to advance individual notification or maintaining a public revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Global Privacy Notice lists several categories of data collected (account info, hearing health data, analytical/cookie data, location, device info) but the enumeration is not exhaustive and some categories are described only in general terms.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy notice broadly states data is collected directly from users during account setup and automatically during app use, but does not fully specify each technical method (e.g., SDK telemetry, Bluetooth event logging) used to capture hearing device data.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Cochlear's policy is silent on explicit user data ownership; data is processed by Cochlear for service delivery and legitimate business purposes, leaving ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents and carers may request deletion of a child's personal information by contacting Cochlear, and account closure is supported (taking up to 10 days), but there is no self-service deletion tool and some data may be retained by law.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy notice states data is retained only as long as necessary for stated purposes and as required by law, but does not specify concrete retention periods (e.g., number of days or years) for different data categories.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Cochlear states it implements 'technical, organisational and administrative measures' to protect personal information and uses de-identification and aggregation where practical, but does not enumerate specific technical safeguards (e.g., AES-256 encryption, SOC 2).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Data Sync to the Cochlear Cloud is referenced, and the company claims security measures are in place, but the privacy notice does not explicitly confirm end-to-end or in-transit/at-rest encryption standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The app's user guide recommends using a strong password for Cochlear accounts and advises users not to share credentials, but the policy does not confirm enforcement of strong password rules at registration.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is found in the privacy policy or terms of use; login is via email and password only.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cochlear's privacy notice acknowledges the use of cookies, web beacons, Ad-IDs, and other tracking technologies, but a dedicated, itemized cookie policy listing each cookie by name and purpose was not found on the nucleussmartapp.com domain.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy notice references sharing with Cochlear Group affiliates, clinicians, analytics providers (Google Analytics), and payment processors (Stripe) by name or category, but does not provide a complete named list of all third-party sub-processors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Specific data shared with each named third party (e.g., Stripe receives payment info, clinicians receive Remote Check results) can be partially inferred from context, but the policy does not present a structured per-party data mapping.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No clear opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing (beyond contacting Cochlear directly) is described in the accessible policy text; data sharing with clinicians is integral to app functionality and cannot be opted out of without losing core features.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy notice states that in corporate transactions the acquiring company's use of data remains subject to the existing notice, and contractual arrangements with group companies are implied, but explicit data processing agreements with all third parties are not confirmed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Cochlear reserves the right to update the privacy notice by posting changes on its website without committing to proactively notifying users of changes to third-party sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No evidence of advertising or ad networks was found in the Nucleus Smart App; the app is a medical device companion tool with no advertising functionality.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The app does not appear to use targeted behavioral advertising; the privacy notice states Cochlear does not sell personal information, and the app's purpose is clinical hearing management.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google Analytics is used on Cochlear's websites, and the privacy notice acknowledges that analytics providers may combine data across sites, but an opt-out mechanism (e.g., Google Analytics opt-out link) is referenced in some Cochlear web contexts though not confirmed for the app itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy notice acknowledges use of cookies, web beacons, and Ad-IDs for analytical purposes on Cochlear's web properties, but it is unclear whether these tracking technologies operate within the Nucleus Smart App itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can contact Cochlear to exercise privacy rights, and some analytics opt-out options are referenced, but a clear, dedicated opt-out mechanism specifically for data sharing with analytics or advertising-adjacent vendors is not prominently documented.

r522.riskReason: NVDA is a free, open-source, locally installed screen reader that does not collect any personally identifiable information from the software itself, requires no account or registration, displays no ads, and all optional telemetry can be fully disabled by the user.
r522.parentSummary: NVDA (NonVisual Desktop Access) is a free, open-source screen reader for Windows developed by NV Access, an Australian nonprofit. The software itself collects no personally identifiable information — all optional usage statistics and update checks can be disabled entirely, and nothing the screen reader reads on screen is ever sent anywhere. The only personal data NV Access may collect is voluntarily provided information such as email addresses for mailing lists or donation details processed through PayPal, and no data is sold or used for advertising purposes.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy does not describe a formal advance-notification process for policy changes, nor is a revision history or versioning system mentioned, though the policy is publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy clearly lists all categories of data that may be collected — including update-check telemetry, IP address, website visit metadata, voluntarily submitted email/contact info, and health information — and explicitly states that no PII is collected by the NVDA software itself.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically explains how data is collected: via the optional automatic update check, voluntary form submission, email contact, PayPal donations, and website server logs.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Because NVDA requires no account and collects no PII through the software, user data ownership is a non-issue for the core product; the policy does not claim company ownership of user data and data collection is minimal and opt-in.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy does not provide a defined process for users to request deletion of their personal data; users who contact the organization may be removed from mailing lists, but no formal deletion mechanism is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not specify any data retention periods for any category of data collected, including website logs, email addresses, or donation records.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states that NV Access takes 'best care possible' to protect information and references organizational IT Risk Management Policies, but does not enumerate specific technical security measures applied to collected data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The corporate/government page confirms data sent via the optional update check is transmitted over SSL using TLS v1.2, but the policy does not address encryption of data at rest or for all data types (e.g., email correspondence).
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account or registration is required to use NVDA, so strong password enforcement is not applicable; this criteria is effectively met by the no-account-required design.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: NVDA requires no account or login of any kind, making MFA a non-issue and satisfying the intent of this requirement by eliminating the attack surface entirely.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy does not include a cookie policy, does not list cookies by name or purpose, and does not reference any cookie consent mechanism for the nvaccess.org website.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy broadly references 'service providers and volunteers' such as marketing and fundraising consultants and PayPal as recipients of data, but does not name specific third-party companies beyond PayPal.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: PayPal's data sharing is described (name, email, postal address shared back to NV Access; financial details not shared), but data shared with other unnamed service providers and consultants is described only in general terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications and mailing lists via unsubscribe links or by contacting NV Access directly, and the NVDA software's optional telemetry can be fully disabled; no third-party data sharing for advertising exists.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states personal information is shared with service providers only as necessary for their tasks, but does not explicitly state that these third parties are contractually bound to data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not describe any process by which users would be notified if new third-party data-sharing arrangements are introduced.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No advertisements of any kind are displayed in the NVDA software or on the NV Access website; the organization is a nonprofit funded by donations and grants.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no targeted advertising of any kind associated with NVDA or the NV Access platform; user data is not used for ad targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: There is no third-party ad tracking associated with NVDA; the software is locally installed and the website does not reference any ad tracking partnerships.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacons or ad-related tracking methods are referenced or identified in the privacy policy; only functional server log data is mentioned for the website.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There is no data sharing with advertisers at all, so no opt-out mechanism is needed; this is fully satisfied by the absence of any advertising relationships.

dataCollected: Social media profile data (via Twitter, Facebook, LinkedIn referrals)
dataSharedWith: Online session platforms (Google Meet, Zoom, Skype)

r523.riskReason: The platform serves K-12 students including those under 13 with only basic parental consent language, lacks a Terms of Service, does not specify encryption or formal security measures, reserves the right to update policies without notice, and relies on third-party platforms (Zoom, Skype) whose own data practices are not governed by O.W.L.'s policy.
r523.parentSummary: O.W.L. Educational Services collects contact information, payment data (handled by third-party processors like Stripe or PayPal), and personal details such as learning styles to customize services. For children under 18, the platform states it requires parental or guardian permission before collecting or using personal information, and parents may request to review or delete their child's data by contacting the company directly. However, the platform warns that policy updates may occur without notice, does not publish a separate Terms of Service, and online tutoring sessions may run through external tools like Zoom or Skype, which fall outside O.W.L.'s privacy protections.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy explicitly states updates may be made 'without notice' and only recommends users check the site periodically, with no advance notification process or revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data types (contact info, payment info, personal interests, learning styles, social media referral data) but does not provide a comprehensive, exhaustive enumeration of all data collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that data is collected when users 'use the site or reach out' or via third-party social platforms, but does not detail specific collection methods such as forms, cookies, or session tracking.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is not explicitly addressed; the policy describes how data is used and protected but neither affirms user ownership nor explicitly claims company ownership, leaving this ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents can request deletion of a child's data by contacting O.W.L. via email or phone, but there is no self-service deletion mechanism and the process requires manual verification, representing a limited deletion pathway.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated anywhere in the policy; there is no mention of how long collected data is stored or when it is purged.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states data is 'held securely and confidentially' with access limited to employees who need it, but no specific security measures (e.g., firewalls, access controls, audits) are described.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly acknowledges that 'transmission of information via the internet is not completely secure' and any transmission is 'at your own risk,' with no mention of encryption being used.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not mention password requirements, strong password enforcement, or any account security standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in the policy or on the site.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are mentioned with a brief definition and the ability to accept or decline them, but no list of specific cookies, their purposes, or categories is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third-party payment processors (Stripe, PayPal, banks) and online session tools (Zoom, Skype, Google Talk) are named, but no other third parties are disclosed, leaving the full list incomplete.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Payment data shared with payment processors is implied, but the policy does not specify what data is shared with each named third party (e.g., session platforms like Zoom) beyond general caution to users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users may opt out of marketing data processing by contacting O.W.L. in writing, but there is no clear opt-out process for data shared with third-party processors or session platforms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not state that third-party vendors are contractually required to follow any data protection standards or vendor agreement obligations.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not indicate that users will be notified if third-party relationships or data-sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy states that client data is not sold, rented, or leased to third parties, and no advertising activity is described or evident on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no indication of any targeted advertising program or behavioral tracking for ad purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is disclosed or evident, and client data is explicitly stated to not be sold or leased.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies are acknowledged but their specific tracking purposes are not detailed, leaving ambiguity about whether any tracking beyond functional use occurs.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: While users can opt out of marketing data processing by writing to O.W.L., the process is manual and not clearly defined, making it only partially accessible.

dataCollected: Speech-to-text audio input (processed by third-party AI, not retained)
dataSharedWith: Commercial AI speech-to-text providers (data not retained after processing)

r524.riskReason: ObjectiveEd explicitly prohibits selling or marketing with student data, encrypts data in transit and at rest, and claims compliance with COPPA and FERPA, though its privacy disclosures exist on a single web page rather than a formal, versioned policy document with a dedicated ToS.
r524.parentSummary: ObjectiveEd collects only the minimum student data needed to deliver its reading and special education curriculum tools, including student performance and usage data stored in U.S.-based encrypted data centers. The platform explicitly states it will never sell, rent, or share student data without prior written consent, does not market to students, and allows schools to request deletion at any time. Parents should note that a third-party AI service is used for speech-to-text processing, though the vendor states that provider does not retain any input or output data after processing.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: ObjectiveEd states it will notify the designated school contact of any changes to the subscription agreement, but there is no publicly versioned policy history or revision log available on the website.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: ObjectiveEd states it minimizes data to educational objectives and maintains an updated list of student data collected, but that list is only available upon request rather than published publicly.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The student data privacy page describes general data minimization practices and mentions AI-based speech-to-text processing, but does not specifically enumerate all methods of data collection (e.g., cookies, account registration forms, in-app tracking).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: ObjectiveEd explicitly states it will never sell, rent, transfer, disclose, or distribute personal or student data without prior written consent, strongly implying the school/user retains ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The platform states that all student data is removed upon request or upon subscription termination, and is cleared from all backups at the next backup cycle, constituting a full deletion commitment.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Data deletion upon subscription termination is stated, but no specific retention duration (e.g., number of days data is held during an active subscription) is publicly disclosed on the website.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: ObjectiveEd describes multiple specific security measures including 24/7 monitoring in U.S. data centers, staff training, background screening, PHRP-certified research ethics, and an available Data Security and Incident Response Plan.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The student data privacy page explicitly states that data is encrypted both in transit and at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of password strength requirements, password enforcement policies, or SSO/LTI integration is made in any publicly accessible policy document.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI login options is found in any publicly accessible policy or product documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy is published on the objectiveed.com website; the student data privacy page does not address cookie usage, tracking technologies, or browser-based data collection.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: ObjectiveEd mentions use of commercial AI providers for speech-to-text processing but does not name the specific vendor(s); no other third parties are identified by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The only disclosed data shared with a third party is speech audio input processed by an unnamed AI provider, with a claim that no data is retained; specific data fields shared are not enumerated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The platform states it does not share student data with any third party without a written school request, effectively providing schools with full control and an implicit opt-out by default.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: ObjectiveEd states the AI provider's data and privacy policy confirms no retention of input or output data, indicating a contractual or policy-level commitment from the third-party provider.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Schools are notified of changes to the subscription agreement (which encompasses data privacy commitments), but the process for notifying of specific third-party provider changes is not explicitly described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: ObjectiveEd explicitly states it does not market to students and does not knowingly allow any third party to use its service to market to students, indicating no ads are displayed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is conducted; the platform explicitly prohibits marketing to students by itself or third parties.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party tracking for advertising purposes is disclosed or indicated; the no-marketing commitment effectively prohibits ad-related tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacons or advertising tracking methods are disclosed or described; the platform's stated practices do not include any advertising-related tracking mechanisms.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising or data sharing with advertisers occurs, there is nothing to opt out of, which satisfies this requirement by default.

dataCollected: Payment information (via PayPal/Patreon/Open Collective if donating)
r525.riskReason: OBS explicitly states services are not intended for children under 13, has no K-12 or FERPA compliance provisions, references ad networks and third-party trackers, and the submitted URL (obsopenbroadcastersoftware.com) is not the official OBS site, raising additional legitimacy and provenance concerns.
r525.parentSummary: OBS (Open Broadcaster Software) is a free, open-source video recording and live streaming desktop tool operated by Wizards of OBS LLC; its services are explicitly not intended for anyone under 13 years old, and there are no stated COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance commitments. The platform collects usage data, device identifiers, IP addresses, and cookies, and shares data with third parties including Google Analytics, payment processors, and potentially ad networks, with limited controls for users to opt out. Schools should be aware that OBS is a general consumer software tool with no educational data protection agreements and is not designed or vetted for K-12 use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states changes will be communicated via email or through the Services, but no revision history or versioned archive is publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data (IP address, device identifiers, usage analytics, payment info) but does not comprehensively enumerate every specific data point collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes collection methods (cookies, account registration, third-party integrations) but lacks full specificity about each collection mechanism.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy explicitly states that collected information 'is considered an asset of Company' and may be transferred in a merger or acquisition, indicating company ownership rather than user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may contact the company to request data deletion, but there is no self-service deletion tool and the process and timeline are not clearly defined.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state any specific data retention period or general retention timeline for any category of data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy does not describe any specific technical security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or security certifications.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The OBS software supports RTMPS (secure streaming protocol) for outbound streams, but the privacy policy itself does not explicitly state that stored personal data is encrypted.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of password strength requirements, enforcement policies, or SSO/MFA integration is made anywhere in the terms or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI integration is mentioned; the forum/account system uses basic username/password without stated MFA support.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are mentioned generally and some purposes described (personalization, session management, analytics), but a full enumerated list of all cookies and their specific purposes is not provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Some third parties are named (Google Analytics, PayPal, Open Collective, Patreon), but ad network partners and other data processors are referenced only in general terms without full identification.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy indicates data shared with payment processors includes name, address, and payment info, and Google Analytics receives usage data, but a complete per-third-party data mapping is not provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An opt-out from targeted advertising is referenced via industry opt-out tools (NAI, DAA), but no direct in-platform opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not state that third-party data processors are contractually bound to follow equivalent data protection standards or vendor agreements.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not commit to notifying users when third-party sharing relationships change; the general change notification clause covers policy updates but not specific third-party changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy references 'ad networks' and targeted advertising opt-out mechanisms, indicating third-party ads may be displayed through or associated with the Services.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy acknowledges that third-party ad networks may target users based on online activity, and does not disclaim all behavioral targeting of users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Industry-standard opt-out links (NAI, DAA) are referenced for opting out of targeted advertising, providing a partial but externalized opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy references cookies, web beacons, and tracking technologies used by third-party ad partners without clearly limiting their use to functional purposes only.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Opt-out of targeted advertising is mentioned via third-party opt-out tools, but no direct, clear in-product process for opting out of data sharing with advertisers is described.
