r561.riskReason: Powtoon expressly acknowledges COPPA and FERPA compliance and offers an Education account tier, but its privacy policy leaves key questions unanswered — including whether student data is sold, whether targeted advertising occurs, and whether third-party analytics providers operate independently on student data — raising concerns flagged by Common Sense Media as a 'Warning' rating.
r561.parentSummary: Powtoon collects personal information such as name, email, device data, and usage activity, and may share it with analytics, marketing, and cloud hosting third parties. The platform states it complies with COPPA and FERPA and claims not to collect personal information directly from students under 13 without parental or school consent. However, independent evaluators note it is unclear whether student data is sold, used for targeted advertising, or collected by third-party trackers for their own purposes, which warrants caution for K-12 deployments.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy notes it was last updated January 2025 and the TOS references posted changes for fee updates 14 days in advance, but there is no explicit advance notification process or revision history archive described for general policy changes.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists categories of data collected (name, email, address, usage data, device data) but does not provide a fully exhaustive enumeration, and student-specific data collection details are limited.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states that some data is automatically collected and some is voluntarily provided, but does not specifically detail every collection mechanism (e.g., SDKs, pixel tracking, form inputs) in a comprehensive manner.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership for user-created content is implied to remain with the user, but the policy is ambiguous — the Enterprise TOS explicitly states company ownership of enterprise content, and the general policy does not make user ownership unambiguous for all account types.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may request account deletion, which is processed within 30 days, and withdrawing consent triggers erasure of personal information from systems, satisfying full deletion capability.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The TOS references a 14-day content retention period for free users and 90 days for enterprise, and the policy states data is kept while the user remains subscribed, but a precise post-account-closure retention schedule is not clearly stated for all data types.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The DPA and Microsoft Teams privacy policy reference encryption, firewalls, network segregation, static code analysis, and annual penetration testing, but the main consumer-facing privacy policy only makes a general security statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Supporting policy documents (DPA, MS Teams policy) mention encryption and technical controls, but the primary privacy policy does not explicitly confirm end-to-end or at-rest encryption, making this only partially documented for most users.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Powtoon supports SSO via Google and Microsoft and integrates with Okta, which satisfies this criterion as SSO typically enforces strong credential requirements at the identity provider level.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Powtoon supports SSO (Google, Microsoft, Okta) and two-factor authentication via SMS is noted in third-party security profiles, meeting the standard for MFA or SSO availability.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges the use of cookies and third-party analytics cookies but does not provide a full cookie inventory with individual names, categories, and purposes; it only describes cookies generally.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third-party categories are named (cloud hosting, payment processors, CRM, analytics, marketing providers) and specific vendors such as AWS, HubSpot, Google Analytics, and Facebook are identifiable via the supply chain, but the main privacy policy itself does not name them explicitly.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by third-party purpose category rather than specifying what particular data fields are shared with each named vendor, resulting in only partial disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications by contacting support@powtoon.com, but opting out of analytics or third-party service provider data sharing is not described as an accessible self-service process.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that third-party service providers are bound by contractual protections and data transfers include approved safeguard clauses, but the language is general rather than a robust supplier accountability framework.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not describe any process for notifying users when third-party service providers change or when new data-sharing relationships are established.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Powtoon does not explicitly state that no advertising is shown to users; the policy references 'marketing service providers' as third parties who receive data, and Common Sense Media flags advertising practices as unclear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy does not explicitly prohibit targeted advertising, and Common Sense Media independently rates the targeting advertising question as 'unclear,' making this only a partial meet.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Analytics providers are noted to set their own cookies on user devices, which could enable third-party tracking, but there is no explicit opt-out mechanism described for this tracking activity within the student-facing experience.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy acknowledges use of analytics cookies and third-party service provider cookies for usage tracking, but does not clearly distinguish functional-only tracking from advertising-linked web beacons or pixel tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can email support to opt out of marketing communications, but there is no clear, dedicated opt-out process specifically for data sharing with advertising or marketing partners as distinct from general communications.

dataSharedWith: Service providers/vendors acting on PRB's behalf
r562.riskReason: PRB (prb.com/prb.org) is a demographic research nonprofit, not a purpose-built K-12 EdTech platform, and its privacy policy contains no COPPA, FERPA, or student-specific data protections, no minimum age requirements, no Terms of Service, vague third-party data sharing disclosures, and acknowledges that third-party tools on the site may process personal data including for potential sale.
r562.parentSummary: PRB (Population Reference Bureau) is a nonprofit research organization, not a dedicated K-12 student platform. Its privacy policy discloses that it may collect names, email addresses, and credit card information from visitors, and that third-party tools on the site may process personal data. There are no student-specific protections, no COPPA or FERPA commitments, and no minimum age restrictions stated anywhere in the policy — making this site unsuitable as a vetted K-12 EdTech tool without additional district-level controls.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Terms of Service page was found, and the privacy policy does not describe any advance notification process or revision history for policy changes.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data types (name, email, credit card) but does not comprehensively enumerate all data collected, particularly regarding third-party tracking tools acknowledged elsewhere on the site.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is entered by users or collected when using the website, but does not specifically detail automated collection methods or third-party tracking mechanisms used on the site.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not address data ownership; there is no statement that users own their data, and the organization retains the data it collects without ownership clarification.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy contains no provision allowing users to request deletion of their personal data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or general retention statement is provided anywhere in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy mentions only that data is stored behind a firewall and that employees are trained via handbook — no specific security measures such as encryption standards or access controls are described.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption of data in transit or at rest is made anywhere in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account creation is required for basic site use, but the policy makes no mention of password requirements for any optional accounts or newsletter subscriptions.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO is made; no account system with MFA is described.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The site acknowledges third-party tools that may process personal data and references a 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' link, but no cookie policy listing specific cookies and their purposes was found.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy mentions sharing with 'companies who work on behalf of PRB' but does not name any specific third-party vendors or service providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with each third party is provided; sharing is described only in general terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described within the privacy policy itself, though a 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' link is referenced on other site pages.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that third-party companies working on PRB's behalf have no right to use data beyond what is necessary, providing a general contractual obligation statement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention notifying users if third-party sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The site acknowledges that third-party tools may process personal data potentially for advertising purposes, with a 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' link indicating possible targeted ad activity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The existence of a 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' opt-out link on the site indicates possible third-party targeted advertising, but no explicit disclosure of advertising practices is made.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking for advertising is implied by the 'Do Not Sell' link but no opt-out process specifically for ad tracking is described in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No disclosure of web beacons, tracking pixels, or other tracking technologies is made in the privacy policy, despite third-party tools being acknowledged on the site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described in the privacy policy; only a vague external link reference is noted on other pages of the site.

r563.riskReason: PreKinders is a site explicitly targeting Pre-K and Preschool teachers and their young students, yet it runs Mediavine programmatic interest-based advertising with third-party tracking cookies and behavioral targeting — practices incompatible with COPPA — and its privacy policy contains no COPPA disclosures, no parental consent mechanisms, no minimum age statement, no data retention policy, and no FERPA acknowledgment.
r563.parentSummary: PreKinders collects email addresses from users who sign up for its newsletter and uses Google Analytics and the Mediavine ad network, which places third-party tracking cookies and behavioral advertising tags on all visitors, including teachers and potentially students. The site does not explicitly address COPPA compliance, does not restrict access by age, and does not disclose how long data is retained or provide any parental consent mechanisms. Parents and school administrators should be aware that visiting this site exposes users to interest-based advertising technology and third-party data collection with no clear K-12 privacy protections in place.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy page exists but search results return only a one-line site description with no visible policy text, and there is no stated process for notifying users of policy changes or any revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The site mentions email collection via newsletter signup and implies analytics/ad data collection, but does not publish a comprehensive enumerated list of all data types collected in its privacy policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Data collection methods (newsletter form, Google Analytics, Mediavine cookies) can be inferred from context and the site's technology stack (WordPress, WooCommerce, Mediavine), but are not explicitly and fully documented in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy does not address data ownership; the site's use of Mediavine ad tech and third-party analytics means user behavioral data is effectively shared with and may be retained by external parties without clear user ownership language.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No deletion rights, opt-out process, or user data removal mechanism is described anywhere in the accessible privacy policy or terms of use.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or retention/deletion policy is stated anywhere in the privacy policy, which is a direct deficiency under COPPA requirements given the site's child-directed audience.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, security audits) are described in the accessible privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses Cloudflare (per technology stack data) which provides HTTPS/TLS in transit, but the privacy policy does not explicitly mention encryption or security certifications.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account creation is required for basic site access or content downloads, so password enforcement is largely not applicable, but the shop/WooCommerce component likely requires account creation without any stated password policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of MFA or SSO anywhere in policy documentation; the WooCommerce-powered shop likely uses basic username/password without MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The site uses Mediavine advertising which deploys first- and third-party cookies and tracking tags, but the privacy policy does not provide a complete cookie list with categories and purposes as required for full compliance.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Mediavine is referenced as an ad management partner and Google Analytics is implied through the technology stack, but specific named third parties receiving user data are not fully enumerated in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The data shared with Mediavine and its partners is described at a category level (usage data, cookie info, device info, geolocation, interaction data) but is not mapped per individual third party in the PreKinders privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out process for third-party data sharing or Mediavine advertising is described in the PreKinders privacy policy; the site does not link to opt-out tools (e.g., NAI, DAA) from its own policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: There is no statement in the privacy policy that third-party vendors (Mediavine partners, Google) are contractually required to protect user data or adhere to PreKinders' privacy standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy contains no commitment to notify users when third-party advertising partners or data processors change, which is a significant gap given Mediavine's large and changing partner ecosystem.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The site actively runs Mediavine programmatic display advertising, which means targeted and interest-based ads are displayed to all site visitors, including educators accessing pre-K teaching resources.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Mediavine serves interest-based advertising using behavioral tracking data, meaning ads are targeted based on users' browsing history and profiles — confirmed third-party behavioral targeting is in use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking via Mediavine's ad stack (tags, pixels, beacons, cookies) is confirmed and no opt-out mechanism is provided within the PreKinders site itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Mediavine's ad technology uses cookies, tags, pixels, beacons, and similar technologies for ad targeting and optimization, as reflected in the standard Mediavine publisher privacy policy language — no functional-only tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out from data sharing with advertisers is offered or linked to from the PreKinders privacy policy; users have no clear mechanism to prevent their data from being used for targeted advertising.

r564.riskReason: Prezi uses third-party advertising cookies, shares data with ad networks, allows AI training on public user content, lacks explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance commitments, and has no dedicated K-12 student data protections — making it a high-risk platform for use with minors in K-12 schools.
r564.parentSummary: Prezi collects a broad range of personal data including name, email, device identifiers, location, and usage behavior, and shares this data with third-party advertisers, analytics providers, and AI training partners for public content. While Prezi states it does not sell personal information and provides data deletion rights, it lacks explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance declarations and serves targeted advertising cookies, posing notable risks for student users. Parents and schools should be aware that free accounts make all presentations public by default, and that student data may be used for advertising and AI model improvement purposes.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Prezi states it will notify users of material changes via email, user interface, or other reasonable means, but there is no publicly accessible revision history or change log for the policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and CCPA/CPRA notices enumerate specific categories of data collected including contact data, account data, social media data, usage data, device information, and payment data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Prezi clearly describes how data is collected — through account creation forms, service usage, cookies, web beacons, server logs, pixel tags, and third-party integrations.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Prezi states users control their own user-generated content, but Prezi acts as the data controller for all personal data processed, and retains a broad, perpetual license to use public content including for AI training and marketing.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request full deletion of their personal data and account via email to privacy@prezi.com or through a support ticket, though some data may be retained for legal or fraud-prevention purposes.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Prezi states data is retained as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected and to comply with legal obligations, but no specific retention timeframes (e.g., 90 days, 2 years) are provided for most data categories.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The DPA and privacy policy reference TLS encryption, firewalls, access logging, password complexity enforcement, full disk encryption, and periodic penetration tests and vulnerability scans.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Prezi explicitly states use of industry-standard TLS encryption between client-to-server and server-to-server communications, and full disk encryption on internal systems.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The DPA notes that password complexity is enforced for Prezi internal systems, but there is no explicit statement in the user-facing ToS or privacy policy that strong password requirements are enforced for end-user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: MFA is enforced internally for Prezi staff accessing high-risk systems per the DPA, but there is no stated MFA or SSO/LTI option for end users or school administrators in the reviewed policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Prezi has a dedicated Cookie Policy that lists and describes cookie categories including strictly necessary, functional, analytics, and marketing cookies, along with opt-out instructions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references third-party advertisers, ad networks, analytics providers, AI partners, and linked platforms (e.g., Slack, Salesforce, Google), but does not name specific companies in the main privacy policy; a separate subprocessors list exists.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy policy groups data sharing by category of third party (e.g., advertisers receive device identifiers or contact info; AI partners receive public content inputs) but does not specify exact data fields shared per individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of advertising data sharing by updating cookie settings via the in-app cookie manager, but opt-out from all third-party data sharing is limited and not straightforward for all categories.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Prezi states that all service providers must meet Prezi's security and privacy standards before gaining access to user data and are obligated not to use it for other purposes, with DPA agreements in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The DPA provides 10-day advance email notice to business customers when new subprocessors are added, but individual consumer users have no equivalent notification mechanism beyond reviewing an online subprocessors list.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Prezi's cookie policy explicitly acknowledges marketing/advertising cookies placed by advertising networks, and the privacy policy confirms working with third-party advertisers and ad networks, indicating ads are present.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Prezi shares device identifiers and contact information with advertising partners, and marketing cookies track users across sites to deliver relevant ads, confirming third-party targeted advertising of users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Prezi allows third-party advertising cookies with user tracking, but provides a cookie settings manager (green cookie icon in-app) to opt out, offering limited but available opt-out from ad tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy and cookie policy confirm use of web beacons, pixel tags, and other tracking tools by both Prezi and third parties for advertising and marketing purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of advertising data sharing by updating cookie preferences via the in-app cookie manager, but the opt-out process is described only briefly and lacks a clear standalone opt-out mechanism for all ad-related data sharing.

r565.riskReason: Primary Apps is explicitly designed for children aged 5–13, yet displays Google-served third-party targeted advertising with tracking cookies and web beacons, has no COPPA or FERPA compliance statements, no Terms of Service, and no age-gating or parental consent mechanism.
r565.parentSummary: Primary Apps (primaryapps.co.uk) is a free maths games site designed for children aged 5–13 that collects usage data, cookies, and advertising identifiers via Google AdSense and third-party ad partners, which may track children's browsing activity across the internet. The site does not require an account, has no Terms of Service, and does not mention COPPA, FERPA, or any parental consent process. Parents should be aware that third-party advertising cookies are served to child users, and there is no clear prohibition on behavioral profiling of children.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it may be updated but gives no advance notification process, no revision history, and no method to alert users of changes before they take effect.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists cookies, web beacons, IP addresses, analytics data, and advertising identifiers, but does not comprehensively enumerate all data types in a clear structured list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy provides a general statement that data is collected through cookies, analytics, and advertising technologies but does not specifically describe every collection mechanism.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not address data ownership; there is no statement that users own their data, and the operator's relationship with advertising partners implies commercial use of visitor data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may request access, correction, or erasure by contacting the site, but the process is informal (contact page only) with no self-service deletion tool or stated response timeline.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is kept 'only for as long as reasonably necessary' but provides no specific retention periods or minimum timeframes for any category of data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy contains no description of specific security measures, technical safeguards, or organizational controls used to protect personal data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy makes no mention of encryption for data in transit or at rest, and no encryption test result or statement is provided.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account creation is required to use the platform, so password enforcement is not applicable and this requirement is effectively met by default.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required to access the platform, making MFA requirements not applicable; this criterion is effectively satisfied by the no-account design.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy lists four cookie categories (essential, analytics, advertising, preference) with general purposes, but does not enumerate specific cookies by name or provide a full cookie table.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references 'hosting providers, analytics providers, technical support providers and advertising partners' as categories but does not name specific third-party companies (other than Google).
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing broadly by partner type without specifying what particular data elements are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users in the UK/EEA can manage consent through a consent management platform or browser settings, but opt-out options for users outside those regions are not clearly described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy contains no statement that third-party service providers or advertising partners are contractually required to comply with equivalent data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may be updated to reflect changes in advertising and measurement technologies but does not commit to notifying users when specific third-party partners change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states the site may display Google-served third-party advertising, including Google AdSense, to all visitors including children aged 5–13.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy acknowledges that Google and third-party vendors may use cookies to serve ads based on users' previous visits to this and other sites, confirming behavioral/targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third parties including Google may place cookies and use web beacons for ad serving and tracking; opt-out is only available via consent management in UK/EEA regions, not universally.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy explicitly confirms use of cookies, web beacons, IP addresses, and similar tracking technologies by third parties for advertising purposes on this child-directed site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users in the UK/EEA may update advertising consent choices through on-site consent options or browser settings, but there is no universal or clearly described global opt-out process.

r566.riskReason: Proctorio holds strong compliance certifications (FERPA, COPPA, SOC 2, ISO 27001) and does not sell data, but its collection of audio, video, screen recordings, and behavioral data from minors during exams represents an inherently sensitive and invasive data profile, and actual data collected varies significantly based on institution-configured settings.
r566.parentSummary: Proctorio is an online exam proctoring tool that may collect webcam video, audio, screen activity, gaze detection data, and truncated IP addresses from students during exams, but only when specific settings are enabled by the school or instructor. All exam recordings are encrypted with Zero-Knowledge Encryption, meaning even Proctorio itself cannot access them — only institution-approved educators can decrypt and review them. Proctorio does not sell student data, does not use advertising trackers or cookies, and has been independently certified as compliant with FERPA, COPPA, and SOPIPA; however, parents should be aware that the level of monitoring can be extensive depending on how the school configures the platform.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Policy changes are posted on the website with a banner notice and tracked on GitHub for version history, but users are only encouraged to review periodically rather than receiving direct advance notification; continued use constitutes acceptance.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy explicitly lists data types collected including audio, video, screen recordings, IP address (truncated), gaze/face detection data, keystroke anomalies, web traffic, and device metadata, with the caveat that actual collection depends on institution-enabled settings.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy clearly explains that data is collected via browser extension during active exam sessions only, through institution-configured settings, and through direct contact or website forms when Proctorio acts as data controller.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy states that test-taker Personal Information maintained in the institution's exam platform is the property of the institution, creating a split ownership model where Proctorio acts as data processor; ownership of data collected when Proctorio is data controller is less clearly defined.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Data deletion rights exist but are primarily exercised through the institution rather than directly by the student; Proctorio retains data for up to 30 days after contract end before transferring or destroying it, limiting direct student-initiated deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Retention periods are disclosed: recording data is stored as little as 7 days depending on institution requirements, and data is kept up to 30 days post-contract termination before transfer or destruction, with specific periods disclosed to test-takers on the 'Before You Begin' page.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Proctorio details multiple specific security measures including three-layer AES-GCM encryption, TLS 1.2/1.3 transmission, daily vulnerability scans, semi-annual penetration tests, SOC 2 Type 1 audit, ISO 27001:2022 and ISO 27018 certifications, and an ethical hacker bug bounty program.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Proctorio uses Zero-Knowledge end-to-end encryption for all exam recordings, TLS 1.2/1.3 for data in transit, and AES-GCM for the encryption layer, with independent audits confirming appropriate implementation; Proctorio itself cannot decrypt the stored recordings.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Proctorio uses Single Sign-On (SSO/LTI) exclusively for test-taker authentication and does not maintain its own registration or login system, eliminating the need for password enforcement while meeting the spirit of this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Proctorio exclusively uses Single Sign-On (SSO) and LTI integrations through the institution's LMS for authentication, with no separate Proctorio account creation required, effectively satisfying MFA requirements through institutional SSO.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Proctorio explicitly states it manages sessions without cookies or HTML Web Storage and runs cookie-free domains with zero ad trackers and zero third-party cookies; only functional tracking occurs, fully meeting this criterion.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Proctorio identifies categories of third parties (service providers, payment processors, identity verification providers) but does not publicly name specific vendor companies in the privacy policy, providing only general categories rather than specific named entities.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy policy groups data shared with third-party service providers broadly (hosting, Help Center, analytics for institutions) without detailing which specific data fields are shared with each category of provider, making it partially rather than fully disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Test-takers have limited opt-out options since data collection is controlled by the institution; students can contact their institution to adjust settings, but no direct self-service opt-out mechanism from third-party data sharing is provided to individual students.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states that all third-party service providers can only use data for Proctorio's specified business purposes as defined in Proctorio's written agreement with them, and Proctorio remains liable under DPF Principles for third-party processing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes are posted to the website with a banner and tracked on GitHub, but does not explicitly commit to proactively notifying users of changes to specific third-party relationships; users are encouraged to review periodically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Proctorio explicitly states it has zero ad trackers and does not display advertisements to users; the platform is a B2B service deployed through educational institutions with no consumer-facing advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Proctorio explicitly states it does not use client-side tracking pixels for advertising, marketing, or targeting, and does not engage in any targeted advertising directed at students or test-takers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Proctorio runs cookie-free domains, uses zero third-party cookies, and does not use client-side tracking pixels, eliminating third-party ad tracking entirely from its platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Proctorio uses only functional tracking mechanisms necessary for exam delivery; it explicitly disclaims use of advertising web beacons, tracking pixels, or any marketing-oriented tracking technologies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because Proctorio does not engage in advertising or share data with advertisers, there is no need for an opt-out mechanism; this criterion is fully satisfied by the absence of the practice itself.

r567.parentSummary: ProgressTrak's website (progresstrak.com) does not appear to publish any accessible Privacy Policy or Terms of Service, meaning there is no public documentation of what data is collected from students or how it is used. Without these foundational disclosures, schools and parents have no way to assess whether the platform handles student data safely or in compliance with federal law. Schools should not deploy this platform with student data until full legal documentation is provided and reviewed.

r568.riskReason: While the extension explicitly states no data is sent to external servers and no third-party sharing occurs, there is no formal Terms of Service, no age restrictions or COPPA/FERPA acknowledgment, the project is archived and unmaintained, and the extension requests browser tab access which could theoretically expose browsing habits.
r568.parentSummary: ProKeys is a free, no-account-required Chrome text-expander extension that stores all user data (typed snippets and settings) locally on the device or synced via the user's own Google account — no data is sent to the developer's servers or shared with any third party. The developer has publicly committed not to sell the extension to avoid risks of data misuse, and the Chrome Web Store confirms no user data is collected by the developer. However, there is no formal Terms of Service, no stated minimum age, no explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance language, and the project has been archived with no active maintenance, which may concern schools seeking ongoing compliance assurances.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No formal policy change notification process is stated anywhere; the GitHub-hosted privacy policy has no revision history, versioning, or advance-notice mechanism described.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy identifies user-created snippet data and settings as the only data stored, but does not explicitly enumerate all possible data types (e.g., browser tab metadata accessible via declared permissions) leaving some ambiguity.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically states all data is stored in Chrome local or sync storage areas implemented by the browser, clearly explaining the collection mechanism.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy makes clear that user data belongs to the user and is stored in user-controlled Chrome storage; the developer explicitly disclaimed any server-side access or ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No formal data deletion process or user request mechanism is described; the policy only states data is lost upon uninstalling the extension, with no self-service deletion option offered.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data persists only as long as the user uses ProKeys and is deleted on uninstall, but provides no specific retention period in days or a formal general retention statement beyond this basic description.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls) are described; the policy relies on Chrome's built-in storage security without elaborating on what protections are in place.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is not explicitly mentioned by the developer; data security relies implicitly on Chrome's storage infrastructure, which does use encryption, but this is not stated in the policy itself.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account or password is required to use ProKeys, so strong password enforcement is not applicable and the compliance criterion is satisfied by the account-free design.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required to use ProKeys, eliminating the need for MFA; optional Chrome sync uses Google account authentication which supports MFA at the platform level.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy is provided anywhere; the extension itself does not use cookies, but the prokeysextension.com website has no cookie disclosure, and the GitHub-hosted policy does not address cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states user data is not shared with any third party, satisfying the disclosure requirement by confirming the absence of third-party sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Because no data is shared with any third party, this criterion is met by the explicit statement of no third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: There is no third-party data sharing to opt out of, so this criterion is satisfied by the policy's clear statement that data is not shared with third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No mention is made of any vendor agreement, data processing agreement, or supplier accountability framework, as the developer appears to operate as a solo project with no third-party processors documented.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No notification process for third-party changes is described; while currently there are no third parties, the policy does not address what would happen if that changed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No ads are displayed in ProKeys; it is a free, open-source extension with no advertising model described or observed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising exists or is mentioned; the extension has no ad-serving or behavioral profiling capability.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is present; the policy states data is not shared with any third party and the Chrome Web Store confirms no data collection by the developer.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacons, tracking pixels, or ad-related tracking methods are described or used; data handling is limited to local Chrome storage for functional purposes only.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There is no data sharing with advertisers whatsoever, making an opt-out process unnecessary and this criterion met by design.

r569.riskReason: ProQuest does not serve ads within its core products and states data belongs to users, but it explicitly tracks users on its public-facing websites for third-party remarketing, uses third-party analytics cookies, makes changes to the TOS without prior notice, and does not explicitly address COPPA compliance or minimum age restrictions for K-12 student users.
r569.parentSummary: ProQuest collects contact details, usage/activity data, IP addresses, and cookies when students use its research databases and services. The platform states it does not sell student data and does not display ads inside its research products, and users have the right to request data deletion. However, ProQuest may track user activity on its public information websites and share data with third-party contractors, and the privacy policy does not explicitly state COPPA or FERPA compliance or a minimum age requirement for student users.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: ProQuest's Terms of Use state changes can be made 'at its sole discretion at any time and without prior notice,' meaning users are not guaranteed advance notification of policy changes.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy provides a reasonably detailed list of data collected, including contact details, usage data, IP addresses, device identifiers, payment information, and automatically collected tracking data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically explains data is collected through direct user input, automatic technological means (cookies, tracking), and from third-party data aggregators.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: ProQuest's blog states 'data about an individual user belongs to that person, not to ProQuest,' but the main privacy policy identifies ProQuest LLC as the 'data controller,' creating some ambiguity about practical ownership and control.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users have the right to request data deletion via a Data Subject Request form, and the privacy home page explicitly states users have the right to ask that their information be deleted.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not specify a precise retention period for user data; it only vaguely states data is collected to the extent necessary to provide services, with no defined timeframe.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy lists specific security measures including secured servers behind firewalls, internal reviews of data collection practices, industry-standard encryption, and physical security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly mentions 'industry-standard encryption technologies' as part of its security measures, indicating encryption is used to protect stored data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The terms reference password-based access controls and institutions are responsible for managing passwords, but there is no explicit mention of enforcing strong password requirements for end users.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: ProQuest supports IP-address-based authentication and institutional SSO (e.g., via EZProxy), which partially meets MFA/SSO requirements, but no explicit MFA offering for individual users is described in the policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: ProQuest maintains a dedicated Cookie Policy page that categorizes cookies (analytics, geotargeting, registration/session, third-party) and provides a Cookie Consent Manager, meeting the standard for a documented cookie policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy states data is shared with contracted third parties but does not name specific vendors; Google Analytics is referenced on the Privacy Home page as a paid analytics provider, but a comprehensive named list is absent.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups third-party data sharing broadly (processors, social networks, advertisers) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each category of third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of personal data disclosure to third parties at the point of collection, and a Data Subject Request process is available, providing a meaningful opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: ProQuest states it 'remains responsible for personal data shared with third parties for processing on our behalf' and vets third parties against its own security and privacy standards, indicating vendor agreements are in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Terms of Use allow changes without prior notice, and while the privacy policy references giving notice before a merger/acquisition changes data handling, routine third-party changes do not require user notification.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: ProQuest does not serve advertising within its core research products, but explicitly states it may track activity on public-facing websites to serve remarketing ads through third-party ad networks after users leave.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted ads are shown inside the ProQuest research platform itself, but the policy discloses participation in third-party remarketing/retargeting based on activity tracked on ProQuest's public information websites.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party analytics and remarketing tracking occurs on ProQuest's public-facing websites; a Cookie Consent Manager is offered to manage preferences, providing limited but available opt-out capability.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy discloses use of anonymous analytics cookies via a third-party provider and geotargeting cookies, but also acknowledges third parties may set their own cookies on some ProQuest pages for tracking purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out mechanism is available via the Cookie Consent Manager and the Data Subject Request process, but the opt-out path for the third-party remarketing specifically is not clearly documented in a single, prominent location.

r570.riskReason: The platform explicitly collects personal data for targeted advertising and shares it with marketing partners and third parties, offers only an email-based opt-out, has no stated FERPA or SOPIPA compliance, no specific security controls, no cookie inventory, no MFA, and no FERPA-specific protections — making it unsuitable as-is for K-12 student use without significant contractual safeguards.

Schools considering this platform for any K-12 use should obtain a written Data Processing Agreement addressing FERPA obligations before proceeding.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states the company will communicate policy changes, but no advance notification timeline or publicly maintained revision history is documented.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several categories of personal information (name, email, password, payment info, usage data) but uses 'without limitation' language, leaving the full scope of data collection unclear.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states data is collected when users register and use the site, but does not specifically enumerate all collection mechanisms such as cookies, analytics tools, or tracking pixels.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms and Conditions assert that all site materials are the property of ProSolutions Training, and the privacy policy does not affirm user ownership of personal data, indicating the company implicitly claims control.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may contact support to request removal of data (e.g., for children under 13), but no self-service deletion mechanism or general right-to-delete process for all users is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained 'as long as needed' for the original purpose or as permitted by law, which is a vague general statement with no specific retention period defined.

complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what data is shared with each category of third party; all disclosures are described in grouped, general terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An email-based opt-out is available ('Privacy Opt Out' to support@prosolutionstraining.com), but it is not a simple self-service opt-out and has noted exceptions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not state that third-party recipients are contractually bound to follow the same privacy standards or that a data processing agreement is in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not include any commitment to notify users if the list of third parties with whom data is shared changes.

complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms targeted advertising using user data, and data is also shared with marketing partners and affiliated organizations for their own promotional use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party tracking for advertising purposes is described; only a general email-based opt-out from promotional communications is mentioned.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No disclosure of web beacons, tracking pixels, or analytics tracking technologies is present in any policy document, leaving tracking methods entirely undisclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An email-based opt-out from promotional and third-party marketing communications is provided, but the process is manual, requires sending an email, and has stated exceptions.

complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google Tag Manager is present on the platform and can facilitate third-party tracking, but no opt-out or disclosure of its use for ads is publicly available.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The presence of Google Tag Manager suggests potential web beacon or pixel tracking, but no disclosure or limitation of such tracking methods was found.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers was found in any publicly accessible policy or help documentation.

r579.riskReason: QuiverVision explicitly states it may transfer customer data as a business asset in a merger or sale, collects geolocation and device data, does not specify a data retention period, updates its privacy policy without prior notice, and lacks explicit FERPA compliance language or named third-party disclosures required for K-12 deployment.
r579.parentSummary: QuiverVision collects names, email addresses, device identifiers, IP addresses, geolocation, and usage data from registered users, stating it retains student data for educational purposes and encrypts it in transit and at rest. However, the platform may share personally identifiable information with affiliates, co-branding and network partners, and could transfer all customer data — including student data — to buyers in a future merger or asset sale, which poses a meaningful risk for school use. The privacy policy can be updated at any time without advance notice to users, and no specific data retention period or explicit FERPA compliance commitment is stated.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it may be updated 'without prior notice' and only posts a revised date at the top of the page; no advance notification process or revision history archive is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several data types (name, email, IP address, device identifiers, geolocation, usage data) but uses 'including but not limited to' language, leaving the full scope of collection open-ended.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy describes collection through user-provided forms and automatic technical means (cookies, device data), but does not specifically enumerate all collection methods such as web beacons or pixel tracking on the main policy page.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not assert user ownership of data, and explicitly states that customer data is a transferable business asset in a merger or sale, effectively treating data as company-owned property.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents can submit a written deletion request for student data and self-initiated account deletion is referenced in the TOS, but no self-service deletion portal or defined response timeline is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated anywhere in the privacy policy; the policy is silent on how long personal data is kept after the educational purpose is fulfilled.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'appropriate technical and organisational measures' against unauthorized processing in a GDPR clause, but does not enumerate specific security controls such as access controls, audits, or certifications.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states that student data is encrypted in transit and at rest at all times.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Neither the TOS nor the privacy policy mentions password strength requirements, enforcement of strong passwords, or SSO/MFA for account access.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in any publicly available policy or documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy does not include a dedicated cookie policy listing individual cookies, their purposes, or their durations; cookie use is only implied through references to tracking usage data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy refers broadly to 'co-branding partners,' 'network partners,' and 'companies in the QuiverVision family' but does not name any specific third-party services or vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of which specific data elements are shared with which third-party category is provided; sharing disclosures are grouped in general terms only.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described; users are told their only option if they do not consent to transfers is to stop using the platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states it will 'require any such recipient to comply with the provisions of this Privacy Policy,' which is a general contractual statement but does not detail enforcement mechanisms or named vendor agreements.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may be updated without prior notice and does not commit to notifying users specifically when third-party sharing relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The TOS references 'banner advertisements or hyperlinks displayed on the Service' from advertisers or third parties, indicating ads may be displayed to users within the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The platform does not explicitly state it prohibits targeted or behavioral advertising; the presence of advertiser references in the TOS and no opt-out mechanism suggests potential third-party targeting is not ruled out.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No opt-out from third-party tracking is offered; the policy lacks any Do Not Track (DNT) response statement or opt-out mechanism for ad-related tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy does not describe web beacons or pixel tracking, but collects geolocation, usage patterns, email open/click data, and device identifiers — methods commonly used for ad targeting — without clear disclosure of their advertising use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described; the only recourse stated for users who object to data transfers is to discontinue use of the platform entirely.

dataSharedWith: Vetted third-party service providers (categories not individually named in publicly accessible policy)
No advertising third parties in student-facing areas
r580.riskReason: Quizalize explicitly prohibits selling children's data, bans third-party advertising in student-facing areas, uses school official consent under COPPA, follows NIST cybersecurity standards, and commits to 90-day data deletion upon account closure — representing strong K-12 privacy practices with only minor gaps in specificity around third-party vendor naming and cookie disclosures.
r580.parentSummary: Quizalize collects basic student account information (name, username, email) and academic performance data for educational purposes only; children under 13 cannot create their own accounts and must be set up by a teacher or school acting under COPPA's 'school official' consent model. The platform explicitly states it never sells children's data and never uses it for marketing or advertising, and personal data is permanently deleted within 90 days of account deletion. Zzish Limited, the parent company, aligns with FERPA, COPPA, NIST cybersecurity frameworks, and offers district-level data privacy agreements for schools requiring additional protections.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The COPPA Policy states Quizalize will notify schools and parents of material changes, but the main privacy policy and TOS do not clearly describe a full advance-notification process or publicly maintained revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The COPPA Policy and Terms of Service reference data collection of student names, emails, quiz/performance data, and device information, but a comprehensive enumerated list of all data types is not consolidated in one publicly accessible document.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The Terms of Service and COPPA Policy describe that data is collected through account creation by teachers, quiz participation, and platform use, but do not provide specific technical detail on all collection mechanisms (e.g., automatic tracking, cookies).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The COPPA Policy and Terms of Service make clear that student and user data belongs to the user/school and is not claimed by Zzish for commercial purposes; student data is never sold and is only used for educational service delivery.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The COPPA Policy explicitly states that when a student account is deleted, personal information is permanently deleted within 90 days, and parental/school requests for deletion are honored.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The COPPA Policy specifies a 90-day permanent deletion window upon account closure or student departure, providing a concrete retention and deletion timeframe.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Quizalize's help documentation references adoption of NIST Cybersecurity Framework practices, but the publicly accessible privacy policy does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as firewalls, access controls, or audit logging.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The platform uses HTTPS (standard TLS encryption in transit) as evidenced by the secure domain, but explicit confirmation of at-rest encryption is not stated in the publicly accessible privacy policy or COPPA policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Students can participate without creating accounts using only a class code and name, and teacher accounts are created via Google SSO or email/password; strong password requirements are not explicitly documented in the public-facing policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Google SSO is available for teacher login, which supports single sign-on as a form of federated authentication, but explicit multi-factor authentication (MFA) support is not mentioned in the public policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A cookie policy page exists at app.quizalize.com/cookie-policy, and the platform acknowledges cookie usage, but the publicly searchable content of that page did not return a full enumerated list of cookies with individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The COPPA Policy states third-party services are 'carefully vetted and bound by strict data protection agreements,' but does not name specific third-party vendors or service providers in the publicly accessible policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policies confirm third parties are used for service operations and are contractually bound, but do not specify which data fields are shared with each third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The COPPA Policy explicitly prohibits third-party advertising in student-facing areas and states children's data is never sold, effectively providing a structural opt-out equivalent for the most sensitive data sharing scenarios.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The COPPA Policy explicitly states that any third-party services used are 'carefully vetted and bound by strict data protection agreements,' meeting the requirement for vendor accountability.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The COPPA Policy states Quizalize may update the policy and will notify schools of material changes, but does not specify a formal notification process for changes in third-party vendor relationships specifically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The COPPA Policy explicitly states Quizalize does not include third-party advertising or links to external websites in student-facing areas of the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The COPPA Policy and Terms of Service state that children's information is never used for marketing or advertising purposes, with no targeted advertising to students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party advertising tracking is present in student-facing areas per the COPPA Policy, and there is no indication of cross-site tracking of students for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: A cookie policy page exists but the specific tracking technologies used (web beacons, pixels, etc.) and their purposes are not fully enumerated in accessible policy text, making a definitive assessment of all tracking methods unclear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because Quizalize explicitly does not serve ads to students and does not share student data with advertisers, no opt-out mechanism is needed; the structural prohibition itself fully meets this requirement.

r581.riskReason: While Quizbot.ai claims COPPA and FERPA compliance and does not sell data, the Terms of Service allow changes without notice, third-party service providers are not specifically named, Google advertising cookies may be set on student browsers, and the platform does not respond to Do Not Track signals — posing meaningful risks for K-12 deployments.
r581.parentSummary: Quizbot.ai collects basic account information (name and email), billing details, and usage/analytics data including IP address and browsing behavior. The platform explicitly states it does not sell personal data and claims compliance with COPPA, FERPA, SOPIPA, and several state student privacy laws. However, Google advertising cookies may be placed on user devices, third-party service providers are referenced but not individually named, and the Terms of Service reserve the right to change without advance notice — factors that warrant caution before deploying with students under 18.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy (quizbot.ai/page/privacy, last updated Nov 2023) states changes may be made and the updated date will reflect this, but the Terms of Service (quizbot.ai/page/terms) explicitly reserve the right to update without notice, creating an inconsistency that partially meets the standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy at quizbot.ai/page/privacy lists identity/access data, billing information, website interaction data, and voluntary correspondence, but does not enumerate all data types in a single consolidated list — for example, IP address and click-stream data are mentioned in narrative text rather than a clear inventory.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically describes how data is collected: directly from users at signup, automatically via browser interactions, through billing transactions, and via voluntary correspondence — meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy at quizbot.ai/page/privacy explicitly states 'it is your data, not ours' and the Terms of Service state 'We claim no intellectual property rights over the material you provide' — clearly affirming user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy at quizbot.ai/privacy-policy lists deletion as a user right and states requests will be responded to within 30 days, and the quizbot.ai/page/privacy policy indicates data is deleted upon account closure — meeting the full deletion standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy specifies that deleted account data is removed within 90 days, backup data may be retained up to 180 days, and anonymized usage data may be retained indefinitely — providing a sufficiently specific retention statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy lists specific security measures including SSL/TLS encryption in transit, secure servers with restricted access, access controls limited to authorized personnel, and regular security audits — meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Both the quizbot.ai/page/privacy and quizbot.ai/privacy-policy pages confirm all data transmitted is encrypted using SSL/TLS protocols and data is stored on secure encrypted servers — meeting the encryption standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service place responsibility for account and password security on the user but do not specify enforcement of strong password requirements, only implying user accountability — partially meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI integration is found in either the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy pages for quizbot.ai — not meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions session and persistent first-party cookies and third-party analytics cookies (e.g., Google), but does not provide a full enumerated list of all cookies with their individual purposes — partially meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references 'trusted third-party service providers' and Google for marketing activities, but does not provide a complete named list of all third parties used — only partially meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states data is shared with third-party service providers to operate the platform and with Google for ad effectiveness, but does not specify exactly which data fields are shared with each named or unnamed third party — not meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can control cookies via browser settings and opt out of marketing emails, but there is no clear opt-out mechanism for third-party service provider data sharing beyond account deletion — partially meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states data is shared with 'trusted' third-party providers but does not explicitly require those providers to adhere to a vendor data processing agreement or equivalent contractual obligation — only a general implied trust statement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Neither the Terms of Service nor the Privacy Policy include a commitment to notify users when third-party service providers change — the ToS explicitly reserves the right to update without notice, not meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy at quizbot.ai/page/privacy discloses a Google advertising cookie partnership for ad effectiveness tracking, indicating some advertising-related tracking occurs before and possibly after login — only partially meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Google advertising cookies are used to evaluate ad effectiveness for users arriving via Google ads, which constitutes a form of platform-level ad targeting, though no confirmed behavioral retargeting of logged-in users is described — partially meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google ad cookies may be set on user browsers and the site explicitly states it does not respond to Do Not Track signals, limiting users' ability to opt out of third-party tracking — partially meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy acknowledges Google sends tracking cookies for ad conversion purposes and that click-stream data (browser type, OS, pages visited, duration) may be collected, but the full scope of tracking methods is not comprehensively disclosed — partially meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can control cookies via browser settings and opt out of marketing emails, but no clear, dedicated opt-out mechanism for advertising data sharing specifically (e.g., Google ad tracking) is provided within the platform itself — partially meeting this standard.

dataCollected: Usage data (clicks, mouse movements, scrolling, typing activity)

r582.riskReason: Quizlet participates in PRIVO's COPPA Safe Harbor program and does not sell children's data, but third-party advertising partners track and serve personalized ads to general users, data profiles are created for ad targeting, and the TOS explicitly states advertising policies can change without notice.
r582.parentSummary: Quizlet collects account information (name, email, date of birth), detailed usage data, and device identifiers from all users, and allows third-party advertising partners to use cookies and tracking technologies to serve personalized ads to users on the platform and elsewhere. Children under 13 require parental consent and receive a restricted experience with no data sold, though de-identified or aggregated child data may still be used for research and commercial purposes. Parents can review, modify, or delete a child's account data at any time, and Quizlet holds PRIVO COPPA Safe Harbor certification, but the presence of targeted advertising and third-party tracking for general (13+) users is a notable concern for K-12 school deployments.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Privacy Policy indicates an effective/last-updated date, but Common Sense Media notes no change log or past policy versions are made available, and the TOS states advertising policies may change without notice.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy Policy clearly enumerates categories of personal data collected including identifiers, usage/behavioral data, device data, and content created, satisfying the requirement for a comprehensive data listing.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The Privacy Policy specifically describes how data is collected — through account registration, direct user interaction, automatic collection via the platform, and third-party authentication services like Google, Facebook, and Apple.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Users retain control over content they create and can delete it, but Quizlet explicitly reserves rights to use de-identified or aggregated data (including from children) for research, analysis, marketing, and commercial purposes, leaving ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may delete their account at any time via Settings, and the Privacy Policy states created content will be deleted in accordance with data retention policies, satisfying the full deletion requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The Privacy Policy states data is retained as long as an account is active or as needed for legitimate business or legal purposes, but does not specify a concrete retention period in days or months, making this vague.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Privacy Policy references encryption and 'generally accepted industry standards' for data protection, but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as access controls, audits, or data segmentation practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Quizlet's terms specify that the website and apps use encryption and that third-party payment processor connections are also encrypted, meeting the encryption standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Privacy Policy and TOS make no mention of strong password requirements or enforcement, nor is there a stated SSO-only access model for school accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) or LTI/SSO integration is made in the publicly available Privacy Policy or TOS; standard username/password login is the default.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Quizlet references a separate Cookie Policy and mentions the use of cookies and tracking tools, but the main Privacy Policy only broadly describes their use without listing all cookies and their specific purposes inline.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy references a maintained subprocessor list and broadly names categories of third parties (advertising partners, analytics providers, payment processors, customer support), but does not name specific vendor companies in the policy itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with third parties is described by category rather than by specific data fields per named third party, making it unclear exactly what data each third party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An opt-out for targeted advertising and data sharing is available via the 'Your Privacy/Cookie Choices' link and by emailing privacy@quizlet.com, but the opt-out is not prominently surfaced during onboarding or for school/child accounts specifically.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Privacy Policy states that service providers and subprocessors process data in accordance with Quizlet's instructions, Privacy Policy, and confidentiality or security requirements, meeting the vendor agreement standard.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The TOS explicitly states that Quizlet may change its advertising and commercial content policies without notice, failing to guarantee notification of third-party or advertising partner changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Quizlet allows third-party advertising companies to display advertisements within the Services and uses user data to target those ads, meaning targeted ads are actively displayed to general (13+) users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Quizlet and its third-party advertising partners use collected user data and device-level information to serve personalized/targeted advertisements, and data profiles are created for ad personalization purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertisers use cookies and tracking pixels to collect data from users on the Quizlet platform; a limited opt-out is available via the Privacy/Cookie Choices page, but it is not a full opt-out from all tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Quizlet's Privacy Policy confirms third-party advertising companies use cookies, pixels, and other technologies to track users across the Service and on third-party sites, indicating ad-related tracking beyond functional use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out process exists via the 'Your Privacy/Cookie Choices' link and email to privacy@quizlet.com, but the process is not clearly described step-by-step in the policy and its effectiveness for K-12 school contexts is unclear.
