r634.riskReason: Slides Translator (by Automagical Apps, hosted at slidestranslator.com and livepolls.app) explicitly claims FERPA, COPPA, and GDPR compliance, stores no PII for school/domain customers, does not sell data, encrypts all data in transit and at rest, and uses Google-hosted infrastructure — making it a low-risk tool for K-12 use.
r634.parentSummary: Slides Translator by Automagical Apps collects minimal data: no student PII is stored for school or domain license users, and any analytics data sent to Google Analytics is anonymized to a random string and domain name only. The platform explicitly claims FERPA and COPPA compliance, does not sell user data, and encrypts all data in transit and at rest on Google-hosted servers. The primary concern for K-12 districts is that the formal privacy policy (hosted on livepolls.app) sets a minimum age of 18 and lacks explicit policy change notification procedures, so schools should ensure domain-level licensing is in place to guarantee the no-PII protections apply.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it may be revised, but no advance notification process or formal revision history mechanism is explicitly described for users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists device/usage/log data, IP address, and location, and the product-level policy notes no email/PII is recorded during translation; however, the full enumeration of all possible data types across individual vs. domain licenses is spread across multiple documents and not consolidated in one place.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically states that data is collected automatically when users visit/use the service, via cookies and similar technologies, and through Google Workspace API access during add-on use.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The automagicalapps.com privacy policy explicitly states 'your data...will always remain yours' and that Google user data is never shared or transferred beyond what is strictly necessary to operate the service.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Account termination and data deletion are available upon request, but some data may be retained in backup archives or for legal compliance purposes, and the process is not fully self-service.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy states data is kept only as long as necessary for stated purposes or as required by law, but no specific retention period (e.g., 90 days) is given — the statement is general rather than specific.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy and product pages specifically list encryption in transit and at rest, Google Cloud-hosted infrastructure, and data processing agreements with subprocessors as security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: All data transmitted on the network is explicitly stated to be encrypted both in transit and at rest across all product pages and the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The add-on operates through Google Workspace SSO (Google account login), which enforces Google's password and authentication standards — no separate password is required.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The service uses Google Workspace SSO/OAuth for authentication, which supports MFA at the Google account level, satisfying this requirement for school deployments.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A separate Cookie Notice exists (https://www.livepolls.app/slides_translator/cookie) and cookies/web beacons are acknowledged, but some cookies are noted as not yet fully categorized by their providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google (Analytics, Firebase, Translate API), Stripe (payments), and unspecified subprocessors are referenced, but a complete named list of all subprocessors is not publicly provided in one place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing broadly by category (Google services, Stripe, subprocessors) rather than specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The platform explicitly states it does not sell data and does not use data for advertising or profiling, and users can opt out of interest-based advertising; no meaningful third-party sharing for non-operational purposes exists.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The automagicalapps.com privacy policy states that data processing agreements are concluded with all subprocessors to ensure secure and compliant data handling.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The cookie policy notes it may be updated but does not commit to proactively notifying users of third-party subprocessor changes; users are advised to revisit policies periodically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The platform explicitly states it does not use data for advertising or profiling purposes, and no ads are displayed within the Google Slides add-on interface.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy and product pages explicitly state user data is never used for advertising or profiling, and no targeted advertising is conducted.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is used; Google Analytics data is anonymized (random string + domain name only) and is not used for ad targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies and web beacons are acknowledged in the Cookie Notice, but some are not yet fully categorized — their use appears functional/analytical rather than for advertising, though full classification is incomplete.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The platform's policy states it will never use data for advertising purposes, and users may opt out of interest-based advertising; the no-advertising stance effectively removes the need for a separate advertiser opt-out.

dataSharedWith: OpenAI (user-entered text only, for slide generation)
r635.riskReason: SlidesAI lacks any COPPA-specific disclosures, age restrictions, parental consent mechanisms, data retention policy, cookie policy, or FERPA provisions, making it unsuitable for direct student use in K-12 without significant additional school-level controls.
r635.parentSummary: SlidesAI collects your email address for authentication and sends any text you type into the tool to OpenAI's servers to generate slides; no other personal data is claimed to be shared with third parties. The platform states it does not sell user data and uses HTTPS encryption plus encryption at rest. However, there is no minimum age requirement, no COPPA or FERPA compliance statement, no cookie policy, no data retention schedule, and no parental consent process, which are significant concerns for K-12 use involving minors.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy and terms of use provide no stated process for advance notification of changes or a revision history; users are told continued use constitutes acceptance.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy identifies email address and user-entered text as the primary data collected, but does not address usage metadata, IP addresses, device identifiers, or analytics data that may be collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states data is collected via Google OAuth for authentication and through direct user input, but does not fully explain automated or passive data collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly assign data ownership; it states data is used for service delivery and not sold, but does not explicitly affirm that users own their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can submit a deletion request via email to a support address, but there is no self-service deletion mechanism and no stated response timeframe or confirmation process.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or retention policy is stated anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of use.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references HTTPS encryption in transit and encryption at rest, as well as emergency breach response procedures, but does not describe specific technical or organizational security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states all communications occur via HTTPS and all data is encrypted at rest, satisfying encryption requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Authentication is handled entirely via Google OAuth and SSO, which enforces Google's password and security standards, meeting this requirement by proxy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: SlidesAI uses Google OAuth for all authentication, which supports Google's native MFA/2SV capabilities, meeting this requirement via SSO.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy does not include any cookie policy, list of cookies used, or disclosure of tracking technologies, despite the platform operating as a web-based service.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Only OpenAI is named as a third-party recipient of data; no other vendors, analytics providers, payment processors (e.g., Paddle), or infrastructure providers are disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states only user-entered text is sent to OpenAI for processing, but does not describe what data, if any, is shared with other undisclosed vendors such as Paddle (the payment processor).
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing (including OpenAI processing) is described; users cannot opt out without ceasing to use the core product.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not state that third-party processors (including OpenAI) are bound by data protection agreements or must adhere to the same privacy standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no stated process for notifying users if third-party sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy and terms of use contain no mention of advertising, and the product appears to be a paid/subscription tool with no ads served to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No evidence of targeted advertising exists in the policy or product description; the platform is subscription-based and does not reference ad targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No opt-out or disclosure related to third-party ad tracking is provided; while ads appear absent, the lack of a cookie policy leaves third-party tracker usage unaddressed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacon, pixel, or tracking technology disclosure is made anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described; the absence of any advertising or tracking disclosure means this cannot be assessed or confirmed.

dataCollected: Social login data (Google, Facebook, Apple username and profile info)
dataSharedWith: LiveRamp Inc. (identity resolution and targeted advertising)
IAB Europe advertising partners and header bidding platforms (Rubicon Project, Index Exchange, DistrictM, Amazon APS, OpenX)
r636.riskReason: Slidesgo is explicitly designed for adults 18+, runs personalized/targeted advertising for free users via a broad network of third-party ad partners, shares user data including hashed email and IP with LiveRamp for cross-device advertising, and lacks robust K-12-specific data protections in its general consumer-facing policies — though its separate Teams/Education plan claims COPPA and FERPA compliance for subsidiary (student) accounts.
r636.parentSummary: Slidesgo collects personal data including name, email, IP address, browser data, and usage behavior, and for free-tier users displays personalized ads powered by a large network of third-party advertising partners including Google, LiveRamp, and IAB vendors. The platform's standard Terms of Service require users to be at least 18 years old; however, a separate educational Teams subscription allows school admins to create student accounts without entering personal information for those subsidiary accounts, with Slidesgo claiming COPPA and FERPA compliance for that specific use case. Parents should be aware that the general platform is ad-supported and shares data with many third parties for targeting purposes, and schools should ensure they are using the managed Teams/Education plan — not individual free accounts — for student use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states the last revision date is shown at the top and recommends users review it periodically, but there is no stated process for advance notification to users before changes take effect.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data (identification data, login data, payment data, usage data, cookies, social login data) but the full enumeration is spread across multiple sections and sub-policies, making it incomplete as a single consolidated list for K-12 review.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected — directly from users during registration, passively via cookies and tracking technologies, and from third-party platforms like Google, Facebook, and Apple during social login.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy designates Freepik Company S.L.U. as the Data Controller, implying the company holds ownership and control over data; user ownership is not explicitly affirmed, creating an unclear ownership posture for K-12 purposes.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their account per the FAQ, but users with an active subscription cannot delete their account until the subscription expires, representing a conditional and time-delayed deletion option.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Retention periods are mentioned for some processing activities (e.g., one year for recruitment data, 'maximum period necessary' for AI assistant queries) but a comprehensive, consistent retention schedule for all user data types is not provided in a single location.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy makes a general commitment to using 'top-tier service providers' and mentions PCI-DSS Level 1 certification for payment processing via Stripe, but does not enumerate specific technical security controls (e.g., firewalls, access controls, SOC 2) for the main platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Payment data transmitted to Stripe/PayPal is described as encrypted, and the site uses HTTPS, but the privacy policy does not explicitly state that all stored user data is encrypted at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service instruct users to keep their password confidential, but there is no stated enforcement of strong password requirements (e.g., minimum length, complexity rules) for standard accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) or LTI/SSO integration for school environments is made anywhere in the publicly available Terms or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A detailed Cookie Policy is available at slidesgo.com/legal/cookies with a granular consent management panel (OneTrust) listing cookie categories, purposes, and third-party partners, along with a full cookie table.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy and cookie policy specifically name third parties including LiveRamp, Google, Facebook, Twitter, Stripe, PayPal, Hotjar, Cloudflare, Rubicon Project, Index Exchange, DistrictM, Amazon APS, and OpenX.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: While specific third parties are named, the data shared with each party is described at a category level (e.g., 'email in hashed form, IP address, browser info' to LiveRamp) rather than providing a precise per-party data inventory for all partners.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of non-essential cookies via the OneTrust consent panel and reject advertising cookies granularly, but opting out of LiveRamp sharing when entering an email at login is not clearly available and advertising is mandatory for free users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that third-party data processors operate under contracts that establish their duties to Freepik as data controller, and that personal data will not be used for other purposes beyond what is stipulated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy notes the revision date at the top and recommends periodic review but does not commit to notifying users specifically when third-party data processor relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Slidesgo explicitly states in both the Terms and Privacy Policy that personalized advertisements are displayed to free users, with no age-based exceptions for K-12 student users on standard accounts.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The platform uses cookies, LiveRamp identity resolution, and a broad IAB header bidding network to serve interest-based and behaviorally targeted ads to free users, confirming user-level targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Users can reject advertising cookies via the OneTrust panel, providing some opt-out capability, but third-party ad partners (Google, IAB vendors, LiveRamp) conduct additional tracking whose full opt-out path is not consolidated in one place.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy confirms use of tracking cookies, pixel tags, behavioral retargeting, real-time bidding, and cross-device identification (via LiveRamp) for advertising, which go well beyond functional tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out from advertising cookies is available via the OneTrust cookie consent panel, but the process for opting out of data already shared with LiveRamp or downstream IAB partners is unclear and not straightforwardly actionable.

dataSharedWith: Named subprocessors and service providers (listed at slido.com/terms)
r637.riskReason: Slido is a B2B platform not designed for K-12 use: it lacks explicit COPPA compliance or minimum age requirements, the free Basic plan treats all data as public, third-party advertising cookies are present, and there is no stated FERPA framework or student data protections.
r637.parentSummary: Slido collects participant data including names, email addresses, IP addresses, poll responses, and usage/device information to operate its audience engagement service. Data may be shared with its parent company Cisco, named subprocessors, and third-party advertising and analytics partners, with opt-out available for interest-based ads. Slido is a business-focused tool with no stated minimum age, no COPPA compliance language, and the free Basic plan explicitly treats collected data as public — making it a significant privacy risk for K-12 student use without additional contractual protections.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Slido publishes updated legal documents with effective dates and a changelog, and previous versions are archived, but proactive advance user notification is opt-in via email subscription rather than automatic.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Slido's Privacy Data Sheet lists key data categories (name, email, IP address, usage/device data, poll responses), but the full enumeration is spread across multiple documents (Privacy Data Sheet, Cookie Policy, Cisco Privacy Statement) rather than a single comprehensive list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy documentation states data is collected directly from users, automatically via cookies and web logs, and from integrations (e.g., Zoom), but specific collection mechanisms per data type are described only in supplemental PDFs rather than the main policy page.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Slido explicitly states 'you own all your data at all times and decide on the level of privacy,' and the DPA confirms the customer is the data controller, meeting ownership transparency requirements.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request account deletion and data deletion via the help center or support, and the DPA obligates Slido to delete or return all customer personal data upon contract end, constituting full deletion capability.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Slido states data is stored for the duration of the contract and deleted upon termination, but no specific numerical retention period (e.g., 30, 90 days post-contract) is prominently stated in the main policy, making the retention timeline vague for standard accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Slido's security page details specific measures including AWS hosting, regular third-party penetration testing, access controls, incident response policies, and role-based access management, meeting the requirement for specific security measure disclosure.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Slido uses HTTPS and TLS for data in transit and stores data securely in databases on AWS, with encryption confirmed by third-party documentation, satisfying encryption requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Slido explicitly states it does not enforce strong password complexity requirements for user accounts, citing NIST guidance, which fails the strong password enforcement standard for K-12 contexts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Slido supports SAML-based SSO (e.g., Okta, OneLogin) for paid plans and the security page references MFA, but these features are not available on the free Basic plan, resulting in only partial coverage.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Slido has a dedicated Cookie Policy page that distinguishes first-party and third-party cookies and mentions advertising and analytics categories, but does not provide a comprehensive named list of every cookie with individual purpose descriptions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Slido references a list of subprocessors and service providers at slido.com/terms, and names Cisco as a parent-company subprocessor, but the main policy page broadly generalizes rather than naming all third parties inline.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Privacy Data Sheet and subprocessor list provide some detail on what data goes to which provider, but specific data-per-third-party mappings are not consolidated in the main privacy policy and require navigating multiple supplemental documents.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of interest-based advertising cookies via Cookie Settings, and can object to data sharing via a Privacy Request form, but opting out of all third-party data sharing is not straightforward for non-Enterprise customers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The DPA and Terms explicitly require all subprocessors to maintain reasonable data practices and confidentiality, and Slido assumes liability for subprocessor acts and omissions to the same extent as if performing services directly.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Customers can subscribe to email notifications of new subprocessors, but notification is opt-in and the default is simply updating the online list — meaning customers who have not subscribed may not be proactively informed of changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Slido's privacy documentation confirms that third-party advertising partners may display interest-based ads using cookies, including on other sites, which goes beyond platform-based-only advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Third-party partners are confirmed to use cookies and similar technologies to provide advertising based on browsing activities and interests, constituting confirmed interest-based user targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: An opt-out from interest-based advertising is available via Cookie Settings and via Google Analytics opt-out, but third-party tracking cookies are active by default and opt-out requires user action, providing only limited opt-out capability.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Slido's privacy policy confirms use of cookies, web logs, web beacons, and similar tracking technologies by Cisco and engaged third parties for advertising purposes, not just functional tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out from interest-based advertising and from Cisco sharing data with third parties for marketing is available via a Privacy Request form and Cookie Settings, but the process is not clearly surfaced for K-12 contexts and requires users to proactively seek it out.

dataCollected: Student caseload data (names, goals, session notes)
dataSharedWith: Service providers as required by law
r638.riskReason: SLP Now processes sensitive student PHI and IEP data but explicitly shifts COPPA and FERPA compliance responsibility to the educator/school rather than assuming it directly, creating a compliance gap for K-12 deployments.
r638.parentSummary: SLP Now is a membership platform for speech-language pathologists that stores student caseload data, session notes, IEP information, and PHI on HIPAA-compliant servers. The platform does not directly collect data from children but processes student data entered by SLPs; it contractually places the burden of obtaining parental consent and FERPA compliance on the school or educator rather than taking on that responsibility itself. Payment data is not stored by SLP Now and is handled by PCI-DSS-compliant processors, but the privacy policy provides limited detail on specific third parties used, cookie practices, data retention timelines, and user deletion rights.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service state material changes become effective 30 days after posting and reference a prior versions URL, but the Terms themselves say changes can be made 'with or without notice,' making notification only partially guaranteed.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists broad categories of personal information collected (contact info, payment info, usage data, PHI/PII submitted by users) but does not enumerate every specific data field collected, leaving some ambiguity.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states data is collected directly from users via telephone, text, email, website, apps, and automated IT/security systems, adequately describing collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service state 'as between you and us, we own all the foregoing' regarding service content, and do not clearly affirm that user-submitted student or educator data remains owned by the user or school.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The Terms of Service indicate users may terminate accounts at any time, and the privacy policy references user rights, but no explicit, clear self-service data deletion process or timeline is described in the publicly available policies.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Neither the privacy policy nor the terms of service specify a data retention period or general retention timeline for user or student data after account termination.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The platform claims HIPAA-compliant servers and a BAA is incorporated into terms, but the privacy policy itself provides only a general security statement without listing specific technical measures such as encryption standards or access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: HIPAA-compliant server storage is claimed on the product page, implying encryption at rest and in transit, but the privacy policy does not explicitly state encryption is used throughout the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy and terms of service make no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is found in the publicly available terms or privacy policy, though the community login page references SSO as an option.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy does not include a dedicated cookie policy, does not list cookies by name or purpose, and makes no mention of cookie consent management or opt-out mechanisms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy names payment processors as a third-party category and references cloud server providers, but does not name specific third-party vendors (e.g., Stripe, AWS) used in the service.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Third-party sharing is described at a categorical level (payment processors, legal requirements) without specifying which data fields are shared with each specific third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in the privacy policy or terms; users are not given a process to limit or decline such sharing outside of account termination.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Terms of Purchase include FERPA-aligned language stating SLP Now will not disclose educational records without consent, but no explicit vendor data processing agreements with third-party subprocessors are described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy and terms of service do not include any provision notifying users when third-party subprocessors or sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: There is no indication in the privacy policy or terms that advertising of any kind is displayed within the platform; the service is subscription-based.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is described or implied in any of the policy documents; the platform is a paid professional tool with no ad-based revenue model indicated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is described in the policies; the platform does not appear to use advertising networks or behavioral tracking for ad purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy does not address web beacons or pixel tracking, leaving tracking methods for analytics purposes unclear beyond general automated system monitoring.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising or ad-related data sharing is indicated, there is no need for an ad data-sharing opt-out, and this is effectively met by the absence of such practices.

r639.riskReason: SLP Stephen explicitly restricts its platform to users 18 and older, has no FERPA or SOPIPA compliance language, no dedicated Terms of Service, no cookie policy, no MFA, and no student data protections — making it unsuitable for K-12 school use without significant additional vetting.
r639.parentSummary: SLP Stephen (owned by Beat Stuttering, LLC) collects names, email addresses, billing information, and IP/usage data from users of its website. The site explicitly states it is directed to individuals 18 years and older and claims COPPA compliance by stating it does not collect data from anyone under 18. However, the platform has no dedicated Terms of Service, no FERPA or SOPIPA compliance language, and no cookie-specific policy, meaning it lacks the formal K-12 student privacy protections expected of an EdTech tool used in schools.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states it reserves the right to change without notice but also says it will notify users via email or a prominent website notice for material changes — these contradictory statements result in only partial compliance.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data types (name, email, billing info, IP address) but does not provide a comprehensive enumeration of all data collected, including cookies or analytics data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes that data is collected via contact forms and account creation but does not specifically detail all collection mechanisms such as cookies, tracking pixels, or analytics.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states Beat Stuttering, LLC is the data controller and does not clearly affirm that users own their own data; ownership is implicitly held by the company.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion of their personal data at any time by contacting stephen@slpstephen.com, which satisfies the deletion requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained for 'the minimum amount of time necessary' but provides no specific retention period or timeframe, making this only a general/vague statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy does not list any specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, firewalls, access controls) used to protect personal data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption in transit or at rest anywhere in the policy or on the website.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy notes users are responsible for maintaining password confidentiality but does not enforce or recommend strong password standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration anywhere in the policy or on the website.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: There is no cookie policy; the only reference to cookies is a general mention that IP addresses may be used to diagnose server problems, with no list of cookies or their purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy refers generically to a 'hosting provider, newsletter provider, payment processors, or team members' but does not name any specific third-party companies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what particular data is shared with each category of third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: There is no opt-out mechanism described for third-party data sharing beyond the general deletion request process.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states data processors are used for 'technical and organizational purposes' and claims reasonable efforts for GDPR compliance, but provides no formal vendor agreement terms or binding obligations.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention any process for notifying users when third-party processors or partners change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy does not address advertising at all; it is unclear whether ads are displayed to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No advertising or targeting policy exists; the absence of any ad-related disclosure means targeted advertising cannot be ruled out.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure regarding third-party tracking for advertising purposes is made anywhere in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No mention of web beacons, tracking pixels, or other ad-tracking technologies is made in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out mechanism for data sharing with advertisers is described anywhere in the policy.

r640.minAge: 18 (adults only; platform explicitly states services are for adults only and not for children under 13)
dataCollected: Student progress monitoring and assessment data
dataSharedWith: Subprocessors (third-party contractors for data storage and access)
r640.riskReason: SLP Toolkit has strong student data protections via its SDPA and FERPA compliance, but its use of the Meta Pixel and GA4 for advertising measurement on its marketing site introduces third-party tracking concerns, and the main privacy policy explicitly excludes student/FERPA data from its coverage, creating a documentation gap.
r640.parentSummary: SLP Toolkit is a tool designed exclusively for licensed Speech-Language Pathologists (SLPs) and school staff — students do not have accounts and do not directly interact with the platform. Student data such as name, date of birth, grade, IEP dates, and progress monitoring results is collected by SLPs for educational service purposes and is governed by a Student Data Privacy Agreement (SDPA) that affirms FERPA compliance, states that student data is owned by the user/institution, and prohibits sale of that data. However, the platform's marketing website uses Meta Pixel and Google Analytics (GA4) cookies for advertising measurement, which parents and administrators should be aware of when evaluating the platform's overall data practices.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states a revision date is posted and significant changes trigger email notification, but minor/non-significant changes take effect immediately upon posting without advance notice, making notification incomplete.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Educator/user personal data types are listed in the privacy policy (name, email, IP, browser, location, role), and student data elements are enumerated in the SDPA and knowledge base, but the main privacy policy explicitly excludes student/FERPA data from its coverage, creating a split documentation gap.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically explains that data is collected automatically (IP, browser, OS, pages visited) upon site visit, and voluntarily when users register or fill out forms, with the SDPA covering how student data is entered by SLPs.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The SDPA explicitly states that all student data 'is and will continue to be the property of and under the control of the User,' and the privacy policy confirms student institutional records are the property of the institution.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can manually delete data within the application interface at any time, and upon account cancellation, data is scheduled for deletion within 30 days; GDPR/CCPA deletion rights are also referenced.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is deleted on a 30-day schedule after account cancellation, but does not specify a broader retention period for active accounts beyond 'as long as your subscription is active,' which is vague for compliance purposes.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The SDPA and associated DSPA reference industry-standard security practices, periodic risk assessments, employee training, and backup procedures, but the main privacy policy only offers a general statement that 'reasonable measures' are taken without listing specific controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The SLP Toolkit knowledge base states that all student data is encrypted when stored in databases, satisfying the encryption requirement for data at rest; transmission security is referenced via industry best practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The signup page notes passwords must meet certain requirements, but the policy does not explicitly detail or enforce specific strong password standards (e.g., minimum length, complexity rules) in the published documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) or SSO/LTI integration was found in the publicly available privacy policy, terms of service, or SDPA documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy for the main site mentions 'Cookies and Meta Business' and the companion Kit site lists GA4 and Meta Pixel cookies, but does not provide a comprehensive cookie inventory with individual purposes for each cookie type.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The knowledge base acknowledges that subcontractors are used to store and access student data and states their information is listed in a knowledge base article, but specific subprocessor names are not enumerated directly within the main privacy policy or SDPA.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The SDPA states subprocessors enter into written agreements to protect student data, but the specific data elements shared with each named subprocessor are not itemized in the publicly available policy documents.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can manage cookies via browser settings to limit some third-party tracking, and can opt out of marketing emails, but there is no explicit opt-out mechanism from subprocessor data sharing for core service functions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The SDPA explicitly requires SLP Toolkit to enter into written agreements with all subprocessors requiring them to protect student data consistent with the terms of the SDPA, meeting the vendor agreement requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states that changes to the privacy notice will be posted and a revision date updated, and significant changes will trigger email notification, but there is no specific commitment to notify users when individual subprocessors or third parties change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The marketing website uses Meta Pixel for advertising measurement, indicating ads are run (though targeted at adult SLP professionals, not students); the platform itself does not display ads to users inside the app.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The Meta Pixel is used to measure advertising campaign effectiveness and understand user actions on the site, which constitutes possible third-party behavioral targeting of site visitors, though not of students within the application.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Users can manage cookie/tracking settings via browser privacy controls, but no explicit opt-out from Meta Pixel or GA4 tracking is offered within the site itself beyond browser-level controls.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Both GA4 cookies and the Meta Pixel are disclosed in the Kit/companion privacy policy, but the main SLP Toolkit privacy policy references 'Cookies and Meta Business' only generally without fully detailing the tracking mechanisms used.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Browser-level cookie management is referenced as a way to opt out of tracking, but no clear in-platform opt-out process for data sharing with advertising measurement third parties (Meta, Google) is described.

r641.riskReason: Smashy Road displays personalized ads, uses Unity Ads for third-party advertising, tracks users across apps and websites, and has no COPPA/FERPA compliance provisions, making it inappropriate for K-12 school use.
r641.parentSummary: Smashy Road (by Bearbit Studios) collects email addresses when voluntarily provided and routes third-party advertising through Unity Ads, which may track users across apps and websites for targeted advertising. The platform explicitly states it does not target users under 13, but provides no COPPA-compliant parental consent mechanism or child-specific protections. Common Sense Media rated this app with a 'Warning' due to concerns about personalized advertising and user tracking, making it a poor fit for school deployment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it may change and links to the current version at smashyroad.com/privacy, but does not describe a process for advance notification to users of material changes.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy identifies email and correspondence as personal data collected, and mentions non-personal data via third-party APIs, but does not comprehensively enumerate all data types collected (e.g., device identifiers, ad tracking data).
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states email is collected when users 'nominate to specifically allow' collection and correspondence is kept if users contact support, but the mechanism for third-party API data collection is only vaguely described.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not address who owns the data; it makes no statement affirming user ownership and implicitly treats collected data as company-controlled with no user ownership clause.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy references the right to access and correct personal information under the Privacy Act but does not clearly describe a full deletion process; it only mentions a written access request process with potential administrative fees.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state any specific or general data retention period, leaving users uninformed about how long their data is stored.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy contains no description of specific security measures, encryption standards, or technical/organizational controls used to protect user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption is made anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of use for data in transit or at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account creation is required to use Smashy Road, so password enforcement is not applicable and does not pose a risk.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account registration is required for the core game, making MFA and SSO not applicable and not a compliance gap.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy states Bearbit Studios itself does not use cookies to track web movement, but acknowledges third-party APIs (like Unity Ads) may track users; no detailed cookie inventory or opt-out mechanism is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Unity Ads is named as a third-party partner with a link to their privacy policy, but no other third parties are specifically identified by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify which data elements are shared with Unity Ads or any other third party; data sharing scope is entirely undisclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism from third-party data sharing (including Unity Ads) is described in the policy; users have no documented recourse.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not assert that third-party partners are bound by contractual data protection agreements or that Bearbit Studios holds them to privacy standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not commit to notifying users if third-party partners change, are added, or removed; it simply disclaims responsibility for third-party sites.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Common Sense Media's evaluation confirms that personalized advertising is displayed within the app, which is a significant concern for K-12 use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: According to Common Sense Media, user information is used to track and target advertisements on third-party websites or services, confirming active user-level ad targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Unity Ads integration enables cross-app and cross-website tracking for advertising purposes, and no opt-out from this tracking is described in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Third-party tracking via Unity Ads APIs is confirmed, but the policy does not disclose specific tracking methods such as web beacons, SDKs, or device fingerprinting used by these partners.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out mechanism from advertiser data sharing is provided anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of use, leaving users with no documented way to limit ad-related data use.

dataCollected: Donor contact information uploaded by participants
dataSharedWith: Facebook and Twitter (only via optional user-initiated share functionality)
Law enforcement / legal authorities (when required by law)
Successor entities in the event of merger or acquisition
r642.riskReason: While Snap Raise makes strong no-sell/no-share pledges and claims COPPA compliance, its policies contain multiple gaps: no explicit FERPA acknowledgment, vague data retention language, no MFA described, third-party SDK integrations without named vendors, policy-change notice that is optional ('and/or email'), and cookies used for behavioral tracking without a granular cookie list.
r642.parentSummary: Snap Raise collects names, email addresses, phone numbers, mailing addresses, and payment information from group leaders, participants, and donors to operate school fundraising campaigns. The company explicitly states it does not sell or share user data with third parties for marketing purposes, claims COPPA compliance by restricting use to users 13 and older, and uses SSL encryption for financial data. However, the privacy policy does not explicitly address FERPA, data retention periods are only vaguely described as 'no longer than necessary,' and the platform uses cookies that track user IDs and browsing behavior whose full scope is not itemized.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states changes will be posted on the page 'and/or' sent by email, meaning advance notification by email is optional rather than guaranteed, and no versioned revision history is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Snap Raise privacy policy lists key data types (name, email, mailing address, phone, credit card), but does not comprehensively enumerate all data collected such as IP address, device identifiers, or full cookie data categories.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states data is collected when users register, place an order, or use the app, and cookies are used to track IDs and browsing behavior, providing a clear explanation of collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; it restricts Snap Mobile from selling or transferring data but does not affirmatively grant data ownership rights to users.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: There is no clearly described self-service data deletion process for users; users can opt out of marketing emails, but the policy does not address the right to request full deletion of personal data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is not retained 'longer than is necessary' and is disposed of safely, but provides no specific retention timeframe, making this a vague rather than a specific retention statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'a variety of security measures' and mentions SSL encryption and certified data centers with ISO, PCI DSS, SOC, and NIST standards on the security page, but the privacy policy itself does not enumerate specific technical controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: SSL/TLS encryption is explicitly stated for sensitive and credit card data transmission, and the security page confirms use of certified, standards-compliant data centers.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy and terms do not describe any password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are acknowledged and a consent banner is present, but the policy does not provide a granular list of all cookies used, their names, or their specific purposes beyond general preference and behavior tracking.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Stripe is named as the payment processor and Facebook/Twitter are mentioned for optional share functionality, but third-party SDK vendors integrated into the app are not individually named.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy broadly states that only information transmitted through user-initiated share actions goes to Facebook/Twitter, but does not specify what data fields are shared with Stripe or SDK partners.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing emails via unsubscribe, but there is no described process for opting out of data sharing with operational third parties such as Stripe or SDK providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not include explicit contractual language requiring third-party vendors to adhere to equivalent data protection standards, only noting that third-party sites have their own independent privacy policies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes will be posted on the page and/or sent by email, which partially covers notification of third-party changes, but does not commit to proactive advance notice specifically for third-party data-sharing changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Snap Raise explicitly states it does not sell user data for advertising and is a fee-based platform, with no indication that ads are displayed to users within the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The platform's stated business model is a service fee rather than advertising revenue, and the policy explicitly prohibits selling or sharing data for promotional purposes without user consent.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Cookies track user IDs and browsing behavior and third-party SDKs are integrated into the app, but the policy does not clearly specify whether any of these involve third-party ad tracking or provide a straightforward opt-out from such tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies are used for behavioral tracking (unique ID, preferences, browsing behavior) but the policy does not clarify whether these are purely functional or include any third-party web beacon or tracking pixel activity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An unsubscribe process for marketing emails is described, but there is no clear opt-out mechanism specifically for data sharing with any third-party advertising or analytics services.

dataSharedWith: Dynavox Group affiliates (administrative and support purposes)
Sub-processors (product development, technical support, cybersecurity, sales, marketing, HR, IT)
Other app users (teacher-to-student page set sharing feature)
r643.riskReason: Tobii Dynavox explicitly states it does not sell personal data and acknowledges COPPA obligations for under-13 users, but the privacy policy does not specifically address FERPA, lacks specific data retention periods, uses third-party analytics and advertising cookies on its website, and does not name all sub-processors or specify what data each receives.
r643.parentSummary: Snap Scene, by Tobii Dynavox, is an AAC communication app designed for children with speech and language disabilities; it collects names, email addresses, device IDs, photos, audio recordings, and usage data to operate the service and may sync this data to Tobii Dynavox servers when used online. The company states it does not sell personal data and acknowledges it must obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting data from children under 13, which is a positive protection for K-12 use. However, the privacy policy does not explicitly address FERPA compliance, does not name all third-party sub-processors, and the company's website uses advertising and analytics cookies, raising concerns for schools seeking full FERPA and SOPIPA compliance.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states material changes will be communicated via email, website updates, or in-app patch notes, but no revision history or archive of prior versions is publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy notice lists several categories of data (contact info, device ID, IP, usage data, photos, audio recordings, organization details) but does not claim to be an exhaustive list and notes some services may collect data not listed in the policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes collection through direct user input, account creation, and product/service interaction, but does not comprehensively detail every collection method (e.g., passive SDK-based collection in the app).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states data is used only for internal purposes and service delivery, and Tobii Dynavox explicitly does not sell or trade personal information, implying user ownership or at minimum non-commercial stewardship of the data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can contact privacymanager@tobiidynavox.com to request deletion under GDPR rights, but no self-service deletion tool is described and the process is not clearly defined for U.S. K-12 school contexts or for data stored locally on devices.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention periods are stated in the publicly accessible privacy notice; the policy does not address how long user data, photos, or audio recordings are retained either on-device or on servers.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy mentions use of encryption, access controls, and secure servers, but does not detail specific security frameworks, certifications (e.g., SOC 2), or audit practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is explicitly mentioned as a security measure applied to personal data, indicating at minimum encryption in storage and transit is in place.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy and terms of service do not address password strength requirements or enforcement policies for user accounts on mytobiidynavox.com.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is found in the publicly available terms or privacy notice for Snap Scene.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A separate cookie policy exists at us.tobiidynavox.com/pages/cookie-usage-statement that lists categories of cookies (functional, analytics, advertising, social), but does not enumerate every specific cookie by name and purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy notice references 'Sub-Processors' supporting business functions and provides a general list of categories (support, cybersecurity, marketing, HR, IT) but does not name specific third-party companies in the publicly accessible policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with sub-processors is described only by functional category (e.g., analytics, support) rather than specifying what data types each specific third party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can contact Tobii Dynavox to exercise data rights including objection to processing, but no simple self-service opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described for U.S. users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy notice explicitly states all sub-processors are contractually bound to adhere to GDPR and applicable privacy law data protection obligations, indicating vendor agreement requirements are in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states Tobii Dynavox will notify users of material changes through email, website, or in-app notices, but does not specifically commit to notifying users when sub-processors change or are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Tobii Dynavox website uses advertising cookies; however, the Snap Scene app itself, as an AAC tool, does not appear to display third-party ads within the app interface, creating a partially compliant situation depending on context.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Advertising cookies on the Tobii Dynavox website are described as tailoring marketing and may involve third-party ad targeting; it is unclear whether this extends to app users, making full compliance unconfirmed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The cookie policy acknowledges third-party analytics and advertising cookies (including Google Analytics) on the website with some opt-out guidance, but does not clearly state whether in-app tracking for ads occurs or provide a complete opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy discloses use of pixels and tags from third parties that may place cookies for behavioral advertising and analytics, but does not comprehensively list all tracking technologies used across both the website and the app.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The cookie policy references opt-out options for Google Analytics and mentions users can manage cookies through browser settings, but a clear, comprehensive opt-out process for all advertiser data sharing is not explicitly documented.

dataCollected: Biometric data (face, hands, voice via camera/lenses)
r644.riskReason: Snapchat is a consumer social media platform that collects extensive personal data including location, biometrics, and AI chat content, displays targeted advertising to minors as young as 13, is not designed for K-12 educational use, has no FERPA agreement, has no school/district data privacy controls, and has been the subject of FTC enforcement actions related to harm to young users.
r644.parentSummary: Snapchat (snap.com) collects a wide range of personal data from users including name, email, phone number, location, photos, messages, device information, and biometric data through camera features, and uses this data to deliver targeted advertising and personalize content. While Snapchat states it does not sell personal data, it does share information with advertising partners and third-party service providers, and third-party advertising partners may use tracking cookies to build interest profiles. Snapchat is a general consumer social media platform, not an educational tool — it has no FERPA compliance, no school data privacy agreements, and the FTC referred a complaint against Snap in January 2025 alleging the company's AI chatbot caused risk and harm to young users, making it a high-risk platform for K-12 school use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Snap publishes effective dates for policy updates (current Privacy Policy effective April 7, 2025) and prior versions are archived, but there is no explicit advance notification requirement stated for general users before changes take effect.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy Policy provides a detailed list of data categories collected including name, email, phone, date of birth, photos, videos, messages, location, device info, biometrics, advertising identifiers, and AI chat content.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically explains data is collected directly from users during sign-up and use, automatically via device/usage signals, and from third parties such as advertisers and linked services.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Snap grants itself a broad license to use, display, reproduce, and distribute user content for operating and improving services, creating ambiguity about true user data ownership; user ownership is not explicitly affirmed.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can access, update, delete, and download their data through in-app self-service tools, and account deletion triggers data deletion, with GDPR-based deletion rights also honored.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Retention periods are described generally (e.g., Snaps delete after being opened, location varies by precision), with references to a support page for product-specific periods, but a single comprehensive retention schedule is not provided in the main policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states Snap takes 'reasonable steps to protect the confidentiality and security of personal information' but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as encryption protocols, access controls, or audit practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The Privacy Policy does not explicitly disclose whether user data is encrypted at rest or in transit; encryption is not mentioned as a security measure in the main policy text.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service recommend selecting a strong password and enabling two-factor authentication but do not enforce strong password requirements as a technical control.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Two-factor authentication is available and mentioned in the Terms of Service as a recommended account security measure, but it is optional rather than required or enforced.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Snap maintains a dedicated Cookie Policy at snap.com/cookie-policy that categorizes cookies by purpose and references a Cookie Information Page listing specific cookies, duration, and use.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy identifies broad categories of third parties (service providers, advertisers, affiliates, integrated partners) but does not name specific companies in the main policy; a separate service provider category list is referenced.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with third parties is described by category rather than specifying exactly which data fields go to which specific third party, making it difficult to assess precise data flows.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can adjust some ad preferences and opt out of certain data uses, but opt-out from all third-party data sharing is not clearly available; ad targeting opt-out is limited and platform-dependent.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states service providers process data on Snap's behalf under contractual terms, and subprocessors in business services must follow legally binding terms, but the main consumer privacy policy only makes a general statement about this.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The US State Privacy Notice states it will be updated periodically and at least every 12 months, but there is no specific commitment to notify users in advance of changes to the list of third-party subprocessors or sharing partners.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Snapchat explicitly states in its Terms of Service that it shows ads and recommends content based on user interests, and the Privacy Policy confirms targeted advertising is displayed to users including those aged 13 and older.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Snap and third-party advertising partners use user data including demographics, location, activity, and interest inference to deliver targeted advertising, including within the My AI feature.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising partners may use tracking cookies to build interest profiles and deliver relevant advertising on other third-party sites across the internet, with no confirmed ability to opt out of all such tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Snap uses cookies, web beacons, web storage, and unique advertising identifiers to collect activity data for advertising purposes, and may collect information from third-party websites using Snap-provided cookies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Some ad preference controls are available in-app and through state privacy rights requests (e.g., CCPA opt-out), but a single clear, universal opt-out from all advertiser data sharing is not prominently described in the main policy.

dataSharedWith: Teachers and school officials (within partner school)
Parents and legal guardians (authorized by Customer)
r645.riskReason: Snappet explicitly prohibits ads, prohibits selling student data, acknowledges COPPA and FERPA compliance, uses zero-knowledge encryption for the supplemental service, and restricts data use strictly to educational purposes.
r645.parentSummary: Snappet collects student names, exercise responses, learning progress, and usage data solely to provide its educational platform, and explicitly states it does not sell student data or use it for advertising. Data is shared only with the student's school, authorized parents, and vetted service providers who are contractually bound to follow the same privacy standards. The platform acknowledges COPPA and FERPA compliance, uses encryption to protect student data, and provides a process for parents to request data access, correction, or deletion through their school.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states Snappet may update it from time to time and references notification, but does not clearly describe an advance-notification process or maintain a public revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates categories of data collected including registration information, exercise responses, progress tracking, usage data, device identifiers, and cookies, providing a reasonably comprehensive list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes data collected via account registration, platform usage/interaction, and automated technologies such as cookies, pixel tags, and local storage.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service explicitly states users retain ownership of their content and data, and Snappet does not claim ownership rights in user content.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Deletion is available but must be routed through the school/Customer, who then submits to Snappet; parents and students cannot delete data directly without school intermediation, limiting direct user control.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy mentions anonymous student accounts in the Supplemental Service are deleted nightly, but does not state a specific retention period (e.g., number of days or years) for identifiable student data in the full Partner School service.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references physical, technical, and administrative safeguards and access controls, but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as firewalls, intrusion detection, or audit logs.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly mentions zero-knowledge encryption for the Supplemental Service, and encrypted transmission of student names that Snappet cannot decrypt, indicating meaningful encryption use.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy and terms do not explicitly describe password strength requirements or enforcement; account login exists but password policy specifics are not disclosed.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) is found in the publicly available privacy policy or terms of service; SSO or LTI integration is not explicitly described.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies, session and persistent cookies, pixel tags, Flash cookies, and local storage, with some purpose descriptions, but does not provide a comprehensive categorized list of all cookies and their specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references broad categories of third-party service providers (application management, data hosting, customer service tools) but does not name specific third-party vendors or companies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states providers receive only what they need to perform their function but does not specify exactly which data types are shared with each category of third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No clear self-service opt-out from third-party data sharing is described; schools can direct Snappet on data use but individual users (parents/students) have no direct opt-out mechanism described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy explicitly states Snappet requires third-party service providers and partners to comply with the Privacy Policy and maintain confidentiality, security, and integrity of data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy notes it may be updated from time to time but does not commit to notifying users specifically when third-party service providers change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states there are no ads in the Services and student data is not used for advertising to students or anyone else.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly confirms no targeted advertising using student data; student data is never used for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy states advertising cookies are not used when logged in as a Partner School, and the Platform does not engage in third-party ad tracking for contracted school users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While advertising cookies are blocked within the logged-in Partner School platform, the policy mentions cookies and pixel tags may be used on the public site for ad optimization if consent to advertising cookies is given, which is somewhat unclear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: For contracted school users, no advertising data sharing occurs; for public site visitors, the policy implies consent-based advertising cookie use, and opt-out appears available via cookie settings, representing a clear enough process.

dataCollected: Log data (usage data, IP address, browser type)
r646.riskReason: SnapType self-claims COPPA/FERPA/GDPR compliance and no account is required, but the privacy policy is severely outdated (last updated January 2017), the Terms of Service simply defers to Apple's standard EULA with no school-specific data protections, advertisement cookies and third-party analytics trackers are present on the website, and no specific data retention period, security measures, or third-party vendor names are disclosed.
r646.parentSummary: SnapType is a K-12-focused app tool that claims COPPA, FERPA, and GDPR compliance and does not require students to create an account. However, the privacy policy has not been updated since January 2017 and lacks specifics on data retention, named third parties, and security measures; the website uses third-party analytical and advertisement cookies that track visitors across websites. Parents should note that while the app itself may collect minimal student data, the supporting website employs broader tracking technologies whose third-party recipients are not clearly named.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy was last updated January 5, 2017 with no stated notification process for future changes or revision history available to users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy references collection of log data and cookie-based data generally, but does not comprehensively enumerate all data types collected within the app itself.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy indicates data is collected via website use and mobile applications generally, but does not specifically describe the mechanisms of in-app data collection.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is not explicitly addressed in the policy; it is neither clearly assigned to the user nor claimed by the company.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No user data deletion mechanism or process is described anywhere in the privacy policy or on the website.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated anywhere in the privacy policy for any category of data collected.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy does not describe any specific security measures used to protect user or student data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of encryption is made in the policy, though the website serves over HTTPS indicating transport-layer encryption is in use.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account creation is required to use the app, eliminating password-related risks for student users.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required to use the platform, so MFA and SSO concerns are not applicable to student end-users.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The website discloses the existence of necessary, functional, analytical, and advertisement cookies, but does not list specific cookie names, durations, or the identities of third-party cookie providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third parties receiving data are not named; the policy only references unnamed analytics and advertising cookie providers without identification.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what data is shared with each third-party category; data shared via advertisement and analytics cookies is grouped without detail.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The cookie consent mechanism offers an opt-out for non-essential third-party cookies, but the opt-out process is general and not specifically tailored to student or school data contexts.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor data processing agreements or contractual obligations placed on third-party cookie providers are mentioned in the policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no stated process for notifying users if third-party data recipients change; the policy has not been updated since 2017.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly acknowledges advertisement cookies that are used to provide visitors with relevant ads and marketing campaigns, indicating ads-related tracking is present on the website.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Advertisement cookies described in the policy are used to track visitors across websites and collect information to provide customized ads, indicating third-party targeting is present.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The cookie consent tool offers an opt-out for advertisement cookies, but its implementation and effectiveness for K-12 school contexts is unclear and not COPPA-specific.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Advertisement cookies that track visitors across websites are confirmed in the policy, indicating cross-site tracking methods are in use beyond purely functional tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: A 'Do not sell my personal information' link is present on the privacy policy page, but the broader opt-out process for advertising data sharing is not clearly described or COPPA-aligned.

r647.riskReason: SocialBee is a commercial social media management platform built for businesses and adults, with no minimum age stated, no COPPA or FERPA provisions, no student data protections, and third-party data sharing (including Google Analytics) without K-12-specific safeguards.
r647.parentSummary: SocialBee collects personal information including names, email addresses, IP addresses, browser data, and usage logs, and shares data with affiliated companies, Google, and third-party service providers. The platform is designed for business social media management, not for K-12 students, and contains no COPPA, FERPA, or child-specific privacy protections. Parents and schools should be aware that this platform is entirely unsuitable for direct student use and poses significant compliance risks if deployed in a K-12 environment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service includes a last-updated date (November 3, 2024) and the Privacy Policy was last updated in late 2024, but there is no explicit advance notification process or revision history described for users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, IP address, log data, usage data, contact details) but does not provide a fully exhaustive enumeration of all data types collected across all service features.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy describes some collection methods (registration forms, server logs, contact forms) but does not comprehensively explain all collection mechanisms, particularly for third-party integrations and social media account data.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service states users retain ownership of their content but grants SocialBee a broad license to access, copy, distribute, and store user content for service provision, leaving ownership ambiguous in practice.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: SocialBee maintains an explicit Deletion Policy at socialbee.com/deletion-policy/ allowing users to request full deletion of personal data by emailing success@socialbee.com, with confirmation provided after deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy states log files are deleted after seven days and references legal retention obligations of up to 10 years, but does not provide a clear, unified retention schedule for all data types collected.
