r648.riskReason: Socrative collects identifiable student and teacher data, uses Google Analytics and session/persistent cookies, does not explicitly confirm encryption at rest, relies on teachers rather than independently obtaining verifiable parental consent under COPPA, and does not clearly disclose what specific data is shared with each named third-party sub-processor.
r648.parentSummary: Socrative collects personal information such as student names, school name, location, activity data, and device metadata to provide its classroom assessment services. Student data is never used for advertising, and Socrative states it will not sell student personal data; however, data is shared with several third-party sub-processors including Intercom and Customer.io, and the policy does not specify exactly what data each third party receives. Parents of children under 13 should be aware that COPPA consent is obtained via the teacher rather than directly from the parent, and the policy does not clearly address encryption at rest or specific data retention timelines.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Privacy Policy states changes will be posted on the website with a last-updated date visible (July 9, 2025), but does not explicitly commit to advance notification before changes take effect.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy Policy provides a detailed list of data collected including name, email, phone number, country, school name, school type, user ID, password, activity, device metadata, and student-specific incidental data such as class enrollment and profile pictures.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected — directly from users at registration, automatically via usage and cookies, and incidentally through teacher-uploaded content — satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Use indicate users own their content, but Showbie is designated as both Data Controller and Data Processor depending on context, creating some ambiguity about ultimate data ownership for student records.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may contact Socrative to request data deletion, but the policy does not provide a self-service deletion mechanism or clearly specify the timeframe within which deletion requests are honored.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy references retention in general terms tied to the purpose of collection, but does not state a specific numeric retention period for student or teacher data, making this only a partial meet.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states that 'appropriate security measures' are implemented to protect personal information, but does not enumerate specific technical or organizational measures beyond this general statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Socrative's support documentation confirms SSL/TLS encryption in transit, but the Privacy Policy itself does not explicitly address encryption at rest, resulting in only partial credit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy and Terms of Use contain no mention of password complexity requirements or enforcement of strong passwords, and no SSO-only model is mandated for student access.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the publicly available Privacy Policy or Terms of Use.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Privacy Policy acknowledges the use of both session and persistent cookies and references Google Analytics, but does not provide a full cookie list with individual purposes for each cookie type.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Socrative's support documentation names specific sub-processors including Amazon CloudFront, Intercom, and Customer.io, satisfying the requirement for named third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: While sub-processors are named, the policy groups the data shared with them broadly by business function (e.g., billing, support, marketing) and does not enumerate the exact data fields shared with each third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users may unsubscribe from marketing notifications at any time, but there is no clearly described opt-out process for broader third-party data sharing with sub-processors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states Showbie uses sub-processors to process data 'more effectively' and references a Data Processing Addendum for institutional customers, but does not explicitly state all third parties are contractually prohibited from using data for their own purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may change from time to time with changes posted on the website, but does not specifically commit to notifying users when new third-party sub-processors are added.

complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms no targeted advertising is directed to student users, and teacher-directed marketing is for Socrative's own products, not third-party targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy discloses use of Google Analytics and session/persistent cookies for activity tracking, but does not clearly describe an opt-out mechanism for analytics-based tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Session and persistent cookies are disclosed and Google Analytics is mentioned by name, but the full scope of tracking methods (web beacons, pixels, etc.) and their purposes are not individually enumerated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can unsubscribe from marketing notifications, but a clear, comprehensive opt-out from all forms of data sharing with advertising or analytics sub-processors is not explicitly described in the policy.

r649.riskReason: SoftSchools.com displays third-party targeted ads including Google DART/DoubleClick cookies to all users including K-12 children, with no COPPA-specific disclosures, no parental consent mechanism, and no explicit protections for users under 13.

The privacy policy contains no COPPA-specific language, no age-screening, no parental consent process, and no data deletion rights for parents — raising significant concerns for school use with students under 13.

complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out via Google Ad Settings and the NAI Opt Out page is mentioned in the policy, but the process is vague, indirect, and not designed for parental use on behalf of children.

r650.riskReason: SOLIDWORKS is a professional CAD/engineering tool designed for adult professionals and enterprises, with no minimum age requirement, no COPPA or FERPA disclosures, no K-12-specific data protections, and broad data sharing with affiliates, business partners, and third-party resellers without granular controls for student data.
r650.parentSummary: SOLIDWORKS (by Dassault Systèmes) collects personal and professional information such as name, email, organization details, usage data, and product activation data, and shares it broadly with affiliates, resellers, and third-party service providers for marketing and business purposes. The platform is designed for professional engineers and enterprises, not K-12 students, and its privacy policy contains no mention of COPPA, FERPA, minimum age requirements, or protections specific to minors or student data. Schools deploying SOLIDWORKS for K-12 students should be aware that there are no documented student data protections, and the terms grant DS SolidWorks broad rights to use user communications for commercial and non-commercial purposes.

r653.riskReason: SpanishChecker.com is actively used in K-12 classrooms, yet it displays targeted advertisements via Ezoic and unnamed partners, collects geolocation and advertising IDs from all visitors including potential minors, has no minimum age requirement, no COPPA or FERPA disclosures, and no Terms of Service document whatsoever.

r655.riskReason: PASCO explicitly claims full COPPA, FERPA, and SOPIPA compliance, does not collect or store student PII in the SPARKvue application, collects no data from users under 18, includes no advertising, and any crash reporting is entirely optional with data restricted to internal technical support.
r655.parentSummary: SPARKvue (by PASCO Scientific) does not collect, store, or transmit any personal information from students — no account is required for students to use the app, and PASCO explicitly states it does not collect information from anyone under 18. The software collects only optional, anonymous usage analytics via Google Analytics (which can be opted out) and voluntary crash reports; no advertising is present and no student data is sold or shared for non-educational purposes. PASCO self-certifies compliance with COPPA, FERPA, and California's SOPIPA, making it one of the more privacy-protective EdTech tools available for K-12 classrooms.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: PASCO reserves the right to modify policies at any time upon posting to its website, but no advance notification process or revision history is explicitly committed to for end users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Software Privacy Policy clearly states the app does not collect, store, or transmit any personal information, and enumerates the two narrow exceptions (optional crash reports and Shared Sessions screen names).
complianceNotes.DCQ2: PASCO specifically describes how each category of data is collected — Google Analytics for usage, optional user-initiated email for crash reports, and PASCO server relay for Shared Sessions screen names.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states student data is never collected or stored by PASCO, effectively meaning no student data ownership is asserted; what little optional data exists is used strictly for internal diagnostics.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Full deletion is allowed upon written request to the PASCO Privacy Officer for any retained data, but no self-service deletion tool is described and the process requires a written request, indicating limited rather than full on-demand deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is not retained (Shared Session data is deleted when sessions end, crash data is used internally), but no specific retention period in days is stated for the minimal optional data that is temporarily held.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: PASCO describes a secure server with limited employee access, a VPN (SSL-encrypted internal network), and HTTPS encryption on the general website as specific security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states the PASCO internal network uses SSL encryption and the website uses HTTPS encryption throughout, confirming encryption in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No student account is required to use SPARKvue, which satisfies this requirement; for educator PASCO Portal accounts, no specific password policy is stated in publicly available documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No MFA or SSO requirement is explicitly documented for educator accounts; students do not require accounts at all, partially satisfying this criterion but leaving educator accounts without confirmed MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: PASCO has a dedicated cookie policy page describing two categories (Essential and Functionality cookies) with the ability to opt out via browser settings, but specific third-party cookie names within Functionality cookies are not individually listed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: BugSplat LLC is named as the third-party crash report processor and Google Analytics is named for usage data, but no comprehensive list of all third-party integrations is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy specifies crash report data goes to BugSplat and usage data to Google Analytics, but the precise data fields shared with each party are not fully enumerated in one place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of Google Analytics data collection within the app, crash reports are entirely voluntary, and no other third-party student data sharing occurs, effectively constituting a full opt-out.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: PASCO explicitly states that PASCO entities and business partners handling data are governed by PASCO's privacy policies and bound by confidentiality agreements.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: PASCO reserves the right to modify privacy statements at any time without a stated advance-notice obligation, meaning third-party changes may not trigger proactive user notification.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Student Privacy Policy and Software Privacy Policy both explicitly state that PASCO software does not include any advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising of any kind is conducted; the policy explicitly states no ads are included in the software.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is present in SPARKvue; the only third-party analytics (Google Analytics) is limited to feature usage and can be opted out.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Usage data collected via Google Analytics is strictly for reporting on feature usage and does not support ad tracking; no web beacons for advertising are mentioned or implied.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There is no advertising ecosystem to opt out of; users can opt out of the only analytics collection (Google Analytics) directly within the application.

dataCollected: Usage/analytics data (clickstream, session duration, page views)
Social media profile data (when interacting with ads on third-party platforms)
dataSharedWith: Analytics vendors (abstracted/non-PII only for Sphero Edu)
Trusted advertising partners (for targeted advertising on main site)
Social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Reddit, Snapchat, Discord, Twitter) for behavioral advertising
Third-party service providers for business operations
r656.riskReason: Sphero Edu has strong child-specific protections including COPPA compliance and no PII sharing with third parties, but the main sphero.com platform uses third-party behavioral advertising trackers and shares data with social media ad networks, which could pose risks if not properly separated from the educational environment.
r656.parentSummary: Sphero collects account information such as name, email, age, and usage data to operate its services; for students under 13 using Sphero Edu, accounts must be set up by a parent or educator, only abstracted (non-personally identifiable) data is shared with analytics vendors, and no PII is shared with third-party vendors. The broader sphero.com site does engage in targeted advertising and shares data with social media ad partners, though Sphero states this is opt-outable and does not apply to child accounts under applicable law. Parents can request data deletion by contacting Sphero's Data Protection Officer at dpo@sphero.com.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states updates may be made over time and users are notified when Sphero 'believes it is necessary,' but no guaranteed advance notice period or formal revision history archive is documented.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates specific categories of personal data collected including identity data, contact data, payment data, usage/analytics data, device data, geolocation, user content, and sensory inputs.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly describes multiple collection methods: data provided directly by users, data from device usage, data from cookies and tracking technologies, and data collected via third-party advertising interactions.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The general privacy policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; the Sphero Edu DPA with school districts clarifies that student data remains the exclusive property of the LEA, but this is not reflected in the main consumer-facing policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their Sphero account at any time per the Terms of Use, and data deletion requests can be submitted via email to dpo@sphero.com or through the CCPA request form.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy references data retention only in general terms tied to service provision and legal obligations; no specific retention periods (e.g., 90 days, 1 year) are explicitly stated for different data categories.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Sphero's security page lists specific measures including data encryption, internal security reviews, third-party penetration testing, security monitoring, and a bug bounty program.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Sphero explicitly states that data is encrypted in transit and at rest where possible, meeting the encryption standard for stored and transmitted data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Sphero Edu supports optional third-party SSO authentication, but the general platform does not document enforcement of strong password requirements; password strength policies are not explicitly described.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Sphero Edu supports third-party authentication integrations (SSO options) but multi-factor authentication is not explicitly offered or required as a standalone feature for standard accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Sphero references a Cookie Policy page and mentions use of session and persistent cookies, web beacons, and advertising cookies, but the cookie policy page content was not fully retrievable; cookies are mentioned generally rather than individually enumerated with purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: For Sphero Edu, abstracted data is shared with analytics vendors but their names are referenced on a support page rather than enumerated directly in the main privacy policy; the main site references social media ad platforms by name (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, etc.).
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared with advertising partners broadly and does not provide a per-third-party breakdown of exactly which data fields are shared with each named partner.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of data sale or sharing (targeted advertising cookies) via a cookie management tool on the website, and Sphero provides a dedicated CCPA opt-out form and CCPA phone number for California residents.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy makes a general statement that trusted partners process data on Sphero's behalf, but specific contractual obligations or Data Processing Agreements binding third parties are not described in the consumer-facing privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy states it may be updated from time to time with notice when Sphero 'believes it is necessary,' which does not guarantee notification specifically when third-party sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The main sphero.com site explicitly states that Sphero and third parties collect user data to deliver 'more relevant advertising on our Site and elsewhere on the internet,' though Sphero Edu as an educational product does not display ads to students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy acknowledges behavioral advertising and profiling across sites and devices through social media ad partners on the main site; Sphero Edu does not target students with ads, but the main platform's advertising practices are not fully excluded for educator accounts.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party behavioral advertising tracking is confirmed on the main sphero.com site via social media platforms, but an opt-out mechanism is available through the cookie management tool and CCPA process.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Sphero confirms use of cookies, web beacons, and similar technologies for both functional and advertising purposes; the distinction between tracking solely for ads versus functional use is not fully transparent in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: A clear opt-out mechanism for data sale or sharing with advertisers is provided via the website's cookie management function, CCPA request form, and a dedicated phone number, meeting the requirement for a clear opt-out process.

dataSharedWith: Third parties in event of merger, acquisition, or bankruptcy
r657.riskReason: SplashLearn has a dedicated Child User Privacy Policy, explicitly prohibits selling student data or targeted advertising based on student data, holds a Common Sense Privacy Verified Seal, and offers Data Privacy Agreements compliant with FERPA, COPPA, and GDPR; however, third-party cookies on the general platform and data transfer provisions in mergers/acquisitions merit continued monitoring.
r657.parentSummary: SplashLearn collects limited data from child users—primarily a first name, gender, username, and activity/progress data—solely for educational purposes, and requires parental or school consent before any child account is created. The platform does not sell student data, does not display third-party ads to children, and does not use child data for behavioral ad targeting. Parents can request access to, correction of, or deletion of their child's data at any time by contacting SplashLearn directly, and the platform has earned a Common Sense Privacy Verified Seal and maintains state-specific Data Privacy Agreements.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use states that continued use after changes constitutes acceptance and that users will no longer be able to use the service if they reject new terms, but does not clearly specify an advance notification period or maintain a publicly accessible revision history/changelog.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and CCPA notice enumerate specific categories of data collected including identifiers, usage data, education records, commercial information, device/location data, and cookies, providing a comprehensive listing.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly describes how data is collected—directly via account creation and forms, automatically through cookies and usage of the service, and through teachers/school administrators who provide student identifiers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: For school-context student records, the Terms of Use explicitly states that educational institutions retain full ownership rights to student data, aligning with FERPA and California AB 1584 requirements.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy provides a 'right to be forgotten' and parents can request full deletion of child data by contacting help@splashlearn.com; however, some data may be retained post-deletion for legal obligations.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained until the account is deleted and only as long as necessary, with child data retained only while the account is active, but no specific numeric retention period (e.g., 90 days) is defined.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references a 'comprehensive Security Program' protecting confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and restricts internal access to authorized personnel under confidentiality obligations, but specific technical security measures (e.g., encryption standards, audits) are not detailed in the public-facing policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Data is described as protected by a password and hosted by third-party providers with 'enhanced security measures,' but explicit mention of end-to-end or at-rest encryption is absent from the public privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy references password protection and advises users to select and protect passwords appropriately, but does not state that strong/complex passwords are technically enforced on the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No explicit mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) is made in the public privacy policy or terms of use; teachers can use QR-code login for students, but MFA for adult accounts is not addressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: SplashLearn has a dedicated Cookie Policy and Preference Center that lists categories of cookies (strictly necessary, analytics/ad-measurement) and their purposes, including a distinction between first-party and third-party cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy categorizes third-party partners as analytics partners and payment processors (Stripe, PayPal, Apple, Google) and references a separate support page listing specific service providers, but inline policy naming of all vendors is incomplete.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: While broad categories of shared data are described per partner type (e.g., payment processors receive billing data, analytics receive usage data), granular data-per-vendor breakdowns are not fully enumerated in the main privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Parents can contact SplashLearn at any time to stop data collection, disclosure, or delete child data entirely, and U.S. state law opt-out rights for data sale/sharing are provided with a 12-month lock-in after opt-out.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The CCPA notice states that when disclosing personal information to third parties for business purposes, SplashLearn enters a contract requiring recipients to keep data confidential and use it only for the specified purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The iKeepSafe profile notes SplashLearn will not make material changes to Terms or Privacy Policy without prior notice, but the main Terms of Use page does not prominently commit to pre-notification of third-party provider changes specifically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states that SplashLearn does not display third-party advertisements on its services, and any advertising is limited to SplashLearn's own platform marketing campaigns.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states it does not engage in targeted advertising based on Student Data or Child User Personal Data, and the Child Privacy Policy confirms no behavioral ad profiling of child users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: While no third-party ad tracking is used for child users, the general privacy policy acknowledges that third-party cookies may collect adult user data for measuring ad campaign effectiveness, with a stated opt-out right but without full opt-out clarity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy acknowledges use of pixel tags, web beacons, clear GIFs, and JavaScript, and analytics cookies may be used for ad-measurement (not personalization); this is disclosed but tracking methods are grouped rather than individually itemized.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users have the right to opt out of data sale or sharing under applicable U.S. State Privacy Laws with instructions provided in the privacy policy, and opt-out requests are honored for a minimum of 12 months before re-authorization is sought.

r658.minAge: 16 (website policy bars users under 16; TOS restricts to 18+)
dataCollected: Student roster data (district, school, teacher, class, grade)
dataSharedWith: Fraud protection and credit risk reduction organizations
r658.riskReason: The privacy policy is a generic website policy not tailored to K-12 student data; it explicitly permits third-party marketing disclosure, uses web beacons and advertising tracking, retains prior-year student data indefinitely, lacks explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance statements, does not name specific third parties, has no stated data retention period, and the website's minimum age (16) is inconsistent with COPPA's 13-year threshold, leaving schools with significant compliance gaps.
r658.parentSummary: SpringMath collects student roster and academic assessment data (names, school identifiers, screening/progress scores) entered by district administrators, as well as website usage data including cookies, web beacons, location data, and device information from educators who log in. The privacy policy permits sharing personal information with third-party marketers unless users opt out and allows data transfer to successor companies in a sale or merger, which raises concerns for a K-12 platform. There is no explicit statement of COPPA or FERPA compliance, no named third-party vendors, and no defined data retention or deletion schedule for student records, leaving important protections unaddressed.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy does not describe an advance notification process or maintain a public revision history; users are not promised notice before material changes take effect.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists broad categories (name, address, email, phone, usage data, location data, device info, student roster/assessment data) but does not comprehensively enumerate all data fields collected within the application platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected directly from users, automatically through navigation, and via third-party interactions, but does not specifically describe how student academic/assessment data is collected or ingested from district rosters.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not assign data ownership to users; it implies company control by stating personal information may be transferred to successors in a merger or sale without user consent.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may request deletion by emailing support, but the policy notes deletion requires deleting the entire account and that cached or archived copies may persist, constituting limited rather than full deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated for any data category; prior-year student data is retained indefinitely and accessible via account login, with no deletion schedule disclosed.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy acknowledges that security measures are in place and employee access is restricted to need-to-know, but does not enumerate specific technical security controls such as firewalls, access controls, or audit logging.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (at rest or in transit) appears in the publicly available privacy policy or terms of use, failing to meet this standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Accounts require a username and password per the terms of use, but no enforcement of password strength requirements or complexity rules is stated in the policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the public-facing policies; MFA availability cannot be confirmed.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and web beacons by name and describes browser opt-out mechanisms, but does not provide a full list of cookies with their individual purposes or a cookie inventory table.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy refers only to broad categories of third parties (subsidiaries, contractors, marketers, successors) without naming any specific vendors, analytics providers, or sub-processors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No disclosure specifies which data elements are shared with each third-party category; the policy groups all disclosures together without per-party data mapping.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An opt-out for third-party marketing disclosures is mentioned via a checkbox on data collection forms, but the process is not clearly described and no opt-out exists for service-provider sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The FAQ states employees and consultants must comply with applicable privacy policy provisions, but no formal contractual requirement or Data Processing Agreement obligation for external third-party vendors is publicly stated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not commit to notifying users when third-party relationships change or new third parties are added; no update notification process for third-party changes is described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states the company may use collected information to display advertisements to advertisers' target audiences, confirming advertising is part of the platform's data use model.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms user data may be used to match advertisers' targeting criteria, constituting targeted advertising use of personal information without explicit restriction for K-12 users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Web beacons and cookies are disclosed as tracking technologies, and interaction with ads may result in advertisers inferring user attributes; no opt-out of this third-party tracking is offered beyond browser-level cookie refusal.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Web beacons (clear gifs, pixel tags) are explicitly mentioned as being used for user tracking and ad-related statistics, indicating tracking beyond purely functional purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out of third-party marketing data sharing is referenced via a checkbox on data collection forms, but the mechanism is unclear and not described as a persistent, accessible opt-out for all users.

r659.riskReason: The Stanford History Education Group platform (stanfordhistoryeducationgroup.com) has no dedicated Terms of Service or Privacy Policy, and Common Sense Education explicitly flags the absence of a privacy policy as a critical concern for K-12 use.
r659.parentSummary: The Stanford History Education Group website (stanfordhistoryeducationgroup.com) does not publish a dedicated Privacy Policy or Terms of Service specific to this platform, making it impossible to determine what data is collected from K-12 students, how it is used, or what protections are in place. Common Sense Education has flagged the lack of a privacy policy as a notable concern. Note: SHEG has since transitioned to the Digital Inquiry Group (DIG), an independent nonprofit as of January 2024, and parents and educators should check inquirygroup.org for any updated policies.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Privacy Policy or Terms of Service were found on the platform, so no policy change notification process can be evaluated.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: No privacy policy exists on the platform; there is no disclosure of what data is collected from users.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: No policy document describes how data is collected from users of this platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: No policy exists to clarify data ownership; it is entirely silent on this issue.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No policy or mechanism for users to request deletion of their data has been identified.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or statement of any kind is provided, as no privacy policy exists.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No security measures are described anywhere in platform-specific documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No statement about encryption in transit or at rest is available for this platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform appears to require no account for most content access, but no password or SSO policy is documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required for basic resource access, but no MFA or SSO documentation exists for any optional account features.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy specific to this platform is published; cookie usage and purposes are entirely undisclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No privacy policy means there is no disclosure of which third parties, if any, receive user data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No information about what data, if any, is shared with third parties has been disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is documented or available.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor agreements or third-party data handling requirements are mentioned anywhere.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No process for notifying users of changes to third-party sharing arrangements exists.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No policy discloses whether advertisements are displayed on the platform or in what form.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Targeted advertising practices are not disclosed; it cannot be confirmed or denied.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure exists regarding third-party tracking technologies used for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No information is provided about the use of web beacons, pixels, or other tracking methods.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out mechanism for data sharing with advertisers is described or available.

r660.riskReason: Stash (stash.com) is an adult financial investment platform with a minimum age of 18 that collects highly sensitive financial and personal data including Social Security numbers, shares data with marketing and advertising partners for cross-site ad targeting, and has no COPPA, FERPA, or K-12 student privacy provisions whatsoever, making it entirely unsuitable for use in K-12 educational settings.
r660.parentSummary: Stash (stash.com) is an adult-only financial investing and banking app designed for users 18 and older, requiring sensitive personal and financial data such as Social Security numbers, bank account details, and billing information. The platform shares user data with advertising and analytics third parties for targeted marketing across the web, and there are no protections or provisions for children or students. This platform is not an EdTech tool and should not be used in K-12 schools under any circumstances.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use instructs users to check the platform regularly for amendments to account contracts, but there is no clear advance notification process or publicly accessible revision history provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and security page enumerate data types collected including name, address, phone, email, SSN, financial information, device/technical data, and communication records.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states data is collected directly from users during sign-up, automatically through platform use, and from third-party sources including social networks and public data.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Use and Privacy Policy do not clearly state that users own their data; Stash claims broad rights to use and share data, and data ownership is not explicitly granted to users.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may request account cancellation within 3 business days per the Terms of Use, but no self-service data deletion portal is described and charges prior to cancellation are non-reversible.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy states data is retained 'as long as reasonably necessary' for legal, regulatory, and business purposes without specifying a concrete retention period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Stash explicitly lists security measures including 256-bit encryption, SSL/TLS, session end-timers, login thresholds, biometric options, and PCI DSS compliance audits.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The platform uses 256-bit encryption for personal data and fund purchase history, and TLS for data in transit between the app and servers.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No explicit mention of strong password enforcement policies is found in the publicly available Terms of Use or Privacy Policy pages reviewed.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Two-factor authentication is available but described as optional and limited to active debit account customers, rather than being universally enforced.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy acknowledges use of cookies, pixel tags, web beacons, and session logs, but references a separate 'Stash Cookie Statement' without fully listing all cookies and their purposes inline.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy broadly references categories of third parties (marketing providers, analytics providers, payment processors) but does not name all specific third-party companies used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with third parties is described by category of vendor function rather than specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No clear opt-out mechanism from third-party data sharing is provided to users; the policy indicates cross-site advertising data sharing occurs without offering an easy opt-out process.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states vendors process personal data 'on behalf of Stash' under agreement to deliver their services, but does not detail contractual data protection obligations imposed on third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not state that users will be notified of changes to specific third-party vendor relationships; only general policy amendments are referenced.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Marketing and advertising providers are explicitly used to market Stash's products to users across third-party websites, confirming ad display beyond the platform itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy confirms use of marketing and advertising providers to target users 'even across third-party websites,' constituting confirmed cross-site targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party analytics and advertising providers deploy cookies and pixels to track users and measure ad performance with no explicit opt-out mechanism described in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms use of pixel tags, web beacons, and similar technologies by third-party advertising and analytics vendors to track user behavior and ad performance.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process from data sharing with advertisers is described; users are not given a mechanism to prevent their data from being used for cross-site advertising purposes.

dataSharedWith: Content providers and vendors (for AP Statistics Review Course and subscription services)
Subsequent owners or operators in the event of a merger or sale

r661.riskReason: Stats Medic (operated by Math Medic, LLC) lacks a dedicated privacy policy on statsmedic.com itself, relies on an outdated 2021 policy at mathmedic.com that makes no explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance claims, permits data sharing with third-party content providers and successor entities, uses cookies for marketing purposes, and does not address data deletion, data retention periods, minimum age requirements, or student-specific protections.
r661.parentSummary: Stats Medic is operated by Math Medic, LLC, and its privacy practices are governed by a policy last updated in February 2021 at mathmedic.com — no dedicated policy page exists on statsmedic.com itself. The platform collects names, email addresses, passwords, and school information from registered users, and may share data with content providers, company affiliates, and successor entities in business transactions. There are no explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance statements, no minimum age requirement disclosed, no data deletion or retention policy, and cookies are used for marketing purposes, raising significant concerns for schools deploying this tool with K-12 students.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states it 'may change from time to time' and directs users to check it often, but does not commit to advance notification or maintain a formal revision history beyond a single 'last updated' date (February 24, 2021).
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some categories of data collected (name, email, password, school name, page visit data) but the list is incomplete and does not account for all data types likely collected by the platform (e.g., student submission data, assessment responses).
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that data is collected when users become members, communicate via email, or visit pages, but does not specifically detail how each data type is collected (e.g., forms, automated tracking, LMS integration).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not address user data ownership; it reserves broad rights to disclose and transfer all collected information to parent companies, subsidiaries, and successors, implying company control over user data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy contains no process or mechanism for users to request deletion of their personal data; no deletion rights are described anywhere in the policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not state any data retention period or general retention framework; there is no mention of how long user data is kept or when it is deleted.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy does not describe any specific security measures, encryption standards, access controls, or technical safeguards used to protect user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (in transit or at rest) is made anywhere in the policy or on the platform's public-facing pages.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy makes no mention of password strength requirements, enforcement policies, or SSO options; account creation is required for student digital access.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: There is no mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration in the privacy policy or terms of use; no MFA options are documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges cookie use and notes cookies are used 'to market to certain individuals,' but does not provide a full list of cookies, their purposes, or distinguish between functional and tracking cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy broadly references content providers, vendors, parent/subsidiary companies, and law enforcement but does not name specific third-party companies or services receiving user data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with each third-party category is provided; the policy only states data 'may be shared' with broadly described groups.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described anywhere in the policy; users have no documented recourse to limit sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not state that third parties are contractually bound to data protection standards or that Math Medic assumes vendor accountability for third-party data handling.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes will be posted to the website, which could cover third-party changes, but does not specifically commit to notifying users when new third parties are added or when sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states cookies are used 'to market to certain individuals the products our website sells,' indicating marketing/advertising use that goes beyond functional cookies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The use of cookies for marketing to site visitors implies behavioral or interest-based targeting, and the policy does not clarify whether this targeting extends to students or minors.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy does not address third-party ad tracking technologies, pixels, or beacons, and provides no opt-out for tracking used in connection with marketing cookies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy acknowledges marketing cookies are set but provides no detail on whether web beacons, pixels, or other tracking methods are used alongside cookies for advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers or marketers is described; the policy does not mention any mechanism to decline marketing-related data use or cookie-based profiling.

r664.riskReason: StoryJumper explicitly prohibits ads, does not sell student data, expressly claims COPPA/FERPA/PPRA compliance, requires parental or educator consent for children under 13, uses SSL encryption, and provides a comprehensive Data Processing Addendum and breach notification protocol for Educational Accounts.
r664.parentSummary: StoryJumper collects basic account information such as name, email, username, and date of birth, along with usage data like IP address and device type, primarily to operate its story-creation service; for children under 13, parental or educator consent is required before any data is used. There are no third-party ads on the platform, student data is not sold or used for commercial profiling, and data is kept only as long as the account is active with full deletion available upon request. For school accounts, the school is considered the data controller, parents can request access or deletion through the school administrator, and StoryJumper explicitly commits to FERPA, COPPA, and PPRA compliance with a formal breach notification process.

complianceNotes.DCQ3: For Educational Accounts, the policy explicitly states the school (EAA) owns student data; for Independent Accounts, users own their content, and StoryJumper acts only as a processor.

complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is kept only while the account is active and deleted upon request, but does not specify a precise numeric retention period (e.g., 90 days) for any post-account data, making this only partially defined.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Data Processing Addendum and Data Security & Breach Statement describe specific security measures including SSL encryption, performance monitoring, cloud-based redundancy, DDOS protection, and role-based access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: StoryJumper explicitly states it uses SSL encrypted connections and industry-standard encryption mechanisms for data in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Educational Account Agreement makes the school administrator responsible for securing usernames and passwords but does not specify enforcement of password complexity or strength requirements.

complianceNotes.SECQ5: A Cookie Policy page exists and distinguishes between first-party and third-party cookies and their purposes, but third-party cookies are not individually named and users are told to contact third parties directly for details, making disclosure only partial.

complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Educational Account Privacy Statement explicitly requires that vendors receiving student personal information are contractually obligated to implement the same privacy and security commitments.

complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration options is made anywhere in the available policy documents.

r668.riskReason: StudyFetch's standard (non-enterprise) consumer privacy policy permits uploaded user content — including student-generated materials — to be used for AI training, SEO, and derivative works, and does not explicitly prohibit sale of student data, contain verifiable age-gating for users under 13, or name all specific third-party recipients of data, creating significant COPPA, FERPA, and SOPIPA compliance gaps for K-12 use outside of an enterprise agreement.
r668.parentSummary: StudyFetch collects personal information including name, email, profile picture, and all content students upload (documents, videos, audio, images) and may use that content to train its AI models and improve its platform unless an enterprise contract is in place. The platform claims COPPA and FERPA compliance specifically for institutional/enterprise clients, but the standard consumer-facing privacy policy does not include explicit COPPA parental consent mechanisms, a minimum age gate, or a prohibition on selling student data. Parents should be aware that uploaded educational materials may be processed by third-party AI providers such as Anthropic, and that YouTube features may expose students to YouTube advertisements over which StudyFetch states it has no control.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy is dated August 9, 2024, and references updates, but there is no explicit statement about advance notification to users before changes take effect or a maintained revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, uploaded content, social media profile data, cookies, YouTube API data), but does not provide an exhaustive enumerated list of every data type in a single consolidated section.
