complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references third-party service providers and social media login platforms (Google, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, LinkedIn) but does not name specific analytics or advertising vendors used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what particular data is shared with each third-party category; sharing disclosures are grouped and vague without per-vendor breakdowns.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described; users are told they can disable cookies in the browser but there is no comprehensive opt-out of advertising data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states the company is 'not responsible' for third-party sites and places no stated contractual limits on how third parties may use shared data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may update periodically but does not commit to notifying users specifically when third-party sharing relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The EULA and associated policies explicitly describe serving video, textlink, interstitial, and pop-up advertisements to users based on browsing behavior, confirming targeted ads are displayed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy and EULA confirm that advertisements are targeted based on web content the user views and browsing history, constituting confirmed user-level behavioral targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertisers receive cookie and behavioral data for targeting purposes, and no meaningful opt-out from third-party ad tracking is described for general users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The platform explicitly uses cookies, web beacons, and other tracking technologies for advertising purposes, confirming tracking for ads is active.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear or accessible opt-out process from advertiser data sharing is described; browser cookie disabling is the only mentioned mechanism, which is insufficient for full ad tracking opt-out.

dataCollected: User-generated content (if submitted via support or social)
dataSharedWith: Advertising networks (Meta/Facebook, Index Exchange, PubMatic, Magnite/Rubicon, Yieldmo, Amazon, TripleLift, Smaato, LoopMe, Xandr, Vidazoo, InMobi, Primis, Open Web Technologies, Rise Engage, Freestar)
Cloud/backup providers (Google Play Games, Apple Game Center)
r670.riskReason: Sudoku.com (operated by Easybrain) explicitly targets users 16+ and serves targeted advertising via a large network of third-party ad partners, making it entirely unsuitable for K-12 deployment where students may be under 13 or 16.
r670.parentSummary: Sudoku.com is operated by Easybrain Limited and collects device identifiers, IP addresses, usage data, and cookie/pixel-tag data from visitors, including through a large network of third-party advertising partners such as Meta, Amazon, Google, and many others. The platform states it is intended only for users over age 16 and does not have COPPA protections for children under 13. Targeted advertising is actively served to users, data is shared broadly with ad networks, and there are no school or student-specific data protections, making this platform inappropriate for K-12 educational use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Easybrain privacy policy states it may be updated and users are advised to check periodically, but there is no advance notification mechanism or revision history provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists broad categories of data collected (device identifiers, usage data, IP address, in-app purchase data) but does not provide a fully exhaustive itemized list of every data type collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy provides a general description of how data is collected (automatically, directly from the user, from third-party platforms) but lacks specifics on each collection method for each data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly state that users own their data; data is processed under 'legitimate interests' of Easybrain, implying company control without explicit user ownership acknowledgment.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request data deletion via in-app Privacy Rights settings or by emailing privacy@easybrain.com, but the process requires routing through in-app support and is not a direct self-service deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not state a specific data retention period for website users; it only vaguely states data is held as needed for business purposes without defined timeframes.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy references data protection and fraud prevention but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or audit practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The website uses HTTPS (standard TLS encryption in transit), but the privacy policy does not explicitly describe encryption practices for data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account is required to use Sudoku.com, so strong password enforcement is not applicable and this criterion is effectively met by the no-account design.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required to use Sudoku.com, so MFA is not applicable and this criterion is met by the no-account design.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Sudoku.com has a dedicated Cookie Policy page (sudoku.com/page/cookies-eu/) that lists cookie categories (strictly necessary, analytics, advertising) and names specific third-party cookie providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Cookie Policy and privacy policy name specific third-party advertising and analytics partners including Meta, Index Exchange, PubMatic, Magnite, Yieldmo, Amazon, TripleLift, Smaato, LoopMe, Xandr, Vidazoo, InMobi, Primis, and others.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Third parties are listed by name with links to their policies, but the specific data elements shared with each individual partner are not itemized; sharing is described in aggregate terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: A 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' opt-out link is referenced in the cookie consent tool, and opt-out of targeted ads is available via device settings, but the process is not straightforward for all users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy makes a general statement that data is shared with trusted partners but does not explicitly state that all third-party advertising vendors are bound by data processing agreements or supplier contracts.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not commit to notifying users when the list of third-party advertising partners changes; the cookie policy lists current partners but may be updated without user notice.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Sudoku.com displays targeted advertising to all users via a large network of ad partners including pixel tags and interest-based ad networks, which is confirmed throughout the cookie and privacy policies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states that advertising networks use device identifiers, cookies, and tracking technologies to deliver personalized ads based on user interests and activities.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising tracking (including via Meta Pixel, device advertising IDs, and multiple ad networks) is active with no simple opt-out; the available opt-out requires navigating device OS settings.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy explicitly confirms use of Pixel Tags and similar tracking technologies for ad delivery and performance measurement by third parties.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: A 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' preference option is mentioned in the cookie consent manager, and device-level opt-out instructions are provided, but the process is unclear and fragmented across multiple systems.

dataCollected: App usage/activity data (screens viewed, actions taken)
Parent email address (optional, for newsletter only)
Support contact information (if user contacts support)
dataSharedWith: Third-party newsletter service providers (parent email only)
r671.riskReason: The app collects minimal data (only anonymous usage analytics and optional parent email for newsletter), contains no ads, requires no account, and the developer explicitly states COPPA compliance and does not sell or share child data with third parties for commercial purposes.
r671.parentSummary: Superhero Comic Book Maker by Duck Duck Moose (a Khan Academy subsidiary) collects only anonymous, non-personal usage data (e.g., screens viewed) to improve the app, and optionally a parent's email address solely for a newsletter. The app is free, contains no third-party advertising, requires no account creation, and the developer states compliance with COPPA. No personal information is collected from children, and the privacy policy is hosted on duckduckmoose.com rather than the listed platform URL, as the platform URL does not appear to host its own standalone privacy or ToS pages.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states changes will be notified by email if they affect email address use, but there is no mention of a revision history or advance notice for all other types of policy changes.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy explicitly lists the limited data collected: anonymous app usage data (screens, actions, duration) and optional parent email addresses for the newsletter — a clear and complete disclosure.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states data is collected through use of the mobile applications and optionally through a parent-facing newsletter signup form, clearly explaining the collection mechanism.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states that non-personal usage data is used solely to improve applications and email addresses are used solely for newsletters, implying user ownership and no commercial data exploitation; no claim of data ownership by the company.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy does not provide a mechanism for users or parents to request deletion of usage data; it only notes that child personal data provided via support will be deleted, and newsletter email can be unsubscribed from but no broader deletion right is stated.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not specify any data retention period for usage analytics data or newsletter email addresses, leaving retention duration completely unaddressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy makes no mention of specific security measures, encryption standards, or security protocols used to protect the data that is collected.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit encryption statement is found in the Duck Duck Moose privacy policy, though Google Play store listings for other DDM apps indicate data is encrypted in transit; this is not confirmed in the formal privacy policy text.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account creation is required to use the app, effectively removing password risks entirely and meeting the spirit of this requirement through a no-account model.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The app requires no account and therefore no login credentials, making MFA moot and satisfying this requirement through a no-account architecture.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies are used on the website to improve service quality, but does not enumerate cookie types, purposes, or provide a dedicated cookie policy; only a general statement is made.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy states that newsletter emails are shared with 'third party service providers' for newsletter fulfillment but does not name those providers specifically.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy indicates parent email is shared with newsletter service providers but does not specify what data is shared with other potential third parties such as law enforcement, and grouping is used rather than per-party disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of the newsletter at any time by unsubscribing, and since no other data sharing occurs for commercial purposes, there is effectively a clear opt-out mechanism available.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy implies newsletter service providers operate under its instructions but does not explicitly state that third parties are contractually bound by a data protection agreement or vendor contract.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention notifying users if third-party service providers change or if new third parties are added to the data sharing arrangement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The developer and Apple App Store listings explicitly state the app contains no ads or third-party advertising, fully satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: With no advertising of any kind present in the app, there is no targeted advertising and this requirement is fully met.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is used in the app; the developer explicitly states no third-party advertising is included.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy only references cookies on the website for service improvement, not for advertising or ad-related tracking within the app itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no data is shared with advertisers and the app contains no ads, there is nothing to opt out of, effectively meeting this requirement by design.

dataCollected: Third-party integration profile data (e.g., Facebook, LinkedIn, Google, Microsoft)
r672.riskReason: SurveyMonkey is a general-purpose business platform not designed for K-12 use; it explicitly prohibits minors under 16 from holding accounts, collects broad personal data, uses third-party advertising cookies and web beacons for retargeting, and lacks a dedicated COPPA compliance program for student respondents despite a recently launched enterprise-only FERPA feature.
r672.parentSummary: SurveyMonkey collects account holder information (name, email, usage, device data) and may use advertising cookies and third-party ad networks to track and retarget users across the web, including through web beacons. Student survey responses are controlled by the teacher/school (the 'Creator'), not SurveyMonkey directly, but the platform does not offer COPPA compliance for respondents under 13 and only recently introduced a limited FERPA-compliant option for enterprise school customers. Parents should be aware that SurveyMonkey is primarily a business tool, and its advertising and data-sharing practices make it a high-risk platform for routine K-12 student data collection.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Privacy policy posts an effective date and states changes will be posted on the website with possible email notification, but it is unclear whether advance notice is given before changes take effect or whether a full revision history is maintained.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy clearly lists data categories collected from Creators, Respondents, and Visitors, including account data, usage data, device data, survey responses, and third-party integration data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically describes how data is collected — directly from users, automatically via cookies/device data, and from third-party integrations such as Facebook, LinkedIn, Google, and Microsoft.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Survey response data is owned and managed by the Creator (school/teacher), not SurveyMonkey, but ownership of platform-level data (account, usage) is not explicitly assigned to the user, creating ambiguity.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Account holders can request deletion of their own account and data, but respondent data deletion must go through the Creator, not SurveyMonkey directly, limiting deletion rights for students taking surveys.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The DPA references data destruction within 3 months of termination, but the general privacy policy does not state a specific retention period for active accounts or respondent data, making this vague for typical K-12 use.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: SurveyMonkey maintains SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS 3.2 certifications, conducts annual third-party penetration tests, runs a 24/7 incident response team, and trains developers in secure application practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The terms state encryption is used for data in transit and at rest, and survey URLs use SSL (HTTPS), meeting the encryption standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy references password-based authentication and security policies, but does not explicitly state that strong/complex passwords are enforced by the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: SurveyMonkey supports SSO and multi-factor authentication (MFA) as security features on its platform, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: SurveyMonkey provides a detailed Cookie Notice listing required, functional, and advertising cookies with their purposes, as well as a separate page for cookies used on survey pages, including opt-out mechanisms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references categories of third parties (advertising networks, analytics, integration partners, affiliates, subprocessors) but does not name every individual third-party company in the main privacy notice; a separate subprocessor list exists.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared by third-party category rather than specifying exactly which data fields go to which individual partner, making it only partially transparent.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users in some locations can manage cookie/advertising preferences via a Cookie Preferences link, but opt-out is location-dependent and not universally available, providing limited control.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: SurveyMonkey enters into confidentiality and data processing terms with all subprocessors and partners, requiring them to maintain high standards of privacy and security.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The DPA allows customers to subscribe to subprocessor change notifications and object within 30 days, but the general privacy policy does not clearly commit to notifying all users before third-party changes take effect.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: SurveyMonkey uses advertising cookies on its main website and end pages to market services and retarget users on third-party websites; while advertising cookies are not used on survey-taking pages, ads are still present in the broader platform experience.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy and cookie notice confirm that third-party advertising networks and Google Analytics are used for targeted/retargeted advertising based on user behavior and browsing history.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: SurveyMonkey contracts with third-party advertising networks that collect IP addresses and use web beacons and cookies to track users across websites for ad targeting, with no robust opt-out for all users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie notice confirms use of web beacons and third-party ad network cookies for tracking user activity across websites to serve targeted ads, which is a concern for K-12 environments.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: A Cookie Preferences tool is available to users in some locations, but the opt-out is not universally available and the process for fully opting out of all advertiser data sharing is unclear and inconsistent across regions.

r673.riskReason: Sutori explicitly claims COPPA, FERPA, SOPIPA, and GDPR compliance, states it does not sell data, displays no advertising, restricts under-13 user actions, and confirms no data is shared with third parties.
r673.parentSummary: Sutori collects basic account information such as name and email to provide its educational timeline tool; for students under 13, full names are never displayed publicly and certain actions like making work public are restricted. Sutori states it does not share student data with any third parties, does not display advertising, and does not sell user data, with its business model based solely on paid subscriptions. The platform claims compliance with COPPA, FERPA, SOPIPA, CCPA, and GDPR, and uses encryption for all data in transit hosted on Heroku (AWS infrastructure).

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Sutori's privacy policy and terms pages do not render full readable text in search results, and no explicit advance notification process or revision history is publicly documented in help materials.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Help documentation references collection of name, email, usage/activity data, and content created, but the actual privacy policy page does not render its full data inventory list in available sources.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Sutori indicates data is collected via sign-up forms and through use of the platform (Google/Clever/Microsoft SSO options noted), but a comprehensive statement of all collection mechanisms is not fully detailed in accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Sutori states its business model is subscription-based, not data-based, refuses to sell data, and user content ownership is implied to remain with the user, aligning with user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Sutori's help documentation explicitly states users can delete their account at any time from their profile page, and all associated stories and data are also deleted.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period (in days, months, or years) is stated in any publicly accessible Sutori documentation or help articles.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Sutori references security best practices at every level and automated vulnerability scanning before deployments, but does not enumerate specific security controls (e.g., SOC 2, penetration testing) in a detailed security policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Sutori explicitly states all communication between servers and users is encrypted using modern standards, covering written content and all media uploads and downloads.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Sutori supports SSO via Google, Microsoft Office 365, Clever, and Facebook, which can enforce strong passwords, but no explicit password strength enforcement policy for native Sutori accounts is documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Sutori supports SSO login via Google, Clever, and Microsoft (which can enforce MFA at the identity provider level), but no native MFA option for Sutori-specific email/password accounts is documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Sutori's help documentation references functional cookies and third-party service domains to whitelist (including Crisp.chat for support chat), but a comprehensive cookie policy listing all cookies and their purposes is not clearly published.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Sutori states no data is shared with third parties for student data, but its platform integrates with Google Classroom, Clever, and uses Heroku/AWS for hosting — these infrastructure providers are not named as data recipients in a formal third-party list.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No specific breakdown of what data (if any) is shared with infrastructure or integration partners (e.g., Heroku/AWS, Google Classroom, Clever) on a per-party basis is documented.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Sutori explicitly states student data is not shared with any third parties, making third-party data sharing opt-out effectively moot and fully protective.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Sutori's general compliance claims and subscription-based model imply vendor accountability, but no formal data processing agreement (DPA) or supplier responsibility clause is publicly referenced.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No formal process for notifying users of changes to third-party relationships is documented in Sutori's publicly available policies or help articles.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Sutori explicitly states there is no advertising on the platform, making it fully protective against ad-based data concerns.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Sutori confirms no advertising exists on the platform, which means no targeted advertising is conducted using student or teacher data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The absence of advertising on Sutori means no third-party ad tracking is employed; the platform's stated no-ads policy covers this requirement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While Sutori denies advertising, its help documentation references third-party service domains including Crisp.chat (support chat), which may use functional tracking — a comprehensive web beacon or pixel disclosure is not provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because Sutori states it has no advertising and does not share data with advertisers, there is no advertiser data sharing to opt out of, which fully satisfies this requirement.

dataCollected: Diagnostics and usage data (opt-in, not linked to identity)
Crash data (opt-in, not linked to identity)
Performance data (opt-in, not linked to identity)
Device identifiers (when signed into Apple Account)
iCloud sync data (if iCloud is enabled)
dataSharedWith: Apple service providers (under data processor agreements)
r674.riskReason: Swift Playgrounds is an Apple-developed app with minimal data collection (only opt-in, non-identity-linked diagnostics), no advertising, no third-party tracking, explicit COPPA compliance mechanisms for child accounts, and strong Apple platform security protections.
r674.parentSummary: Swift Playgrounds, developed by Apple, collects minimal data — primarily optional, anonymized diagnostics and usage information that is not linked to your child's identity. Apple explicitly states it does not sell personal data and does not share student data with third parties for marketing or advertising purposes. The app can be used without an Apple Account; if a child Apple Account is used, Apple requires verifiable parental consent in compliance with COPPA, and parents can manage data through Apple's Family Sharing controls.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Apple posts advance notice of material privacy policy changes on its website at least one week prior, but a revision history log is not publicly maintained in a readily accessible format.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Apple's App Store privacy nutrition label and privacy policy identify the data types collected by Swift Playgrounds (diagnostics, usage data, crash data — all non-identity-linked), and Apple explicitly states what is and is not collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Apple's privacy policy and App Store privacy label specifically describe how data is collected (opt-in device analytics, iCloud sync if enabled, Apple Account data if signed in), satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Apple's privacy policy affirms user data rights and Apple explicitly states it does not claim ownership over user content; users retain ownership of their data and code created in the app.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Apple provides a Data and Privacy portal (privacy.apple.com) where users can request full deletion of their Apple Account and associated data, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Apple's privacy policy states data is retained 'only for so long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected,' but does not specify exact retention durations for Swift Playgrounds diagnostic data, making this only a general retention statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Apple's privacy policy references administrative, technical, and physical safeguards, and the Apple Platform Security guide details encryption, secure enclave, and other specific security measures used across Apple services.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Apple's platform uses end-to-end encryption and encryption at rest for iCloud data; all App Store and network communications use TLS, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Apple Account requires strong passwords by default (minimum length, complexity requirements enforced at account creation), and the app supports Face ID/Touch ID (SSO-equivalent biometric authentication).
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Apple Account supports and encourages two-factor authentication (2FA), which is required for many Apple services; child accounts are managed under parent Family Sharing which also supports 2FA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Apple's privacy policy mentions cookies and similar technologies and their purposes in general terms, but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of all cookies used by Swift Playgrounds specifically, though the app itself does not use web-based cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Apple's privacy policy identifies categories of entities data may be shared with (Apple-affiliated companies, service providers, law enforcement) but does not name specific third-party vendor companies used in connection with Swift Playgrounds.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Apple groups data sharing by purpose category rather than specifying exactly which data types are shared with each individual third-party service provider, providing a partial but not fully granular disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Apple does not share student data with third parties for advertising or marketing; for the limited service-provider sharing that occurs, users can opt out of analytics sharing entirely via iOS Settings, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Apple's privacy policy states that service providers must adhere to Apple's privacy standards and are contractually obligated to protect user data at the same level as Apple's own policies require.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Apple's privacy governance page states it posts advance notice of material policy changes but does not specifically commit to notifying users of changes to individual third-party service provider relationships.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Swift Playgrounds displays no third-party advertisements; Apple's education guidelines explicitly prohibit behavioral advertising in apps using the ClassKit educational framework.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Apple explicitly prohibits behavioral or targeted advertising in Swift Playgrounds and education apps; no user targeting occurs based on in-app behavior.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking SDKs are present in Swift Playgrounds; Apple's AppTrackingTransparency framework would require explicit user consent for any tracking, which is not applicable here.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No advertising-related web beacons or tracking pixels are used in Swift Playgrounds; only functional on-device processing and optional anonymized diagnostics occur.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There are no advertisers to opt out of sharing data with, as Swift Playgrounds does not engage in advertising data sharing; Apple's broader opt-out controls are available through iOS privacy settings.

dataCollected: Student demographic data (ethnicity, gender, IEP status, English Learner status)
dataSharedWith: University of Oregon research database (de-identified, opt-in by school)
University of Oregon Internal Review Board (IRB)
r675.riskReason: SWIS Suite is a school-operated, staff-only K-12 behavior data platform with no advertising, no third-party commercial data sharing, strong encryption, FERPA compliance, MFA support, and school/licensee data ownership; the primary residual risk is limited public transparency on cookie policy, data retention timelines, and the fact that detailed privacy terms are embedded in a non-public license agreement rather than a publicly accessible privacy policy.
r675.parentSummary: SWIS Suite (by PBISApps at the University of Oregon) collects student behavior and discipline referral data entered by school staff — including student names, demographics, IEP status, and incident details — for the purpose of school-wide decision making under a PBIS framework. Data is owned exclusively by the school (the licensee), is not sold or used for advertising, and research use requires a separate opt-in agreement with all personally identifying information removed. Parents and guardians may review or request corrections to their child's data by contacting their school directly.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy and security statement on pbisapps.org does not explicitly describe an advance-notification process or revision history for policy changes; terms are primarily embedded in a downloadable license agreement rather than a versioned public policy page.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The public privacy page broadly references that the SWIS Suite license agreement details what personal information is collected, but does not enumerate all data types directly on the public-facing policy page; specific data types (behavior, demographics, IEP status) are partially disclosed across product pages.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The platform describes that data is entered by school staff and imported from Student Information Systems, but the public policy does not comprehensively detail every collection method (e.g., automatic SIS import, mobile app logging) in a single policy document.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy statement explicitly states that all information, data, and content transmitted by the Licensee remains the sole property of the Licensee, with the school retaining exclusive control over student and staff data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents and guardians may review and request changes to student data by communicating with their school, providing a correction pathway, but there is no stated direct user-initiated deletion mechanism or process timeline documented publicly.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The public privacy and security statement does not specify data retention periods or a general retention schedule; no retention timeline is stated on any publicly accessible policy page.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The platform states it maintains a comprehensive security program designed to protect the security, privacy, confidentiality, and integrity of student personal information, and the product page advertises end-to-end encryption with servers behind a secure firewall.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The SWIS product page explicitly states data is protected with end-to-end encryption on servers housed behind a secure firewall, meeting the encryption standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform is a licensed school-staff-only system requiring institutional account setup managed by a certified SWIS facilitator, which functions as enforced access control; no public documentation of specific password complexity rules was found, but the institutional account model and MFA availability satisfy this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: PBISApps explicitly supports and allows districts to require multi-factor authentication for all users of PBISApps applications, with MFA available as a configurable security upgrade for school accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy or list of cookies with purposes is provided on the public-facing privacy and security page; cookie usage practices for the web application are not disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy statement identifies the University of Oregon research database and IRB as recipients of de-identified data under opt-in agreements, but does not name any additional third-party service providers or technology vendors used to operate the platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy notes that only de-identified, aggregated data goes to the research database, but specific data elements shared with any technology infrastructure vendors or subprocessors are not enumerated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Research database data sharing is explicitly opt-in at the school level via a separate signed data sharing agreement, meaning no data is shared without affirmative school consent, which effectively provides a full opt-out.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy statement affirms FERPA compliance for research database activities and notes IRB oversight, and the license agreement structure places contractual responsibility on PBISApps; the platform explicitly claims responsibility for maintaining a comprehensive security program.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The public policy does not describe any process for notifying licensees of changes to third-party relationships or subprocessors; no mention of third-party change notification is found in available public documentation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No advertising of any kind is displayed within the SWIS Suite platform; it is a licensed institutional tool with no ad-based revenue model.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no targeted advertising, behavioral profiling for commercial purposes, or use of student data for advertising; the platform explicitly states data is not shared for cross-context behavioral advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is present or disclosed; student data is not used for or shared with advertising networks.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No advertising tracking methods are described or known to be used; however, the absence of a public cookie policy means tracking methods for functional or analytics purposes on the web application cannot be fully verified.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising or advertiser data sharing occurs, there is nothing for users to opt out of; this criterion is effectively met by the platform's no-advertising model.

dataCollected: Usage data (pages visited, access times, access duration)
Email open and click tracking data
r676.riskReason: Switch Classroom explicitly states data is never sold or used for advertising and uses SSL encryption, but third parties are not specifically named, no MFA is described, no explicit FERPA or SOPIPA compliance is stated, and the age-13 restriction lacks a formal verifiable parental consent mechanism.
r676.parentSummary: Switch Classroom (by Switch Energy Alliance, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit) collects teacher account information such as name, email, and usage/log data to operate its free energy education platform; it explicitly states collected data is never sold or used for advertising purposes. Students no longer log in directly — teachers download materials and deploy them via their own LMS (e.g., Google Classroom, Canvas), which significantly reduces direct student data exposure. However, specific third-party vendors are not named in the policy, no explicit FERPA or COPPA Safe Harbor certification is claimed, and the policy relies on a general statement that data is shared with hosting and service providers under contractual protection.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states SEA will notify users of significant changes via email and/or a prominent site notice, but no revision history or versioning system is mentioned.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data types (email, usage data, cookies, log data, pixel tags) but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of all personally identifiable information collected at registration.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes data collection at account registration and through site interaction, but lacks specific detail on each collection mechanism (e.g., forms, analytics tools, SDKs).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly assert user ownership of data; it states SEA collects and uses data to operate services but does not explicitly disclaim ownership or affirm user data rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their account and all associated data either through account settings self-service or by contacting classroom.support@switchon.org, satisfying full deletion capability.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as necessary to provide services and comply with legal obligations, but no specific retention period (e.g., number of days or years) is stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states SEA uses 'technical safeguards' to protect personal information but does not enumerate specific measures such as access controls, auditing, or encryption at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states that all site information including sensitive information is encrypted using SSL (Secure Socket Layer) technology.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy places account confidentiality responsibility on the user but does not describe any password strength requirements or enforcement mechanisms by the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI integration is made anywhere in the policy or terms of use.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges use of cookies, user sessions, and pixel tags but does not provide a categorized cookie list with specific purposes; a separate Cookie Policy page is referenced in the site footer but its full contents were not retrievable.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references third-party hosting vendors and contractual service providers but does not name any specific companies or services.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of which specific data types are shared with which third parties is provided; sharing is described only in broad terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of email communications, but no broader opt-out from third-party data sharing with service providers is described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states SEA takes 'appropriate measures' to ensure third parties protect user data in accordance with the privacy policy, representing a general contractual obligation claim without specifics.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no statement indicating that users will be notified if third-party vendors or data-sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states that collected data is never sold or used for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy affirmatively states data is not used for advertising, and there is no indication of behavioral or targeted ad profiling.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party advertising tracking is described or implied; the nonprofit's stated mission and explicit no-advertising policy support this rating.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Pixel tags and cookies are listed as tracked data types without full explanation of their purpose, creating some ambiguity about whether any are used for non-functional tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since data is explicitly stated to never be used for advertising, there are no advertisers to opt out of sharing data with, satisfying this criterion by absence of the practice.

r677.riskReason: Talk & Comment explicitly claims FERPA and COPPA compliance, does not sell student data, encrypts all voice notes in transit and at storage, and enforces read-only mode for users under 13 with guardian consent required for recording — though the public privacy policy page itself is sparse and full independent verification of all stated practices is limited.
r677.parentSummary: Talk & Comment is a voice feedback tool used primarily by teachers in K-12 classrooms; it collects email, name, voice recordings, and usage analytics, encrypts all audio in transit and at rest, and explicitly states it never sells student data. Students under 13 are restricted to read-only mode by default, and recording requires verifiable parental or guardian consent managed through the school. Free recordings are retained for 90 days and can be deleted at any time, and the platform claims full FERPA and COPPA compliance.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The TOS and Privacy Policy pages exist with dated content (December 2025) but no publicly documented advance notification process or revision history is evident from available sources.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The help center and about page mention voice recordings, email, name, and usage analytics are collected, but the actual privacy policy page returned minimal content and a comprehensive enumerated data list is not confirmed from the policy document itself.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The help center states data is collected through account registration and voice recording activity, and extension metadata confirms analytics collection via PostHog and Google Analytics, but explicit policy language on collection methods is not fully accessible.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The About page explicitly states 'Your voice notes are yours' and the platform confirms it does not train AI on user data, indicating user ownership of content.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The help center explicitly states users 'can delete recordings anytime from your library,' satisfying the full deletion requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Free recordings are stored for 90 days and Pro recordings never expire — a specific retention period is stated, meeting the threshold for this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The help center states all voice notes are encrypted during transmission and storage, but no further specifics (e.g., AES-256, TLS version, SOC 2 certification) are publicly documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The platform explicitly states 'All voice notes are encrypted during transmission and storage,' confirming end-to-end encryption of the primary data type.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No public documentation was found specifying whether strong password enforcement or SSO/LTI integration is required for account creation on the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI login options was found in publicly available documentation or policy pages.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Chrome extension's host permissions include PostHog and Google Analytics domains indicating analytics cookies/tracking are used, but no detailed cookie policy enumerating all cookies and their purposes was found in the available privacy policy content.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Chrome extension manifest confirms PostHog (us.i.posthog.com) and Google Analytics are used as analytics third parties, but these are identified from technical inspection rather than a named third-party list in the privacy policy itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No per-third-party breakdown of exactly what data is shared with PostHog versus Google Analytics is publicly documented in the accessible policy pages.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The help center states data is never shared with third parties without consent, but no explicit opt-out mechanism for analytics third-party sharing is described in available documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The general statement that data is never shared without consent implies some vendor control, but no explicit Data Processing Agreement or supplier accountability clause is publicly referenced.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No specific language about notifying users of changes to third-party relationships was found in the accessible policy content.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The platform is a teacher/classroom tool with no advertising model; no ads of any kind are displayed to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The platform explicitly states it does not sell student data and does not use student data for targeted advertising; no targeting of any kind is evident.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The platform claims it never shares data with third parties without consent and has no advertising partnerships; no third-party ad tracking is indicated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: PostHog and Google Analytics are used for product analytics via the extension (confirmed by host permissions), which involves some tracking, but this appears to be functional/analytics tracking rather than advertising-oriented tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or data sharing with advertisers occurs, there is nothing to opt out of, effectively meeting this criterion by design.

r678.riskReason: Tampermonkey is a developer-oriented browser extension that requires broad permissions to access all websites a user visits, is not designed for K-12 educational use, lacks any COPPA/FERPA/SOPIPA compliance disclosures, has no minimum age requirement, no dedicated student data protections, and allows third-party userscripts that can access and modify any webpage content.
r678.parentSummary: Tampermonkey is a browser extension for running userscripts — it is not an educational platform and was not designed for K-12 students. It collects anonymous usage data such as extension version, browser type, and truncated IP addresses, but has no stated COPPA compliance, no minimum age requirement, and no student data protections. Most critically, the extension grants broad access to all websites a user visits and allows installation of third-party scripts of unknown origin, posing significant privacy and security risks for minors in a school environment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Terms of Service page was found and no policy change notification or revision history process is publicly stated on tampermonkey.net.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Tampermonkey publicly discloses some collected data (extension version, language, browser/OS type, truncated IP, anonymous statistics) via Chrome Web Store listings, but a comprehensive standalone privacy policy listing all data is not easily accessible.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: Data collection methods are described only at a general level (HTTP requests, anonymous statistics toggle) in extension store listings, without a detailed standalone policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: No data ownership statement is found; the privacy policy does not clarify whether users or Tampermonkey owns collected data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No user-facing data deletion mechanism is described in any accessible policy or documentation for the extension itself.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated anywhere in Tampermonkey's official documentation or privacy disclosures.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls) are described in publicly available Tampermonkey policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit encryption commitment is stated in the privacy disclosures; the extension uses both HTTP and HTTPS for script syncing.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account is required to use Tampermonkey, so password enforcement is not applicable and this criterion is met by default.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required to use Tampermonkey, so MFA is not applicable and this criterion is met by default.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Tampermonkey's website references a 'Cookie Settings' link in the footer indicating some cookie management exists, but no detailed cookie list with purposes is publicly documented.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No specific third-party data recipients are named in any accessible Tampermonkey privacy documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with any specific third party is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out process for third-party data sharing is described in the available documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor agreement or data processing obligations imposed on third parties are mentioned in Tampermonkey's public disclosures.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No process for notifying users of changes to third-party sharing arrangements is stated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Tampermonkey does not explicitly state it is ad-free; the extension and many userscripts it manages may interact with or inject advertising content, and this is not addressed in policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No policy statement addresses whether user data is used for targeted advertising, leaving this unresolved and representing a risk.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No policy addresses third-party tracking for advertising purposes, and the extension's broad page-access permissions make this a significant unresolved concern.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No policy addresses web beacons or tracking methods used for advertising; the extension's ability to run arbitrary scripts on all pages makes tracking risk indeterminate.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out mechanism for advertising data sharing is described anywhere in Tampermonkey's public documentation.

r679.riskReason: TD Snap (Tobii Dynavox) states it does not sell personal data and acknowledges COPPA obligations, but the privacy policy is a general corporate policy not specifically tailored to K-12 educational use, third-party sub-processors are not individually named, advertising and analytics cookies are used on the web platform, there is no explicit FERPA or SOPIPA commitment, and specific data retention periods are not defined.
r679.parentSummary: TD Snap is an AAC communication app by Tobii Dynavox used widely in K-12 special education settings. When used online, it collects user profile data (name, email, pictures), device/technical information, and usage data, which can be synced to Tobii Dynavox cloud servers in the United States. Tobii Dynavox states it does not sell personal data and uses encryption to protect stored data, but its privacy policy is a broad corporate policy that does not specifically address K-12 school or student data protections, does not name individual sub-processors, and does not state specific data retention timeframes, which may be a concern for school administrators evaluating FERPA and COPPA compliance.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states changes will be provided with notice (e.g., email notification), but a full revision history is not publicly maintained and users are expected to review terms regularly on their own.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy notice lists several categories of data collected (contact info, device ID, IP address, usage data, user profiles, pictures), but the TD Snap-specific policy directs users to the Apple App Store for app-level privacy details rather than providing a comprehensive standalone list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes data collection methods (direct user input, automatic collection via device use, third-party analytics) but does not provide a detailed, TD Snap-specific breakdown of exactly how each data type is collected within the app.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy and terms confirm user data remains user-owned (Tobii Dynavox does not claim ownership of user content), and the mytobiidynavox.com policy explicitly states personal information is not sold, traded, or rented.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may request deletion of personal data by contacting privacymanager@tobiidynavox.com, and the policy states that upon account deletion, data is deleted or anonymized; full deletion rights are afforded under applicable law including CCPA and GDPR.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained until it is 'no longer necessary' on a case-by-case basis and that some purchase data may be retained for tax purposes, but no specific retention periods (e.g., 90 days, 1 year) are stated, making this vague.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy notice references 'a combination of technical and organizational measures, including encryption, access controls, and secure servers,' and the security white paper details Azure cloud hosting with restricted staff access, but the in-app or K-12-specific security measures are not comprehensively documented in the main policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The myTobiiDynavox Security White Paper explicitly states all user data stored at rest is protected using 256-bit AES encryption via Azure cloud services, and HTTPS/TLS is used for data transmission.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of strong password enforcement requirements or minimum password standards is made in the publicly available terms or privacy policy for TD Snap or the myTobiiDynavox account platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Neither MFA nor SSO/LTI integration for K-12 school login is mentioned in any TD Snap or myTobiiDynavox documentation found; the platform relies on standard account-based login.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references 'sub-processors' supporting business functions but does not name specific third-party companies; it notes a list is 'available' but does not link directly within the main policy text found.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Third-party data sharing is described in broad functional categories (analytics, support, marketing, etc.) rather than specifying which data types are shared with which specific vendors, making per-party disclosure incomplete.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The cookie policy mentions third-party advertising and tracking services offer opt-out options, and CCPA opt-out rights are referenced, but a clear, simple opt-out process for all third-party data sharing specific to TD Snap school users is not prominently provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states all sub-processors are 'contractually bound to adhere to data protection obligations consistent with GDPR and other applicable privacy laws,' indicating vendor agreement requirements are in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states users will be notified of privacy policy changes (e.g., via email), but does not specifically commit to notifying users when sub-processors or third-party partners change, relying instead on periodic policy updates.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The TD Snap app itself does not appear to serve ads, but the Tobii Dynavox website and myTobiiDynavox platform use advertising and social media cookies, creating a gray area for school-context use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The cookie policy acknowledges use of advertising cookies and third-party analytics (including Google Analytics) on the web platform, though the app itself is not confirmed to serve targeted ads to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party analytics cookies including Google Analytics are used on Tobii Dynavox web properties; opt-out is mentioned as available through third-party privacy policies, but the process is not streamlined for school administrators.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy confirms use of advertising, performance, and social media/content cookies on web properties; tracking methods are listed by category but not all individual trackers are enumerated in a single accessible table.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Opt-out of targeted advertising is mentioned via references to NAI, DAA, and Google Ads Settings in related Tobii policies, but the process is indirect and not clearly presented as a single opt-out mechanism within the main TD Snap privacy documentation.

r680.riskReason: The platform uses Facebook Pixels and Google Analytics on its site, third-party data collection is acknowledged with limited opt-out, sale of data is not explicitly prohibited, and COPPA/FERPA compliance is not explicitly stated despite being used with children under 13.
r680.parentSummary: Teach Your Monster to Read collects personal information from teacher/parent account holders (such as name, email, and usage data) and student usernames and performance data to operate the game service; student accounts can only be created by adults, and the platform states data is used solely to deliver educational services. Third-party tools including Google Analytics and Facebook Pixels are used on the website, which introduces some tracking, though the policy states third parties are contractually bound not to use data for other purposes. Data sale is not explicitly addressed, COPPA compliance is not directly claimed, and the policy is governed by UK GDPR rather than US law, which may leave some gaps for US-based school districts.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The User Agreement states changes will be posted and users notified on their Account Homepage, but no formal revision history or advance notice period is specified.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists some data categories (name, email, usage, session data) but defers a full list to a separate page and does not comprehensively enumerate all data collected from students.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general description of how data is collected (registration, use of the service, cookies) but does not detail every collection method with specificity.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is not explicitly assigned to the user; the policy frames data processing around contractual necessity, leaving ownership ambiguous rather than explicitly affirming user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request account deletion and the policy references data subject rights under UK GDPR, but no clear self-service deletion tool or streamlined deletion process is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The User Agreement states inactive accounts are deleted after 3 years and data is retained only as long as necessary for the contracted purpose, constituting an adequate retention statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy states that 'appropriate technical and organisational measures' are taken to guard against unauthorized processing, but does not enumerate specific security controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The platform uses HTTPS (implied by web delivery and UK GDPR obligations) but the privacy policy does not explicitly mention encryption of data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform allows teachers to set student passwords and even offers a no-password option for young students, with no mention of enforced password complexity requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the policy or user agreement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A separate cookie policy exists and lists cookie types (functional, analytical, targeting) and names Google Analytics and Facebook Pixel, but does not provide a full granular cookie inventory with opt-in controls.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The cookie policy names Google Analytics and Facebook Pixel, and a third-party providers page exists, but the full list of third-party service providers is not comprehensively named in one place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by purpose category rather than specifying exactly which data elements are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The cookie policy mentions browser-level cookie blocking as the mechanism to opt out of third-party cookies, but no dedicated opt-out process for third-party data sharing is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy and User Agreement explicitly state that all third parties are bound by contractual provisions and may only use personal data for the described purposes in compliance with UK GDPR.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy states changes will be posted on the page but does not commit to proactively notifying users of changes to specific third-party providers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The mobile app states there are no in-game adverts; however, the website uses Facebook Pixel tracking, suggesting some advertising infrastructure exists around the platform perimeter.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy does not confirm that behavioral or targeted advertising is or is not displayed to users, and Common Sense Media notes this is unclear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Facebook Pixel and Google Analytics are used for tracking site visitors with no explicit opt-out mechanism provided to users beyond browser-level cookie blocking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Facebook Pixel is explicitly acknowledged in the cookie policy as a tracking tool used to understand how visitors access the site, constituting tracking beyond purely functional purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers or ad-tracking services is described; only generic browser cookie settings are mentioned as a workaround.
