r682.riskReason: TeachingBooks explicitly collects no student PII, commits to no sale or behavioral targeting of student data, and self-certifies compliance with FERPA, COPPA, and GDPR under OverDrive's comprehensive privacy program.
r682.parentSummary: TeachingBooks does not collect any personally identifiable information from students — only adult educators are asked to register with a name, work email, zip code, and professional interests. The platform explicitly commits to not selling user data, not targeting students with behavioral advertising, and encrypting all data at rest and in transit using AES-256 and SSL/TLS 1.2+. Students can access content without signing in at all, and the platform self-certifies compliance with both FERPA and COPPA.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The subscriber agreement states TeachingBooks reserves the right to send email about service changes, but no formal advance-notification process or revision history is explicitly documented in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states no student PII is collected, and adult data collected is listed as name, work email, zip code, profession, and interests in children's books.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly states data is collected via registration forms completed voluntarily by adult educators, and the Chrome Extension collects search terms and IP address if optionally installed.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states user information 'is always yours: private, never shared, removable anytime' and commits to not selling any user PII, indicating clear user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may close their account at any time by contacting TeachingBooks via email, and the sign-in page states data is 'removable anytime.'
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states inactive accounts may have usage details removed and that customer contact information is retained, but no specific retention period in days or years is stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy lists specific measures including annual third-party security audits, anti-intrusion software, AES-256 encryption at rest, SSL/TLS 1.2+ in transit, and salted/hashed password storage.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states data in transit is encrypted using SSL/TLS 1.2+ and data at rest is encrypted using AES-256.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not explicitly describe password strength requirements or enforcement of complex passwords, though OAuth2 secure logins are mentioned for student access.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The policy explicitly states secure logins via OAuth2 protocols are used without student data transference, and the platform supports SSO-style access for students without requiring individual accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookie categories (functional, performance, research/analytics, and remarketing) are listed with purposes under OverDrive's cookie policy, but the remarketing cookies for OverDrive websites add ambiguity for the TeachingBooks-specific context.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: JWPlayer is specifically named as a third-party service used for embedded content playback, and OverDrive is identified as the parent company, but other third parties receiving aggregate data are only described as 'approved third parties' without being named.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states JWPlayer does not receive PII and that only aggregate, anonymous, non-user-specific usage data is shared with approved third parties, but specific data elements per third party are not individually enumerated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy commits to not sharing student PII and states no student data is collected; adult users can close accounts and opt out of email communications, constituting an effective opt-out of data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: JWPlayer is stated to be configured consistently with TeachingBooks' policies and no PII is transferred through it, but no explicit vendor agreement or contractual responsibility clause for all third parties is described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The subscriber agreement reserves the right to notify users of service changes via email, but does not specifically commit to notifying users when third-party data processors change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states no behavioral advertising is directed at students, and no advertisements are shown within the educational platform itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy explicitly commits to 'not use or disclose any student information for behavioral targeting of advertising to students,' and no user targeting for ads is described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy commits to no behavioral tracking of students for advertising purposes, and student access requires no account creation, limiting any tracking exposure.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: OverDrive's cookie policy includes remarketing and targeting cookies described as applicable to 'OverDrive websites only' and not in educational products, but the boundary between OverDrive and TeachingBooks contexts is not fully clear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of research and remarketing cookies through the OverDrive cookie preference center, and opting out of research cookies automatically opts out of remarketing cookies as well.

r683.minAge: 18 (direct accounts); under 13 permitted only via school/institution COPPA authorization
dataCollected: Customer content (files, documents, audio, video, images)
r683.riskReason: While TeachShare has strong student data protections via its DPA and explicitly prohibits targeted advertising on student data, the website-level privacy policy discloses third-party behavioral advertising, web beacons, and tracking technologies that are not fully enumerated, and the platform grants itself a broad perpetual license to user content for product improvement, creating residual risk for K-12 deployments.
r683.parentSummary: TeachShare collects account information (name, email) from teachers and school staff only — not directly from students — and processes student data solely to provide its educational services under a formal Student Data Privacy Addendum. The platform explicitly prohibits using student data for targeted advertising and commits to never selling student data. However, the website-facing privacy policy permits third-party behavioral advertising trackers and web beacons that are not individually named, which may be a concern for schools reviewing full data flows.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The platform privacy notice explicitly states that material changes to policies affecting student data will be communicated to Educational Institutions before new data uses take effect, satisfying the advance notification standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The platform privacy policy lists several data categories (contact info, customer content, payment info, support data, usage data) but does not provide a fully exhaustive enumeration, particularly regarding cookies and all automated collection types on the website layer.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy notes data is collected directly from users and automatically as they navigate the site, but does not provide specific detail about all automated collection mechanisms such as analytics SDKs or pixel tags beyond a general reference.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Users are granted a license to their content and TeachShare claims a broad 'irrevocable, perpetual, transferable, sublicensable' license for platform improvement, creating ambiguity over effective ownership of teacher-uploaded content.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may request deletion by emailing hey@teachshare.com, but the policy states personal information cannot be deleted except by deleting the entire account, which constitutes a limited rather than granular deletion right.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Neither the Platform Privacy Notice nor the Terms of Service specifies a defined retention period for user or student data after account termination or service conclusion.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Student Data Privacy Addendum references 'reasonable administrative, physical and technical safeguards' but does not enumerate specific security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or audit practices in the publicly available documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is not explicitly described in the platform or student privacy documentation; the website privacy policy references SSL for payment data via Stripe, but in-platform encryption at rest or in transit is not confirmed.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The login page confirms users must be 18 or older and Google OAuth SSO is offered, which satisfies the strong authentication/SSO standard without relying on self-managed passwords.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Google OAuth/SSO is available as a login mechanism, satisfying the SSO equivalence standard for MFA; no direct MFA configuration details are provided but SSO mitigates this gap.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The website-level privacy policy mentions browser cookies, Flash cookies, and web beacons generally but does not provide a specific enumerated cookie list with individual names, categories, and purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Stripe is named as a payment processor and 'AI service providers' are referenced as recipients of student data, but the specific AI vendors are not named in the publicly available policy documents.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by category of recipient (payment providers, AI service providers, legal authorities) rather than specifying exactly what data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of promotional email communications, and NAI opt-out is referenced for behavioral advertising on the website, but there is no clear in-platform opt-out mechanism specifically for all third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Student Data Privacy Addendum explicitly requires that third parties receiving student data be 'contractually bound to maintain the confidentiality of the Student Data and comply with data protection requirements consistent with those provided in this DPA.'
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The platform privacy notice explicitly commits to notifying Educational Institutions before making material changes to how student data is collected or used, satisfying the notification-of-changes standard.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Student DPA prohibits targeted advertising to students, but the website-level privacy policy acknowledges that third-party advertisers serve interest-based ads on the website, creating a partial compliance state depending on context of access.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Student data is explicitly prohibited from use in targeted advertising per the DPA, but the website privacy policy acknowledges third parties 'may use this information to provide you with interest-based (behavioral) advertising,' which applies to teacher/staff accounts on the website layer.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The website privacy policy acknowledges third-party behavioral tracking but states the platform does not control third-party tracking technologies; an NAI opt-out link is referenced but no direct platform-level opt-out control is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The website privacy policy explicitly describes web beacons and third-party ad network tracking technologies used across the site, including for behavioral advertising purposes, which confirms tracking beyond functional use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The privacy policy references the NAI opt-out tool for behavioral advertising but does not provide a clear, first-party opt-out mechanism for data sharing with advertisers directly within the platform or account settings.

dataSharedWith: Third-party service providers (payment processing, marketing partners)
Social media companies (Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram)
Law enforcement or legal process requestors
r684.riskReason: While student data protections are strong and explicitly FERPA/COPPA-compliant, the platform uses third-party targeted advertising and tracking technologies (cookies, web beacons, Google Analytics) for non-student consumer users on the same service, creating ambiguity and potential risk in K-12 deployments.
r684.parentSummary: TeachTown Social Skills collects student educational records, usage data, and account information under the direction of the school, and explicitly states it does not use student data for advertising or profiling beyond educational purposes. However, the platform does engage in interest-based targeted advertising and third-party tracking for non-student (consumer) users, and employs cookies, web beacons, and Google Analytics across its service. Parents should be aware that while student data protections align with FERPA and COPPA, the broader platform has advertising-related data practices that apply to educator and consumer accounts.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service states TeachTown reserves the right to modify the agreement and will provide notice of material changes, but no explicit revision history or changelog is publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy comprehensively lists collected data categories including identifiers, educational institution information, student data, device/usage information, and third-party sourced data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected — through registration forms, third-party SSO integrations (ClassLink, OneRoster), tracking technologies, and social media interactions.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy explicitly states that as between TeachTown and the Educational Institution, student data is owned and controlled by the Educational Institution.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can update account information via the Account page and may request deletion, but the policy does not provide a clear, straightforward self-service deletion process for all data types.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not specify a defined data retention period; it addresses data security and use limitations but lacks a stated timeframe for how long data is retained.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy lists specific security measures including data encryption, firewalls, access controls, periodic audits, NIST framework alignment, and annual SOC 2 compliance audits.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states the use of data encryption as part of its security safeguards, and the platform supports HTTPS throughout.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform requires login credentials but does not explicitly state enforcement of strong password policies; SSO via ClassLink/OneRoster is supported, partially addressing this.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform supports SSO integrations (ClassLink, OneRoster) which provide federated authentication, but dedicated MFA is not explicitly mentioned as available or required.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies, web beacons, embedded scripts, and tracking technologies generally with some opt-out guidance, but does not provide a full enumerated list of each cookie and its specific purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references service providers, advertising networks, social media companies, Google Analytics, ClassLink, and OneRoster, but does not provide a complete named list of all third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Third-party data sharing is described by category rather than specifying exactly which data elements are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Opt-out mechanisms are referenced for interest-based advertising via NAI and DAA opt-out tools and Google Ads Preferences, but these are browser-based and unreliable across devices and sessions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Terms of Service states TeachTown agrees to treat student data as confidential and not share it with third parties other than as described, indicating vendor-level contractual responsibility.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not explicitly state that users will be notified when third-party service providers or advertising partners are changed or added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states student data is not used for advertising, but confirms that targeted ads are served to consumer/educator users on the same platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: TeachTown explicitly prohibits targeted advertising using student data, but does conduct interest-based advertising targeting non-student consumers using browsing history and device data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising networks and social media companies are permitted to track user behavior across the service and other websites, with opt-out available only through external NAI/DAA tools.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy discloses the use of cookies, web beacons, embedded scripts, and Google Analytics for advertising purposes, but the tracking methods are broadly described rather than fully enumerated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Opt-out from interest-based advertising is possible via NAI, DAA, and Google Ads Preferences links provided in the policy, though the process is cumbersome and not persistent across devices or browsers.

r685.riskReason: TeachVid collects student personal data and progress information but publicly links to no accessible, standalone Privacy Policy or Terms of Service page, making it impossible to verify any COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance commitments, data retention limits, security measures, or parental rights.
r685.parentSummary: TeachVid is a language-learning platform that requires student registration (collecting name, email, and password) and tracks activity scores, completion data, and time on task. The platform embeds YouTube videos via the YouTube API, meaning YouTube's own advertising and tracking applies within the embedded player. No publicly accessible Privacy Policy or Terms of Service page could be found on the site, so parents and schools cannot verify how student data is stored, shared, or protected.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No standalone Privacy Policy or Terms of Service page was found on teachvid.com, so no policy change notification process or revision history is available to users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Registration documentation from a third-party guide indicates name, email, and password are collected, and the platform tracks scores and progress, but no comprehensive data list is published in an accessible policy document.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: There is no publicly available policy page explaining how data is collected (e.g., via forms, cookies, or automated tracking); the site only references cookie acceptance with no further detail.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: No Terms of Service or Privacy Policy was found that addresses data ownership; the company's ownership claim over user data is entirely unaddressed publicly.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No policy or mechanism for users or parents to request data deletion was identified anywhere on the platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or policy is stated anywhere on the accessible portions of the site.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, audits) are described anywhere in publicly accessible site content.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (in transit or at rest) was found in any accessible page or document on the site.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No information about password strength requirements or enforcement was found; registration requires a password but no policy details are provided.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration for secure login was found on the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The site acknowledges the use of cookies with a consent banner on every page, but no cookie policy listing specific cookies, their purposes, or opt-out options is publicly accessible.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No third-party disclosure list is published; the only identifiable third party is YouTube (used for video embedding via API), but this is not formally disclosed in any policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: There is no published breakdown of what specific data is shared with YouTube or any other third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described or available to users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor or data processing agreements with third parties are referenced or disclosed on the platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No process for notifying users of changes to third-party data sharing relationships is described anywhere on the site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: YouTube videos embedded via the API carry YouTube's own branding and advertising as explicitly stated on the FAQ page, meaning ads are displayed within the platform to students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Because YouTube's ad-supported embeds are used without any stated opt-out or ad-free arrangement, students may be subject to YouTube's targeted advertising algorithms.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: YouTube's embedded player can involve YouTube/Google tracking technologies; no opt-out or disclosure of this third-party tracking is provided by TeachVid.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: YouTube's embedded video player likely uses tracking cookies and web beacons per Google's policies, and TeachVid provides no disclosure or control mechanism for this.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers (including via YouTube embeds) is described or available on the TeachVid platform.

dataSharedWith: Affiliates and brands within TeamBuildr network
Acquirers/successors in event of company sale
Studios and teams associated with user accounts
r686.riskReason: While TeamBuildr holds iKeepSafe COPPA safe harbor certification and claims FERPA compliance, the platform uses advertising cookies and third-party targeting cookies, displays ads to users 18+, and acknowledges that sharing data with affiliates may constitute a 'sale' of personal information in some jurisdictions, creating notable risk for K-12 deployments involving minors.
r686.parentSummary: TeamBuildr collects personal information including names, email addresses, IP addresses, device data, and athletic performance/workout data from users to provide its strength and conditioning services. The platform participates in the iKeepSafe COPPA safe harbor program, does not knowingly collect data from children under 13 without appropriate consent, and expressly states it supports school FERPA compliance. However, parents should be aware that third-party advertising cookies are used on the platform, and data may be shared with analytics providers, advertising partners, and affiliates, which warrants review before school-wide deployment for younger student-athletes.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy is dated June 21, 2023 and the terms of use October 8, 2025, indicating revisions occur, but the policy states changes may be posted without advance individual notification, only via website posting — no proactive advance notification process is clearly described.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists identifiers, IP address, device information, activity and workout data, cookies, usage data, and billing information, providing a reasonably comprehensive enumeration of data types collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes collection through direct user input, website visits, cookies and tracking technologies, and via third-party analytics providers, constituting a clear description of collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The User Agreement states user-uploaded content is the user's exclusive property, but TeamBuildr explicitly retains full ownership of 'Aggregated Statistics' derived from user/customer data, creating a split and partially unclear ownership model.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy includes a section on user rights and choices, and users may request deletion, but the process is not explicitly detailed as a self-service option — deletion appears to require contacting TeamBuildr, and conditions or waiting periods are not fully clarified.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy references a 'Data Retention' section but search results do not reveal a specific retention period stated in days or months — the retention statement appears general rather than specific.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy references security for the Services and the EULA references security risk monitoring, but specific technical security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, penetration testing) are not enumerated — only a general security posture is implied.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit statement about encryption of data in transit or at rest was found in the retrieved policy text, though the platform operates via HTTPS; encryption is not expressly confirmed in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Use place sole responsibility for password security on the user but do not specify enforcement of strong password requirements (e.g., length, complexity, or technical controls).
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration was found in the Terms of Use or Privacy Policy, and the platform appears to rely on username/password only.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: TeamBuildr has a dedicated Cookie Notice page that categorizes cookies (Strictly Necessary, Functionality, Targeting/Advertising) and provides a Cookie Consent Tool, meeting the requirement for listed cookies with purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references 'service providers,' 'analytics providers,' 'advertising partners,' and 'affiliates' in broad categories but does not name specific third-party companies by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by category of third party rather than specifying exactly what data elements are shared with each individual third party, providing only a partial disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: A Cookie Consent Tool is provided to opt out of non-essential cookies including targeting cookies, and some advertising opt-outs are referenced, but a comprehensive, easy opt-out from all third-party data sharing is not clearly described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that when TeamBuildr transfers data to third-party agents, TeamBuildr retains liability if the agent processes data inconsistently with stated principles, indicating vendor accountability obligations exist.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No specific process for notifying users when third-party sharing arrangements change is described; policy updates are posted on the website without guaranteed advance individual notice of third-party changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy states ads may be displayed to app users from 'trusted advertising partners,' and the cookie notice confirms advertising/targeting cookies are used, but ads appear limited to partner networks rather than open ad exchanges.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy states that for users 18 or older, personal information may be used to display more relevant advertisements, and targeting cookies are used for interest-based ads — users under 18 appear excluded from targeted advertising, but this age-based restriction is not robustly enforced.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising cookies are used and the Cookie Consent Tool allows opting out of targeting cookies, but third-party tracking by advertising networks is acknowledged and opt-out requires active use of the consent tool.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy and cookie notice acknowledge use of web beacons, pixel tags, and similar tracking technologies by analytics and advertising providers, though the cookie consent tool provides some controls.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The Cookie Consent Tool provides a mechanism to opt out of targeting/advertising cookies, and users can contact TeamBuildr to exercise privacy rights, but the opt-out process for all forms of data sharing with advertisers is not consolidated or clearly documented in one place.

dataCollected: Content submitted in forums and lessons
dataSharedWith: Analytics vendors (Sailthru, CleverTap, Mixpanel, ComScore, VWO, HubSpot, Google Analytics)
Trusted third-party vendors for membership benefits
r687.riskReason: TED-Ed displays personalized advertising, uses tracking technologies to build user profiles for ad targeting on third-party sites, and collects data beyond what is required for educational use — all significant concerns for K-12 student users.
r687.parentSummary: TED-Ed collects personal information including name, email, usage data, and location from users who create accounts, and uses this data partly for personalized advertising and third-party ad targeting platforms like Meta, TikTok, and Google. While TED states it does not sell personal data, it does share it with numerous third-party vendors for analytics and advertising purposes, and it is unclear whether strong contractual data-use restrictions apply to those vendors. Children under 13 may not create accounts without verifiable parental consent, but the platform's broad data sharing and advertising practices are a concern for any K-12 deployment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy displays a version date and notes material changes will be announced for 30–60 days, but there is no advance notification process or full public revision history archive.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several data categories (name, email, usage, location, forum content, survey responses) but Common Sense Media found it unclear whether all PII categories collected are fully enumerated.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy describes some collection methods (account registration, cookies, tracking pixels, conversion APIs) in general terms but does not comprehensively map each data type to a specific collection method.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Users grant TED a broad, perpetual, royalty-free license over submitted content per the Terms of Use, making ownership ambiguous rather than clearly resting with the user.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may request account deactivation and contact privacy@ted.com for data changes, but it is not clearly stated whether full deletion of all personal data is available upon request.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not state a specific data retention period; it implies data is held as long as needed but provides no concrete timeframe or retention schedule.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'commercially reasonable physical, technical and administrative controls' and breach notification processes, but does not enumerate specific security technologies or standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy makes no mention of encryption for data at rest or in transit, which is a noted gap in independent evaluations of TED-Ed's policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: There is no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement; the policy does not address password security standards for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the publicly available policies for ed.ted.com.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and tracking technologies generally and references an opt-out mechanism via browser settings and TED's footer, but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies with individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Several specific vendors are named (Sailthru, CleverTap, Mixpanel, Stripe, Meta, TikTok, Google, LinkedIn), which is a partial disclosure, but the full list of all third parties receiving data is not comprehensively enumerated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by vendor category or use case rather than specifying precisely which data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of targeted advertising via browser settings or TED's footer controls, but this is a browser-level mechanism rather than a clear, platform-level opt-out tied to each third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states vendors are 'trusted' and implies some oversight, but does not explicitly state that all third-party vendors are bound by data processing agreements that restrict how they may use shared data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy notes it may be updated from time to time with version-date disclosure, but does not commit to proactively notifying users specifically when third-party data-sharing relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: TED-Ed's policies clearly state that personalized advertising is displayed to users, making this a confirmed concern for K-12 use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: User information is explicitly used to track and target advertisements on third-party platforms such as Meta, TikTok, Google, and LinkedIn, confirming user-level ad targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking technologies collect data from users for advertising purposes on both TED's own sites and third-party sites, with only browser-level opt-outs available and no platform-level blocking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms use of tracking pixels, conversion APIs, and behavioral profiling for advertising, which constitutes confirmed advertising-driven tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: TED references an opt-out index for deactivating targeted advertising added in the June 2025 policy update, but the opt-out process relies on external industry tools rather than a simple in-platform control, making it unclear and partially accessible.

dataCollected: Photos and videos uploaded or shared
Information about other users provided by account holder
dataSharedWith: Servers in the United States, China, and Hong Kong
r688.riskReason: Tello EDU is a K-12 drone/app platform made by China-based Ryze Tech in partnership with DJI; its privacy policy explicitly states data may be routed to servers in the US, China, and Hong Kong, the platform explicitly states it is NOT directed to children under 16 (contradicting its K-12 marketing), there is no dedicated COPPA or FERPA language, no explicit prohibition on student data sale, no specific mention of encryption, and third-party data sharing practices — including with DJI, which has documented security concerns — are inadequately disclosed for a K-12 educational context.
r688.parentSummary: Tello EDU is a programmable drone and companion app developed for K-12 students by Shenzhen Ryze Technology, a Chinese company that partners with DJI. The platform collects personal information including name, email, location, and photos/videos, and its privacy policy acknowledges data may be stored or processed on servers in the United States, China, and Hong Kong. Despite being marketed explicitly for K-12 education, the Ryze Tech privacy policy states the product is 'not directed to children under the age of 16' and lacks COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance language, presenting significant data privacy concerns for school use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Ryze Tech policy states material changes will be attempted to be communicated with reasonable notice before they become effective, but there is no revision history or advance notification mechanism clearly documented for users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, location, photos/videos, usage data, device identifiers) but uses non-exhaustive language ('including but not limited to') leaving the full scope of collection unclear.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy describes some methods of collection (account registration, product use, uploads, customer service contact) but does not comprehensively explain all technical means by which data is gathered from the app and drone.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not affirm user ownership of data; data retention language states Ryze may retain submitted information indefinitely for backups, archiving, fraud prevention, analytics, or legal obligations, implying company control.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may update, correct, or delete certain account information via account preferences or by contacting Ryze, but the policy reserves the right to retain data indefinitely after account closure for various stated purposes, limiting full deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states retention period is determined by the purpose of use and legal obligations but provides no specific timeframes, making it vague rather than a concrete retention commitment.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states Ryze uses 'certain physical, organizational, and technical safeguards' but explicitly acknowledges no security measure is perfect and provides no detail on what specific protections are in place.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy makes no mention of encryption of data at rest or in transit, and the platform's connection to servers in China and Hong Kong raises further concerns about data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: There is no mention of password strength requirements, password enforcement policies, or SSO options anywhere in the available Ryze Tech policy documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is present in the policy or product documentation, and the product is not designed for LMS integration.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Ryze Tech privacy policy does not include a cookie policy, does not list cookies used, and does not distinguish between functional and tracking cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy mentions sharing data with DJI and unspecified third-party service providers but does not name other specific third parties by name in a comprehensive list.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what particular data is shared with each named or unnamed third party; data sharing disclosures are grouped and general.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in the Ryze Tech policy; users are not given a clear process to limit sharing with DJI or other third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states third-party sites have their own privacy policies but does not assert that Ryze holds third-party partners, including DJI, to contractual privacy standards or a vendor agreement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy says users should check periodically for changes but does not commit to notifying users specifically when third-party sharing relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Ryze Tech privacy policy does not address whether advertising is displayed within the app, and the companion app's K-12 context means any advertising exposure would be of concern.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy is silent on targeted advertising practices within the Tello EDU app; given its affiliation with DJI — which has documented ad network partnerships — targeted advertising cannot be ruled out.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure exists about third-party tracking for advertising purposes within the Tello EDU platform, and no opt-out mechanism for any such tracking is described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy makes no mention of web beacons, pixel tags, or other tracking technologies that may be used within the app or on the website.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There is no opt-out process described for data sharing with advertisers, and the policy's lack of transparency on advertising practices means compliance cannot be confirmed.

r689.minAge: 13 (apps not intended for children under 13; school must obtain COPPA consent)
dataSharedWith: Advertisers (Google DoubleClick, Facebook, Yahoo, Pubmatic, Rubicon Project)
r689.riskReason: TI has a dedicated education data policy that prohibits selling or marketing student data, but the main ti.com site uses extensive third-party advertising cookies (Google DoubleClick, Facebook, Yahoo, Rubicon) that apply to the broader platform where education tools are hosted, and account deletion of student records is not fully supported.
r689.parentSummary: Texas Instruments collects names, email addresses, and usage data for account-based educational software, and explicitly states it does not sell or use student data for advertising. However, the broader TI website uses third-party advertising trackers (including Google, Facebook, and Yahoo cookies) that may capture activity on education-related pages. TI retains student data for the license term plus one year, and parents or guardians can submit data requests via TI's Information Request Form, though removing a student from the admin system does not automatically delete their account.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: TI reserves the right to change policies at any time without prior notice, recommending users periodically review; no advance notification process or revision history is explicitly provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The education-specific data policy lists user data types (name, email, license association), but the main privacy policy broadly references 'a broad variety of information' without exhaustively listing all data categories collected on the general site.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically states data is collected through TI websites, online services, design and computing tools, blogs, and mobile applications, and the education policy clarifies data is gathered when users create accounts for app access.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: TI does not explicitly state that users own their data; the Terms of Use grants TI a broad, perpetual, royalty-free license over user-submitted content, leaving ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can submit data deletion requests via TI's Information Request Form, but deleting a student from the admin system does not delete their account, indicating only partial or process-dependent deletion capability.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The education data policy states TI retains user data for the term of the applicable software license plus one additional year, which is a specific and documented retention period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: TI specifically lists security measures including secure servers, firewalls, encryption, backups, and usernames/passwords as part of its administrative and technical safeguards.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy and education data policies explicitly mention encryption as a commercially available security technology in use, and HTTPS is required for platform communications.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: TI requires passwords for account access but does not explicitly state it enforces strong password policies or complexity requirements in its published policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in TI's published privacy or terms policies for K-12 student accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: TI provides a detailed cookie policy listing specific cookies by name, domain, purpose, and expiration, including strictly necessary, analytics, and advertising cookies with opt-out instructions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The education data policy references 'certain third parties' for service support without naming them; the cookie policy names specific ad partners (Google DoubleClick, Facebook, Yahoo, Pubmatic, Rubicon) but these are not in the education-specific policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Third-party sharing is described in grouped categories (service providers, payment processors, advertisers) rather than specifying exactly which data elements are shared with each named party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: TI's cookie policy provides opt-out links for some advertising partners (e.g., Salesforce DMP), but opt-out from all third-party data sharing is not clearly or comprehensively documented in a single location.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The education data policy states that third-party service providers may only access user data under 'strict confidentiality, security and privacy terms,' indicating vendor contractual obligations are in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Neither the privacy policy nor the education data policy describes a process for notifying users when third-party partners change; TI simply reserves the right to update policies at any time.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The education data policy explicitly states TI does not use or share user data for marketing or advertising purposes, but the main ti.com site (where education tools are accessed) does display ads driven by third-party trackers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Student user data from the education apps is explicitly not used for targeted advertising per the education data policy, but the broader TI platform uses behavioral and preference-based ad targeting on its general website.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Some opt-out links are provided in the cookie policy for specific ad trackers, but third-party tracking via Google DoubleClick, Facebook pixel, Yahoo, and others is active on TI sites with only partial opt-out coverage.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy explicitly lists multiple web beacons and tracking pixels (Google DoubleClick, Facebook, Pubmatic, Rubicon, Yahoo) used for targeted advertising across TI's sites, including education.ti.com.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Some opt-out mechanisms are referenced in the cookie policy for specific networks, but there is no single, clear, comprehensive opt-out process from all advertising data sharing documented for K-12 users.

dataCollected: Usage data (pages visited, time on site)
r690.riskReason: Textivate is a Spain-based platform governed only by GDPR with no mention of COPPA or FERPA compliance, uses Google Analytics to track all users including students, relies on implicit consent by use, and its privacy policy has not been updated since June 2018.
r690.parentSummary: Textivate collects student identifiers (names set by teachers), activity scores, and usage data including IP addresses, and shares analytics data with Google Analytics. The platform is operated by a Spanish company and is governed by GDPR only — it makes no mention of COPPA or FERPA compliance, which are required for U.S. K-12 use. Parents should be aware that consent is obtained implicitly by use of the site, and the privacy policy has not been updated since 2018.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states it is kept under regular review and updates are posted on the same page, but no revision history or advance notification process is described, and the policy has not been updated since June 2018.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data types (student names/identifiers, activity scores, IP addresses, contact form data, usage data via Google Analytics) but does not provide a comprehensive, structured inventory of all data collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes how data is collected (registration, contact forms, cookies, Google Analytics) but lacks specificity for all data types, particularly for student-facing data collection.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state who owns the data; it references user authorization for processing but does not clearly affirm that users retain ownership of their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request full deletion of their data by emailing the Data Protection Officer, and teachers can self-delete resources and class lists directly within the platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state any specific or general data retention period for any category of data collected.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states that 'appropriate measures' have been taken to protect personal information but does not list any specific technical or organizational security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (in transit or at rest) is made anywhere in the privacy policy or terms and conditions.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy and terms and conditions make no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in any available policy or documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy identifies three categories of cookies (non-essential notification cookies, Google Analytics cookies, and essential functional cookies) but does not provide a full cookie inventory with specific names and purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google Analytics is named as a third-party service that receives usage data, but no other third parties are specifically identified despite the platform using payment processing and hosting services.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states that Google Analytics cookies 'do not store any personal information' and 'we do not share the data,' but does not detail what data flows to each third party involved in service delivery.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is provided; users are only told they can disable cookies but that doing so will break the site.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No mention is made of contractual obligations, data processing agreements, or vendor accountability requirements imposed on third parties such as Google Analytics.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not describe any process for notifying users if third-party partners change or if new third parties are added.

complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out mechanism for data sharing with advertisers or analytics platforms is offered; disabling cookies is noted as an option but would break site functionality.

r691.riskReason: ThatQuiz self-claims COPPA compliance and minimal student data collection, but its privacy policy and terms of service are sparse, leaving third-party sharing, data retention periods, encryption practices, deletion rights, and advertising practices unclear or unaddressed.
r691.parentSummary: ThatQuiz collects no personal or identifying information from students — only numerical test scores, which are kept private to the registered teacher. Teacher registration requires basic account information, and server logs may collect browser and IP data from all visitors. The platform claims COPPA compliance, but its policies lack detail on security measures, data retention, third-party relationships, and deletion rights, which limits a full independent assessment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy and terms of service provide no stated process for notifying users of policy changes or maintaining a revision history.

complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that servers automatically log browser-provided data, but does not specifically describe how teacher registration data or student score data is collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly address data ownership; it states student data is private to the registered teacher but does not confirm users own their data or that ThatQuiz disclaims ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy and terms of service contain no mention of a user right or mechanism to request deletion of their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated anywhere in the published privacy policy or terms of service.

complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party tracking for advertising purposes is disclosed, but absence of disclosure is not equivalent to confirmed absence of tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookie use is acknowledged as required for site functionality, but no detail is given on whether web beacons or ad-tracking methods are employed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described, and no affirmative statement that student or user data is never shared with advertisers is present.

r692.riskReason: The Farmer's Almanac is a general consumer content and commerce website — not an EdTech platform — that displays third-party targeted advertising, uses persistent tracking cookies for remarketing, shares anonymous data with advertisers, and has no FERPA compliance, SOPIPA compliance, or school-oriented data protections whatsoever.
r692.parentSummary: The Farmer's Almanac website collects personal information such as name, email, address, and browsing data when users register or make purchases, and uses persistent cookies to track users for advertising purposes including remarketing through Google, Facebook, and Instagram. The site states it does not knowingly collect data from children under 16, but it is a general consumer website with no student data protections, no FERPA or SOPIPA compliance, and it shares anonymous behavioral data with third-party advertisers. This platform is not designed or suitable for K-12 educational use, and its advertising-driven data practices pose significant privacy risks for student users.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy contains no stated process for advance notification of policy changes, no revision history, and no version date visible in the policy text itself.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several data types (name, address, email, phone, credit card, IP address, usage data, cookies) but uses 'include, but are not limited to' language, leaving the full scope of data collection undefined.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states data is collected when users provide it or through cookies and third-party services, but does not specifically describe all collection mechanisms (e.g., pixel tracking, web beacons) in detail.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not state that users own their data; Geiger's parent company claims full intellectual property rights over site content and does not affirm user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The store's terms allow users to request deletion via email to customer service, but the main site policy does not provide a clear, self-service deletion mechanism for all collected data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not specify any data retention period or timeframe for how long personal information is kept after collection or account closure.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy contains no description of specific security measures, encryption standards, or technical safeguards used to protect collected personal data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: There is no mention of encryption (at rest or in transit) anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of use.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy mentions that creating an account requires a username and password but does not state any password strength requirements or enforcement mechanisms.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI is made anywhere in the policy; no account security beyond basic username/password is described.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions persistent cookies and their general purposes (e.g., basket ID, browsing history, affiliate tracking) but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies with individual names and purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names some specific third parties (Google Analytics, Akismet, Amazon Associates, Google/Facebook/Instagram for remarketing) but does not provide a complete list of all advertising or data-sharing partners.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared by category of third party rather than specifying exactly what data is shared with each named partner, making per-party disclosure incomplete.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy mentions the option not to receive promotional emails and the ability to remove cookies via browser settings, but provides no clear opt-out from third-party data sharing for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that third-party service providers are governed by their own privacy policies but makes no claim that those vendors are contractually bound to follow Farmers' Almanac's data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not state that users will be notified if third-party sharing partners change; it only says users can contact the company with questions.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly confirms that third-party advertising companies are used to serve content and advertisements on the website, including remarketing ads from Google, Facebook, and Instagram.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms advertisers may use cookies to match ads to browsing history and that remarketing companies serve ads based on past visits, constituting confirmed user-level behavioral targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party remarketing and advertising cookies are used with no clear opt-out mechanism provided within the site itself; browser-level cookie removal is the only suggested recourse.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms use of persistent tracking cookies, affiliate tracking links, and remarketing pixels from multiple third-party platforms for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The policy mentions the option to opt out of promotional emails and browser-based cookie removal, but does not provide a clear, dedicated process for opting out of data sharing with advertising partners specifically.

r693.riskReason: The platform expressly states it does not sell student data or use it for behavioral advertising and discloses security measures including TLS encryption, but FERPA/HIPAA and state-specific compliance obligations are only guaranteed with a paid 'Compliance Add-On,' leaving standard K-12 institutional subscribers with uncertainty about the full scope of legal protections in place.
r693.parentSummary: The Social Express, operated by Brighten Learning, collects student account data, learning progress, usage logs, device information, and cookies to deliver its K-12 social-emotional learning program. The company states it does not sell student personal information or use it for behavioral advertising, and it uses transport-layer encryption and access controls to protect data. However, full FERPA and state-specific compliance protections are conditioned on purchasing a separate paid 'Compliance Add-On,' which means standard subscribers should carefully review their district's data privacy agreement before deploying the platform.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The TOS states material changes will be communicated via email or posted notice, but no formal revision history or versioned archive of past policies is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Brighten Learning privacy policy provides a detailed enumerated list of data collected, including account/profile data, student learning data, device/technical data, support communications, and payment records.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy explicitly describes multiple collection methods including voluntary account submission, learning platform activity, and automated collection via cookies, web beacons, flash cookies, and persistent identifiers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly state that users or schools own their data; data access and deletion requests must go through organization admins or parents, implying institutional control rather than explicit user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Deletion is permitted but routed through organization admins or parents with unspecified verification requirements and legal exceptions, limiting direct individual deletion rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Student data retention is stated as the active term plus 60 days post-deletion, and support logs are retained up to 12 months, providing specific enough retention criteria to satisfy this standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy lists administrative, technical, and physical safeguards including encryption in transit, access controls, monitoring, employee training, and industry-standard file encryption for COPPA/FERPA-protected data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Transport Layer Security (TLS) is explicitly stated for all user data transmission to and from the learning platform, and industry-standard file encryption is cited for stored protected data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The acceptable use policy requires users to keep credentials confidential and not share or circumvent authentication, but no explicit enforcement of strong password standards (e.g., complexity requirements) is documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is explicitly mentioned in the publicly available policies; account-based login is required with username/password only.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The website uses a cookie consent manager that categorizes cookies (essential, analytics including Google Analytics) and allows toggling, but specific named third-party cookies and their individual purposes are not fully enumerated in a comprehensive cookie policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references 'authorized subprocessors' for hosting, analytics, support, and payments, and names Google Analytics, Google Webfonts, Google Maps, and reCaptcha as external services, but a complete named vendor list for all subprocessors is not published.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy broadly states subprocessors receive data needed to perform their functions but does not itemize exactly which specific data fields are shared with each named subprocessor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can disable Google Analytics tracking via the cookie consent manager, but no broader opt-out mechanism for all third-party subprocessor sharing is explicitly described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states subprocessors are 'contractually bound to limited use' and that personal information is not disclosed without express written consent from the school, indicating vendor agreements are in place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may be updated periodically and that material changes will be communicated, but does not specifically commit to notifying users when subprocessors are added or changed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states Brighten does not use student personal information for behavioral advertising, and no in-platform ads are described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy expressly prohibits use of student data for targeted advertising purposes, and de-identified usage data may only be used for improving educational products as permitted under COPPA and FERPA.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google Analytics is used on the marketing website with a toggle opt-out, but it is unclear whether analytics cookies are fully blocked from firing before consent on the student-facing platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The legacy K-12 policy acknowledges use of cookies, flash cookies, web beacons, and persistent identifiers for usage tracking, but does not confirm these are limited to strictly functional purposes across all platform components.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out for Google Analytics tracking is available via the cookie consent manager, but a unified, clearly labeled opt-out for all data sharing with any analytics or service providers is not prominently documented.

r694.riskReason: The TV Teacher serves K-12 students including children under 13, requires account login for its streaming platform, and has no publicly discoverable Terms of Service or Privacy Policy on its website, leaving all COPPA, FERPA, and SOPIPA obligations entirely unaddressed.
r694.parentSummary: The TV Teacher (thetvteacher.com) is a handwriting instruction video platform for K-12 students that requires an email-based account login to access its streaming content. Despite serving young children, no Privacy Policy or Terms of Service document could be found on the website or through web search, meaning parents have no disclosed information about what data is collected, how it is protected, or whether it is shared or sold. Schools should not deploy this platform until the vendor provides compliant privacy documentation.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Privacy Policy or Terms of Service was found on thetvteacher.com, so no policy change notification process can be assessed.

complianceNotes.DCQ4: No Privacy Policy or Terms of Service exists to grant or describe any user data deletion rights.

complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure addresses third-party tracking for advertising purposes; no opt-out is offered or described.

r695.riskReason: Thesaurus.com is a general-audience consumer site that actively uses third-party advertising networks, web beacons, SDKs, and device identifiers to deliver targeted advertising, and while it claims COPPA compliance for school-based use, its default ad-targeting infrastructure poses significant data privacy risks for K-12 students who access the site outside a managed school district agreement.
r695.parentSummary: Thesaurus.com (operated by Dictionary.com, LLC) collects a broad range of data including IP addresses, device identifiers, search activity, and browsing behavior, and shares this data with third-party advertisers and analytics providers to deliver targeted advertising. The site claims COPPA compliance and states it does not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 outside of school-based programs, but the site is a general-audience consumer product with extensive third-party ad tracking active by default. Parents should be aware that students visiting the site on personal or school devices outside of a formal National Student Data Privacy Consortium district agreement may be subject to behavioral advertising tracking.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states it will revise the date at the top and provide additional notice for material changes, but no versioned revision history or advance notification timeline is specified.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy provides a detailed list of data categories collected, including identifiers, usage data, device data, and information provided directly by users.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes multiple collection methods including direct user input, cookies, web beacons, SDKs, device identifiers, and third-party sources.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly state that users own their data; the terms imply Dictionary.com controls and processes all collected data without granting user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion of personal information by emailing privacy@dictionary.com or via account settings; parental deletion rights for children's data are also addressed.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy references data retention in general terms and states data will be deleted if parental consent is not received, but does not specify precise retention periods for most data categories.

complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO in the privacy policy or terms of service; the platform does not appear to offer MFA for standard user accounts.

complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking for advertising is confirmed and active; opt-out is available via a footer link and browser controls, but tracking is on by default and opt-outs are cookie-dependent.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms use of cookies, web beacons, SDKs, and device identifiers by third parties for advertising tracking purposes, which goes beyond functional tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out mechanism is available via the 'Do Not Sell My Info' footer link and Consent Management Window, but the process is not straightforward and may not be fully effective across all devices and sessions.

r696.riskReason: ThinkIB.net (InThinking) collects minimal personal data, does not sell user data, and stores data on an encrypted GDPR-compliant server in Ireland, but the combined legal/privacy page lacks explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance statements, does not specify a minimum age for student users, uses Google Analytics without a full cookie disclosure, and provides only a general rather than comprehensive privacy policy.
r696.parentSummary: ThinkIB.net, operated by InThinking, collects only names and email addresses (and optionally country and teaching statistics) from users, stores all data on an encrypted server in Ireland under GDPR, and explicitly states it does not sell or share user information with third parties (except sharing workshop participant details with the IB Organization). Parents and students may request deletion of their data at any time via email or the contact form, which is a positive protection; however, the platform does not explicitly address COPPA or minimum age requirements, and uses Google Analytics for anonymous site usage tracking.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: InThinking states it will notify Account Managers by email of material changes to the Privacy Policy and Terms, but no revision history or changelog is publicly available on the legal page.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy states only names and emails are required, with optional country and teaching statistics, but does not comprehensively list all data types (e.g., IP addresses, session data from Google Analytics) that may be collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy notes data is collected via account registration and optionally provided by users, but does not specifically explain how Google Analytics collects anonymous usage data or what technical methods are used.

complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy explicitly states that teachers, students, or parents can request deletion of data at any time via email or the contact form, satisfying full deletion rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not specify any data retention period; there is no stated timeframe for how long user data (names, emails) is retained after account termination or subscription expiry.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states data is stored on a private server in Ireland that uses encryption and conforms to GDPR, but does not enumerate specific security measures such as access controls, audits, or breach notification procedures.

complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions session cookies and Google Analytics cookies in general terms and links to allaboutcookies.org for more information, but does not provide a full enumerated list of cookies with their names, types, duration, and purposes.

complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states IBO workshop participant details are shared with IBO but does not specify exactly what data is shared; Google Analytics data sharing is described only as anonymous usage data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy explicitly states data is not sold or shared with third parties except IBO for workshop participants, and users can request data deletion at any time, effectively providing opt-out through data removal.

complianceNotes.SHRQ5: InThinking states it will notify Account Managers of material policy changes, which would include changes to third-party data sharing arrangements, but no specific process for notifying about third-party changes is detailed.

complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no indication of any targeted advertising or behavioral advertising practices; Google Analytics data is described as anonymous and used only for site improvement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google Analytics is used for anonymous usage tracking and is identified as a third party, but no opt-out mechanism from Google Analytics tracking is provided directly on the site (only a link to Google's own privacy page).
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy mentions session cookies and Google Analytics but does not specifically address web beacons, pixel tags, or other tracking technologies; tracking appears limited to functional session cookies and anonymous analytics.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No data is shared with advertisers per the stated policy, but there is no explicit opt-out process described for the Google Analytics anonymous data collection that does occur.

r697.riskReason: Thinking Blocks Addition is hosted on Math Playground, a kidSAFE COPPA-certified site that explicitly does not collect personally identifiable information from children, uses only contextual (non-behavioral) advertising, and limits data collection to anonymous persistent identifiers for internal operations.
r697.parentSummary: Thinking Blocks Addition is part of Math Playground (mathplayground.com), which does not collect names, emails, or other personally identifiable information from children using the free site — only anonymous data like IP address, cookies for game progress, and device/browser info. The site is certified annually by kidSAFE for COPPA compliance and displays only contextual ads (not targeted to individual users) through a single COPPA-compliant advertising partner. Parents and teachers who optionally subscribe do provide an email and payment details, but no student data is required for classroom use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states changes will be posted and parents will be notified of material changes affecting children's data, but no revision history or changelog is publicly maintained.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and data security plan clearly enumerate all data collected: IP address, cookies, device/browser info for free users, and email/payment for subscribers — or explicitly states no PII is collected from children.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes collection methods including cookies, embedded scripts, and persistent identifiers, explaining how each operates during site use.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states that aggregated information is for internal use only, no PII is collected from children, and user-submitted content becomes the publisher's property only for voluntary submissions — children's data is not claimed by the company.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy explicitly grants parents the right to review and request deletion of any personal information collected about their child, and Math Playground states it does not collect such data from children.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The data security plan states retention is limited to what is necessary for site operation, but no specific retention period in days or months is defined for any data category.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The data security plan mentions reasonable administrative, technical, and organizational measures and use of third-party providers with encryption, but does not enumerate specific in-house security controls beyond general statements.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The data security plan references third-party providers (Google, Cloudflare, Netlify) that implement encryption, but Math Playground itself does not explicitly confirm end-to-end encryption or specify encryption standards for data in transit or at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account is required for students to use Thinking Blocks Addition on the free platform, eliminating password-related risks for the core K-12 use case.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No student account is required to use the free version of the platform, making MFA a non-issue for the primary K-12 use case.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies and embedded scripts with general descriptions of their purpose (game progress, interaction tracking), but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies with individual names and specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The data security plan names Google, Cloudflare, and Netlify as infrastructure providers and references a single advertising partner, but does not name the advertising partner explicitly in the privacy policy.

complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The data security plan states that third-party providers are required to support appropriate privacy and security practices and process data only as needed, but does not reference formal Data Processing Agreements or binding contractual obligations by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not address how or whether users will be notified if Math Playground changes its third-party service providers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Ads are displayed on the free version of the site to general visitors; however, a paid ad-free subscription is available, and all ads are COPPA-compliant contextual ads — not targeted to individual users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Math Playground explicitly prohibits behaviorally targeted advertising and uses only contextual ads not based on individual user browsing behavior, meeting the spirit of this requirement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The advertising partner is kidSAFE COPPA-certified and ad networks may use aggregated (non-personal) visit data only; no individual user tracking for ads is permitted, and an opt-out link is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Embedded scripts and cookies are described for functional and contextual ad delivery purposes, but the policy does not provide full clarity on whether all third-party ad network scripts constitute web beacons used for cross-site tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out link to the Network Advertising Initiative is provided for ad preferences, but the process is not clearly explained within the policy itself and relies on a third-party external tool.
