r698.riskReason: Thinkuknow.co.uk is operated by the UK National Crime Agency's CEOP Education team, does not collect personal data from child visitors, restricts professional accounts to verified adults over 18, and operates under GDPR/UK DPA 2018 with a named Data Protection Officer — presenting minimal risk for K-12 deployment as a curriculum resource tool.
r698.parentSummary: Thinkuknow.co.uk is a free online safety education platform run by the UK government's National Crime Agency (NCA-CEOP) for children aged 4–18. The child-facing website sections do not collect or store personal data about child visitors — only anonymous cookie/analytics data is gathered. Professional and educator accounts (restricted to adults 18+ working with children) do collect registration and usage data stored with third-party providers Ensono and Salesforce, and the site uses Google Analytics, Vimeo, and Facebook cookies which can be opted out of via the site's cookie settings.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy notice states it is reviewed regularly and will be updated before new processing begins, but no advance user notification mechanism or published revision history is documented.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy clearly states that no personal data is collected from child visitors, and specifically lists all data types collected from professional account holders including registration details, usage statistics, and downloaded resource records.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy explicitly describes how data is collected: via registration forms (stored by Ensono), via Salesforce for resource downloads, and via cookies (functional, analytical, and marketing) during website use.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The child-facing policy states no personal data is collected, and the professional policy makes clear data is used solely to administer accounts and improve services — implying user/public-interest ownership, not commercial ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy references GDPR rights including the right to erasure, and provides a DPO contact (DPO@nca.gov.uk) for requests, but does not provide a self-service deletion mechanism or clear step-by-step process for account deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated in the publicly available policy text — the policy does not articulate how long professional registration data or education session records are held before deletion.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states a general commitment to keeping information safe and references GDPR compliance, but does not list specific technical security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or audit logging.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site serves content over HTTPS (implied by standard NCA/GOV infrastructure), but the policy itself does not explicitly confirm end-to-end encryption of stored data or data in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No password strength requirements or enforcement policies are mentioned in the terms of use or privacy notice for professional account registration.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in any publicly available policy documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The cookie policy clearly lists all cookie categories (essential, analytical via Google Analytics, and marketing via Vimeo/Facebook) with their purposes, and provides opt-out instructions via cookie settings and browser controls.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy notice specifically names Ensono (website host) and Salesforce (CRM) as third-party data processors, and the cookie policy names Google, Vimeo, and Facebook as third-party cookie processors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Ensono is described as storing registration/login data and Salesforce as storing profile and resource download records, but the specific data fields shared with Google, Vimeo, and Facebook via cookies are not individually detailed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Analytical and marketing cookies from Google, Vimeo, and Facebook can be opted out of via the site's Cookie Settings tool, but no opt-out mechanism is described for data shared with Ensono or Salesforce as core service processors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy references Ensono's own privacy policy (ensono.com/privacy-policy) and implies contractual obligations via GDPR processor agreements, but does not explicitly confirm signed data processing agreements with all named third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy notice does not contain any provision notifying users when third-party data processors change or when new third parties are added to the processing chain.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The child-facing website sections do not display advertising; however, marketing cookies set by Facebook and Vimeo on the professionals section indicate potential ad-related tracking before and after login.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no confirmed targeting of users with personalized ads by the platform itself, but the presence of Facebook and Vimeo marketing cookies creates the possibility of third-party user profiling for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Facebook and Vimeo marketing cookies may track user behavior for advertising purposes on third-party platforms; users can opt out via the site's cookie settings, but the opt-out is not prominently enforced by default.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Marketing cookies from Vimeo and Facebook are acknowledged in the cookie policy as potentially tracking device activity, but the full scope of web beacon or pixel-based tracking methods is not explicitly detailed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Cookie settings on the site provide a mechanism to opt out of analytical and marketing cookies including Facebook and Vimeo, but the opt-out process is described only briefly without a clear, standalone user-facing guide.

dataCollected: Not specified — policy pages exist but render no readable content publicly
r699.riskReason: Although legal/policy URLs exist at thisissand.com, none of the policy pages render any substantive readable content, making it impossible to verify any K-12 data privacy protections, COPPA compliance, data retention practices, or third-party sharing disclosures for a platform widely used by students.
r699.parentSummary: Thisissand is a sand art creation and sharing platform accessible via web and mobile app, developed by Beige Elephant Oy. While the platform does have legal/privacy policy pages listed at thisissand.com/legal/, none of those pages returned readable policy content during this review, leaving data collection, sharing, and protection practices entirely unverifiable. Until substantive policy disclosures are publicly accessible and reviewed, schools and parents should exercise caution before allowing students to use this platform.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Policy change notification process cannot be assessed because no readable policy content was returned from any of the thisissand.com/legal/* pages.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: No data collection list is publicly accessible; all privacy policy pages at thisissand.com rendered only the homepage tagline with no substantive content.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The method of data collection is entirely undisclosed due to unreadable policy pages.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is not addressed in any accessible policy document on the platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No information on user data deletion rights or processes could be found in any accessible policy page.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or policy statement is accessible from any of the platform's legal pages.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No security measures or data protection practices are described in any accessible policy page.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption practices are not disclosed; the platform's legal pages do not render substantive content.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Account registration is optional per third-party descriptions, but there is no accessible policy stating password or SSO requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO support is found in any accessible policy or publicly reviewed documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookie usage policies are entirely absent from accessible policy pages, with no list of cookies or their purposes provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No third-party vendors or service providers are named in any accessible policy document for this platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: What data is shared with which third parties is undisclosed due to unreadable policy pages.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in any accessible policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor agreement or third-party contractual obligations are disclosed in any accessible policy page.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No notification process for changes to third-party relationships is described anywhere in accessible documentation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Third-party descriptions note the app does not display ads, but this is not confirmed in any accessible official policy or ToS document.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Targeted advertising practices are not addressed in any accessible policy, making compliance unverifiable.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking for advertising is not disclosed or disclaimed in any accessible policy document.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Web beacon or tracking technology usage is entirely undisclosed due to inaccessible policy content.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described in any accessible policy page.

dataCollected: Usage data (pages visited, links clicked, frequency/duration of activities)
Third-party login data (e.g., Google account info)
r700.riskReason: Thunkable uses third-party advertising partners and tracking technologies (including pixel tags, web beacons, and interest-based advertising) that may be active for school-age users, and it relies solely on schools to obtain COPPA consent for under-13 students without providing explicit FERPA-compliant data processing agreements or prohibitions on commercial data use for students.
r700.parentSummary: Thunkable collects personal information including name, email, IP address, device identifiers, and usage data from registered users, and shares this data with third-party analytics and advertising partners who may deliver personalized/interest-based ads. The platform sets the minimum age at 13 but allows schools to enroll younger students by delegating consent responsibilities to the school rather than obtaining direct parental consent. Parents of students under 13 should be aware that Thunkable does not explicitly prohibit commercial use of student data or targeted advertising in educational contexts, which presents meaningful COPPA and K-12 privacy compliance risks.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use state that changes will be communicated by posting updated terms and updating the 'Last Updated' date, but there is no advance notification process or revision history archive disclosed.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (IP address, device identifiers, usage data, email, location) but does not provide an exhaustive enumeration of all data types collected across all contexts.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically describes how data is collected — directly from users, automatically through technologies, and from third-party sources such as app stores and social login providers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Ownership of user data is not explicitly stated; the policy describes Thunkable's broad rights to collect, use, and share data, but does not affirmatively declare that users own their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The Terms of Use reference a delete option for user content and apps, and the privacy policy mentions honoring deletion requests per applicable law, but a clear, self-service full account and personal data deletion process is not explicitly described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not specify any data retention periods or provide a general retention timeline for personal data collected from users.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy references security goals such as detecting security incidents and fraud prevention but does not enumerate specific technical security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, firewalls).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption in transit or at rest is made anywhere in the publicly available privacy policy or terms of use.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy and terms of use make no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement of strong password policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration for school accounts is disclosed in the privacy policy or terms of use.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies, pixel tags/web beacons, and local storage technologies in general terms and categorizes them (security, performance, functionality, advertising), but does not provide a named list of all cookies with individual purposes and durations.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references broad categories of third parties (analytics providers, advertising partners, social media platforms, APIs/SDKs) but does not name specific third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by third-party category without specifying which data elements are shared with each specific third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy references opt-out of promotional emails and some state privacy rights, but there is no clearly described opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing specifically for students or school contexts.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy makes general references to third-party relationships but does not explicitly state that all third-party vendors are contractually bound to uphold equivalent data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not state that users will be notified if Thunkable's third-party sharing relationships change; it only states the policy itself may be updated with a date change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Terms of Use explicitly contemplate the use of Google AdMob for serving ads within user-built apps, and the privacy policy references advertising- or targeting-related tracking technologies on Thunkable's own services.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy confirms that third-party advertising partners use tracking technologies to deliver 'interest-based advertising' or 'personalized advertising' based on user activity, including for school-aged users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising partners are described as setting tracking tools (pixel tags, web beacons, cookies) to collect user activity data with no clear opt-out mechanism disclosed specific to the school or student context.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy explicitly references pixel tags/web beacons and advertising- or targeting-related tracking technologies used by third parties on Thunkable's services for ad delivery purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The policy references some state-level privacy rights (e.g., opt-out of sale under CCPA) but does not provide a clear, user-friendly opt-out process from advertiser data sharing for K-12 users or their guardians.

r701.riskReason: Tiller (tiller.com) is a personal finance platform explicitly prohibiting use by anyone under 18, requires linking real bank accounts and financial credentials, collects sensitive financial data shared with third-party aggregator Yodlee, and makes no mention of COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance — making it wholly inappropriate for K-12 educational deployment.
r701.parentSummary: Tiller (tiller.com) is a personal finance spreadsheet automation service, not a K-12 EdTech platform; its own privacy policy explicitly states that visitors under 18 are not permitted to use the service or submit personal information. The platform collects sensitive financial data including bank account transactions and financial credentials through a third-party aggregator (Yodlee), and while it states it does not sell personal data, it shares data with analytics and service providers. There are no COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA disclosures, no student data protections, and no parental consent mechanisms — this platform should not be used in any K-12 school context.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states material changes will be notified via email or a website notice and the last-revised date is shown, but no formal revision history or advance notice period is specified.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, transaction data, log files, IP address, clickstream) but does not provide a fully exhaustive enumeration of every data type collected across all service components.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically describes how data is collected — directly from users, via Yodlee for bank transactions, automatically via log files and cookies, and through third-party analytics — meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Tiller explicitly states users exclusively own and control their financial data stored in their own Google Sheets or Excel spreadsheets, and the company does not lock data into proprietary formats.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can close their account and transaction data will be deleted from Tiller's servers, but certain information (email address, communications) is retained for analytical and legal purposes after account closure, limiting full deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state a specific data retention period; it only notes some data may be retained after account closure for analytical or legal reasons without specifying any timeframe.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'appropriate security measures (including physical, electronic and procedural measures)' but does not enumerate specific security controls or frameworks in detail.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states transaction data is transmitted with TLS and stored with 256-bit AES encryption, meeting the encryption requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service instruct users to 'keep your password confidential' but do not enforce or specify any password strength or complexity requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mentioned in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy; the help center mentions Google's optional MFA as a recommendation but Tiller does not enforce or natively offer it.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies and scripts are used for authentication, settings, and measuring advertising effectiveness, and that third-party analytics providers also use cookies, but does not provide a full itemized list of cookies with individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy names Yodlee as a data-sharing partner and references Google and analytics providers generally, but does not provide a complete named list of all third-party service providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states data is shared with Yodlee for bank transaction collection and with payment processors, but does not specify exactly which data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The privacy policy provides no mechanism for users to opt out of third-party data sharing with Yodlee or analytics providers; use of the service implicitly requires data sharing with these third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states service providers 'may have access to personal information needed to perform their functions' but does not include explicit contractual language requiring third parties to adhere to equivalent data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states material changes to how user data is treated will be communicated, but does not specifically address notification when new third-party data-sharing relationships are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Tiller explicitly states it does not run ads and is funded solely by subscriptions, meeting the requirement that no ads are displayed to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy and security page explicitly state Tiller never sells financial data to advertisers or uses it for targeted advertising, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: While Tiller itself does not use data for advertising, the policy acknowledges third-party analytics providers (unnamed) use cookies and tracking technologies on its site, with no clear opt-out mechanism described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy mentions cookies and scripts are used by Tiller and third-party analytics providers, and social media widgets may set cookies and collect IP addresses, but does not clarify whether any of this constitutes ad-related tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear process is described for users to opt out of data being shared with or tracked by third-party analytics or social media widget providers; the only guidance is browser-level cookie controls.

dataCollected: Anonymous usage data (exercises done, games played, time spent)
r702.riskReason: Timestables.com is operated by a Netherlands-based company (BVK Productions B.V.) with no explicit COPPA compliance statement, no Terms of Service document, no minimum age requirement stated, and displays Google AdSense ads (even if tagged as child-directed), creating moderate risk for U.S. K-12 deployment without additional school-level controls.
r702.parentSummary: Timestables.com collects minimal personal data — only a nickname and password if an account is created, plus anonymous usage data and standard technical information like IP address and browser type for all users. The site displays ads via Google AdSense but states these are tagged as child-directed to prevent behavioral tracking, and no personalized advertising cookies are used. Account data is retained for 2 years and is deleted immediately upon account deletion, but there is no formal Terms of Service document and no explicit COPPA compliance declaration, which may be a concern for U.S. school use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy statement notes it is subject to change and shows a revision date of November 2023, but does not describe an advance notification process for users when changes are made.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy clearly lists all data collected: IP address, browser type, device/system, pages visited, cookies, and for account holders — nickname, password, medals, diplomas, and exercise scores.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states how data is collected — via account creation, contact forms, cookies, and automatic technical logging during site use.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state who owns the data; it describes user rights (access, deletion, portability) under a GDPR-style framework but makes no clear declaration of user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users have the right to request deletion of personal data, and the policy states that deleting an account immediately wipes all accompanying data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states account data is saved for 2 years, and general data is retained as long as necessary for stated purposes or legal obligations — a specific retention period is provided.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy lists specific security measures including encryption, network security, backups, availability control, breach response plan, physical security, virtual access control, data access control, and entry control.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is listed as one of the security measures, but no further detail is provided on the type or scope of encryption (e.g., in-transit vs. at-rest); the site does use HTTPS.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Account creation requires only a nickname and password with no mention of password strength requirements, complexity enforcement, or SSO; no strong password policy is documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO is made anywhere in the privacy policy or on the site; accounts use only nickname and password.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The site has a dedicated cookie statement page listing two specific cookie types — functional cookies and anonymized Google Analytics cookies — with no personalized advertising cookies permitted.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references Google AdSense and Google Analytics as third-party services, but does not provide a comprehensive named list of all third-party data processors used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy notes Google Analytics receives anonymized data and Google AdSense serves child-directed ads, but does not provide a detailed breakdown of exactly what data each third party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: There is no clear opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing described; cookie consent is mentioned but a full opt-out process for third-party services is not documented.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy does not state that third-party vendors are contractually bound to follow a data protection agreement or vendor agreement with Timestables.com.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it is subject to change but does not commit to notifying users when third-party data sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The site displays Google AdSense ads to support free access, so ads are present; however, the site states ads are designed to be child-directed and non-behavioral.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Timestables.com explicitly states ads are specially designed to prevent behavioral tracking and the site is tagged with Google as child-directed, prohibiting interest-based targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The site states it does not use or allow personalized advertising cookies, and Google AdSense is configured with child-directed treatment to prevent behavioral tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie statement confirms only functional cookies and anonymized Google Analytics cookies are used; no tracking beacons or cookies for ad targeting are permitted.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Cookie consent is required before cookies are placed, but no explicit opt-out mechanism specifically for data sharing with advertisers is described in the policy.

dataCollected: Usage data (games played, frequency of visits)
r703.riskReason: TinyTap uses third-party remarketing and behavioral advertising cookies, shares data with Google and Facebook for targeted ads, collects special categories of data from children under 13, and the policy lacks a specific data retention period or explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance declarations.
r703.parentSummary: TinyTap collects personal information including your child's name, birth date, game usage activity, and device data, and uses it for product improvement, marketing, and to display personalized advertisements. Data is shared with third-party advertising and analytics platforms including Google and Facebook for remarketing purposes, meaning your child's behavior on TinyTap may be used to target ads on other websites. While parental consent is required before children use the platform and some deletion rights are offered via email request, the policies are outdated, vague on retention timelines, and do not explicitly claim COPPA or FERPA compliance.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The children's privacy policy states changes will be posted on the website and app, but there is no advance notification process or maintained revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data types (name, birth date, usage data, device info, special categories) but mentions 'special categories of data' without specifying what they are.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that data is collected when users register and automatically through usage, but does not fully detail all collection methods for each data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Ownership of user data is not explicitly stated; the policy focuses on how data is used rather than affirming user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion via email, and account cancellation is available through the website, app, or email, but the policy reserves the right to retain some data even after deletion requests.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is kept 'as long as we need it for the purposes described,' which is a vague general statement without a specific retention period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states TinyTap follows 'generally accepted industry standards' to protect personal information but does not list specific security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The children's policy does not explicitly mention encryption, though the FindIt-specific policy references encrypted channels; the main platform policy lacks encryption detail.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Use and Privacy Policy make no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: There is no mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration in the main platform policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and web beacons and lists general categories of use (personalization, advertising), but does not provide a comprehensive list of all specific cookies and their individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Google Analytics, Google AdWords, and Facebook as third-party partners, but uses broad language ('businesses we work with') without a complete named list of all third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared with third parties generally rather than specifying exactly what data is shared with each named third party (e.g., Google vs. Facebook).
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of Google and Facebook remarketing through those platforms' settings, and users can email TinyTap to stop marketing use, but no simple in-platform opt-out mechanism is described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Terms of Use state agreements are in place with international partners requiring equivalent privacy protections, but there is no explicit contractual obligation stated for all third-party advertisers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes will be posted on the website and app, but does not specifically commit to notifying users when third-party partners change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: TinyTap explicitly uses remarketing to advertise on third-party websites and serves personalized ads to users based on past visits, including to children.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms that cookies and third-party vendors are used to serve ads based on past visits and behavioral data, constituting confirmed behavioral targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Opt-out links are provided for Google and Facebook ad tracking, but third-party tracking is active by default and opt-out requires navigating to external platforms.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy explicitly confirms the use of web beacons (pixel tags) that work with cookies to identify users and user behavior, and states these may be shared with third parties for advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can email TinyTap to opt out of personalized advertisements, and external opt-out pages for Google and Facebook are referenced, but no clear in-platform opt-out process is described.

dataCollected: Anonymous browser type and software/hardware details
Usage and activity data (pages visited, content accessed)
dataSharedWith: Website development and maintenance service providers
Third-party video platforms (YouTube, Vimeo) via embedded players
Third-party advertising networks (via embedded video platforms)
r704.riskReason: TKSST explicitly bars children under 13 from registering and collects minimal personal data, but third-party video platforms (YouTube/Vimeo) embedded on the site use cookies, web beacons, and interest-based ad targeting that TKSST acknowledges it cannot control, posing residual tracking risk for student users despite 'no-cookie' embed mitigations.
r704.parentSummary: TKSST (The Kid Should See This) is a free, curated educational video site that does not require account creation for browsing and explicitly prohibits children under 13 from registering. The site collects minimal personal data—primarily email addresses for newsletter opt-ins by adults—and states it does not collect IP addresses or device identifiers. However, third-party video platforms embedded on the site (such as YouTube) may use cookies and web beacons for interest-based advertising, and TKSST acknowledges it has limited control over these external trackers, though it uses 'no-cookie' YouTube embeds as a partial mitigation.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states changes are communicated only by revising the date at the top of the policy, with no advance notification mechanism or revision history archive described.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy clearly states IP addresses, device identifiers, and geolocation are not collected, and describes browser/usage analytics and cookies, but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of all data types collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected—directly from users (e.g., email for newsletters), automatically via cookies and web beacons, and passively through third-party embedded video platforms.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly address data ownership; it describes use and sharing of data by TKSST and third parties without clearly stating that users own their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy allows newsletter opt-out and states that data from children under 13 will be deleted upon discovery, but does not describe a general self-service data deletion process for adult users or members.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not specify any data retention period or general retention statement for user data collected through the site or membership accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references protecting information but does not enumerate specific technical or organizational security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, audits).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS (indicated by the domain), but the privacy policy does not explicitly mention encryption of data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account is required for basic site use; optional membership accounts are managed through third-party payment/membership platforms that enforce their own credential standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No student account is required for core platform use; optional adult membership accounts rely on third-party platforms, making MFA/SSO requirements moot for the primary educational use case.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges use of cookies and web beacons generally, but does not provide a detailed table or list of specific cookies, their names, purposes, and durations.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references sharing with 'entities that help manage and provide the Services' (development, email distribution, analytics) but does not name specific third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by category of service provider without specifying which data types are shared with each specific third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing emails via unsubscribe links, and the NAI and DAA opt-out pages are referenced for third-party ad targeting; no opt-in to most data sharing is required since the site requires no registration.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states data is shared with service providers 'only to the extent that these entities need the information to perform their services,' implying contractual limits, but no explicit vendor agreement or data processing agreement requirement is stated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not describe any process for notifying users when third-party service providers change or new data-sharing relationships are established.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The site aims to be ad-free for members and uses member support to offset ad costs, but non-member browsing may encounter ads served through embedded third-party video platforms such as YouTube.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: TKSST itself does not engage in targeted advertising, but acknowledges that embedded video platforms (YouTube) may deliver interest-based ads and that TKSST has no control over this.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: TKSST uses 'no-cookie' YouTube embeds to minimize third-party tracking, and references NAI and DAA opt-out pages, but cannot fully prevent third-party tracking from embedded video platforms.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy discloses use of cookies, web beacons, and pixel tags for user activity tracking, and acknowledges third-party platforms may use similar technologies, but does not clarify which are strictly functional versus advertising-related.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The policy references both the NAI consumer opt-out page and the DAA consumer opt-out page, providing clear pathways for users to opt out of interest-based advertising from participating third parties.

r705.minAge: Not specified (directed to institutions; COPPA compliance delegated to subscribing schools)
r705.riskReason: Infobase explicitly acknowledges FERPA school-official status, prohibits sale of student data, limits data collection to educational purposes, uses SSL encryption, and grants parents deletion rights under COPPA.
r705.parentSummary: Today's Science, published by Infobase (formerly Facts on File), collects standard account and usage data such as names, email addresses, IP addresses, and browsing activity to operate the service and improve the platform. Infobase explicitly states it does not sell student data, does not use student data for commercial purposes, and restricts data sharing to internal technical agents and legal obligations. The platform acknowledges FERPA obligations as a school official and complies with COPPA by allowing parents to review and delete their child's data, though its primary privacy policy was last updated in May 2022, which may not reflect the most current regulatory requirements.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Infobase reserves the right to update its policy at any time but does not explicitly commit to advance notification or maintain a public revision history; users are expected to check the policy periodically.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy describes categories of data collected (name, email, IP, usage data) but uses open-ended language ('including but not limited to') rather than providing a fully exhaustive enumeration.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states that data is collected when users access online services and during routine business operations, but does not specifically detail every collection mechanism (e.g., cookies, server logs, forms) in a structured way.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy clearly states that student data is not used for commercial purposes and that Infobase acts as a data processor/school official under FERPA, implying user and institutional ownership of education records.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents can direct Infobase to delete their child's personal information, and registered users can update or delete account information, satisfying full deletion rights under COPPA and FERPA.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as necessary to fulfill purposes and comply with legal obligations, but does not specify a concrete minimum or maximum retention period in days or years.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Infobase references 'reasonable technical, physical, and administrative safeguards' and continual network monitoring, but does not enumerate specific security frameworks (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001) or controls by name.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) encryption is used to protect data during transmission, meeting the encryption requirement.

r710.riskReason: PRC-Saltillo experienced a significant data breach in August 2024 that exposed names, addresses, dates of birth, and medical information (including of minors), and while the privacy policy includes student-specific protections and explicitly states student data is not disclosed to third parties, the policy lacks explicit COPPA compliance language, specific encryption standards, clear data retention periods, and the ToU age gate of 18+ is inconsistent with the reality that the product is widely used with K-12 students.
r710.parentSummary: TouchChat, made by PRC-Saltillo, is an AAC communication app used by students with speech and language challenges; it collects account information, device data, usage telemetry, and optionally health-related information, which is used to provide and improve the service but not sold or used for targeted advertising. The privacy policy includes a dedicated school and student section acknowledging FERPA obligations and states that student data is not disclosed to third parties, and parents or schools can request inspection, amendment, or deletion of student information by contacting the privacy officer. However, PRC-Saltillo suffered a cyberattack in August 2024 that exposed sensitive personal data including that of minors, and the policy lacks explicit COPPA compliance statements and specific technical security details such as encryption standards, which schools should carefully evaluate before deployment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it 'may be updated' and will update the Effective Date each time, but does not commit to advance notification before changes take effect, and no version/revision history is publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy enumerates specific categories of data collected including Identity, Contact, Medical, Financial, Profile, Technical, and Marketing data, as well as biometric data where applicable.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes collection via direct interactions (forms, correspondence), automated technologies (cookies, web beacons, pixels, APIs, SDKs, server logs), and interactive features (live chat).
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; PRC-Saltillo asserts IP ownership over the site and platform, making data ownership ambiguous for user-generated content.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy provides a mechanism for parents/students to request deletion of student data through their Educational Authority (school), and a privacy officer contact is provided for direct requests.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained 'no longer than is necessary' and lists factors considered for retention periods, but does not specify any concrete timeframes (e.g., 90 days, 1 year), making this vague.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references physical, technical, and procedural safeguards, a Privacy Officer and Security Officer, and post-breach commitments to additional cybersecurity measures, but does not enumerate specific technical controls in the main policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: SSL/DigiCert certificates are mentioned for the website storefront in older policy documents, and MFA and encryption are cited in breach communications, but the current main privacy policy does not explicitly state encryption standards for data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform uses SSO via auth.prc-saltillo.com (OAuth/OpenID Connect), which typically enforces password policies at the identity provider level, but no explicit password strength requirements are stated in the policy or ToU.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: PRC-Saltillo's breach response communications reference multi-factor authentication as a security measure already in place, suggesting MFA is used internally, but it is not explicitly offered to end users as a documented account security option.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A dedicated Cookie Policy exists at prc-saltillo.com/cookie-policy that lists each cookie category (necessary, analytics), names specific vendors (Google Analytics, Stripe, YouTube), and explains their purpose, though it notes both necessary and analytics cookies are enabled by default.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Cookie Policy names Google Analytics, YouTube, and Stripe as specific third parties, but the main privacy policy only broadly references 'vendors' and 'service providers' for other data processing without naming them.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Cookie Policy specifies what each named cookie vendor receives, but the main privacy policy does not detail what specific data fields are shared with each service provider category beyond grouping them broadly.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can set browsers to block cookies per the Cookie Policy, and a privacy officer contact exists for data requests, but there is no self-service opt-out dashboard or granular opt-out mechanism described for third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that student information is not disclosed to third parties and references contractual obligations with Educational Authorities, but does not explicitly state that all third-party vendors are bound by equivalent data protection agreements.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it 'may be updated' without committing to user notification when third-party vendor relationships change, so users may not be proactively informed of changes to third-party sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: PRC-Saltillo explicitly states it does not use Google Analytics remarketing or advertising features and does not sell information through analytics; no ads are displayed within the TouchChat app itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states PRC-Saltillo 'does not sell or share personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising,' and no targeted advertising is conducted using student or user data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google Analytics is used for site analytics only with advertising features disabled, and PRC-Saltillo states it does not sell or share data through this tool; no third-party advertising trackers are described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy and Cookie Policy acknowledge use of web beacons, pixels, SDKs, and server logs for analytics, and while advertising use is disclaimed, the presence of these tracking technologies without a full listing of all third-party SDK/pixel vendors warrants a Partially rating.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can contact the privacy officer at privacy@prc-saltillo.com or call 1-800-262-1984 to exercise data rights including opt-out of any applicable sharing, and state-specific rights (e.g., California CCPA) are acknowledged with a clear contact process.

r712.riskReason: Toy Theater explicitly states it uses Google AdSense and third-party cookies on a child-directed platform, and the Terms of Service grant Toy Theater a broad, perpetual, irrevocable license over any user-submitted content, creating notable risks despite the platform's COPPA-aligned data minimization posture.
r712.parentSummary: Toy Theater does not collect personal information from children under 13 and states it uses only contextual (non-targeted) advertising via Google AdSense. However, the platform does use third-party cookies from Google Analytics and AdSense, and automatically collects technical data like IP addresses and device identifiers from all users, including children. Parents should also be aware that if children submit any creative content, the Terms of Service grant Toy Theater a sweeping, royalty-free, perpetual license to use that content for any commercial purpose.

r713.riskReason: Trackwrestling, operated under FloSports, is actively used by K-12 wrestlers (including middle schoolers) and collects extensive personal and athletic data—including athlete name, school, weight, and competition results—that is explicitly shared with and sold to advertising networks, marketing partners, and data analytics providers, with no stated COPPA or FERPA compliance and no child-specific data protections in the governing privacy policy.
r713.parentSummary: Trackwrestling collects a wide range of personal and athletic data from users—including names, contact information, payment data, device identifiers, geolocation, and detailed athlete statistics like weight class, school, and competition results—which are shared with and in some cases sold to advertising networks, marketing partners, and analytics providers. The platform is owned by FloSports, whose privacy policy governs Trackwrestling and explicitly acknowledges selling identifiers and internet activity data to advertising networks; it does not disclaim COPPA or FERPA compliance, and contains no child-specific protections despite the platform being widely used by K-12 student-athletes. Parents should be aware that their child's athletic profile data (name, school, graduation year, competition results) may be provided or sold to third-party business partners.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The FloSports Terms of Service states it will notify users of material changes by posting a notice and provides 30 days before changes take effect, but there is no publicly maintained revision history or changelog.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The FloSports privacy policy (which governs Trackwrestling) provides a broad but reasonably detailed list of data categories collected, including identifiers, contact info, payment data, device data, geolocation, demographic info, and athletic performance data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected directly from users, via third-party platforms linked at registration, analytics tools, social networks, and advertising networks, but does not specifically detail collection methods for the Trackwrestling event-registration and athlete-profile context.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The EULA grants FloSports a broad, perpetual, worldwide license to reproduce, distribute, and use submitted data, and explicitly permits providing or selling Statistical Data (including athlete name, school, and results) to business partners—indicating the company effectively claims broad rights over user-submitted data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy references a Data Subject Access Request process and a right to deletion in some circumstances, but the EULA's perpetual license and the public nature of athlete profiles suggest significant limitations on full deletion rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state a specific data retention period for athlete profiles or event data; no general retention statement or timeframe is provided for the core Trackwrestling data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy makes only a general statement about protecting personal information; no specific technical or administrative security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, audits) are described.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS, indicating transport-layer encryption, but the privacy policy does not mention encryption of stored data or describe any encryption practices.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of strong password requirements or enforcement is made in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy for Trackwrestling user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO integration is made in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The platform includes a cookie preference center and a 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' link, and categories of cookies (functional, analytics, advertising) are described generally, but specific third-party cookie vendors are not individually named.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy mentions broad categories of third parties (advertising networks, analytics providers, social networks, business partners, rights holders) but does not individually name specific third-party vendors used on Trackwrestling.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data disclosed by category (identifiers, demographics, payment, geolocation, etc.) and states all categories are disclosed to business partners and service providers, but does not map specific data elements to specific third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: A 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' opt-out link is present in the site footer, and device-level opt-out for ad personalization is described, but the opt-out is a California-focused CCPA mechanism and does not offer a universal or easily accessible opt-out for non-California users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy references requiring service providers to protect data in general terms but does not describe specific contractual obligations imposed on third-party advertising partners receiving Trackwrestling athlete data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy states FloSports may update the policy at any time; there is no specific commitment to notify users when new third-party data-sharing relationships are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Trackwrestling Services page explicitly promotes advertising opportunities on the platform, stating ads are shown to users and can be filtered to relevant audiences—confirming ads are displayed to authenticated users including student-athletes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The FloSports privacy policy confirms sharing personal data with third parties for interest-based advertising, and the Trackwrestling services page states ads 'can be filtered down to relevant audiences based on who they are and what they're browsing,' confirming targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising partners may use their own cookies and tracking technologies to build interest profiles and serve targeted ads; FloSports explicitly does not alter behavior in response to Do Not Track signals, indicating no effective restriction on third-party tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy and EULA acknowledge use of cookies, web beacons, pixels, advertising identifiers, and device IDs for tracking; these are used for advertising purposes including by third-party partners.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: A 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' opt-out is present in the footer as a California CCPA right, but a clear, universal opt-out process for all users from data sharing with advertisers is not prominently described or easily accessible.

r714.minAge: Under 13 with parental consent (school/customer consent required)
dataCollected: Temporary voice input (Hotel Front Desk feature)
dataSharedWith: Successor entities in mergers or acquisitions
r714.riskReason: Transfr expressly addresses COPPA and FERPA compliance and limits student data to educational purposes, but third-party analytics providers may receive cookie/tracking data and specific third-party identities are not named, creating partial transparency gaps.
r714.parentSummary: Transfr collects student names, usernames, email addresses, usage data, personal interests, and in some features temporary voice input; for students under 13, consent must be obtained by the school before any data is collected or used. The platform states it limits student data to educational purposes only and does not sell student data, and it expressly commits to FERPA and COPPA compliance. However, third-party analytics providers may receive cookie and tracking data, and the policy does not name these third parties specifically, which is a notable transparency concern for parents and administrators.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use state that material changes will be notified to users, but no revision history or changelog is publicly maintained on the policy pages.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy specifically lists categories of data collected including names, usernames, email addresses, usage details, IP addresses, metadata, interests, voice input, and cookie data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly states data is collected directly from users via forms, automatically via cookies and tracking technologies, and from third parties such as customers and business partners.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users or educational institutions own their data; ownership terms are ambiguous and not clearly defined in either the ToS or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy states Transfr will promptly respond to requests from educational institutions to delete student data, but individual student or parent deletion requests are not explicitly addressed with a clear process.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as necessary to fulfill its purposes and satisfy legal requirements, but no specific retention periods (e.g., number of days) are given.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy references safeguards and security practices but does not list specific technical security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or audit procedures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of encryption (e.g., TLS, AES) is made in the privacy policy or terms; HTTPS is implied by the website but not stated as a formal security measure.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Neither the Terms of Use nor the Privacy Policy mention password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration options is present in the publicly available Terms of Use or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and tracking technologies generally, including distinguishing functional from activity-tracking cookies, but does not provide a full itemized cookie list with names and specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references sharing with 'online analytics providers' and 'business partners' but does not name any specific third-party vendors by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data shared with third parties broadly and does not specify which data types are shared with each individual third-party category.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users may contact privacy@transfrvr.com to opt out of marketing communications, and CCPA opt-out rights are referenced, but a clear and simple opt-out mechanism for all third-party sharing is not fully described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not explicitly state that third-party analytics or data partners are contractually required to follow Transfr's data protection standards, only that student data is used for educational purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not state that users or schools will be notified if third-party sharing relationships change; updates to the policy itself are announced for material changes only.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy states student data is collected only for educational purposes and not for commercial use, and there is no indication that ads are displayed within the student-facing platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Transfr explicitly states that student personal information is used only for the benefit of the customer and students and for no other commercial purpose, indicating no targeted advertising of students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party analytics providers may place cookies or tracking tools on the site per the CCPA disclosure, which could constitute limited third-party tracking, though student-specific tracking for ads is disclaimed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy acknowledges use of cookies and tracking technologies including for analytics purposes but does not fully itemize or distinguish which tracking methods are used strictly for functionality versus analytics.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out email address (privacy@transfrvr.com) is provided and CCPA opt-out rights are mentioned, but the process for opting out of data sharing with analytics providers is not clearly described step-by-step.

dataCollected: Behavioral and interaction data (mouse movements, interaction timing)
dataSharedWith: Subprocessors (listed separately on Trello Subprocessors Board)
r715.riskReason: Trello is a general-purpose productivity platform not designed for K-12 use; it collects extensive personal data, employs targeted advertising cookies, shares data with third-party advertisers, has no stated COPPA or FERPA compliance, exposes user profile information publicly by default, and suffered a significant 2024 API data scraping incident affecting over 15 million users.
r715.parentSummary: Trello (owned by Atlassian) collects a wide range of personal data including names, email addresses, profile photos, device information, IP addresses, and all board/card content created by users, and shares this data with advertising partners, analytics providers, and third-party Power-Up developers. The platform uses targeting and advertising cookies by default, and while an opt-out mechanism exists via 'Manage Preferences,' Trello does not make any COPPA- or FERPA-specific commitments and is not designed as a children's or student-focused tool. Public profile information such as full name, username, and avatar are visible to anyone on the internet unless manually changed, which poses meaningful privacy risks for K-12 students.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Atlassian notifies users of privacy policy changes and publishes update summaries, but the ToS states users may be bound by changes without explicit advance notification for free plan users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Atlassian Privacy Policy comprehensively lists categories of data collected including account info, device data, usage data, content, cookies, and behavioral/interaction data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly describes how data is collected — directly from users, automatically through service use, from third-party platforms, and via cookies and tracking technologies.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: User-generated content is treated as customer data, but Atlassian's broad license to use, store, and process data makes ownership ambiguous; the policy does not explicitly affirm that users own their data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can deactivate accounts and request deletion, but the policy notes some data may be retained for legal or recordkeeping obligations, and community/public posts may persist after account closure.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states retention depends on data type, purpose, and legal requirements but does not specify concrete retention periods for most data categories, making this vague for K-12 compliance purposes.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Atlassian publishes detailed security policies referencing encryption, cryptographic mechanisms, access controls, incident response, and AWS-hosted infrastructure with multiple availability zones.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Atlassian deploys AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit, confirmed via published security standards and independent reports.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Atlassian recommends strong passwords and supports SSO, but strong password enforcement is not explicitly mandated by default for all Trello free-tier users.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Two-factor authentication is available and encouraged but is optional rather than enforced; SSO is available on paid/enterprise plans only.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Atlassian maintains a detailed Cookies and Tracking Notice that categorizes cookies by type (strictly necessary, functional, performance, targeting/advertising, social media) and describes opt-out mechanisms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references broad categories of third parties (advertising partners, analytics providers, subprocessors, social media) but does not name each specific third-party company in the main policy; a separate Subprocessors list exists.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with third parties is described in grouped or categorical terms rather than specifying exactly which data elements are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: A 'Manage Preferences' opt-out tool exists for third-party advertising data sharing, but it is not prominently surfaced and the opt-out is limited in scope and does not cover all sharing categories.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Atlassian's GDPR documentation confirms subprocessors are contractually required to meet applicable data management, security, and privacy standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy indicates Atlassian may update third-party arrangements but does not commit to proactive user notification when specific third-party subprocessors or advertising partners change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Atlassian uses targeting/advertising cookies and presents advertising relevant to user interests, meaning behavioral ads can be displayed to users including those on the free Trello tier.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The Cookies and Tracking Notice explicitly confirms targeting cookies collect browsing habits to serve advertising relevant to user interests, constituting confirmed user-level targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising tracking is active by default, though users can access cookie preference settings to opt out; the opt-out process is not straightforward for a typical K-12 user.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Atlassian explicitly confirms use of web beacons/tracking pixels by itself and third-party advertising partners for tracking and ad targeting purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out from advertising data sharing is available via Atlassian Account > Privacy > cookie preferences, but the process is not clearly documented in plain language and may not be accessible to students or parents without effort.

dataSharedWith: Successor entities in case of merger or acquisition
r716.riskReason: Trinket explicitly commits to never selling user data and acknowledges COPPA, but delegates parental consent to schools/teachers rather than obtaining it directly, third-party analytics trackers are used with limited disclosure, and no specific data retention period or MFA is documented.
r716.parentSummary: Trinket collects basic account information (name and email), usage/log data, and cookies to operate its browser-based coding platform; it explicitly states it will never sell user data to third parties and does not collect sensitive information such as grades or health data. For students under 13, Trinket relies on the school or teacher to obtain parental consent rather than collecting it directly, which means parents should confirm their school has provided appropriate disclosures. Third-party analytics providers may track usage behavior via cookies and web beacons, and Trinket's own privacy policy does not govern those third-party tracking practices.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The TOS states changes are effective two weeks after posting and the revised date is shown at the top, but there is no advance notification to users via email or a maintained revision history log.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists major data categories (name, email, log data, cookies, IP address, payment info) but does not provide an exhaustive enumeration of all data fields collected, particularly around third-party analytics data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy clearly describes multiple collection methods including direct user input, automatic device/log collection, cookies, web beacons, and third-party analytics services.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Trinket explicitly states it will never sell user data and describes collecting only what is necessary to provide the service, implying user ownership; the policy does not claim company ownership of personal data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The TOS states that accounts for under-13 users discovered without parental consent will be deleted, and users can contact the company, but there is no clearly documented self-service deletion workflow for all users.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state any specific data retention period or general retention policy, making it impossible for users to know how long their data is held.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy states only that Trinket 'takes reasonable measures' to protect personal information, without listing any specific security controls, protocols, or certifications.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The platform uses HTTPS (implied by standard web practice and Data Privacy Framework adherence), but the privacy policy does not explicitly state that data is encrypted in transit or at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The TOS instructs users to maintain password security but does not state that strong passwords are enforced by the platform; no-login use is available for basic features.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in the privacy policy or TOS.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies and web beacons and notes users can reject cookies via browser settings, but does not provide a categorized cookie list with specific purposes for each cookie.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references 'third-party analytics providers' and 'payment processors' as categories but does not name any specific third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy policy groups data sharing by purpose category (analytics, payment processing, legal) without specifying which exact data fields are shared with each type of third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of direct marketing data sharing by emailing hello@trinket.io, but no opt-out mechanism is provided for third-party analytics tracking beyond browser-level cookie rejection.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Data Privacy Framework statement commits that Trinket will only transfer data to third parties that provide satisfactory assurances of protection, but this commitment applies only to EU/UK/Swiss transfers, not all third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy states it may change at any time and encourages users to check periodically, but there is no commitment to notify users specifically when third-party sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy states Trinket will not share information with third parties for direct marketing purposes, but third-party analytics providers are permitted and their tracking practices are not fully governed by Trinket's policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Trinket explicitly prohibits sharing data for direct marketing, but third-party analytics providers may use collected behavioral data (pages viewed, clicks, time on page) for their own purposes outside Trinket's control.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party analytics providers are acknowledged to use cookies and web beacons to track cross-site behavior, but Trinket states its policy does not apply to those third-party tracking technologies, limiting user recourse.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy discloses use of cookies and web beacons including by third parties, but does not clarify whether any of this tracking is used for advertising purposes or provide a clear functional-only guarantee.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can email hello@trinket.io to opt out of direct marketing data sharing, but there is no documented opt-out specifically for third-party analytics or behavioral tracking data sharing.

dataCollected: Name (if voluntarily provided, e.g. newsletter signup)
Email address (in hashed form, shared with identity partners)
dataSharedWith: Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids (CTFK) for Youth Engagement Alliance programming

Third parties for legal compliance or fraud prevention
r717.riskReason: The policy discloses sharing of hashed email and IP addresses with identity partners and advertising companies for interest-based and targeted advertising, does not specify a minimum age, does not address COPPA or FERPA compliance, and the TOS and privacy policy are combined into one outdated page (dated 2019) that lacks key K-12 student data protections.
r717.parentSummary: Truth Initiative collects technical data (IP address, browser, device info) automatically and personal data (name, email, address) only if voluntarily submitted. The platform shares hashed user identifiers with advertising identity partners such as LiveRamp and Adobe Marketing Cloud to enable cross-device and interest-based advertising, with an opt-out available at liveramp.com. There is no stated minimum age, no explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance language, and no dedicated student data protection policy, raising significant concerns for K-12 school use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states that if Truth Initiative decides to use data for a new unanticipated use, it will post the change prominently on the policy page and provide an opt-out, but there is no version history, revision date tracking, or advance email notification process described.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several categories of data collected (IP address, domain, browser, OS, referral source, voluntarily submitted name/email/address), but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list covering all possible data types such as mobile number or behavioral/ad-targeting data collected via identity partners.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes how data is collected (automatically via server logs, voluntarily via forms, and via cookies), but lacks specificity on some collection methods such as how the Adobe Marketing Cloud cross-device tracking operates or how mobile number data is collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not address data ownership; it makes no statement that users own their data, and the practice of sharing hashed identifiers with advertising partners suggests the platform exerts control over user data beyond the user's interests.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy states users may contact Truth Initiative to review and request corrections to their personal information, but does not clearly provide a full data deletion right or process; it only mentions corrections and opting out of communications.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period or schedule is stated anywhere in the policy; the policy is silent on how long personal or aggregate data is retained.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states that 'appropriate security measures' are taken to protect against unauthorized access, and that access is restricted to employees who need the information, but no specific security measures (e.g., encryption protocols, audits, firewalls) are described.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy does not mention encryption of data in transit or at rest; no statement about HTTPS, TLS, or any encryption standard is present.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account creation is required to access the informational site, so password enforcement is not applicable to general use; however, for programs requiring registration (e.g., EX Program), no password strength policy is disclosed.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO is made anywhere in the policy; since most content is accessible without an account, MFA is not addressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies in general terms, noting they are used to track user trends and improve service quality, but does not provide a full cookie list with individual cookie names, types, or specific purposes as required for a full 'Meets' rating.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names some third parties (Campaign for Tobacco-Free Kids, LiveRamp, Adobe Marketing Cloud) but does not provide a comprehensive, enumerated list of all third-party vendors who receive user data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing broadly (vendors for operations, identity partners for advertising, CTFK for youth programming) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An opt-out for the identity partner/advertising data sharing is provided via a link to liveramp.com/opt_out/, but opting out of other third-party sharing (e.g., with CTFK or Adobe) is not clearly addressed, making the opt-out process incomplete.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The thetruth.com privacy policy (associated with Truth Initiative's programs) states that third-party service providers are required to protect the confidentiality of user information and use it for no other purpose, representing a general contractual requirement, though it is not specific about enforcement mechanisms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not state that users will be notified if third-party sharing arrangements change; it only addresses notification when Truth Initiative itself changes its own use of data, not changes in third-party relationships.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly discloses that hashed email addresses and IP addresses are shared with identity partners to enable 'interest-based and targeted advertising,' confirming that targeted ads are facilitated through the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms that anonymized identification codes derived from user data 'may be shared with advertising companies to enable interest-based and targeted advertising,' confirming third-party targeting of users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: An opt-out from the LiveRamp identity partner tracking is available at liveramp.com/opt_out/, but the policy also notes participation in Adobe Marketing Cloud Device Co-op with no clear opt-out described for that tracking, making the opt-out coverage incomplete.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy discloses use of cookies, cross-device tracking via Adobe Marketing Cloud, and hashed identifier sharing with identity partners for advertising—all of which are tracking methods used for ad targeting beyond functional purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: A partial opt-out from advertiser data sharing is available via the LiveRamp link, but it is not prominently displayed, does not cover all advertising partners (e.g., Adobe), and the process is not clearly explained within the policy itself.
