r718.riskReason: TumbleBook explicitly states it does not collect personal data from students under 16, relies on institutional (school/library) subscriptions for access, prohibits student PII submission, and commits that non-aggregated personal data will not be sold or rented without express permission.
r718.parentSummary: TumbleBook (TumbleBookLibrary) is a subscription-based children's e-book platform that explicitly states it does not collect personal data directly from students under age 16, with access granted through institutional credentials issued to schools or libraries rather than individual child accounts. Data collected is primarily usage/technical data (IP address, browser info, cookies) from institutional subscribers and administrators, not from students themselves. The platform uses Google Analytics for service monitoring and commits that personal data will not be sold or rented without express permission, and that data will be deleted within three months of a subscription termination request.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states users will be notified via email and/or prominent notice before changes take effect and that the effective date will be updated, but there is no mention of a revision history log being maintained or publicly accessible.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists cookies, usage data, location data, and subscriber PII as data types collected, but uses the phrase 'may include, but is not limited to,' leaving the full scope of data collection open-ended and not exhaustively defined.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy provides a general statement about how data is collected (via service use, cookies, and direct submission), but does not specify exact mechanisms or triggers for each category of data collection in granular detail.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Use contain a clause stating that any content submitted by users becomes the property of TumbleBooks including all copyright, creating ambiguity about data ownership, though the privacy policy does not explicitly claim ownership of personal data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states that upon subscription termination and at the user's request, all relevant personal data will be securely deleted from TumbleBooks' database within three months, meeting the deletion standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as necessary for stated purposes and specifies a three-month deletion window post-subscription termination, but does not provide specific retention periods (e.g., in days or years) for each data category during active use.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references using 'commercially acceptable means' to protect personal data but does not enumerate specific security measures such as encryption standards, access controls, penetration testing, or security certifications.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy does not explicitly state that data is encrypted in transit or at rest; the site appears to use HTTPS (standard for web platforms), but encryption practices are not documented in the privacy policy itself.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Access to the platform is via institution-assigned shared credentials (username/password distributed to entire schools or libraries), which does not enforce strong individual password policies and is a shared-credential model by design.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform uses a shared institutional username/password model with no mention of MFA or SSO integration; IP authentication is offered as an alternative access method for schools, which provides some access control but is not equivalent to MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy lists three types of cookies used (session, preference, and security) with brief purpose descriptions, and references a separate Cookies Policy at www.TumbleBookLibrary.com, but the separate policy's full contents and named third-party cookies were not fully available in search results.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google Analytics is specifically named as a third-party service provider used for monitoring and analysis; however, other third-party service providers are referenced only generically without being named.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states third-party service providers receive personal data only to perform tasks on TumbleBooks' behalf, but does not specify which data fields are shared with each named or unnamed third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No explicit opt-out mechanism from third-party data sharing (e.g., Google Analytics) is described in the privacy policy itself, though users can instruct browsers to refuse cookies as a general control.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that third-party service providers 'are obligated not to disclose or use [personal data] for any other purpose,' indicating contractual restrictions exist, but does not detail the nature or enforceability of those agreements.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states TumbleBooks will notify users of privacy policy changes generally, but does not specifically address whether users will be notified when new third-party service providers are added or existing ones change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: TumbleBook is a subscription-based educational platform; the privacy policy does not mention advertising, and no evidence of ads being displayed to students or users within the platform was found.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no mention of targeted advertising in the privacy policy or terms of service, and the platform's subscription-only access model is inconsistent with ad-targeting practices.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party advertising tracking is referenced; Google Analytics is used solely for service usage analysis, not for ad targeting, and no advertising network integrations are disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy discloses the use of web beacons, tags, and scripts for service improvement and analysis, which represents some non-advertising tracking, but these do not appear to be used for ad delivery based on available policy language.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or data sharing with advertisers is disclosed, no opt-out mechanism is needed or provided, which is appropriate and consistent with a no-advertising posture.

r719.riskReason: The privacy policy is severely outdated (last updated March 2013), uses cookies for advertising purposes, does not name specific third parties, fails to disclose a data retention period, states residual data remains in archives after deletion, and does not address FERPA, MFA, or encryption explicitly.
r719.parentSummary: Turtlediary collects children's names, email addresses, cookie data, and usage information upon registration and site use, and states it will not sell this data or knowingly share identifiable data of under-13 users with third parties. However, the platform uses cookies for advertising purposes and matches user data with unnamed third parties under confidentiality agreements, which raises concern. The privacy policy has not been updated since 2013 and lacks specifics on data retention periods, named third-party vendors, and modern security measures, making it difficult to fully assess current data protections.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it 'may change from time to time' and will place a 'prominent notice' for significant changes, but there is no revision history, and the policy has not been updated since March 20, 2013 — over a decade of documented staleness.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data types (name, email, cookie data, chat messages, server logs, survey responses) but is not exhaustive and uses broad language such as 'certain information,' leaving gaps in full disclosure.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states data is collected via registration forms, cookies, server logs, and user communications, but does not provide a structured or specific breakdown of each collection method per data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; it implies Turtlediary controls and uses the data for its purposes, creating ambiguity around data ownership for child users.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents may request deletion of their child's account by contacting technical support, but the policy explicitly states 'residual information will remain within our archive records,' meaning full deletion is not guaranteed.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated anywhere in the policy; the only reference to retention is that residual archive data persists after account deletion, which is vague and incomplete.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy mentions internal reviews of data practices and physical security measures to guard against unauthorized access, but does not specify particular security technologies or frameworks in use.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The Terms of Service states that 'certain designated parts of this Website employ technologies to secure your data and the transmissions,' but encryption is not explicitly named or confirmed site-wide.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy notes accounts are password-protected, but there is no mention of password complexity requirements or enforcement of strong password standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: There is no mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration anywhere in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and their general purposes (advertising, support, tracking), and notes users can manage cookies via browser settings, but does not list specific cookies by name or provide a detailed cookie inventory.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references third-party data sharing under confidentiality agreements and with partners, but does not name any specific third-party companies or services.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with each third party is provided; the policy only states data may be matched with third-party data under confidentiality agreements.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy states users will be notified at the time of data transfer and can opt out by not using that particular service, which is a limited and impractical opt-out mechanism rather than a clear, easy process.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states third parties are bound by confidentiality agreements, which provides some vendor accountability, but lacks specifics about contractual data protection obligations.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention any process for notifying users if third-party sharing relationships change; it only states the policy itself may change with a prominent notice.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states cookies are used 'for advertising purposes' and to 'advertise to potential customers on other websites around the web,' confirming ads are displayed including retargeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms cookies are used to advertise to potential customers on other websites, which constitutes behavioral or targeted advertising, including for users of a children-focused platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Cookies used for advertising and cross-site retargeting are described in the policy, but no opt-out mechanism specific to third-party ad tracking is provided beyond generic browser-level cookie controls.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms cookies are used for advertising and anonymous usage tracking, but does not distinguish between tracking methods or clarify whether web beacons or pixel tags are also used.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There is no clear opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers; the only option offered is to disable cookies via browser settings, which the policy itself acknowledges may break site functionality.

dataCollected: Usage data (pages visited, interaction history, completed assignments)
r720.riskReason: Twee shares user data with multiple named third parties including AI providers (OpenAI, Anthropic) and analytics tools (Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity), claims rights to use user-generated content for model training, lacks explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance statements, has no stated minimum age below 13 for student users added by teachers, no specific data retention period, and arbitration is governed by Israeli law creating enforcement uncertainty for U.S. schools.
r720.parentSummary: Twee collects names, email addresses, passwords, user-created content, device details, and usage data from users, including student users added by teachers. This data is shared with third-party services including Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity, OpenAI, and Anthropic for analytics and AI content generation. While Twee states it does not use data for advertising and allows users to request deletion via email, the platform lacks explicit COPPA or FERPA compliance declarations, has no specific data retention timeline, and retains the right to use platform content for AI model training.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy can be updated but there is no clear advance notification process or revision history/versioning system described; users are notified of major ownership changes via email but routine policy update notification is not guaranteed.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Primary data categories (name, email, password, content, device data, usage data) are listed, but the policy uses broad catchall language such as 'any other data voluntarily shared' without fully enumerating all potential data points.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected via account sign-up, Google APIs, browser logs, and cookies, providing a general overview of collection methods but lacking specificity on how each data type is collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service state users retain ownership of their content, but the policy also grants Twee rights to use user-generated content for model fine-tuning and training, creating ambiguous effective ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may request data deletion by contacting privacy@twee.com, but there is no self-service deletion mechanism, no stated response timeframe, and no description of what is fully deleted versus retained.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained 'for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes for which it was collected' but provides no specific retention period or schedule, making this a vague general statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states Twee is 'committed to maintaining the privacy and security of your personal data' and references compliance with Google API policies, but does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as encryption standards or access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of end-to-end or at-rest encryption is made in the privacy policy; the platform uses HTTPS (implied by standard web operations) but encryption is not expressly stated or confirmed in the policy text.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service require unique accounts per user and prohibit credential sharing, implying some account security expectations, but there is no stated enforcement of strong password requirements.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is found in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges the use of session and persistent first- and third-party cookies and states users can opt out via browser settings, but does not provide a detailed cookie list with individual purposes for each cookie.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy specifically names Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google reCAPTCHA as third-party service providers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy identifies named third parties and their general purposes (analytics, AI generation, security) but does not specify which data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of cookies via browser settings, but there is no described opt-out mechanism for data sharing with core third-party service providers such as OpenAI or Anthropic.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy references alignment with Google API policies and standard contractual clauses for cross-border transfers, suggesting some vendor agreements exist, but no explicit statement that all third parties are contractually bound to Twee's privacy standards is made.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states Twee will notify users of material ownership changes via email, but does not commit to notifying users specifically when third-party service provider relationships are added or changed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy states it is Twee's policy to never utilize data for advertising purposes, and no ads are described as being displayed within the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Twee explicitly states data collected via Google APIs will never be used for advertising, and no targeted advertising program is described in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity are used for analytics and may employ tracking technologies; while not framed as advertising trackers, no explicit opt-out for these specific trackers beyond browser cookie settings is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy mentions cookies, user interaction patterns, and device details are collected, and third-party analytics tools (Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity) are in use, but does not clearly enumerate all web beacon or tracking technologies employed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users are directed to browser settings to control cookies, but there is no clear, dedicated opt-out process specifically for data sharing with analytics or AI third parties that may use behavioral data.

dataCollected: Location of access (IP address and device)
dataSharedWith: Physical product fulfillment partners (e.g., Brand Republic)
Business successors in case of sale or merger
r721.riskReason: Twinkl is a UK-based platform primarily governed by GDPR rather than US-specific laws (COPPA, FERPA, SOPIPA), employs third-party advertising and marketing cookies with tracking, does not explicitly state a minimum age, and does not make clear commitments against selling or targeting student data under US K-12 privacy frameworks.
r721.parentSummary: Twinkl collects personal information such as name, email, IP address, payment details, and usage/browsing data from registered users; this data may be shared with third-party advertising, analytics, and marketing partners. The platform is primarily governed by UK GDPR rather than US laws like COPPA or FERPA, and it does not explicitly state a minimum age requirement or provide specific COPPA/FERPA compliance commitments. While Twinkl uses SSL encryption and conducts daily security scans, parents should be aware that marketing/targeting cookies are used and third-party tracking for advertising purposes is present.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The ToS states Twinkl will notify users of 'substantial changes,' but non-material changes are posted without proactive notice and users are deemed to have accepted them on next use, with no revision history provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, IP, usage data, payment info, browsing behavior) but uses broad language such as 'without limitation' suggesting the list may not be exhaustive.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states data is collected via account registration, cookies, log files, web beacons, tags, and pixels, but does not provide granular specifics for each data type collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The ToS states that content submitted by users is the 'sole responsibility of the person from which it originated,' but Twinkl's overall data ownership position is ambiguous and not explicitly stated as user-owned.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may access and amend account data, and GDPR-based erasure rights are referenced, but the deletion process is not fully detailed for US-based K-12 contexts and may involve waiting periods or fees for copies.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained for the duration of account use, with communication data held up to one year, and post-membership data retained for up to three years before secure deletion, providing a general retention statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Twinkl states it employs physical, electronic, and managerial procedures to protect data, uses SSL encryption, and conducts daily vulnerability and malware scans using multiple third-party solutions.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Twinkl explicitly states it uses strong commercial SSL encryption for all interactions, securing login and personal information in transit, and has passed Extended Validation vetting checks.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy and ToS do not mention enforcement of strong password policies or any specific password requirements for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) or SSO/LTI integration options is made in the publicly accessible ToS or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The cookie policy mentions functional, analytics, and marketing/targeting cookies and provides a consent banner, but does not include a fully itemized list of all individual cookies with specific purposes on the main twinkl.com privacy page.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy broadly refers to third parties for payment handling, advertising, marketing, and search engine facilities, but specific named third parties are only partially identified (e.g., Shopify, Brand Republic in the AU shop policy, Google in sub-platforms).
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: What data is shared with each third party is only partially described and grouped by category rather than itemized per specific partner in the main twinkl.com policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can restrict cookie-based third-party sharing via browser settings and cookie consent banners, but a clear opt-out mechanism for all third-party data sharing is not prominently detailed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states that third-party data processors must operate within the terms of the policy and applicable data protection law, and are contractually obligated to protect data in line with GDPR.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy reserves the right to change it at any time and does not commit to proactively notifying users of changes in third-party sharing arrangements specifically.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Twinkl's cookie policy and privacy documentation confirm the use of marketing/targeting cookies and third-party advertising cookies on the platform, indicating ads or ad-related tracking are present.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The cookie policy explicitly states that targeting/marketing cookies are used to track visitors across websites and that third-party cookies may serve tailored advertising, indicating user-level targeting occurs.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Cookie consent banners allow users to opt out of non-essential cookies including targeting cookies, but blocking cookies may not fully prevent data sharing with advertising partners as stated in the AU policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The platform uses web beacons, pixels, and tracking tags as confirmed in the Australian privacy policy, and marketing/targeting cookies are used to build profiles based on browsing behavior.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can manage cookie preferences via a consent panel and opt out of marketing communications via unsubscribe links, but the opt-out process for all advertiser data sharing is only partially described and may not cover all channels.

dataCollected: Voluntarily disclosed demographic data (age, gender, race, sexual orientation)
dataSharedWith: Extension and application developers (upon user grant)
Service providers (e.g., crash reporting, device health)
r722.riskReason: Twitch is a consumer entertainment platform not designed for K-12 use, with a minimum age of 13, extensive targeted advertising to users including teens, third-party tracking cookies, and no FERPA or SOPIPA agreements, making it entirely unsuitable for school deployment.
r722.parentSummary: Twitch collects extensive personal information including name, email, IP address, device identifiers, browsing behavior, and payment data, and shares data with third-party advertisers and analytics providers to serve targeted ads both on and off the platform. The platform prohibits users under 13 and allows teens 13–17 only with parental supervision, but does not offer cross-context behavioral ads to teens unless they opt in. Twitch is a commercial live-streaming entertainment platform with no K-12 educational agreements, no FERPA compliance, and significant advertising and data-sharing practices that pose high risks in a school environment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Privacy Notice states changes are effective upon posting and continued use implies consent, with no advance notice for most users; prior notice is only promised to EU/EEA/UK/Swiss registered consumers, and no policy change log or version history is publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy Notice and State-Specific Disclosures together provide a detailed enumeration of data categories collected, including identifiers, payment info, demographic data, commercial activity, and internet/network activity data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The Privacy Notice specifically describes data collected directly from users (account creation, activity), automatically (cookies, IP, device identifiers), and from third parties (login providers, advertisers), clearly addressing how collection occurs.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Privacy Notice does not clearly state that users own their data; Twitch asserts broad rights to use user content and personal information, and the policy is silent on user data ownership in a meaningful sense.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request access, correction, deletion, and export of their personal data per the State-Specific Privacy Disclosures and Privacy Choices page, satisfying deletion rights, though deletion may impact ability to use the service.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The State-Specific Disclosure states data is kept 'for as long as it is required to fulfill the relevant purposes or as permitted by law,' which is a general retention statement without specific time periods, making this vague rather than fully defined.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Privacy Notice states Twitch takes 'reasonable steps to protect the confidentiality and security of personal information' but does not enumerate specific technical or organizational security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Neither the Privacy Notice nor Terms of Service explicitly state that data at rest or in transit is encrypted; Common Sense Media's evaluation also found no encryption disclosure in the policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service note users are responsible for maintaining account confidentiality and passwords, but there is no mention of enforcing strong password requirements or password complexity rules.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Twitch does not require MFA but optional two-factor authentication is available as a security setting, making this an optional rather than enforced control.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Twitch maintains a dedicated Cookie Notice that distinguishes between functional, operational, analytics, and advertising cookies (including pixel tags, web beacons, and local storage), with a cookie preference banner and settings controls.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Notice references broad categories of third parties (ad networks, analytics providers, extension developers, Amazon) but does not name specific third-party companies used for advertising or analytics.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Privacy Notice and State-Specific Disclosures group shared data by third-party category (e.g., advertisers receive cookie IDs, device identifiers, ad IDs) but do not list exactly what data each named or unnamed party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of targeted/behavioral advertising via the Privacy Choices page and cookie preference settings, but opting out of all third-party data sharing is not fully available and some sharing (e.g., analytics) continues regardless.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Privacy Notice states Extension developers must process data only per the developer agreement, and general contractual limits on third-party data use are referenced, but the scope and enforceability details are not fully disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Privacy Notice states Twitch reserves the right to change it at any time and that continued use implies acceptance, with no commitment to notify users specifically when third-party data sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Twitch explicitly serves targeted and interest-based ads to users on and off the platform, including through Amazon's advertising infrastructure, making advertising a core and confirmed part of the service.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Twitch and its parent Amazon use personal data including browsing behavior, cookie IDs, and device identifiers to deliver interest-based and cross-context behavioral advertising, confirming user-level targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertisers and ad networks directly collect data (including IP addresses and cookie identifiers) from users on Twitch and Twitch explicitly states it cannot control their tracking technologies.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The Cookie Notice confirms use of advertising cookies, pixel tags, web beacons, and local storage for ad targeting and measurement, and third-party advertisers deploy their own tracking technologies on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out is available through the Privacy Choices page and cookie preference settings for behavioral advertising, but the process is fragmented across multiple pages and does not provide a single clear opt-out from all advertiser data sharing.

r723.riskReason: Tynker has strong student-specific protections and explicitly prohibits targeted advertising to students, but third-party tracking cookies and advertising are used for non-student users (parents, teachers) on the same platform, and encryption practices for data at rest are not explicitly confirmed in the student-facing policy.
r723.parentSummary: Tynker collects personal information such as names, email addresses, learning progress, and user-generated content from student users, and requires parental or school consent before any child under 13 can use the platform. The company states it does not sell student data, does not use student data for targeted advertising, and treats education records as confidential under FERPA. However, third-party analytics and advertising cookies are used for non-student visitors, and data may be shared with business affiliates and service providers, so parents should be aware that some third-party data sharing does occur.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy carries an effective date (August 31, 2023) but does not clearly describe an advance notification process or provide a changelog of prior policy versions.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Student User Privacy Policy and EU DPA Exhibit A provide a detailed enumeration of data types collected, including identifiers, learning progress, generated content, cookies, location, and audio/video recordings.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes data collection via direct user input, automatic collection through cookies and tracking technologies, third-party sources, and educational institution pre-population.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Educational Institution Additional Terms explicitly state that education records remain the property of and under the control of the educational institution, and Tynker does not claim ownership of those records.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents, guardians, and educational institutions can request deletion by emailing privacy@tynker.com, and students can delete data via an in-product privacy control panel, though some exceptions apply under CCPA.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained as long as an account is open plus 24 months after account closure for some policies, but specific retention periods vary across documents and are not uniformly stated with a single clear period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references a comprehensive security program using administrative, technological, and physical safeguards, and the GDPR notice mentions firewalls and secure user authentication protocols, but specifics are not fully detailed in the main student-facing policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is referenced in the EU DPA and general security program descriptions, but the student-facing privacy policy does not explicitly confirm encryption of data in transit or at rest, and Common Sense Media noted this as unclear.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy advises users to appropriately select and protect passwords but does not specify enforcement of strong password requirements; no explicit mention of password strength rules is made.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or MFA options is found in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy for student or non-student accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The student privacy policy describes cookies including pixel tags, web beacons, clear GIFs, and JavaScript and notes their purposes, but does not provide a comprehensive categorized cookie list with individual purposes for each cookie type used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references broad categories of third parties (analytics partners, business affiliates, business partners, educational institutions) but does not name specific third-party companies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Third-party categories and their general roles are described, but the specific data shared with each individual third-party category is not itemized per party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can manage cookie settings via browser and can opt out of some sharing, but a clear and easy opt-out process for all third-party data sharing is not explicitly described for student users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Educational Institution Additional Terms state that Tynker provides access to PII from Education Records only to employees and contractors subject to confidentiality obligations as strict as those in the agreement, and prohibits third parties from using education PII for targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states Tynker will make reasonable efforts to notify users if data becomes subject to different privacy practices (e.g., in an acquisition), but does not commit to advance notification for routine third-party changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No targeted ads are displayed to student users on student-targeted pages, but behavioral/interest-based advertising is used for non-student users (parents, teachers) on non-student pages of the same platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The student policy explicitly states no retargeting or advertising cookies are used on student-targeted pages and that student data is not used for behavioral targeting of advertisements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party advertising and tracking services do collect data from non-student users, and the policy acknowledges third-party cookies may be placed on devices; student pages are stated to be excluded but the broader platform is not.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The student policy acknowledges use of pixel tags, web beacons, clear GIFs, and JavaScript cookies, and while student-targeted pages are stated to exclude advertising cookies, these tracking technologies are present platform-wide.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can manage cookies via browser settings and some opt-out is implied, but a clear, dedicated opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is not explicitly described; Do Not Track requests are not supported.

r724.minAge: Under 13 with parental/school consent (COPPA-compliant via school agreement)
dataSharedWith: Partners and Affiliates (hosting, internet development, service providers)
Statistical/aggregated usage data shared with Typesy partners (non-personally identifiable)
r724.riskReason: Typesy has a COPPA-aware EDU policy and prohibits commercial use of children's data, but the privacy policy is vague about specific third parties, lacks detailed data retention periods, does not explicitly list all cookies or named third-party vendors, and the Terms and Conditions page content was not fully accessible for review.
r724.parentSummary: Typesy collects basic account information (name, email), usage and performance data, and session cookies to operate its typing education platform; for school (EDU) accounts, student data is collected only with school consent and is used solely for educational purposes with no promotional messaging sent to children. The platform states it does not sell student data and restricts personally identifiable information access to employees with a business need, and parents may request review or deletion of their child's data by contacting support. However, the policy is somewhat vague about which specific third-party vendors receive data and does not publish a detailed data retention schedule, which limits full transparency.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states changes will be posted and material changes requiring increased rights will require consent via email or site posting, but no formal revision history or versioning system is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy identifies some categories of data collected (name, email, usage, cookies, IP address) but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of all data types collected across all product versions.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy describes some collection methods (account registration, cookies, automatic usage tracking) but does so in general terms without a systematic breakdown per data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is ambiguous; the policy states data is collected and used by Typesy/eReflect for service purposes, but does not explicitly affirm that users own their data or clarify company vs. user ownership rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents and school officials may request review or deletion of a child's personal information by contacting support, satisfying the deletion right requirement for EDU accounts.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as required by law and for service operation, but does not specify a concrete retention period (e.g., number of days/months) making this vague rather than fully defined.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy mentions rigorous security standards and limiting employee access to PII, and states sensitive data like passwords will not be sent unencrypted, but does not enumerate specific technical security controls (e.g., firewalls, encryption standards, audits).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy states sensitive information such as passwords and credit card data will not be transmitted in an unprotected or unencrypted way, indicating partial encryption practices, but full end-to-end encryption is not explicitly confirmed.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of strong password enforcement requirements or policies in the privacy policy or accessible terms; this criterion is not addressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration options in the privacy policy; this is not addressed in available documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The site discloses that cookies are used for experience enhancement and analytics and that session cookies terminate on browser close, but does not provide a full enumerated cookie list with purposes and names as required for a 'Meets' rating.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references 'Partners' and 'Affiliates' as categories of third parties (hosting, internet development, service providers) but does not name specific third-party vendors or services.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states only aggregated, non-personally identifiable statistical data is shared with partners, but does not specify what data is shared with each named third party individually.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Parents and school officials can revoke consent at any time, which effectively allows opting out of data collection for EDU students, but there is no explicit general opt-out mechanism described for third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy implies partners and affiliates operate under agreements with Typesy but does not explicitly state that third parties are contractually bound to privacy and data protection obligations.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes will be posted to the privacy policy page, which would include third-party changes, but there is no specific commitment to proactively notify users of changes in third-party data sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy states that no promotional materials or surveys are sent to children using Typesy EDU, and there is no indication of ads being displayed within the educational platform to students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states that student data collected via school consent is used solely for educational purposes and for no other commercial purpose, indicating no targeted advertising of students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: While the EDU product does not use student data for advertising, the general website uses cookies for analytics and references partners, and specific third-party tracking tools or opt-out mechanisms are not fully disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Session cookies are described as terminating on browser close and as not linked to PII, but the policy does not fully enumerate all tracking technologies (e.g., pixels, beacons) used on the general-audience portions of the site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No explicit opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described in the privacy policy; for EDU users commercial data use is prohibited by policy, but a formal advertiser opt-out mechanism for general users is absent.

r725.minAge: Under 13 with parental consent (school acts as consent proxy under COPPA)
dataSharedWith: Aggregate/anonymized data with third parties (no PII)
r725.riskReason: TypeTastic collects minimal student PII (login ID, first name, password only), explicitly prohibits advertising to students in the School Edition, adheres to the Student Privacy Pledge, and complies with FERPA, COPPA, SOPIPA, and SOPPA.
r725.parentSummary: TypeTastic School Edition collects only a login ID, first name, and password to enable student progress tracking within the platform; no email addresses or sensitive personal information are required. Student data is not sold, not used for advertising, and is never shared with third parties in identifiable form — only aggregated/anonymized data may be shared. The platform uses TLS/HTTPS encryption, adheres to the Student Privacy Pledge, and expressly complies with FERPA, COPPA, SOPIPA, and SOPPA, making it one of the more privacy-protective EdTech options available for K-12 schools.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states material changes will trigger advance notice to schools, and the TOS provides 30-day email notice, but no publicly accessible revision history or changelog is documented.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and service description clearly enumerate collected data as login ID, first name, password, and usage/progress data — a complete and specific list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states data is collected via user registration (school-provisioned accounts) and through in-service activity tracking, clearly explaining how collection occurs.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy explicitly states that the School is the sole owner and controller of PII processed in the Service, with TypeTastic acting only as a processor on the School's behalf.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Deletion is available via contacting the school or TypeTastic at privacy@typingmaster.com, but some data may remain in archive records after deletion for billing and support purposes, limiting full deletion.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained 'as long as needed to provide the Service' and may continue after termination, which is a general retention statement without a specific defined retention period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The service description specifies TLS/HTTPS encryption, password-based access controls, automatic 50-minute session timeout, and role-based access restrictions as concrete security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The service description explicitly confirms TLS (HTTPS) encryption is used for all connections between users and the TypeTastic server, and passwords are stored encrypted.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform supports SSO via Clever and ClassLink, and the TOS prohibits saving passwords on public terminals, satisfying the strong credential management requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: TypeTastic supports Clever Secure Sync and ClassLink single sign-on (SSO/LTI-equivalent), which satisfies the MFA/SSO requirement for the School Edition.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy explicitly states the Service uses only strictly necessary functional cookies (including named Cloudflare cookies), with a link to Cloudflare's cookie policy, fully disclosing cookie usage.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references Cloudflare by name for cookies and European subcontractors under GDPR, but does not provide a complete named list of all third-party service providers or subprocessors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Cloudflare is named but the specific data shared with each third-party subprocessor is not individually itemized; the policy groups sharing disclosures generally rather than per vendor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The School Edition explicitly states no PII is shared with third parties and no advertising tracking occurs, effectively eliminating any need for an opt-out and meeting the spirit of this requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states TypeTastic adheres to GDPR subcontractor requirements and the Student Privacy Pledge, and Student Data is only transferred to parties committed to equivalent privacy protections.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy commits to providing notice to schools before material changes take effect, and the Student Privacy Pledge commitment requires advance notification of changes affecting student data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The TypeTastic School Edition explicitly contains no advertising within the paid/school service; the free public version shows COPPA-compliant ads, but the School Edition is fully ad-free.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy and service description explicitly state that students are not tracked for advertising purposes and no targeted or interest-based advertising is directed to students or users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The privacy policy explicitly states no third-party advertising tracking occurs within the School Edition, and the free version's ads are limited to COPPA-compliant networks that do not collect children's personal data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Only strictly necessary functional cookies (Cloudflare) are used in the School Edition, with no web beacons or tracking technologies used for advertising purposes.

complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service require a valid email to create an account but contain no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords.

complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies, Flash cookies, web beacons, and embedded scripts collectively as 'Tracking Technologies' but does not provide a detailed list of each cookie by name, purpose, or duration.

r742.parentSummary: Vimeo collects personal data including email addresses, IP addresses, device information, viewing history, and inferences about user interests, and uses this data for purposes that include displaying targeted ads on third-party sites. While an opt-out for data sharing for advertising is available via a 'Your Privacy Choices' link, Vimeo is a general consumer platform not designed for K-12 use, and schools should exercise significant caution and consider a formal Data Processing Agreement before use.

r749.riskReason: Vocabulary.com explicitly commits to COPPA and FERPA compliance and does not sell student data, but allows third-party service providers to independently collect data via cookies and web beacons with limited school oversight, and policy change notification is not guaranteed in advance.
r749.parentSummary: Vocabulary.com collects student names, email addresses, grade level, school affiliation, learning performance data, and technical usage data such as IP address and browser type to personalize vocabulary learning. The platform does not sell personal data, restricts student data sharing to educators and authorized school personnel, and acknowledges FERPA and COPPA obligations—with schools acting as consent proxies for students under 13. A notable concern is that third-party service providers (such as Google Analytics) may independently collect data via cookies and web beacons outside Vocabulary.com's direct control, and parents should be aware that data is retained indefinitely unless a deletion request is submitted.

complianceNotes.DCQ4: Deletion is allowed but requires a written request to support, must be fulfilled within 30 days, and excludes de-identified/anonymized data and data moved to personal family accounts, making it a limited rather than full self-service deletion option.

complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS (encryption in transit is implied by standard web practice), but the Privacy Policy does not explicitly state encryption protocols used for data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Users over 13 create their own passwords with no documented enforcement of password strength requirements, though SSO options (Google, Clever, ClassLink, Microsoft) are available that may offload authentication security.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Vocabulary.com supports SSO via Google, Microsoft, Clever, and ClassLink for school accounts, which satisfies the SSO/LTI criterion as an alternative to native MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Privacy Policy acknowledges the use of cookies, web beacons, pixel tags, HTML5 Local Storage Objects, and third-party cookies, and links to a Google Analytics opt-out, but does not provide a comprehensive categorized cookie list with individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy references third-party service providers and specifically names Google Analytics as a third party, but does not enumerate a complete named list of all third-party vendors used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with third parties is described in general categories (service providers, educators, school administrators) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: A Google Analytics opt-out link is provided, and email marketing opt-out is available, but there is no clear, comprehensive opt-out mechanism covering all third-party data sharing for school-based student accounts.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Privacy Policy states Vocabulary.com will 'wherever feasible, contractually obligate' third-party service providers to abide by privacy terms, which is a conditional rather than absolute vendor agreement requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Privacy Policy states the policy may be modified at any time and users should review it frequently, but does not commit to proactively notifying users or schools specifically when third-party relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Privacy Policy mentions promotional emails may be sent and does not explicitly state that no ads are displayed on the platform, leaving ad status partially unclear, though no clear evidence of display advertising within the student learning environment was found.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Third-party service providers placing their own cookies and web beacons may engage in behavioral tracking, and Vocabulary.com states it does not participate in these transmissions, making potential targeting by third parties unclear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party providers can independently place tracking technologies per the Privacy Policy, and while a Google Analytics opt-out is offered, no comprehensive opt-out covering all third-party tracking is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The Privacy Policy acknowledges the use of web beacons and pixel tags by both Vocabulary.com and third parties for personalization purposes, but the distinction between functional and advertising-related tracking is not clearly delineated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out for Google Analytics tracking and email marketing is mentioned, but no explicit, easy-to-use opt-out process covering all third-party data sharing with potential advertisers or data brokers is documented.

r750.riskReason: Vocaroo has a minimal and non-transparent privacy policy that fails to address COPPA compliance, age restrictions, parental consent, data sharing, third-party use, security measures, or student data protections required for K-12 deployment.
r750.parentSummary: Vocaroo is a no-account-required online voice recorder that stores audio recordings on its servers and generates a shareable link accessible by anyone who has it, with no password protection. The platform's privacy policy is extremely sparse and does not disclose what data is collected, how it is protected, whether it is shared with third parties, or whether it complies with children's privacy laws like COPPA. Audio recordings are retained for an unspecified but limited period (reportedly a few months) and there is no confirmed mechanism for users to request deletion of their data.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Vocaroo's privacy policy provides no information about how or when users are notified of policy changes, and no revision history is available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy page at vocaroo.com/privacy returns only a brief tagline and does not enumerate or disclose any specific categories of data collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: There is no statement in the accessible policy text explaining how data is collected (e.g., cookies, server logs, microphone access), leaving collection methods entirely undisclosed.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy does not address data ownership; it is silent on whether users retain ownership of their audio recordings or whether Vocaroo claims rights over uploaded content.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No self-service deletion mechanism is described in the policy; third-party sources note that users may lose the ability to delete recordings if they do not save the deletion link at time of upload.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Third-party sources indicate recordings are retained for a limited period of roughly a few months before deletion, but no specific or confirmed retention period is stated in the official policy itself.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy does not describe any specific security measures used to protect stored audio data or user information on Vocaroo's servers.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Vocaroo uses HTTPS for transmission (transport-layer encryption), but recordings stored on servers have no confirmed encryption at rest and shared links are accessible to anyone without authentication.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Vocaroo requires no account creation or password, so strong password enforcement is not applicable; the platform is login-free by design.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account or login is required to use Vocaroo, making MFA/SSO not applicable; this criterion is met by virtue of no account requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy makes no mention of cookies, their purpose, or any cookie management options, despite the platform likely using session or tracking cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy does not name or reference any third-party service providers, analytics tools, ad networks, or other external parties that may receive user data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Since no third parties are disclosed at all, there is no information about what specific data, if any, is shared with each third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described, and users have no disclosed avenue to limit or prevent such sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy contains no statement that third-party vendors are bound by data processing agreements or required to follow equivalent privacy standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no notification mechanism described for informing users when third-party relationships are added, changed, or terminated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The vocaroo.com homepage references 'No Ads, What Now?' suggesting ads may have previously been displayed or a paid/ad-free tier exists, but the advertising status and any ad delivery to students is not clearly disclosed in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy does not address whether user data or behavior is used for targeted advertising; the ambiguity around ad status and potential third-party tracking leaves this unresolved.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure is made about third-party tracking scripts or ad network trackers that may be active on the site, and no opt-out is offered.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy does not disclose the use of web beacons, pixels, or other tracking technologies beyond what can be inferred from HTTPS usage, leaving tracking methods entirely opaque.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described anywhere in the available policy documentation.

r751.minAge: 16 (policy states no knowing collection from under-16; no COPPA-specific under-13 parental consent process stated)
dataCollected: Payment information (processed via third-party PCI-DSS processors)
Cookies and tracking data (including persistent third-party cookies)
