Business transfer parties (in case of merger/acquisition)
r751.riskReason: Voice Dream collects usage and identity data, uses third-party remarketing and ad-tracking services (Google AdWords, Facebook Ads, SharpSpring), deploys persistent third-party tracking cookies, lacks a verifiable parental consent process for under-13 users, and does not explicitly exclude students or minors from targeted advertising practices, posing significant COPPA and SOPIPA compliance risks for K-12 deployment.
r751.parentSummary: Voice Dream collects personal information such as your child's name, email, device identifiers, and usage behavior, and shares this data with third-party analytics providers (Google Analytics, Amplitude, Mixpanel) and remarketing ad services (Google AdWords, Facebook Ads, SharpSpring Ads). The policy states the company does not knowingly collect data from users under 16 but provides no verifiable parental consent mechanism for children under 13, and does not explicitly prohibit behavioral advertising targeting minors. Parents and schools should be aware that persistent third-party tracking cookies are used and that data may be leveraged to serve targeted ads, raising serious concerns about using this platform in K-12 settings without additional safeguards.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy is dated (September 2024) and the company reserves the right to modify the service with or without notice, but no formal advance-notification or revision history process is described for policy changes.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several categories of personal data (name, email, usage, device identifiers, payment info) but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of every data type collected, leaving some ambiguity.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes collection methods including account registration, app usage, cookies, third-party tracking technologies, and payment processors, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is not explicitly assigned to the user; the policy describes the company's broad rights to use and share data, leaving ownership unclear rather than affirming user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy explicitly grants users the right to request deletion of personal data, and states the company will direct service providers to delete as well, subject to limited legal exceptions.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific retention period is stated; the policy only implies data is retained as long as needed for service or legal purposes without providing concrete timeframes.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references PCI-DSS compliance for payment processors but does not enumerate specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls) applied to user data generally.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is not explicitly mentioned in the privacy policy for general data; PCI-DSS compliance for payment data implies some encryption, but no statement about data-at-rest or in-transit encryption is made.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of strong password requirements, enforcement policies, or SSO/LTI integration for K-12 use; the license agreement and privacy policy are silent on password standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI; an account is required and no enhanced authentication options are described in any policy document.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy describes cookie types including persistent third-party tracking cookies with general purposes, but does not provide a full enumerated list of all cookies used with specific names and purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Specific third-party service providers are named in the policy, including Google Analytics, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Campaign Monitor, Postmark, Google AdWords, Facebook Ads, and SharpSpring Ads.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: While specific third parties are named, the policy groups data shared with them broadly (e.g., 'to monitor and analyze use' or 'to advertise') without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each named party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of email marketing communications, but no clear opt-out mechanism is provided for third-party ad tracking or remarketing specifically; only a general browser-level approach is implied.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states affiliates must honor the privacy policy and that third-party payment processors are PCI-DSS compliant, but does not describe a formal vendor agreement or data processing agreement covering all third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not include any provision notifying users when third-party service providers change or when new third parties are added; this is not addressed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states the company uses remarketing services such as Google AdWords, Facebook Ads, and SharpSpring Ads to serve targeted advertisements after users visit the service, which is inappropriate for K-12 use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states that third-party vendors use cookies and non-cookie technologies to serve users 'advertisements that are likely to be of more interest to You,' confirming behavioral/interest-based ad targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking for ads is confirmed (Google AdWords, Facebook Ads, SharpSpring Ads) and no meaningful opt-out mechanism from this tracking is provided within the platform itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms use of cookies and non-cookie tracking technologies by third-party vendors for advertising purposes, including persistent tracking cookies administered by third parties.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of email marketing via unsubscribe links, but the policy does not describe a clear, accessible opt-out from data sharing with advertising partners; only indirect browser-level controls are implied.

r752.riskReason: The platform displays Google Ads with cross-site tracking, uses Microsoft Clarity for session replay and behavioral monitoring, has no COPPA compliance language, no age gating, and no school or student-specific data protections whatsoever.
r752.parentSummary: Voice Recorder (voicerecorder.com/voicerecorder.org) collects device and usage data including IP addresses and browsing behavior, and displays Google Ads that may track students across websites. The platform also uses Microsoft Clarity to capture session replays and heatmaps. There are no protections specifically for children, no COPPA or FERPA compliance statements, and no minimum age requirement — making it unsuitable for K-12 school use without significant additional safeguards.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The combined Terms & Privacy page at voicerecorder.org provides no advance notification process, revision history, or dated versioning for policy changes.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data collected (IP address, browser type, OS, usage data, pages visited) but does not address whether audio recordings themselves are stored or processed, which is a critical omission for a voice recorder tool.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that data is automatically collected when visiting the site but does not specifically describe the collection mechanisms (e.g., cookies, server logs, third-party SDKs) in adequate detail.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not address user data ownership; it only states that Voice Recorder retains all rights to its own intellectual property, leaving user data ownership entirely unaddressed.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No data deletion process or user right to delete is described anywhere in the policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated for any category of collected data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy contains no description of any security measures used to protect user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No encryption practices are mentioned anywhere in the policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account is required to use the service, which satisfies this criterion by eliminating password-based authentication risk.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required, so SSO/MFA considerations do not apply and the criterion is satisfied by design.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies generally (noting users can disable them in browser settings) and references Google Ads and Microsoft Clarity tracking cookies, but does not provide a full cookie list with individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Google Ads and Microsoft Clarity as third parties receiving data, but does not name all third parties comprehensively (e.g., ad network partners behind Google Ads are not identified).
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what specific data fields are shared with Google Ads versus Microsoft Clarity; data shared is only described in broad terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy references the ability to opt out of Google Ads via Google account settings, but no opt-out is offered for Microsoft Clarity or for other data collection, making the opt-out only partial.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor agreement, data processing agreement, or contractual obligation on third parties to follow privacy standards is mentioned.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no process described for notifying users when third-party data-sharing relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states that Google Ads are displayed on the website, confirming ad display to all visitors including children.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Google Ads is described as using cookies to track user activity across different websites to display interest-based ads, confirming cross-site targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking via Google Ads for ad targeting is confirmed, and while a Google account opt-out path is mentioned, no direct opt-out on the platform itself is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Microsoft Clarity is used for session replay, heatmaps, and behavioral tracking; combined with Google Ads cookie tracking, multiple non-functional tracking methods are confirmed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is provided within the platform itself; users are only directed off-site to Google's settings.

dataCollected: Log data (browser type, frequency and duration of visits, referral URL)
dataSharedWith: Amazon Web Services (hosting and data analytics)
Analytics and infrastructure monitoring service providers
r753.riskReason: VoiceThread explicitly prohibits third-party advertising and the sale of student data, has signed the Student Privacy Pledge, expressly addresses COPPA and FERPA compliance, restricts student account creation to school personnel only, and uses SSL/end-to-end encryption with documented data retention and deletion policies.
r753.parentSummary: VoiceThread collects minimal student data (name and email, entered by school staff — not children themselves) along with automatically collected usage/device data, all of which is used solely to operate the service and is never sold or used for advertising. The platform has a dedicated K-12 version (ed.voicethread.com) with strong protections including no third-party ads, FERPA/COPPA compliance acknowledgments, end-to-end encryption, and administrator-controlled deletion tools. Parents or guardians concerned about specific data practices should contact their school administrator, who holds primary control over student accounts and data retention.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: VoiceThread states it will notify users of material policy changes via website posting and/or email, and specifically requires parental/school consent before making changes affecting students under 18.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates collected data including name, email, photos, videos, audio, usage/activity data, device info, IP address, log data, and cookies, providing a reasonably comprehensive list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes data collected directly from users, data entered by school personnel on behalf of students, and data collected automatically by the service and third-party service providers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: VoiceThread explicitly states it asserts no ownership rights over personal information submitted via the service and that data ownership rights are retained by individual users or their institutions.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users and school administrators can delete accounts and associated content at any time through the management portal, with full purge of deleted data occurring after 90 days.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: VoiceThread provides a detailed data retention policy specifying archival timelines (1–2 years of inactivity), 30-day archive periods before permanent deletion, and full data purge after 90 days of deletion.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: VoiceThread describes specific security measures including SSL/TLS encryption for data transmission, end-to-end encryption for uploads, individual data sandboxes, 24/7 cloud security monitoring, and encrypted password storage with salted hashing.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy and support documentation confirm SSL encryption in transit and end-to-end encryption for uploads, with passwords stored and transferred securely using encryption and salted hashing.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policies reference password security and encrypted password storage but do not explicitly state that strong/complex passwords are enforced on users at the account creation level; LTI/SSO integration is available as an alternative.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: VoiceThread supports SSO and LTI integration for institutional users, providing a federated authentication mechanism, though standalone MFA for individual accounts is not explicitly mentioned in the public policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: VoiceThread publishes a dedicated Cookie Notice at voicethread.com/howto/enabling-cookies/ that categorizes and describes each cookie type (necessary, preference, statistic/session, persistent) and their purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: VoiceThread maintains a publicly accessible list of third-party service providers at voicethread.com/howto/third-party-service-providers/, naming specific vendors such as Amazon Web Services and Campaign Monitor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: While specific vendors are named, the policy groups the data shared with them broadly (e.g., 'minimum information necessary') rather than precisely itemizing which data fields each specific provider receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can block cookies via browser settings and opt out of certain information sharing, but the policy does not describe a simple, centralized opt-out mechanism for all third-party data sharing categories.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states that service providers must adhere to confidentiality and security obligations consistent with VoiceThread's Privacy Policy, and that they have no right to use data beyond what is necessary.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states VoiceThread may update the list of service providers but does not commit to proactively notifying users of every third-party provider change; users are directed to check the published list.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy and K-12 terms explicitly state that third-party advertising is not permitted on Ed.VoiceThread, and no ads are served to student users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policies explicitly prohibit first- and third-party behaviorally targeted advertising to students and state that student information is never used or disclosed for targeted advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: VoiceThread explicitly states it does not permit third-party contextual advertisements or tracking for advertising, and student data is never used for behavioral advertising or shared with advertisers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The Cookie Notice describes cookies as limited to necessary, preference, and statistic functions only, with no advertising or tracking cookies used on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because VoiceThread explicitly prohibits all advertising and does not share student data with advertisers, no opt-out mechanism is needed and the platform fully meets this standard by default.

r754.riskReason: Vooks self-certifies COPPA and FERPA compliance and prohibits student data sale, but uses marketing cookies (Google Ads, Meta) that collect data across third-party sites, and the Storyteller feature collects voice/audio from children, posing moderate privacy risk in K-12 contexts.
r754.parentSummary: Vooks collects account information, usage data, device data, and cookies (including third-party marketing cookies from Google and Meta) to operate and improve its service; it does not sell personal data and prohibits its service providers from doing so. The platform claims COPPA and FERPA compliance, requires an adult to create any account on behalf of a child, and states that student data is deleted or returned to schools at contract end. However, parents and schools should be aware that the Storyteller feature collects voice and audio recordings from children, and third-party marketing cookies (Google Ads, Meta) are used which may track activity across external sites.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Privacy Policy (last updated September 19, 2024) states Vooks will notify users of material changes by email or other appropriate measures, satisfying advance notification requirements.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy Policy enumerates specific data types collected including account info, usage/session data, device data, content interactions, cookie data, payment info, voice recordings, and LMS profile data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected — through account registration, cookies, content interactions, app device data, LMS integration, and the Storyteller feature.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states that student data transmitted by an LEA is the property of and under the control of the LEA, and user-generated content belongs to the Account Creator, indicating user/school data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy states users may request deletion of Personal Information and that student/account data is deleted at contract end, but notes Vooks reserves the right to retain data longer if 'critical to our business,' making deletion only partially unconditional.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy provides specific retention periods: account data retained while active, cookie data up to two years, email lists purged after one year of inactivity, and student data deleted at contract end.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Privacy Policy specifically lists SSL/TLS encryption, server authentication, firewall, intrusion detection, regular backups and audits, trained personnel, and incident response protocols.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states use of SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) technology with server authentication and data encryption for data in transit and on systems.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not explicitly describe or enforce strong password requirements; it only states users are responsible for keeping login credentials confidential.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The policy mentions LMS/SSO integration for school users, which may provide SSO-based access control, but no explicit MFA option is described for standard consumer accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy names all cookie categories and specific vendors: Dynatrace, Stripe (essential/functional), Google Analytics, Hotjar (analytics), and Google Ads, Meta (marketing), satisfying full cookie disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy names specific third-party service providers by category and names specific companies including Stripe, Google Analytics, Hotjar, Google Ads, and Meta.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: While specific third-party companies are named, the policy groups data shared with them broadly (e.g., 'as needed to provide services') rather than specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each vendor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy allows users to opt out of non-essential cookies and account preferences to avoid recommendations, but there is no clear, standalone opt-out mechanism for all third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy explicitly states Vooks prohibits service providers from selling or disclosing Personal Information provided to them and requires all service providers to maintain confidentiality and security standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Privacy Policy states Vooks will notify users of material changes by email or other appropriate notice, which covers notification of changes to third-party relationships.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Vooks explicitly markets itself as ad-free for end users, and the Privacy Policy and platform descriptions confirm no ads are displayed to children using the service.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: While the platform is ad-free for users, Vooks uses Google Ads and Meta marketing cookies to support its own marketing efforts externally, creating a possibility of third-party audience targeting based on platform data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Marketing cookies from Google Ads and Meta are listed as active on the platform; the policy allows opting out of non-essential cookies, but the opt-out process is not prominently explained or easily accessible.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy discloses use of marketing cookies (Google Ads, Meta) that can track activity across third-party sites, which represents tracking beyond purely functional purposes even if no ads are shown in-platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can block or opt out of non-essential cookies per the policy, but the mechanism for doing so is described only vaguely (removing preferences/filters, blocking cookies) without a clear dedicated opt-out tool.

dataCollected: Student assessment scores and exercise answers
Personally identifiable student data (entered by educators)
dataSharedWith: Authorized school district employees and representatives
Third-party service providers (unnamed, as needed to operate the site)
Third parties chosen by the district (with written authorization)
Potential acquirers in the event of a company sale or ownership transfer
r755.riskReason: While Voyager Sopris expressly states COPPA and FERPA compliance and prohibits selling student data, the policy allows data transfer to unnamed third-party service providers, does not name specific third parties, lacks specific retention periods, and permits PII transfer in the event of a company acquisition.
r755.parentSummary: Voyager Sopris Learning collects student names, performance data, assessment scores, and teacher-entered information solely to support educational services provided to school districts. Student data is not sold or used for advertising, and parents or schools can request deletion of a child's personal information at any time. However, unnamed third-party service providers may access student data to operate the platform, and data could be transferred to a new owner if the company is sold.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states updates will be posted immediately to the service, but does not describe advance notification to users or provide a revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy identifies several data types (name, email, phone, student performance scores, cookies, log files) but uses open-ended language such as 'may include other data,' leaving the full list incomplete.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly describes data collection methods including direct user entry, cookies, tracking technologies, and log files.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy implies district ownership of student data (acting as the district's agent) but does not explicitly state who owns educator personal data, leaving ownership partially unclear.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents or schools can request deletion of a child's personal information at any time, and Voyager Sopris states it will not retain student data after a deletion instruction from the district.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states student data will be deleted upon instruction from the school or district but does not specify any fixed retention period or minimum retention timeframe.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references 'industry standard server and network hardware and software' to protect data but does not detail specific security measures such as access controls or audits.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy does not explicitly mention encryption; it references industry-standard protections generally without confirming data is encrypted in transit or at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not mention any password strength requirements or enforcement mechanisms, only that portions of the site are password-protected.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are acknowledged and their general purpose described (tracking usage patterns, improving site function), but no complete cookie list or granular categorization by purpose is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy acknowledges use of third-party service providers but does not name any specific third parties, only describing them in broad terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Third-party providers are said to receive data 'as necessary to perform their obligations,' but no specific data types shared with each provider are enumerated.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Parents and schools may request no further collection or use of a child's data, providing a limited opt-out mechanism, but there is no explicit opt-out for third-party service provider sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Third-party service providers are required to agree to the terms of the Privacy Policy, providing a general contractual obligation, but no specific vendor data protection agreements are described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not include any provision notifying users if third-party service providers change or new ones are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly states that personally identifiable student data is not used to market products or services directly to students or parents.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising to students or parents is described or permitted under the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: There is no indication of third-party tracking for advertising purposes; data use is restricted to educational service delivery.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies and tracking are described only for functional site improvement purposes, with no mention of advertising-related tracking or web beacons for ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising data sharing occurs, there is no need for an opt-out, and the policy effectively meets this requirement by prohibiting advertising use of student data.

dataCollected: Credit card number and expiration date (purchase only, via 2Checkout)
Date and time of website visit (via cookies)
dataSharedWith: Google / YouTube (only if YouTube uploader feature is used)
r756.riskReason: VSDC is a general-consumer desktop video editor with no COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance statements, no minimum age requirements, no student data protections, no data retention policy, no encryption disclosures, no MFA, and no K-12-specific data governance — making it unsuitable for school use without significant additional review.
r756.parentSummary: VSDC Video Editor is a Windows desktop application that states it does not sell or share personal data, and only collects personal information (name, email, address, payment details) when a license is purchased through its third-party payment partner 2Checkout. The free version collects only basic browser-level and cookie data (IP address, browser type, visit timestamps) for site analytics, and states this is not shared with third parties. However, VSDC makes no mention of COPPA compliance, minimum age requirements, student data protections, or K-12-specific safeguards, making it a significant compliance risk for school deployment with student users.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states changes will be posted conspicuously, but there is no advance notification process or revision history maintained for users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data collected (name, email, address, phone, payment info, IP, browser type, timestamps) but does not comprehensively address all data collected by the desktop application itself, only the website.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes how data is collected (during purchase via payment gateway, via cookies during website visits, and optionally via user consent for support), but does not address data collection within the desktop software.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly address data ownership; it implies user control via consent for optional data, but is silent on formal ownership rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy mentions users can request correction or deletion of personal information, but no formal deletion process, timeline, or verification mechanism is described.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated anywhere in the privacy policy or terms and conditions.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, audits) are described in either the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption for data at rest or in transit; the policy only states passwords are not stored in cookies, which is insufficient disclosure.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account is required to use the free version of VSDC, so strong password enforcement is not applicable for standard educational use.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required for the free version used in educational settings, making MFA a non-issue for basic student use.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Cookies are mentioned with a general description of their purpose (preferences, site analytics, personalization) and an opt-out via browser settings, but individual cookies are not named or categorized.

complianceNotes.SECQ2: Data is encrypted at rest using 256-bit AES and in transit using TLS 1.3 by default, meeting a strong encryption standard throughout.

complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform supports SSO via Clever Instant Login and IMS Global LTI certification, satisfying the SSO/LTI standard for this criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions cookies and browser-based tracking technologies generally but does not provide a comprehensive list of each cookie name and its specific purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third-party categories (service providers, affiliates, rostering providers) are described broadly but specific vendor names are not disclosed in the public-facing policies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policies group data sharing with service providers without specifying which data elements are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of promotional emails, and school districts can request deletion, but there is no clear self-service opt-out mechanism for all third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states that contractors and service providers are bound by contractual obligations to keep personal information confidential and use it only for disclosed purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may be updated at any time and continued use constitutes acceptance, but does not commit to notifying users specifically when third-party relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Learning Site privacy policy states that Wayside does not work with advertising partners to show interest-targeted ads to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is confirmed; the policy explicitly states Wayside does not work with advertising partners for interest-based ad targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking is indicated; the platform does not engage advertising partners for user-targeted ads, and no ad-tracking opt-out is needed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy references cookies and behavioral tracking technologies for analytics and personalization purposes, but does not confirm these are used strictly for functional purposes only.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of promotional communications and California/Virginia residents are granted the right to opt out of any sale or sharing of personal information under applicable state law.

dataCollected: Device information (IP address, browser type, OS)
dataSharedWith: Third-party service providers (contractors bound by contract)
r764.riskReason: Wayside Publishing has dedicated student privacy notices and explicitly disclaims targeted advertising, but the platform acknowledges use of marketing cookies, shares data with Google and unnamed third-party service providers, does not list specific retention periods, and the TOS states changes may take effect upon posting without guaranteed direct notice to users.
r764.parentSummary: Wayside Publishing Tejidos (operated via the Wayside Learning Site) collects student names, email addresses, location data, audio/video recordings, and usage activity to support language learning curriculum. The platform explicitly states it does not engage in targeted advertising to students and requires schools to obtain or provide parental consent for children under 13 in compliance with COPPA and FERPA. Data is shared with third-party service providers including Google, though specific vendor names beyond Google are not individually disclosed in the public policies.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Student Information Privacy Notice commits to advance notice of material changes to schools, but the general Learning Site TOS states changes are effective upon posting and only endeavors (not guarantees) to provide direct notice, making compliance partial.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy and Student Information Privacy Notice together provide a detailed list of collected data types including name, email, location, audio/video recordings, activity responses, usage data, device info, and search queries.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policies specifically describe data collection methods including direct user input, automatic collection via cookies, third-party rostering services, and school or parent-provided registration data.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Student Education Records are stated to be within the control of the contracting school, but ownership language is ambiguous for general users and no explicit user-owns-data declaration is made.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Schools can request deletion of student data in writing and Wayside commits to comply, but individual student users cannot directly delete their own data without going through their school, limiting direct deletion rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period (in days, months, or years) is stated anywhere in the publicly available privacy policy or Student Information Privacy Notice.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The GDPR policy details that the platform follows OWASP requirements, uses AWS for storage, and employs AES-256 encryption at rest and TLS 1.3 in transit, meeting the bar for specific security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2/1.3 by default, and payment transactions use SSL, indicating full encryption coverage.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The TOS places responsibility for password confidentiality on the user but does not describe or enforce any specific strong password requirements or complexity rules.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform supports LTI/LMS integration and SSO-style rostering via third-party services, but explicit MFA for standard account logins is not mentioned in available documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The GDPR policy categorizes cookies (session, persistent, statistics, marketing) and describes their purposes, but does not provide a named cookie inventory; marketing/advertising cookies are acknowledged as present.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google is specifically named as a third-party service provider, but other third-party contractors and rostering providers are referenced only in general terms without being individually named.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy explains that data is shared with Google and general third-party service providers for platform operation, but does not enumerate which specific data fields are shared with each named or unnamed third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users may opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information by emailing Privacy@WaysidePublishing.com, and California/Virginia residents have explicit opt-out rights documented in the policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that contractors and service providers are bound by contractual obligations to keep personal information confidential and use it only for disclosed purposes, satisfying vendor agreement requirements.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Student Information Privacy Notice commits to notifying schools before material changes affecting student data use, but the general TOS allows changes to take effect upon posting without guaranteed notification of third-party relationship changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states that Wayside Publishing does not work with advertising partners to show ads targeted to users' interests, and SOPIPA compliance is claimed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy affirmatively states no targeted advertising is served to students, and SOPIPA compliance is asserted, making this a clear no-targeting commitment.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Marketing/advertising cookies are acknowledged as present in the GDPR cookie policy (described as tracking online activity for advertisers), though targeted ads to students are disclaimed; the coexistence creates partial compliance uncertainty.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The GDPR policy acknowledges marketing cookies that track online activity and can share data with advertisers, which introduces third-party tracking methods even if targeted student ads are disclaimed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out process via email to Privacy@WaysidePublishing.com is provided for the sale or sharing of personal information, including for advertising-related sharing under CPRA definitions.

dataCollected: Web viewing and app use data
dataSharedWith: Placer Labs Inc. (location data for market research)
r765.riskReason: WeatherBug collects precise location data and device ad IDs, shares user data with numerous third-party advertisers and data brokers including GroundTruth and Placer Labs, displays targeted advertising, and has no COPPA-specific protections, FERPA compliance provisions, or student data safeguards appropriate for K-12 use.
r765.parentSummary: WeatherBug collects extensive data including your child's precise location, device identifiers, browsing behavior, and usage patterns, which it uses for targeted advertising and shares with multiple third-party advertising and data analytics companies. The app is supported by advertising revenue and confirmed to display personalized ads and share or sell user data with external parties such as GroundTruth and Placer Labs Inc. WeatherBug has no stated COPPA compliance mechanism, no FERPA provisions, and is not designed for K-12 educational use — making it a high-risk platform for school deployment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use state WeatherBug may update terms at any time by posting a revised version and may do so without advance notice, providing no advance notification or accessible revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (location, usage, device identifiers, ad IDs) but does not comprehensively enumerate every data type in a clear, itemized format.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy provides a general statement that data is collected via cookies, web beacons, device identifiers, and similar technologies, but lacks specificity about each collection method and context.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not assert user ownership of data; WeatherBug retains data for business purposes and is silent on user data ownership rights, implying company control over collected data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their account via a 'Delete Account' link or by emailing privacyrights@weatherbug.com, but deletion options are limited and no clear timeline for data removal is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained as long as the account is active or as needed for business purposes, which is vague and does not specify a concrete retention period.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy does not enumerate specific security measures such as encryption standards, firewalls, or access controls to protect collected user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption for data in transit or at rest is made in the publicly accessible privacy policy or terms of use.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of password strength requirements or enforcement is made; account creation details are minimal and no password standards are described.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is present in any available policy documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies, web beacons, tags, scripts, and device identifiers generally, but does not provide a complete list of all cookies with their individual purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Some specific third parties are named on the partners page (Opensignal, Placer Labs, GroundTruth) but the full list of advertising and analytics partners is not disclosed in the main privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The partners page provides some detail on what data is shared with Opensignal and Placer Labs, but the privacy policy groups most third-party sharing without specifying what data each party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Opt-out options exist for some data sharing (e.g., DAA AppChoices tool for GroundTruth/IBA, device location settings for Opensignal) but the process is fragmented, technical, and difficult for average users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No clear statement exists in the main privacy policy requiring third-party vendors to follow a supplier agreement or data processing agreement that holds them to WeatherBug's privacy standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Terms of Use explicitly state WeatherBug may update terms at any time without advance notice, and no process for notifying users of changes to third-party data sharing arrangements is described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Terms of Use confirm the app is supported by advertising and sponsorship revenue, and Common Sense Media confirms personalized advertising is displayed to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy confirms user location and other data are used to deliver targeted ads from local businesses and third parties, and Common Sense Media confirms data profiles are created for personalized advertisements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking for advertising is confirmed and widespread; some opt-out tools (DAA AppChoices) are available but limited in scope and not easily accessible.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms the use of web beacons, cookies, device identifiers, and similar tracking technologies for advertising purposes, indicating tracking extends well beyond functional use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: A partial opt-out process exists via DAA AppChoices and device settings for interest-based advertising (IBA), but it is fragmented, device-specific, and does not cover all advertising data sharing.

r766.minAge: Not specified (designed for students ages 5–10; no account or age gate required)
r766.riskReason: The WeDo 2.0 app collects no personally identifiable student data, requires no account, displays no ads, sells no data, and stores all user-generated content locally on the device only.
r766.parentSummary: LEGO Education's WeDo 2.0 app collects virtually no personal data from students — it does not require an account or login, and no names, emails, or school information are gathered. The only data transmitted to LEGO Education servers is the device IP address, which is necessary for app updates to function. All student-created content (photos, videos, voice recordings, coded work) is saved exclusively on the local device and is never shared with LEGO Education or any third parties.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The LEGO privacy policy states it may be updated and advises users to check back frequently, but does not commit to advance notification or maintain a formal revision history for the WeDo 2.0-specific data privacy page.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The dedicated WeDo 2.0 data privacy page explicitly lists every personal data category and marks each as 'Not collected,' confirming with specificity what is and is not gathered.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy document clearly explains that IP addresses are read when the app communicates with LEGO Education servers (e.g., for updates), and that user-generated content is stored locally on the device.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Because virtually no data is collected or transmitted to LEGO Education, user-generated content remains on the user's device and is not claimed by LEGO Education, effectively giving users full ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No account exists to delete, and on-device content can be removed by the user at the device level, but LEGO Education does not provide a formal data deletion request process specific to the WeDo 2.0 app.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The LEGO privacy policy states data is kept only as long as needed to provide a service or as legally required, but no specific retention period in days is stated for WeDo 2.0 app data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The LEGO short-form privacy policy references using 'secure systems and partners' and cloud storage, but the WeDo 2.0-specific page does not enumerate specific technical security measures such as encryption standards or access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: LEGO's broader privacy documentation mentions secure cloud storage and data protection measures, but explicit mention of end-to-end or at-rest encryption is not present in the WeDo 2.0 app-specific privacy documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account or password is required to use the WeDo 2.0 app, so password enforcement is not applicable and this criterion is effectively met by design.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account or login is required to use the app, eliminating the need for MFA and meeting this criterion by design through a no-account model.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The WeDo 2.0 data privacy page references an 'App Cookie Policy' for functional cookies, but does not provide a fully enumerated list of cookies with their specific purposes within the privacy document itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The WeDo 2.0 privacy page explicitly states the app does not share data with any third-party advertising or tracking service providers, effectively disclosing that there are no such third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Because no data is shared with third parties, this question is moot; the policy clearly confirms no data is uploaded or shared with any external parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No third-party data sharing occurs, so no opt-out mechanism is needed; this criterion is met by the absence of any third-party data sharing.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not detail contractual obligations with third-party processors, though it confirms no data is shared with advertising or tracking providers; LEGO's broader privacy policy references processor agreements in general terms.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The general LEGO privacy policy may be updated without advance notice; the WeDo 2.0-specific page does not include a formal process for notifying users of any future changes to third-party relationships.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The WeDo 2.0 app contains no advertisements whatsoever, and LEGO Education explicitly confirms this in its data privacy FAQ.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: LEGO Education explicitly states that none of the data from the WeDo 2.0 app is used for marketing purposes and no targeted advertising occurs.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The privacy document explicitly states the app does not upload content or share data with third-party advertising or tracking service providers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The app limits tracking to only what is functionally necessary (IP address for server communication), and explicitly confirms no advertising beacons or tracking tools are used.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no data is shared with advertisers and no advertising exists in the app, there is no opt-out needed; this criterion is fully met by design.

r767.minAge: 13 (or with parent/guardian consent and teacher-created account for under-13 students via education.weebly.com)
dataCollected: Billing information (name, address, last 4 digits of credit card)
dataSharedWith: Third-party advertising networks (e.g., interest-based ad partners, NAI/DAA members)
Successor entities in mergers or acquisitions
r767.riskReason: Weebly's general privacy policy permits third-party interest-based/targeted advertising and cross-device tracking with limited opt-out, posing significant risks for K-12 students even though a separate educational addendum references FERPA measures for teacher-created student accounts.
r767.parentSummary: Weebly collects a broad range of data including names, email addresses, device identifiers, browsing activity, cookies, and geolocation to operate its service and deliver targeted advertising. While Weebly states it does not sell personal data and offers an educational platform (education.weebly.com) with some FERPA-aligned protections for teacher-created student accounts, the general platform still uses third-party advertising trackers and interest-based ad targeting that present material privacy concerns for K-12 use. Parents should be aware that Weebly's primary platform is not purpose-built for children and that strong school oversight and use of the dedicated education portal are essential if this tool is used in a K-12 context.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Weebly posts a revision history with dated changelog entries (e.g., January 5, 2023; December 13, 2019), but the general TOS states Weebly can update terms without notice, making advance notification incomplete.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy notice provides a detailed enumerated list of data categories collected including personal information, billing data, cookies, device identifiers, geolocation, and cross-device activity data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy notice specifically explains that data is collected via forms, automated technologies (cookies, web beacons, pixel tags), third-party analytics, and mobile app interactions.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Weebly acknowledges acting as a data processor for some use cases, but personally identifiable information is treated as a transferable business asset in mergers/acquisitions, leaving user ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The educational addendum states records are deleted on request, but for general accounts deletion must be requested through support with no clearly defined self-service deletion tool or guaranteed timeline.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy references data retention in general terms but does not specify a defined retention period in days or months, making this vague rather than fully specified.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The educational addendum references commercially reasonable administrative, physical, and technical safeguards, but the general privacy policy only provides a general security statement without listing specific measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Passwords are stored using a one-way hash function per the older privacy page, and HTTPS is used on the platform, but the current privacy notice does not explicitly state end-to-end or at-rest encryption for all data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of enforcing strong password requirements or complexity rules is found in the terms of service or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration for standard user accounts is found in Weebly's publicly available policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Weebly's privacy notice mentions cookies, web beacons, and pixel tags and groups them by type (session, persistent, third-party), but does not provide an itemized list of each cookie name and its specific purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third-party categories are described broadly (analytics providers, ad partners, affiliates, payment processors), with Facebook named as an example ad partner, but a comprehensive named list of all third parties is not provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy notice groups data sharing by purpose category rather than specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of interest-based advertising via NAI and DAA opt-out pages, and cookie-based opt-outs are available, but the process is limited to browser-level controls and must be repeated per device.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy notice states that service providers are engaged to perform services on Weebly's behalf under data processing agreements, but does not explicitly detail contractual obligations imposed on all third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy notice contains a changelog of past updates but does not explicitly commit to proactively notifying users in advance when specific third-party data-sharing relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Weebly's privacy notice confirms that third-party advertising networks are used to serve interest-based ads to users on Weebly and across the web, which is incompatible with K-12 platform use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy explicitly describes interest-based/targeted advertising based on user demographics, interests, browsing history, and cross-device activity, which constitutes confirmed user targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Opt-out via NAI and DAA opt-out pages is available but is browser- and device-specific, requires manual repetition, and is lost when cookies are cleared, making it a limited rather than robust opt-out.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy notice confirms third-party ad services use cookies, web server logs, and web beacons to track users across websites over time for the purpose of delivering targeted ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out pathway exists via NAI/DAA websites and browser cookie settings, but the process is technically cumbersome, device-specific, and not clearly presented as a simple user-facing control within the platform itself.

r768.riskReason: The Bridge Designer software and its associated website explicitly state that no personal data is collected or stored from any user, making it one of the safest EdTech tools available for K-12 use.
r768.parentSummary: West Point Bridge Designer (now maintained at bridgedesigner.org) is a free, locally-installed offline software tool that does not collect, transmit, or store any personal information from students or users. No account is required to use the software, and no internet connection is needed once it is downloaded. There are no known data privacy risks associated with this platform for K-12 students.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No formal Terms of Service page exists, and there is no documented policy change management or advance notification process described anywhere on the site.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The platform explicitly and unambiguously states that neither the software nor the website collects or stores any personal information from users.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The site clearly explains that the software is locally installed and does not interact with the internet, meaning no data collection mechanism exists.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Since no data is collected at all, there is no data ownership concern; users implicitly retain full ownership by default.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Because no data is collected or stored, there is nothing to delete, satisfying this requirement by virtue of a zero-data model.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The zero-data collection model means there is no retention period to specify; data is never held, which fully satisfies the spirit of this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Security risk is effectively eliminated by the offline, locally-installed architecture that does not transmit or store any user data externally.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No data is transmitted over the internet at all, so encryption concerns are moot and the platform passes this criterion by design.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account or password is required to use the software, satisfying this requirement through a no-account-required architecture.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account or login is required, eliminating any need for multi-factor authentication and meeting this criterion by design.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The software is a locally installed desktop application with no web-based interface, so no cookies are set or used by the platform itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No data is collected, so there is no data to share with any third party; third-party sharing is not applicable.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No data is shared with any third party because no data is collected in the first place.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: There is no third-party data sharing to opt out of, as the platform collects and shares no user data whatsoever.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No third-party vendor agreements are necessary since the platform does not share any user data with third parties.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There are no third-party data sharing arrangements to change or notify users about.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The software is a standalone offline application and displays no advertisements of any kind.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising exists within the platform, as it is an offline educational tool with no ad infrastructure.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party tracking for advertising purposes occurs, as the software does not connect to the internet during use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacons or tracking technologies are used, as the platform is a locally installed desktop application.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: There are no advertisers or data-sharing-with-advertisers practices to opt out of.

r769.minAge: Under 13 with parental consent (school-mediated via COPPA school official exception; students under 18 access via PIN code, no personal student login required)
dataCollected: Usage data (platform interaction for service improvement)
Functional cookies and third-party analytics cookies
dataSharedWith: Potential acquiring entities in merger/acquisition scenario
r769.riskReason: WeWillWrite explicitly prohibits selling or sharing student data, collects only minimal necessary information, operates as a FERPA 'school official,' enforces end-to-end encryption, and maintains active Data Processing Agreements across multiple US states.
r769.parentSummary: WeWillWrite collects only students' first and last name, class association, device recognition data, and written texts for educational purposes, with no student logins required — students access the platform via a teacher-provided PIN. The platform explicitly states it will never sell, rent, or share student data with third parties for any purpose, displays no personalized ads, and does not use student data for AI training. Parents have the right under COPPA to review, request deletion of, or refuse further collection of their child's data by contacting the school or privacy@wewillwrite.com.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Privacy Policy states material changes will be communicated in advance via email or a prominent service announcement, and the policy is versioned with a 'Last Updated' date.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Privacy and Security Overview explicitly lists all student data collected: first and last name, class association, device recognition, and student-written texts, with teacher email also enumerated.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly explains that student data is entered by the teacher or submitted by the student during platform use, and device recognition is collected automatically during platform access.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states WeWillWrite acts as a data processor or 'school official,' meaning student data is owned and controlled by the educational institution, not WeWillWrite.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: COPPA parental rights section confirms parents may request review and deletion of their child's data, and schools may exercise deletion rights on behalf of students through the DPA process.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained 'only for as long as reasonably necessary' for educational purposes and not indefinitely, but does not specify a precise retention period in days or months.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy lists specific measures including encryption at rest and in transit, regular server patching, daily backups with 30-day secure retention, role-based access control, confidentiality agreements, and regular risk assessments.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The platform explicitly states end-to-end encryption for data both in transit and at rest on US-based servers, and encryption at rest is separately confirmed in the Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Students do not require logins and access via a teacher-provided PIN code; teachers create accounts but no specific password strength enforcement policy is detailed — the no-student-login model satisfies the spirit of this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Students access the platform without accounts using a PIN, and teacher accounts are managed through the platform; no explicit MFA or SSO mention for teacher accounts, but the student-facing no-login model meets the no-account-required criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A separate Cookie Policy at wewillwrite.com/cookies exists and describes first-party functional cookies and third-party analytics/performance cookies, but does not provide a fully itemized list of each cookie name and its specific purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy references 'vetted service providers (sub-processors)' for cloud hosting, payment processing, and email delivery, and states a list of trusted partners is provided, but the specific named vendors are not reproduced in the publicly accessible search results.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups sub-processors by function category (hosting, payments, email) rather than specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each named vendor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy explicitly states no personal data is shared with third parties for marketing or advertising, effectively eliminating the need for an opt-out; for essential sub-processors, schools can enforce restrictions via DPA.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The Privacy Policy states all sub-processors are 'contractually bound to protect your information and held to the same standards,' satisfying the vendor agreement requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it will update the posted policy and 'Last Updated' date when changes occur, but does not explicitly commit to proactively notifying users of changes to the specific list of sub-processors.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy and security overview explicitly state no personalized ads are displayed and no advertising data profiles are created for students or teachers.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly prohibits targeted advertising and behavioral profiling, and student data is stated to never be used for commercial or non-educational purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy states no data is shared with third parties for marketing, and no third-party ad tracking is described; student names, schools, and IP addresses are excluded from AI prompts as well.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The Cookie Policy mentions third-party cookies for analytics and performance purposes, which could involve some tracking; the policy does not explicitly confirm all tracking is purely functional with no advertising dimension.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no data sharing with advertisers occurs per explicit policy, there is no applicable opt-out needed; the policy's blanket prohibition on sharing for marketing effectively serves as the opt-out mechanism.

r770.minAge: 18 (per ToS); no age gate enforced in practice
dataSharedWith: Google (Firebase Hosting, Cloud Run, Firestore — infrastructure)
r770.riskReason: The platform displays ads, lacks explicit COPPA compliance or age verification, and its ToS requires users to be 18+ while being actively marketed to and used by K-12 teachers and students.
r770.parentSummary: Wheel of Names collects standard usage data (IP address, browser info, device identifiers) and uses cookies; wheel content is processed locally in the browser unless a user explicitly saves it to the cloud. The site is ad-supported, meaning ads are shown to users (though they can be dismissed), and the platform relies on Google infrastructure which may involve third-party data processing. Notably, the Terms of Service state users must be 18 or older, yet the platform is widely marketed for classroom use, raising COPPA and school-appropriateness concerns that are not formally addressed in the published policies.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it may be updated and recommends periodic review, but does not describe a formal advance-notification process or maintain a published revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy references collection of usage data, IP addresses, device identifiers, and cookies, but does not provide a complete enumerated list of all data types collected in a single clear disclosure.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally states data is collected automatically via usage and through cookies/tracking technologies, but does not specifically describe every collection method (e.g., Google Firebase telemetry) in detail.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Ownership of user-entered wheel content and saved data is not explicitly addressed; the policy does not clearly state that users own their data, leaving ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete account data via account settings or by contacting the platform, and wheel data can be cleared locally, but the policy notes the platform may retain data for legal obligations, making deletion only partially available.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Security logs are stated to be retained for 60 days and then automatically deleted, which constitutes a partial retention statement; a comprehensive retention schedule for all data types is not provided.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy states industry best practices for data encryption and backups are followed, and the FAQ references Google Cloud IAM, access audits, and Firebase firewalls, but specific technical security measures are only described in the FAQ rather than the policy itself.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Data stored in Firestore is automatically encrypted at rest, and all web traffic uses HTTPS encryption in transit, meeting the encryption standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: There is no mention of strong password enforcement requirements in the Terms of Service or Privacy Policy, and no SSO or LTI integration is described.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication is mentioned, and no SSO or LTI integration is offered; standard password-based accounts are the only described method.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The platform mentions cookies are used (session, persistent, functionality), but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies with their specific purposes; ad-network cookies are not fully disclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Google is identified through its infrastructure products (Firebase, Cloud Run, Firestore), but ad network partners and other third parties are not specifically named in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy policy does not specify which data elements are shared with which third parties; the sharing arrangement with Google infrastructure and ad networks is only implied, not itemized.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in the privacy policy; ads can be closed for a session but this does not constitute an opt-out of underlying data sharing.

r773.riskReason: Whiteboard.fi is iKeepSafe-certified for FERPA, COPPA, and CSPC; students require no account, no student PII is sold or shared with advertisers, and only functional cookies are used.
r773.parentSummary: Whiteboard.fi collects minimal data: students only need a name or nickname to join a session, and no student accounts are created. Teacher data (name, email, IP, whiteboard images) is stored for registered teachers but is not shared with third parties or used for advertising. The platform is certified by iKeepSafe for FERPA, COPPA, and CSPC compliance, and student data may not be sold or used for commercial purposes.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states significant changes will be communicated via prominent notice on the site and by email, and a 'Last Updated' date is displayed at the top of the page.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy specifically lists all data collected for registered teachers (name, email, teaching subjects, IP addresses, whiteboard images) and for students (name/nickname and drawn content during session only).
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly states that teacher data is collected upon registration and student data is collected when joining a session, distinguishing between session-only and persistent storage.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Service state user-published content ownership is not transferred to the company, but the policy does not explicitly declare that users own all their personal data; ownership language is partially present.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users have the explicit GDPR 'right to be forgotten' (erasure right), parents and eligible students may request deletion of all student data, and teachers can delete sessions at any time.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Retention periods are specifically stated: session data is deleted after 2 hours (free) or up to 365 days (paid), and student personal information is only kept as long as the account is active or legally required.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states data is treated confidentially, protected from third parties, and accessible only to employees who need it, but does not enumerate specific technical security measures (e.g., TLS version, AES encryption standard).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy references 'adequate processes' for cloud data security and the site uses HTTPS, but explicit mention of end-to-end or at-rest encryption standards is absent from the published policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Students require no account or password at all; teacher accounts integrate with Google/Clever SSO options, and no weak password scenario applies to the student-facing portion of the service.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No student accounts are required; teacher login supports Clever.com integration (SSO/federated identity), satisfying the SSO/LTI criterion for this question.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy explicitly lists all cookies used (whiteboardfi_session, __cflb, xsrf_token), states only strictly functional cookies are used, and confirms no third-party cookies are used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy broadly references sharing with 'affiliates, parent company, subsidiaries, and joint venture partners' but does not name specific third-party vendors or service providers by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy states teacher data is shared with corporate affiliates under the same privacy policy but does not itemize exactly which data fields are shared with each category of affiliate.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Teacher-registered data is explicitly stated to not be shared with third parties for commercial purposes; student data is not sold or released for commercial use, effectively providing a no-sharing baseline with no opt-out needed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy requires that any affiliate or successor receiving personal data must agree to use it consistent with the existing privacy policy, satisfying the vendor agreement requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Users are notified within 30 days of any acquisition or merger event via homepage posting and email, covering the key third-party organizational change notification scenario.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy and Terms of Service contain no mention of ads being served to students; the free tier review notes ads may appear before login for teachers, but student-facing sessions contain no ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Student and children's data is explicitly prohibited from use for commercial or marketing purposes, and no targeted advertising based on user data is described anywhere in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party cookies are used, and the platform explicitly states only functional cookies are deployed, eliminating any third-party ad-tracking mechanism.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Only three strictly functional cookies are listed (session, load balancer, XSRF token); no web beacons, tracking pixels, or ad-related tracking methods are mentioned or in use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no data sharing with advertisers occurs and no advertising tracking is in place, no opt-out mechanism is needed; the prohibition on commercial use of student data is explicitly stated.

r774.riskReason: Wirecast/Telestream explicitly states its services are not designed for children, employs third-party ad networks (Google, Facebook) that use cookies and web beacons for targeted advertising, shares user data with advertisers, and makes no mention of COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA compliance, making it unsuitable for K-12 deployment without significant additional safeguards.
r774.parentSummary: Wirecast, produced by Telestream, is a professional live streaming software platform not designed for children; its privacy policy explicitly states services are not intended for minors and any child data discovered will be deleted. The platform collects personal information including names, emails, payment data, IP addresses, and usage data, and shares this with third-party advertisers including Google and Facebook for targeted advertising purposes. There are no stated COPPA, FERPA, or SOPIPA protections, and the platform uses third-party tracking technologies such as web beacons and cookies for ad personalization, posing significant privacy risks in a K-12 school environment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use reserve the right to modify terms at any time without advance notification, though a general privacy policy update process is referenced; no versioned revision history is publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (contact info, payment info, usage/device data, cookies) but is not exhaustively specific about every data type collected by the software versus the website.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected directly from users, automatically through site use, and via third-party APIs, providing a general but not fully specific account of collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The EULA explicitly states Telestream owns all rights to Licensed Materials and deliverables, and GenAI inputs/outputs are retained by Telestream to improve services, indicating the company asserts ownership or broad rights over user-generated data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: An opt-out email mechanism (privacy@telestream.net) is referenced for marketing preferences, but there is no clear, self-service data deletion process described for all personal data collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The EULA specifies a 3-year audit record retention period, but the privacy policy does not clearly state general data retention periods for all categories of personal information collected.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy references general security practices and a Data Protection Addendum for enterprise clients, but does not publicly enumerate specific technical security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls) on the main policy page.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS for transmission, implying transport-layer encryption, but the privacy policy does not explicitly state end-to-end or at-rest encryption practices for stored user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of strong password enforcement, password complexity requirements, or password policies is made in any publicly available terms or support documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) or SSO/LTI integration for account access is found in the publicly available terms or support pages.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy and a dedicated cookie page describe multiple cookie types (functional, performance, third-party) with general purposes, but does not provide a comprehensive named list of every cookie deployed with its specific purpose and duration.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy names some third parties broadly (Google, Facebook, ecommerce partners) but does not provide a comprehensive, specific list of all third-party service providers used by the platform.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by purpose category (advertising, analytics, legal) rather than specifying precisely which data elements are shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: An opt-out page exists (telestream.net/company/opt-out.htm) and an email opt-out is offered for marketing, but opting out of all third-party ad tracking requires navigating third-party tools not controlled by Telestream.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The EULA references that Telestream processes data in accordance with its Privacy Policy and a Data Protection Addendum for applicable parties, but no explicit statement that all third-party vendors are contractually bound to equivalent privacy standards is made in the public policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Terms of Use state that Telestream may modify or update terms and third-party integrations without advance notice to users, indicating no formal notification process for third-party changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly confirms that third-party ad networks display targeted advertisements to users based on their visits to Telestream sites and other websites.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Telestream confirms it works with Google, Facebook, and other networks that display interest-based and behaviorally targeted advertising based on cross-site user tracking data.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party ad networks including Google and Facebook use cookies, web beacons, and JavaScript on Telestream's site to track users, and opting out requires using each third party's own mechanisms with no centralized opt-out provided by Telestream.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy confirms that third-party ad networks use web beacons (clear GIFs), cookies, and JavaScript on Telestream's site specifically to measure ad effectiveness and personalize advertising content.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out email (privacy@telestream.net) and a dedicated opt-out page are provided for Telestream's own marketing communications, but comprehensive opt-out from all third-party advertiser data sharing is unclear and deferred to third parties.
