r775.riskReason: Wix is a general-purpose website builder not designed for K-12 use, has no FERPA or SOPIPA commitments, admits to sharing and potentially 'selling' personal data with advertising and marketing partners, uses third-party tracking cookies, and has no dedicated student data protections or parental consent mechanisms.
r775.parentSummary: Wix collects a wide range of personal data including name, email, phone, payment info, device identifiers, and usage/cookie data, and shares this data with advertising partners, analytics providers, and social media platforms. Wix states it does not knowingly collect data from children under 16, but offers no COPPA-compliant parental consent mechanism and makes no FERPA commitments, making it unsuitable as a school-approved EdTech tool. Parents should be aware that Wix is a commercial website-building platform—not an educational service—and any student use involves exposure to commercial data collection and potential targeted advertising infrastructure.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Wix's Privacy Policy states changes take effect upon posting and users are expected to review periodically, but there is no clear advance notification process or maintained revision history for users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: Wix's Privacy Policy provides a detailed enumeration of data types collected including user-provided data, automatically collected data, and data from third-party sources such as advertising and marketing partners.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The Privacy Policy specifically describes three collection methods: data provided directly by users, data collected automatically during use, and data received from third-party sources such as social media and fraud detection providers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is ambiguous; Wix's IP clause asserts broad ownership over platform intellectual property, and user data ownership is not clearly stated in plain terms, though users retain content rights in some contexts.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Wix's Privacy Policy includes a 'Right to Delete Your Information' provision allowing users to request deletion of their personal information, subject to legally permissible exceptions.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The Privacy Policy states data is retained 'for the time period reasonably necessary to achieve the purposes described,' which is vague and does not specify any concrete retention periods or timelines.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Wix's Trust Center and Privacy FAQ describe specific security measures including physical, electronic, and procedural safeguards, SOC 2 Type 2 certification, PCI DSS Level 1, and a bug bounty program.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Wix confirms encryption of user personal information, HTTPS/SSL-TLS for data in transit, one-way password hashing, and SSL for payment data, indicating broad encryption coverage.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Wix encourages strong passwords but does not enforce a minimum password strength requirement, only recommending 'tough-to-break passwords with multiple characters and symbols.'
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Wix supports Facebook and Google SSO for individual users and OpenID Connect for enterprises, providing SSO as an option but no built-in mandatory MFA for standard K-12 school accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: Wix mentions cookies in its Privacy Policy and developer documentation and provides a cookie consent banner tool, but the platform automatically places cookies by default and does not provide a fully itemized first-party cookie list within the main Privacy Policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Privacy Policy names broad categories of third parties (advertising partners, analytics partners, social media platforms, fraud detection providers) but does not list specific named companies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The Privacy Policy groups data sharing by category of third party without specifying exactly which data elements are shared with each individual third-party type.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Wix provides a 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' page and supports the Global Privacy Control signal, giving users a mechanism to opt out of data sharing for targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: Wix references a Wix Partner Agreement that binds apps to privacy obligations, and the Privacy Policy states third-party processors are required to maintain data protection standards, but the commitment is general rather than specific.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The Privacy Policy states changes take effect upon posting without requiring advance notice of third-party changes, meaning users may not be proactively notified when new advertising or data-sharing partners are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Wix's own platform displays ads to free-tier users, and the Privacy Policy confirms data is shared with advertising partners and that Wix may have 'sold' or shared personal information with advertising networks in the past 12 months.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Wix confirms sharing personal data with advertising partners for targeted advertising purposes, and users must actively opt out via the 'Do Not Sell or Share' page rather than being opted out by default.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Wix automatically places third-party tracking cookies by default, including advertising/marketing cookies, with no automatic prior blocking, exposing users to third-party ad tracking without explicit prior consent.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Wix uses advertising/marketing cookies and web tracking technologies that collect data about user behavior across sites for ad campaign measurement, with no restriction to functional-only tracking for standard users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out mechanism exists via the 'Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information' page and Global Privacy Control support, but the process requires user-initiated action and is not clearly surfaced during account setup or for minors.

dataSharedWith: Third-party feature providers (e.g., social media integrations)
r776.riskReason: Wizer explicitly prohibits student data advertising and sale, and acknowledges FERPA/COPPA obligations, but third-party data access is loosely defined, the platform uses tracking cookies that may engage third-party services, and Common Sense Privacy evaluation flagged personalized advertising and unclear third-party data collection practices.
r776.parentSummary: Wizer.me collects personal information such as names, email addresses, student IDs, assessment data, and usage/device data to power its digital worksheet platform for teachers and students. The platform explicitly states it will never use student data for advertising or marketing and acknowledges compliance with FERPA and COPPA, requiring parental or school consent for users under 13. However, the platform uses cookies and interacts with third-party services whose specific names and data-sharing terms are not fully enumerated, and Common Sense Privacy has flagged concerns around personalized advertising and unclear third-party data collection.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states users will be notified via email or prominent notice of changes in ownership or data use, but a formal revision history or advance notification timeline for routine policy updates is not clearly documented.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates collected data types including name, email, student ID, password, assessment data, usage information, IP address, device identifiers, browser type, cookies, and billing information for premium accounts.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes data collected through direct user input, automatic tracking technologies (cookies, device identifiers), third-party platforms, and mobile service providers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership language is ambiguous; while Wizer acknowledges user data and student data protections under FERPA, the policy does not make an unambiguous declaration that users own their personal data, and feedback/suggestions are assigned to Wizer.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion of testimonials and personal information, but Wizer explicitly states it may retain data in backup/archive records, aggregated/de-identified data indefinitely, and that worksheets created are not deleted unless specifically requested.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained only as long as necessary to fulfill purposes and satisfy legal requirements, but no specific retention period in days or months is provided, making this a general rather than specific statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy lists specific security measures including SSL/TLS encryption, periodic review of storage practices, physical security measures, and commercially reasonable technical and administrative safeguards.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states all traffic to and from the application is over secure, encrypted protocols (SSL/TLS), confirming encryption in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not specify strong password enforcement requirements for end users; internal employee password policies are referenced but user-facing password strength requirements are not stated.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform supports third-party login via school platforms and LTI integrations but MFA is not explicitly described as available or enforced for end users in the publicly available policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and similar tracking technologies generally and notes users can disable them via browser settings, but does not provide a complete enumerated list of all cookies used and their specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy acknowledges sharing with employees, subcontractors, school/district administrators, and law enforcement but does not enumerate specific named third-party vendors or service providers used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by recipient category rather than specifying what exact data elements are shared with each third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can disable cookies via browser settings and contact Wizer to request data deletion, but no explicit and clear opt-out process for third-party data sharing is described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states sensitive student information is provided only to employees and subcontractors who need it, and the TOS references applicable privacy laws, but a formal vendor agreement or DPA requirement for all third parties is not explicitly stated in the public policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy notes users will be notified of changes in ownership or data use practices, but does not specifically guarantee notification when third-party service providers change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Terms of Service explicitly state a 'No Advertising' section and Wizer states it will never use student data for advertising or marketing, and third-party links are hidden from children.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states Wizer will never use student data to target advertising or marketing to students, and data mining for advertising purposes is prohibited.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The platform uses cookies and third-party integrations that may involve some tracking, and while student-targeted advertising is prohibited, the policy does not fully address whether third-party analytics or tracking tools operate independently on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy acknowledges use of cookies and tracking technologies for functionality and usage analytics, but Common Sense Privacy has flagged that user information may be used to track and target advertisements on third-party websites, creating ambiguity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear, user-facing opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers or third-party trackers is described in the publicly available privacy policy, beyond general browser-level cookie controls.

r777.riskReason: Wonderopolis permanently closed on July 31, 2025, and no publicly discoverable Terms of Service or Privacy Policy pages could be found at any URL, making it impossible to verify any data protections, third-party sharing practices, or compliance claims for a platform that served millions of K-12 students.
r777.parentSummary: Wonderopolis was a free, nonprofit K-12 educational platform run by the National Center for Families Learning (NCFL) that permanently closed on July 31, 2025. The platform did not require account creation for basic browsing, but it allowed users to submit comments, questions, and wonders — and no standalone, publicly accessible Privacy Policy or Terms of Service pages could be located, leaving key questions about data collection, retention, third-party sharing, and COPPA compliance unanswered. Schools and parents should be aware that the site is now offline and should not be recommended for current classroom use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: No Terms of Service or Privacy Policy pages were discoverable at any URL on the site, so no policy change management or revision history process can be evaluated.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: No accessible Privacy Policy was found; data types collected by the platform (e.g., comments, email addresses, usage data, cookies) cannot be confirmed from an official policy document.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: No documentation was found describing how data is collected — whether actively (via forms) or passively (via cookies/tracking) — as no Privacy Policy page is publicly available.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: No policy addressing data ownership was found; it is unknown whether users retain ownership of submitted content or whether NCFL/Wonderopolis claimed ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No deletion rights or user data removal process was documented in any discoverable policy, leaving this compliance point unmet.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention schedule or policy was found in any publicly accessible documentation for this platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, breach notification) were described in any findable policy document.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site used HTTPS (AWS-hosted infrastructure noted in WHOIS records), suggesting transit encryption was in place, but no formal encryption policy was documented.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Account creation is not required to use the platform's primary content, but no password enforcement policy or SSO documentation was found for optional account features.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI integration documentation was found; the platform appeared to have optional accounts with no documented MFA.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy or list of cookies with stated purposes was found; the platform used third-party embeds (e.g., Vimeo videos, ReadSpeaker) that likely set cookies without a disclosed policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No third-party disclosure list was found; third parties referenced in reviews (e.g., Vimeo, ReadSpeaker, outside educational sites) were not formally disclosed in any policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No documentation specifying what data is shared with which third party was discoverable, leaving this requirement entirely unmet.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing was described in any accessible policy or help documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No vendor agreements, data processing addendums, or supplier responsibility clauses were referenced or publicly available.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: No process for notifying users of changes to third-party relationships was described in any findable documentation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Third-party reviewer TechLearning noted the platform was funded philanthropically and users did not have to 'sit through a single ad,' suggesting ads were not displayed — but this is unconfirmed by any official policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No official policy addressing targeted advertising was found; unmonitored external links and third-party embeds (Vimeo, etc.) could enable third-party targeting without disclosure.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No documentation regarding third-party tracking for advertising purposes was found, and embedded third-party services (video players, analytics) may have tracked users without disclosed opt-out options.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: No web beacon or tracking technology disclosure was found; embedded services such as Vimeo and ReadSpeaker likely used tracking technologies that were never formally disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers was described in any discoverable policy or page on the platform.

r778.parentSummary: Wonster Words (by 77SPARX Studio) states it does not collect personal information such as names, addresses, or phone numbers from child users, and does not display advertising or sell personal data to third parties. Anonymous analytics data may be collected to improve the product, and an optional email signup exists for parents. However, the privacy policy does not explicitly address COPPA or FERPA compliance, does not name specific third-party analytics tools used, and does not specify how long any collected data is retained.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Service states the company 'may attempt to notify' users of major changes but places responsibility on users to check for updates, and modifications take effect immediately upon posting — no advance notification is guaranteed and no revision history is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy states no name, address, or phone number is collected and that only voluntarily provided contact info and anonymous analytics data are gathered, but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of all data types collected.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that personal information is only collected when voluntarily provided (e.g., via email or account signup) and that anonymous data is collected for analytics, but does not detail specific collection methods or SDK/tool names.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy does not explicitly address data ownership; it states data will not be sold or shared but is silent on whether the user or the company owns the data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can contact the company at any time via email to request deletion of any data held about them, satisfying the deletion right requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy makes no mention of how long collected data (including optional account or email data) is retained before deletion.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states only employees who need the information for a specific job are granted access to personally identifiable information, but no specific technical security measures (e.g., encryption standards, firewalls) are described.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Google Play's data safety section indicates data is encrypted in transit, but the Wonster Words privacy policy itself does not mention encryption, making this only partially verifiable from the policy document.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: A Wonster Account is optional (not required to use the app), and subscriptions are managed through Apple/Google app stores which enforce their own strong authentication requirements, so this criterion is effectively met.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Account creation is optional and handled through app store ecosystems (Apple ID / Google Account) that support SSO and MFA, satisfying this requirement without a standalone MFA implementation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy does not include any cookie policy, list of cookies used, or statement about cookie practices on the website or in the app.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy states data will not be sold or shared, and mentions anonymous analytics data collection, but does not name any specific third-party analytics or service providers used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No specific data shared per third party is disclosed because no third parties are named in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy states personal information will not be shared with any third party, effectively meaning there is no third-party data sharing to opt out of.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: No third-party vendor agreements or data processing agreements are mentioned in the privacy policy, so there is no stated obligation for third parties to follow data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy does not address notification procedures if third-party relationships change or new data-sharing partners are added.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states 'We do not have advertising in any of our products,' and the app is marketed as ad-free, fully meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Because the app contains no advertising, there is no targeted advertising of any kind, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: With no advertising in the product, there is no third-party ad tracking, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While no ad tracking is used, the policy vaguely references anonymous analytics data collection without specifying whether web beacons or other tracking pixels are used on the website, making this only partially clear.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or ad-related data sharing exists, there is nothing to opt out of, effectively satisfying this criterion.

dataCollected: Usage data (app activity, words studied, progress)

r779.riskReason: The platform is explicitly directed at K-12 children and collects personal data including tracking via third-party ad and distribution networks, discloses data may be used for commercial advertising purposes and shared with marketing partners, and the policies do not clearly address COPPA-specific parental consent processes, children's data deletion rights, or a dedicated FERPA compliance framework for school use.
r779.parentSummary: Word Club Spelling+Vocabulary, operated by the Scripps National Spelling Bee, collects personal information including names, email addresses, usage data, device identifiers, and location inferred from IP addresses when users create accounts. The platform acknowledges it may share data with sponsors, third-party advertising networks, and distribution partners and reserves the right to display advertisements in connection with user content. While the privacy policy states the platform is intended to comply with COPPA and does not sell data in the traditional sense, it acknowledges enabling third-party tracking technologies, and the User Agreement does not clearly outline age-gating or school-specific FERPA protections, raising notable concerns for K-12 use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The User Agreement notes Scripps reserves the right to modify terms and that changes may take effect upon continued use, but does not clearly commit to advance notification before changes take effect; only a general statement that changes will be posted is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, IP, device/browser info, usage data, location inferred from IP, tracking data, preferred pronoun, school affiliation) but the enumeration is not exhaustive or clearly structured for a children's platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy generally describes how data is collected (directly from users, automatically via tracking technology, and from third parties such as schools and sponsors) but does not provide specific detail on each collection method tied to each data type.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The User Agreement grants Scripps broad rights to use user content for advertising and commercial purposes without compensation, and does not assert that users own their data; data ownership is effectively claimed by the company.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy references a right to erasure and states users may contact the company to request deletion, but the process is not clearly defined and is subject to jurisdictional eligibility, making it only partially available to all users.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period is stated in the accessible policies for the Word Club app; the privacy policy does not include a dedicated retention schedule or timeframe for deletion of user or student data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy states Scripps uses security precautions but acknowledges data may be lost, stolen, or misused; no specific security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls) are enumerated in the publicly accessible policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: HTTPS is referenced indirectly through standard app store and web infrastructure, and payment data for Vocabulary.com (a related platform) is described as encrypted via Stripe, but the Scripps/Word Club policy does not explicitly confirm end-to-end encryption for user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Account registration requires a password (as evidenced by password-reset references in app updates), but the policy does not explicitly state that strong password standards are enforced on the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in the User Agreement or privacy policy for the Word Club app.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy acknowledges use of tracking technology including cookies, pixels, and web beacons, but does not provide a complete list of all cookies used, their individual purposes, or a mechanism for users to manage cookie consent.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references broad categories of third parties (sponsors, suppliers, contractors, distribution partners, ad networks) but does not name specific third-party vendors by name in the Word Club-specific policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what data is shared with each category of third party; only general statements about sharing for business purposes and advertising are provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The privacy policy mentions the ability to opt out of marketing emails and interest-based advertising, but the opt-out process for third-party data sharing is not clearly or easily described for app users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The User Agreement makes a general statement that third-party use of user content is subject to their own terms, but does not require third parties to adhere to the same privacy standards as Scripps.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes will be posted on the page but does not commit to proactively notifying users when third-party data-sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The User Agreement explicitly reserves the right to display advertisements in connection with user content and for commercial purposes, which is inappropriate for a K-12 children's platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The User Agreement states user content may be included on advertising networks of distribution and marketing partners, and the privacy policy describes interest-based advertising enabled through tracking technology, indicating targeted advertising is possible.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The privacy policy acknowledges use of tracking technology that enables interest-based advertising by third parties, and states that DNT notices may not be effective, offering only limited opt-out guidance rather than a robust opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy explicitly discloses use of tracking technologies including web beacons and pixel tags for purposes that include interest-based advertising, not solely functional purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: While opt-out links for interest-based advertising are referenced in general terms in the privacy policy, no clear and easy opt-out process specific to student/child users or data sharing with advertisers is provided.

r780.riskReason: No publicly accessible Terms of Service or Privacy Policy could be located for wordvault.com, making it impossible to verify any data privacy protections, COPPA/FERPA compliance, or student data safeguards required for K-12 use.
r780.parentSummary: A Terms of Service and Privacy Policy for wordvault.com could not be found through web search. Without these documents, there is no way to determine what student data is collected, how it is used or protected, or whether the platform meets federal requirements like COPPA and FERPA. Schools and parents should not deploy this platform with K-12 students until the vendor provides clear, publicly accessible privacy documentation.

r781.riskReason: WordArt.com uses targeting and advertising cookies, shares data with advertising networks and third parties, collects sensitive personal and financial data, does not reference COPPA or age restrictions for children under 13, and does not provide a mechanism for parental consent — making it unsuitable for K-12 student use without significant safeguards.
r781.parentSummary: WordArt.com collects a wide range of personal data including names, email addresses, birthdates, financial information, and detailed browsing behavior through targeting and advertising cookies. This data is shared with advertising networks, analytics providers, and business partners, and may be used to deliver personalized ads. The platform makes no reference to COPPA compliance, age restrictions for children under 13, or parental consent procedures, making it a high-risk tool for K-12 classroom use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The policy states changes will be posted on the website and users have 30 days to cancel their account, but there is no advance notification process or publicly available revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists specific categories of data collected including name, gender, birthdate, email, phone, address, financial information, and browsing/purchase data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally describes data collection through user contact, account creation, and cookies, but does not specifically enumerate all technical collection methods in detail.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly state that users own their data; it describes WordArt.com's rights to use and share data under 'legitimate interest' without affirming user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion of their information and cancel their account, but the process requires contacting the company and is not available as a self-service option.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state a specific data retention period or general retention timeline for user personal data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states only that 'reasonable measures' are taken to protect data, without specifying any concrete security technologies or protocols.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of encryption is made; the policy notes that 'no method of transmission over the internet is completely secure' without confirming encryption is used.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy and terms do not mention password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords for account creation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in the terms or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy identifies and categorizes cookies by type — functional, analytical, targeting/advertising, and third-party social media cookies — with descriptions of each.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references broad categories of third parties (advertising networks, analytics providers, business partners) but does not name specific vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by third-party category rather than specifying what data is shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described; the policy states it does not respond to 'Do Not Track' browser signals.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy mentions seeking assurances from third parties that they provide data in accordance with data protection laws, but does not explicitly require a binding vendor data processing agreement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not commit to notifying users when third-party sharing arrangements change; updates are only posted to the website.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly acknowledges the use of targeting and advertising cookies that deliver personalized advertisements to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Targeting and advertising cookies are described as collecting browsing habits to deliver personalized ads relevant to the user's interests, confirming behavioral targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy confirms third-party advertising services track user actions online over time and across different websites, with no opt-out mechanism provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms the use of web beacons and tracking technologies for advertising purposes, including cross-site tracking by third-party ad partners.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is provided, and the policy explicitly states it does not respond to Do Not Track signals.

r782.riskReason: WordBrain (by MAG Interactive) is a general consumer game app that displays third-party targeted ads, shares advertising identifiers with numerous ad partners, lacks any explicit COPPA compliance, FERPA acknowledgment, or school/student-specific data protections, making it unsuitable for K-12 classroom deployment.
r782.parentSummary: WordBrain, developed by MAG Interactive, collects device identifiers, IP addresses, location data, purchase history, and optional account details from all players, including potentially children aged 13+. The app displays advertisements from third-party advertising partners who may receive your advertising ID and IP address to serve personalized ads, with opt-out available only through device-level settings. There is no COPPA-specific children's privacy policy, no FERPA compliance language, and no school or educator agreement — making this app a poor fit for K-12 school use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states that changes will be communicated 'in a visible manner' (e.g., website or in-game popup), but no formal advance notification timeline or versioned revision history is documented.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several data categories (device ID, IP, username, email, purchase history, location, chat content) but does not provide an exhaustive, itemized list of every data type collected across all contexts.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically describes how data is collected — through gameplay, device identifiers, account sign-up, social network login, in-app purchases, and customer support interactions.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; MAG claims usage rights over profile pictures via a license, and data ownership language is absent, leaving ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request full deletion of their personal data via the in-game privacy settings in WordBrain, and the policy confirms MAG will remove all personal data across all games upon such request.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state a specific data retention period; it only notes data is stored for purposes described in the policy with no defined timeframe or retention schedule.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references GDPR-aligned data protection obligations and legal bases for processing but does not enumerate specific technical security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls) used to protect data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption (in transit or at rest) is present anywhere in the publicly accessible privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy and terms do not mention any password strength requirements or enforcement mechanisms for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in the policy or terms; the app is a consumer game with no school identity management support.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The MAG website references a Cookie Notice and distinguishes between strictly necessary and performance/analytics cookies, but a full itemized cookie list with purposes is not provided inline in the main privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references a separate 'MAG Advertising Partners' page for a complete list of advertising and marketing partners, but specific partner names are not embedded directly in the main privacy policy text.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups what is shared with advertising partners (IP address, advertising ID) but does not provide a per-partner breakdown of exactly which data each third party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of personalized ads by disabling the advertising identifier in their device settings, but this is a device-level workaround rather than a direct in-app or policy-level opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not contain any explicit language requiring advertising or data partners to adhere to contractual data protection obligations or a vendor agreement on behalf of users.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states that changes will be communicated visibly, but there is no specific commitment to notify users when advertising or third-party data partners change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy and Common Sense Media review confirm that third-party advertisements (banners, full-screen ads, video ads) are displayed within the game, including to all users regardless of age.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The app uses advertising identifiers to serve personalized/targeted ads from third-party ad partners, with no age-based restriction or child-safe ad mode documented.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party ad partners receive advertising IDs and IP addresses and may track users across apps; opt-out is possible only via device-level advertising ID reset, with limited effectiveness.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms advertising identifiers and IP addresses are shared with ad partners for ad delivery, and third-party tracking technologies (pixels, ad SDKs) are used within the app for advertising purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out from personalized ads is mentioned (via device privacy settings to disable the advertising ID), but the process is indirect, device-dependent, and not clearly described within the policy itself.

dataSharedWith: Third-party advertisers (unspecified, reportedly 371+ ad/tracking vendors via consent framework)
r783.riskReason: WordReference serves ads via a large number of third-party trackers (reportedly 371+), collects IP addresses and behavioral data for ad targeting, has no minimum age requirement, no COPPA parental consent mechanism, no explicit FERPA provisions, and opt-out is impractical given the volume of third-party ad vendors.
r783.parentSummary: WordReference.com collects non-personally identifiable information such as IP addresses, browser type, and language preferences, and uses this data partly for ad targeting on behalf of advertisers. While it states it does not collect names or addresses, it uses a large number of third-party advertising and tracking vendors whose cookies may harvest behavioral data from student users, and there is no age verification, parental consent process, or minimum age requirement stated anywhere in its policies.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy and terms of service contain no advance notification process for policy changes, no revision history, and no dated versioning.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists some data types (IP address, browser type, OS, ISP, language preference, email for forum members) but does not comprehensively address all data collected by the numerous third-party advertising trackers operating on the site.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy gives a general statement that data is collected passively via browsing and cookies, and actively via forum registration, but does not specifically describe each collection method in detail.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy is silent on data ownership; there is no statement that users own their data, and the company does not explicitly disclaim ownership either.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: There is no deletion option or process described in the privacy policy or terms of service for any collected data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states IP logs of unregistered visitors are generally not retained beyond 30 days, but provides no retention period for other data types such as forum member data or ad-targeting data.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No specific security measures (encryption, firewalls, access controls, etc.) are described anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS for transport, passing a basic encryption test, but no explicit encryption policy is stated in the privacy policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No strong password enforcement policy is described; the terms only place responsibility on users to keep passwords confidential.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is mentioned in any policy document.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and references Facebook and Google Analytics cookies generally, but does not list all cookies with their specific purposes; the consent banner reportedly involves 371+ third-party vendors without a simple all-reject option.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy does not name specific third-party advertising or data-sharing partners; it only references Facebook and Google Analytics by name in a cached version.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with each third party is provided in the policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: A vague opt-out is mentioned via cookie deletion and browser add-ons, but no easy or centralized opt-out process is provided, and the consent framework reportedly requires individually opting out of hundreds of vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: There is no statement that third-party partners are contractually required to comply with the platform's privacy obligations or any data protection standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: There is no notification process stated for when third-party data-sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states data is used for targeting ads and measuring ad effectiveness on behalf of advertisers, confirming targeted advertising is displayed to all users including students.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy confirms data is used for targeting ads on behalf of advertisers, indicating user-level behavioral targeting occurs.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party trackers (including advertising networks) operate on the site per the policy and consent framework, with no meaningful opt-out provided to prevent tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Third-party cookies (including Facebook and Google Analytics) are used for advertising purposes with no comprehensive disclosure of all tracking technologies deployed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear or simple opt-out from advertiser data sharing is provided; the opt-out mechanism described (manual cookie deletion or browser add-ons) is inadequate and the consent framework reportedly requires individual opt-out from hundreds of vendors.

r784.riskReason: Word Tag (by Mrs Wordsmith) has strong child-protective policies including no behavioral ads, no sale of children's data, and parental-consent-gated accounts, but its use of AppsFlyer for install attribution — which transmits device and consent signals to Google — introduces third-party data sharing risks that are not fully resolved for a strict K-12/COPPA school-use context, and FERPA/COPPA compliance is not explicitly claimed.
r784.parentSummary: Word Tag (published by Mrs Wordsmith Group Limited) collects contact and payment data from parents/guardians and device identifiers and usage data from children solely to operate the app; children cannot self-register and in-app progress is stored locally without a parent account. The platform does not serve third-party ads to children, does not sell children's data, and requires all third-party processors to sign Data Processing Agreements. However, the app uses AppsFlyer for install attribution and transmits consent signals to Google, meaning some device-level data may flow to third parties depending on consent choices made at setup.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states it may be updated but does not explicitly describe an advance-notification process or maintain a publicly accessible revision history log.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy enumerates specific data categories including contact data, device identifiers, technical/usage data, transaction data, and voice/text transcripts from Ask Armie.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly states data is collected directly from users, automatically via cookies and server logs, and from third parties such as Shopify and PayPal.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state that users own their data; Mrs Wordsmith is identified as the data controller, leaving ownership somewhat ambiguous from a user-rights perspective.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy grants parents the right to request erasure of their child's data and states deletion will occur promptly upon request, satisfying full deletion rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy references a children's data retention schedule and states deletion occurs upon parental request, but does not state a specific maximum retention period in days for most data categories.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy references contractual obligations on third-party processors and Data Processing Agreements but does not list specific technical security measures (e.g., encryption standards, access controls, or audit practices).
complianceNotes.SECQ2: Encryption is not explicitly mentioned in the privacy policy or terms of service; the app passes HTTPS in transit but this is not stated in policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy and ToS do not mention strong password enforcement requirements for parent accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration for school use is present in either the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy references a cookie policy and lists browser opt-out links but does not enumerate all specific cookies by name and purpose within the policy itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: AppsFlyer, Google, Shopify, and PayPal are specifically named as third-party recipients of data in the privacy policy and/or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy broadly groups data shared with third parties by category (attribution data to AppsFlyer/Google, transaction data to Shopify/PayPal) but does not specify exactly which data fields each third party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can decline consent signals for AppsFlyer attribution, but the opt-out process is tied to consent flows at install and is not described as a simple ongoing opt-out mechanism within the app settings.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy explicitly states that all third-party processors must hold a Data Processing Agreement and process data only on Mrs Wordsmith's instructions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy acknowledges third-party relationships but does not explicitly commit to notifying users if those third-party relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy and Google Play listing explicitly state the app does not serve third-party advertising within its apps, making this a clear meet.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy states it does not use persistent identifiers from children to serve behavioural advertising and does not allow third parties to use children's data for targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: AppsFlyer SDK is integrated and transmits consent signals to Google for install attribution, which constitutes limited third-party tracking; consent is required for EEA users but the process for non-EEA (including U.S.) users is less clearly described.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy discloses AppsFlyer SDK integration and consent signals sent to Google, but does not enumerate all tracking technologies (e.g., web beacons, JavaScript tags) used within the app.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can decline ad_personalization consent signals at the attribution consent step, but a clear, standalone ongoing opt-out mechanism for data sharing with advertisers is not described in the policy.

r785.riskReason: WordTap has no minimum age restriction, no COPPA or FERPA disclosures, no dedicated Terms of Service page, explicitly states the privacy policy may be updated without prior notice, places liability for third-party data handling entirely on the user, and is governed exclusively under Israeli law with no US regulatory compliance framework mentioned.
r785.parentSummary: WordTap collects personal information including names, email addresses, IP addresses, usage data, and vocabulary words entered by users, and shares this data with third-party service providers for hosting, marketing, and other services. The platform has no stated minimum age, no parental consent mechanism, and no mention of COPPA or FERPA compliance, making it unsuitable for K-12 deployment without significant additional vetting. Privacy policy changes can be made at any time without advance notice to users, and legal disputes are handled exclusively under Israeli jurisdiction.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states it may be updated at any time without prior notice to users, and responsibility for tracking changes rests solely with the user — no advance notification process or revision history is provided.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several categories of personal data collected (name, email, IP address, usage data, vocabulary words, purchase records) but the disclosure is fragmented and incomplete, with some data types such as cookies only partially described.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states that data is collected through direct user input and automatic collection technologies including cookies, but does not specifically enumerate all collection methods or explain each mechanism in detail.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not assert user ownership of data; it implies WordTap and third parties retain rights to use personal information, and personal data may be transferred to an acquiring entity in a business sale without user consent.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: No data deletion right or process is described in the privacy policy; users are told that if they do not want their data collected, they should simply not use the service, which does not constitute a deletion mechanism.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy contains no statement about how long personal data is retained, nor any specific or general data retention period, leaving this entirely unaddressed.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy contains no description of specific security measures, technical safeguards, or organizational controls used to protect personal information.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption, data-in-transit protection, or any other encryption standard is present anywhere in the accessible policy text.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: There is no mention of password strength requirements, password policies, or single sign-on; account creation is required but no password standards are disclosed.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI integration is present in any accessible policy or platform documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy references a Cookie Policy in section 4 and acknowledges the use of cookies and similar tracking technologies, but does not enumerate specific cookies, their purposes, or their durations — only a general reference is provided.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references categories of third parties (hosting providers, IT services, legal advisers, marketing services, social media services) but does not name any specific third-party companies or vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with each third-party category is provided; the disclosure is grouped and vague.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described; the only option presented is to stop using the service entirely.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy explicitly disclaims any liability for third-party service providers and states that users must comply with the third parties' separate policies — no vendor agreement or data processing obligations on third parties are asserted.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states it may be updated at any time without notice and places the responsibility for tracking changes on the user, meaning third-party changes would also not be communicated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: No statement about whether ads are displayed to users is present in the privacy policy or any accessible platform page; the marketing services mention among third parties implies potential ad-related data sharing.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No disclosure about targeted advertising is made; the reference to 'marketing services' as a third-party category without further explanation leaves targeted advertising status unaddressed and potentially active.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure about third-party tracking for advertising purposes is made, and no opt-out for such tracking is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy references cookies and similar tracking technologies broadly but does not clarify whether web beacons or pixel trackers are used, nor for what purpose beyond general usage data collection.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers or marketing partners is described anywhere in the accessible policy text.

dataSharedWith: Cloud hosting providers (Microsoft Azure, Google Business Suite)
r786.riskReason: Wordwall participates in the iKeepSafe COPPA Safe Harbor program and does not sell student data, but the introduction of marketing/advertising cookies, third-party AI processing of user input, and the placement of responsibility for student data consent on teachers rather than the platform itself creates meaningful compliance gaps for K-12 schools.
r786.parentSummary: Wordwall collects teacher account data (name, email, billing) and may collect limited student data such as name and assignment scores when teachers enable those features, with responsibility for obtaining parental consent placed on the teacher. The platform does not sell user data and participates in iKeepSafe's COPPA Safe Harbor program, but it uses marketing and advertising cookies from third parties and processes AI feature inputs through external providers, which parents and schools should be aware of. Data is stored encrypted on Microsoft Azure servers, and users can request full account deletion by contacting privacy@wordwall.net.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: Terms of Service state that modified terms will be posted on the website, but advance notification to existing users prior to changes taking effect is not clearly guaranteed for all users, only implied through a December 2025 update process.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy describes categories of data collected (name, email, scores, usage, billing, AI inputs) but does not provide an exhaustive enumerated list of every specific data element collected across all user types.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically describes how data is collected — through account sign-up, assignment use, leaderboard entry, support tickets, mailing lists, social media, and public databases — meeting this criterion.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy explicitly states that user data remains the property of the user and that teachers/schools retain the status of Data Controller for student data, clearly affirming user ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Full account deletion is available by emailing privacy@wordwall.net with an Account Deletion Request, with acknowledgment within 48 hours and confirmation once deletion is complete.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy states data may be retained for up to 7 years following end of engagement, with accounting data kept 7 years per VAT regulations and usage statistics kept in perpetuity in anonymised form, meeting the general retention statement standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy describes specific security measures including Microsoft Azure hosting, physical access controls (photo ID, magnetic card readers, CCTV), and restricted remote access limited to known users from known IP addresses.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy and data notice explicitly states all remote access is conducted over HTTPS/SSL encryption and that user data is encrypted, meeting the encryption criterion.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service mention account passwords and the ability to disable user identification codes, but there is no explicit statement that strong password requirements are enforced on the platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform supports SSO integration with VLE providers, which partially meets MFA/SSO criteria, but there is no explicit mention of native MFA being available or required for direct logins.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The updated cookie policy (effective December 2025) introduces a cookie consent manager with categorised controls (Essential, Functional, Analytics, Marketing and Advertising), and a Cookie Preferences link is available in the footer, meeting the criterion for listed cookies with purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy names some third parties (Microsoft Azure, Google Business Suite, Stripe, iKeepSafe, EU Representative) but does not provide a comprehensive named list of all marketing or analytics third parties used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: While some data shared per third party is described (e.g., payment data to Stripe, integration data to VLE/SSO providers), the policy does not provide a full per-third-party breakdown of exactly what data is shared with each marketing or analytics service.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing cookies via the cookie consent manager and can opt out of marketing communications by emailing privacy@wordwall.net, but opt-out from all third-party data sharing (e.g., AI providers) is not clearly available.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states data is only held on systems meeting high compliance standards and that the EU Representative operates under the same privacy policy, but there is no explicit contractual Data Processing Agreement language binding all third parties to the vendor's privacy standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy notes that users will be notified before data is transferred in the event of a merger or acquisition, but it does not clearly commit to advance notification of all third-party relationship changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Terms of Service reference advertising in liability clauses, and the updated cookie policy includes a Marketing and Advertising cookie category, suggesting ads or ad-related tracking may be present, but the nature and placement of ads on the platform are not clearly disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The cookie policy introduces Marketing and Advertising cookies that can be toggled, implying possible third-party targeted advertising, but the policy does not explicitly state whether student-facing or teacher-facing targeted ads are displayed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The cookie consent manager allows users to toggle off Marketing and Advertising cookies, providing some opt-out capability, but it is unclear whether third-party ad trackers are fully disabled or whether any tracking occurs prior to consent on first visit.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy references Google Analytics (per network allowlist documentation) and third-party marketing services using cookies, indicating tracking beyond functional use, but the specific web beacons or tracking methods used are not fully enumerated.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of marketing/advertising cookies via the cookie preferences manager accessible from any page footer, but the process for opting out of data already shared with advertisers or for retroactively withdrawing consent is not clearly described.

dataSharedWith: Schools and institutional subscribers (aggregate, non-identifiable reports)
Law enforcement / legal authorities (when required by court order or subpoena)
Google (optional integration with Google Drive and Google Classroom, though World Book states it does not access Google user data)
r787.riskReason: World Book Online explicitly states it will not sell PII to third parties for marketing purposes, does not display targeted ads, uses industry-standard encryption, and collects minimal data, but the policy lacks explicit data retention timelines, does not clearly name specific third-party service providers, and does not provide a formal data deletion request mechanism for users or parents.
r787.parentSummary: World Book Online collects limited personal information including a first name, optional email for password recovery, and anonymous usage/technical data such as IP address and browsing behavior; it explicitly states it will not sell personal information to third parties for marketing and does not serve targeted advertisements. The platform acknowledges COPPA guidance and advises children under 13 to consult a parent before sharing information, but stops short of providing a formal parental consent or data deletion workflow. Data may be shared in aggregate, non-identifiable form with the subscribing school or institution, and may be disclosed to legal authorities if required by law.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use states that changes are posted in the 'Subscriber News' section of the site and that continued use constitutes acceptance, but there is no stated advance notification period or maintained revision history for the Privacy Policy specifically.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (first name, optional email, security question, usage/technical data, search preferences, cookies), and explicitly states financial data and last name are not collected, but the full enumeration is incomplete and somewhat vague regarding all potential data points.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected — through registration, feedback/email submission, cookie setting, searches conducted, and direct inquiry — meeting the standard for explaining collection methods.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not clearly assert user ownership of data; World Book states data is used for internal purposes and aggregate reporting, but does not explicitly assign ownership to the user, leaving data ownership ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy provides a contact address for questions or to modify/update information but does not describe a formal, self-service process for users or parents to delete their data upon request.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state any specific data retention period or general retention timeline, failing to address how long personal or non-personal information is kept.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states World Book has implemented 'multiple tiers of security measures' to protect data but does not enumerate specific measures such as firewalls, access controls, or audits, constituting only a general security statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states that PII is encoded using 'commercially reasonable technology, consistent with industry standard encryption protocols' that protects data in transit, satisfying the encryption requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Use and Privacy Policy contain no mention of password complexity requirements, enforcement of strong passwords, or use of SSO/MFA in lieu of passwords.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA) or single sign-on (SSO/LTI) integration is made in the publicly available Terms or Privacy Policy, though the technical help page references IP-based and other authentication types for institutional access.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy has a dedicated 'Use of Cookies' section describing session cookies and persistent cookies and what data they collect (IP, browser type, etc.), but does not enumerate all cookie types by name or clearly classify them as functional vs. tracking.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references third-party sharing in the context of legal obligations and institutional subscribers, and mentions Google Drive/Classroom integration, but does not name specific analytics, hosting, or technology vendors used.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups third-party disclosures broadly (e.g., legal authorities, institutional subscribers in aggregate) without specifying which data fields are shared with each category of third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy does not offer a clear opt-out process for third-party data sharing; Google integration is described as user-initiated and optional, but no formal opt-out for other disclosures is described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not include a statement that third parties are contractually required to follow World Book's data protection standards or maintain equivalent privacy safeguards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not include any provision notifying users when third-party relationships change or when new third parties are added to data sharing arrangements.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy and terms do not reference any advertising on the platform, and the platform is a subscription-based educational resource with no indication of ad display to authenticated users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no mention of targeted advertising, behavioral profiling for ads, or ad network integration in the privacy policy or terms, and World Book explicitly states PII is not sold to third parties for marketing.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party ad tracking, retargeting pixels, or ad network cookies are mentioned in the privacy or cookie policies, and the platform's subscription model is inconsistent with third-party ad tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie section describes only functional and session cookies tied to service delivery and user experience monitoring; no advertising beacons or tracking pixels for ad purposes are disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising or data sharing with advertisers is disclosed or evidenced, there is no need for an opt-out mechanism, and this requirement is effectively met by the absence of such practices.

r788.riskReason: The site is freely accessible without an account and widely used by K-12 students, yet it displays advertisements, shares anonymized behavioral data with third-party advertisers, uses tracking technologies (including Google Tag Manager), and its privacy policy does not explicitly address COPPA compliance, children under 13, or age-gating mechanisms.
r788.parentSummary: World History Encyclopedia (worldhistory.org) is a nonprofit educational resource that can be used without creating an account, but it displays advertisements to non-members and collects anonymized behavioral data that may be shared with third-party advertisers. The site uses cookies and tracking tools such as Google Tag Manager for analytics and ad personalization, and users can manage ad-choice preferences via YourAdChoices. No explicit COPPA provisions, minimum age requirements, or child-directed data protections are stated in the privacy policy, which is a concern for schools deploying this platform with students under 13.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use states that users are bound by the version posted at the time of access and that major changes (such as ownership transfers) will be notified via the Publication, but there is no clear advance notification process or revision history for routine policy updates.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy references anonymized behavioral data, cookies, and membership data (name, email, payment), but does not provide a comprehensive enumerated list of all data types collected from general visitors.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy generally indicates data is collected through site usage and membership registration, but does not specifically detail each collection method (e.g., forms, cookies, trackers, Google Tag Manager) in a structured manner.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Data ownership is not explicitly addressed; the policy focuses on use of data rather than clarifying whether users or the organization own the collected data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Account holders can manage consent settings and advertising preferences via YourAdChoices, and membership can be cancelled, but a clear, explicit process for full deletion of all personal data by any user is not described in the accessible policy text.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No specific data retention period or general retention statement was found in the accessible portions of the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The membership page notes industry-standard SSL encryption and secure payment processing, but the main privacy policy does not enumerate specific security measures for general user data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: SSL/TLS encryption is referenced for membership payment processing, but encryption of all user data in transit and at rest is not explicitly confirmed in the general privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: An account is not required to use the core encyclopedia content, so most K-12 student users are not exposed to password-related risks; membership/account creation is optional for adults.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account is required for standard access to the platform, eliminating MFA concerns for the majority of K-12 student users accessing the encyclopedia.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references sharing anonymized data with 'third parties, including advertisers' and the site is confirmed to use Google Tag Manager, but specific third-party partners are not named in the policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify what data is shared with each individual third-party category; it only states that anonymized behavioral data may be shared with advertisers as a group.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users are directed to YourAdChoices to manage interest-based advertising preferences, providing a partial opt-out mechanism, though it is an external tool and not a direct in-platform opt-out.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: There is no stated vendor agreement or contractual obligation requiring third parties to adhere to equivalent data protection standards as a condition of receiving shared data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy and terms of use do not describe a process for notifying users when third-party data-sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Advertisements are displayed to non-member (free) users; members who pay for a subscription receive ad-free browsing, so ads are present for the general K-12 student population that does not have a paid membership.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy states anonymized behavioral data may be shared with advertisers for 'relevant advertising,' suggesting interest-based or behavioral targeting may occur, though it is described as anonymized.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: An opt-out via YourAdChoices is referenced, indicating third-party ad tracking occurs; however, the opt-out process relies on an external industry tool rather than a direct platform control.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The site uses Google Tag Manager and shares anonymized data with advertisers, indicating tracking technologies are in use for advertising purposes, but the policy does not enumerate all tracking methods (e.g., web beacons, pixels) used.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out option is mentioned via YourAdChoices, and privacy consent options can be changed on the site, but the process is not clearly documented in plain language within the privacy policy itself.

dataSharedWith: Data analytics and campaign measurement providers
Third-party sponsors of sweepstakes and contests
Government or public authorities (if legally required)
r789.riskReason: Worldwildlife.org explicitly uses targeted advertising, third-party tracking cookies, engages in list exchanges that qualify as data sales under state privacy laws, does not respond to browser Do Not Track signals, and is not designed or approved for K-12 student use — making it unsuitable and high-risk for school deployment.
r789.parentSummary: Worldwildlife.org (WWF) collects personal information including names, email addresses, payment data, browsing behavior, and device identifiers, and uses third-party advertising companies and cookies to serve targeted ads across devices. WWF shares personal data broadly with vendors, partner nonprofits via list exchanges (characterized as a 'sale' under applicable state laws), and advertising networks, with only a general opt-out mechanism rather than granular controls. The site explicitly states it is not directed at children under 13, has no FERPA or K-12 school-specific protections, and is not appropriate for classroom use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy shows a 'Last Modified' date and links to prior versions, but changes become effective upon posting without advance notice to users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy provides a reasonably detailed list of personal data collected, including names, email, address, payment info, device data, cookies, and behavioral session data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected — via forms, cookies/pixels/web beacons, analytics tools, social media connections, and third-party data sources.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: WWF claims broad rights to use and disclose personal information as it sees fit and does not affirm user ownership of data; the policy is silent on user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion of personal information via a form or email, but the process requires manual outreach and is not an immediate self-service deletion option.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state a specific data retention period or general retention schedule, making this area non-compliant.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy only states 'reasonable organizational, technical, and administrative measures' are used, without specifying what those measures are.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of encryption in the privacy policy or terms; the site uses HTTPS but the policy does not describe encryption of stored data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No mention of strong password enforcement requirements or policies; account login exists but no password strength requirements are described.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration; standard username/password login only.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions cookies and tracking technologies generally and references opt-out tools (NAI, YourAdChoices), but does not provide a comprehensive list of all cookies with their specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Third-party categories are described broadly (marketing vendors, analytics, ad companies, nonprofits) but specific named third-party companies are not listed in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by vendor category rather than specifying what data is shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Opt-out options exist (phone hotline, email, cookie settings) but are cumbersome and not easily accessible, especially for students or parents.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states service providers are engaged but does not explicitly confirm that all third parties are bound by a formal data processing agreement or equivalent privacy obligations.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states changes become effective upon posting, implying third-party relationships may change without direct prior notice to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: WWF explicitly uses third-party advertising companies to serve targeted ads based on user behavior and data received from third parties — ads are displayed to all users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms ads are targeted based on browsing behavior across devices and sites, and data received from third parties, constituting confirmed user targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party ad companies place cookies and use tracking technologies across devices with no indication that tracking is blocked before opt-out; the site does not respond to Do Not Track signals.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: WWF uses cookies, pixels, clear GIFs, web beacons, and session-recording tools (mouse movements, keystrokes, scrolling) for advertising and campaign tracking purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out process exists via NAI and YourAdChoices links, cookie settings, and a phone hotline, but it is not straightforward or clearly labeled for general users.

dataCollected: Information from third-party accounts (Google, Microsoft, Schoology, Canvas, HMH Ed)

Third-party SSO platforms (Google, Microsoft, Schoology, Canvas, HMH Ed)
