complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not describe any process for notifying users if third-party service relationships change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Advertisements are displayed on the main site to general users (including 13+ students), but are not shown on custom puzzle pages — creating a partial but incomplete safeguard for educational use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: Raptive (CMI Marketing) collects and uses data for advertising purposes on the main site, which may include user-targeted advertising based on browsing behavior.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Advertising-related cookies and IP addresses are shared with Raptive for ad targeting; no opt-out is offered within the Jigsaw Explorer interface itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms advertising-related cookies and IP address tracking are used for ad display, indicating third-party tracking methods are active on the main site.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out process for data sharing with Raptive or other advertisers is described in the Jigsaw Explorer privacy policy; users are only referred to Raptive's external policy.

r841.riskReason: JW Pepper uses Google Analytics and DoubleClick advertising cookies for behavioral ad tracking, does not specify a minimum age, lacks explicit COPPA compliance language or parental consent mechanisms, and shares data with multiple third-party ad and marketing vendors — all of which pose significant risks for K-12 use where students under 13 may be involved.
r841.parentSummary: JW Pepper collects personal information including name, email, mailing and billing addresses, order history, employment information, and usage data via cookies when users register, place orders, or subscribe to newsletters. The platform uses Google Analytics and DoubleClick advertising cookies to track user interactions with ads, and shares data with third-party vendors for marketing, payment processing, and database services. While the policy states that personal information is not sold and that third parties are required to maintain privacy and security, there is no explicit minimum age requirement, no COPPA-specific parental consent process, and no dedicated student data protection provisions, making this platform a significant compliance concern for K-12 schools.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states users will be notified of changes on the Privacy Policy page, but there is no advance notification process, revision history, or versioning documented.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several data types (name, email, address, order data, cookies, usage data) but does not provide a fully exhaustive enumeration of all data collected across all services.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically states data is collected when users register, place orders, subscribe to newsletters, respond to surveys, and passively via cookies and third-party trackers.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state who owns the data; ownership is implied to reside with the company as no user data ownership assertion is made.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion via account settings or by contacting customer service, but deletion requires contacting a representative for some changes, making it only partially self-service.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy does not state any specific data retention period or even a general retention statement for how long personal data is kept.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy only states that the company will 'endeavor to protect' security; no specific technical security measures (e.g., firewalls, access controls) are described in the main privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS/SSL for transactions (evidenced by secure.www.jwpepper.com), but the privacy policy does not explicitly mention encryption of data at rest or in transit.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy does not mention password strength requirements or enforcement; only a basic password reset process is referenced in support documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI options are mentioned anywhere in the terms or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions functional cookies, persistent 'Remember Me' cookies, and Google Analytics/DoubleClick third-party cookies, but does not provide a complete categorized list of all cookies and their specific purposes.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy names Google (Analytics and DoubleClick) and describes functional categories of third parties (payment processors, CRM, database, marketing) but does not name all specific third-party vendors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with third parties is described only at a category level (e.g., 'to the extent necessary to perform functions'); specific data fields shared with each named or unnamed vendor are not itemized.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of Google advertising via Google Ad Settings or the Network Advertising Initiative opt-out, but opt-out from other third-party data sharing is not clearly described.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy explicitly states that third parties are required to maintain the privacy and security of personal information processed on the company's behalf.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention notifying users when third-party vendors change or are replaced; only general policy-page update notice is provided.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy explicitly references Google DoubleClick advertising cookies and compilation of ad impression data, confirming that targeted advertising-related tracking occurs.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms use of DoubleClick and Google advertising cookies to compile data on user interactions with ad impressions, indicating third-party behavioral targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Opt-out options are provided via Google Ad Settings and the Network Advertising Initiative, but these are external tools and not a built-in platform control, limiting the opt-out effectiveness.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy confirms use of DoubleClick cookies and other third-party identifiers specifically to track ad impressions and user interactions, constituting ad-purpose tracking/web beacons.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: The policy references opt-out via Google Ad Settings and the NAI opt-out page, but the process is external, browser-based, and not straightforward for school administrators or parents to manage.

dataSharedWith: Law enforcement and government entities (when legally required)
r842.riskReason: KickUp is an educator-facing platform that explicitly bars users under 18, but its privacy policy uses broad tracking technologies, does not name specific third-party vendors, grants itself a perpetual license over public user content, vaguely retains data for unspecified periods, and lacks explicit FERPA/COPPA compliance statements despite serving K-12 school districts.
r842.parentSummary: KickUp is a professional development and coaching platform designed exclusively for educators aged 18 and over in K-12 districts — it is not intended for student use, and any student data incidentally collected (e.g., in uploaded classroom videos) is stated to remain private between collaborators. The platform collects educator personal information, usage data, and uploaded content using a wide range of tracking technologies including cookies, web beacons, and embedded scripts, and shares data with unspecified third-party service providers. While KickUp states it takes privacy seriously and complies with CCPA for California residents, it does not explicitly claim FERPA or COPPA compliance, retains data for an unspecified duration, and grants itself a broad perpetual license over any content users mark as public.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states users will be notified by email and/or platform notice of updates, and an updated 'Effective Date' is provided, but no revision history or change log is maintained or linked.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several categories of personal data collected (name, email, address, phone, demographic info, device/usage data) but does not provide a fully exhaustive or itemized list, and some collected data types are only implied.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes how data is collected: directly from users upon login, automatically via tracking technologies (cookies, web beacons, Flash objects, embedded scripts, mobile SDKs, location-identifying technologies), and through third-party partners.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: KickUp grants itself a royalty-free, worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable license over any user content marked public, and does not clearly affirm that users retain ownership of their data, indicating the policy does not adequately protect user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: California residents can request deletion under CCPA rights described in the policy, but no general deletion mechanism is described for non-California users; users who disagree with policy changes may only terminate their account.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states KickUp 'may retain all information you have submitted for a variety of purposes, including backups and archiving' but does not specify any concrete retention period or schedule, making this vague and incomplete.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states 'appropriate technical and organizational security measures' have been implemented but does not enumerate specific measures such as encryption standards, access controls, or audits, constituting only a general security statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No explicit mention of encryption in transit or at rest is made in the privacy policy; the policy acknowledges that transmissions are at the user's own risk and no guarantees are made, suggesting encryption is not clearly confirmed.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service require users to maintain the confidentiality of their passwords and restrict account access, but there is no mention of enforced password complexity requirements or strength standards.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The policy and terms make no mention of multi-factor authentication (MFA), SSO/LTI integration, or any equivalent access security mechanism beyond standard password-based account management.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy acknowledges use of cookies, Flash objects, web beacons, embedded scripts, mobile SDKs, and location-identifying technologies, but does not provide a dedicated cookie policy listing each cookie by name, type, and purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy discloses categories of third parties (hosting, maintenance, security, data analysis, feature providers) but does not name any specific vendors or companies by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups third-party sharing by service category without specifying which data types are shared with which specific third party, making it impossible to assess data exposure per vendor.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: California residents can opt out of certain data uses under CCPA; non-California users have no explicit opt-out from third-party sharing described in the policy beyond declining to provide data entirely.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that third parties are required to 'process such information in compliance with this Privacy Policy' and are authorized to only a 'limited use,' which is a general contractual obligation statement without specific supplier agreement detail.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not describe any notification process for changes to third-party vendors or data-sharing arrangements; users are only notified of changes to the privacy policy itself, not to the third parties involved.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Terms reference 'advertisers found on or through the KickUp Platform' and the privacy policy mentions contacting users with 'advertising relating to our products and services,' suggesting some advertising context exists but it is not fully clarified.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy does not explicitly confirm or deny targeted advertising based on user data; the broad use of tracking technologies and references to third-party partners for usage data creates ambiguity about behavioral targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy discloses use of third-party partners to assist with automatic data collection via tracking technologies but does not specify whether those partners conduct cross-site tracking for advertising or provide any opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy explicitly lists web beacons, Flash objects, embedded scripts, mobile SDKs, and location-identifying technologies as collection methods, but does not clarify whether these are used for advertising or solely for platform operation.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: California residents have CCPA-based rights to opt out of certain data uses, but no clear 'Do Not Sell My Personal Information' mechanism or general advertising opt-out process is described for all users in the policy.

r843.minAge: Over 12 (Account Holders must be over age 12; minors participate as Participants under an Account Holder)
dataSharedWith: Service providers and contractors (internal operational use)
Group leaders and teachers (aggregate performance summaries)
Third-party analytics providers (implied via tracking technologies)
r843.riskReason: Kid Power (gokidpower.org) states it does not collect PII from minors and claims no sale of personal data, but uses multiple tracking technologies including cookies, beacons, click tracking, and analytics software on a platform explicitly designed for K-12 children, and the privacy policy lacks specific third-party names, explicit COPPA/FERPA compliance statements, a defined data retention period, and MFA/strong password enforcement details.
r843.parentSummary: Kid Power (gokidpower.org), operated by Classroom Champions, collects personal information (name, email, IP address, usage data) from adult Account Holders such as teachers and parents, and states it does not collect personally identifiable information directly from child Participants. The platform uses cookies, beacons, and analytics tracking technologies to monitor usage and performance, and may share aggregate data with research partners and group leaders, but commits not to sell or rent personal information to third parties. While the platform's no-PII-for-minors approach is a positive protection, the privacy policy (last updated April 2020) lacks specificity around named third parties, a defined data retention schedule, FERPA compliance language, and MFA controls, which warrants careful review before school-wide deployment.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states Kidpower (kidpower.org) 'reserves the right to change this User Agreement at any time without notice,' and the gokidpower.org policy (last updated April 2020) does not describe an advance notification process or maintain a revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several data types (name, email, IP address, browser info, clickstream, unique identifiers, usage/activity data) but does not provide a fully exhaustive enumerated list and conflates Account Holder and Participant data without complete clarity.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy describes general collection methods (registration forms, automatic collection, cookies, tracking technologies) but does not detail exactly how each specific data type is collected for each user category.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy states user data is kept confidential and not used beyond service purposes, but does not explicitly affirm that users own their data; ownership is implied rather than stated.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The policy indicates third-party email invitees can request removal, and general contact for assistance is provided, but there is no clear self-service deletion process described for all users.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state any specific or general data retention period; there is no mention of how long data is kept after account closure or service termination.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy mentions use of 'appropriate security measures' and 'appropriate physical, electronic, and managerial procedures' but does not enumerate specific technical safeguards such as encryption standards or access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The main gokidpower.org privacy policy does not explicitly state that data is encrypted in transit or at rest; the related kidpower.org policy mentions SSL, but this cannot be directly attributed to the gokidpower.org platform.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy contains no mention of password complexity requirements or enforcement; there is no reference to strong password policies for account creation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made anywhere in the terms or privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions use of cookies, JavaScript, beacons, tags, and click-tracking, and directs users to a 'tracking technologies' section, but does not provide a named list of each cookie with its purpose.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references 'service providers' and 'research partners' in general terms but does not name any specific third-party vendors or analytics providers by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing by purpose (service providers, research) rather than specifying exactly what data is shared with each named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Account Holders can opt out of marketing communications, but there is no clear process described for opting out of all third-party data sharing or service-provider data transfers.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states employees and contractors are 'obliged to respect confidentiality' but does not describe formal data processing agreements or supplier contracts governing third-party compliance.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not include any commitment to notify users when third-party service providers or research partners change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy does not mention any advertising on the platform, and Kid Power is a nonprofit K-12 philanthropic activity platform with no indication of ads being served to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no mention of targeted advertising or behavioral ad targeting in the policy; the platform does not appear to serve targeted ads.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: While the platform does not appear to use tracking for advertising, it does use third-party tracking technologies (cookies, beacons, analytics) without full opt-out mechanisms described for all tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy discloses use of cookies, beacons, tags, and click-tracking but does not clearly distinguish between functional tracking and any potential advertising-related tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: An opt-out for marketing communications is mentioned, but the policy does not describe a clear process for opting out specifically of data sharing with any advertising or analytics partners.

dataCollected: Time spent on problems and assignments
Security monitoring data via Report URI Ltd
IP address and browser interaction data
dataSharedWith: Amazon Web Services (AWS) - hosting and storage
Successor entity - in case of acquisition or merger
r844.riskReason: Kuta Software holds an iKeepSafe FERPA Badge, explicitly prohibits selling personal data, uses institutional COPPA consent delegation, employs SSL/TLS encryption and NIST-aligned security practices, and provides transparent data retention and breach notification commitments.
r844.parentSummary: Kuta Works collects basic registration information (name, email) and academic activity data (assignment answers, time-on-task) from students, stored securely on AWS servers in the United States. Personal data is never sold or shared with advertisers; it is only shared with a small number of named service providers (AWS, Google Analytics, Google reCAPTCHA, Report URI) and only disclosed to legal authorities if required by law. The platform holds an iKeepSafe FERPA Badge, requires schools to obtain parental consent before student registration, and commits to notifying users of data breaches within 7 calendar days.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Kuta Works privacy policy maintains a dated revision history and commits to posting advance notice of substantive changes on the website; the desktop/main site policy also states users will be notified of changes by a website message.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Kuta Works privacy policy enumerates specific data categories collected from teachers, students, and via third-party services (Google Analytics, reCAPTCHA, Report URI), and the main site policy lists activation data collected from desktop software users.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly states how each data category is collected — entered during registration, collected through Google Analytics/reCAPTCHA interactions, stored in cookies, or collected via Report URI for security monitoring.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Terms of Use grant users ownership of custom questions but also grant Kuta Software a broad royalty-free license to exploit them; ownership of other user data is not explicitly assigned to the user, leaving data ownership partially ambiguous.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Teachers may delete their accounts with a defined deletion timeline (active resources within 7 days, backups within 42 days total), though purchase history is retained and student-specific self-deletion options are not explicitly detailed.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states that anonymous student result data is retained for product improvement purposes and specifies a minimum 90-day advance notice before any data transfer, providing a general but meaningful retention framework.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The Kuta Works privacy policy cites the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, an Information Security and Risk Management Plan, SSL/TLS encryption, AWS security measures, and breach notification procedures as specific security safeguards.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states that SSL/TLS is used to ensure secure communication between the user's browser and the Kuta Works server, and the main site confirms encrypted checkout for purchases.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform assigns temporary passwords to students pre-registered by teachers and requires them to set their own passwords upon first login, but no explicit strong password policy or complexity requirements are stated in the reviewed documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is made in either the privacy policy or terms of use; login relies solely on username and password credentials.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy acknowledges cookies are used to store data collected via Google Analytics and reCAPTCHA but does not provide a comprehensive cookie list with individual purposes; only a general category-level description is given.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The Kuta Works privacy policy specifically names AWS, Google Analytics, Google reCAPTCHA, and Report URI Ltd as the third-party services used, satisfying the requirement to identify third parties by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups data sharing descriptions by third-party service at a category level (e.g., interaction data to Google, security data to Report URI) but does not provide a granular field-by-field breakdown of exactly what data each third party receives.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: There is no explicit opt-out mechanism described for third-party data sharing with Google Analytics or other services; the policy directs users to read Google's privacy policy for more details but does not offer a Kuta-managed opt-out process.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states Kuta Software will only contract with entities that have privacy policies consistent with theirs, and specifies that AWS is bound by the AWS Customer Agreement with defined security responsibilities.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy commits to providing a minimum 90-day advance notice on the website and updating the privacy policy before any data transfer or sharing arrangement changes occur.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Neither the Kuta Works privacy policy nor the main site policy makes any mention of advertisements being displayed to users; the platform operates as a paid, subscription-based educational tool with no ad model.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No targeted advertising is described or implied in either policy; personal data is explicitly stated to never be given, sold, or rented to any other company, group, or person.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy does not describe any third-party tracking for advertising purposes; Google Analytics is used solely for usage trend analysis, and no ad-network tracking is mentioned.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: While Google Analytics and reCAPTCHA use cookies and tracking, the policy only describes these as functional/security tools; however, the full scope of Google's tracking via these services is deferred to Google's own privacy policy, leaving some ambiguity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no data sharing with advertisers occurs and the policy explicitly prohibits selling or renting user data, there is no advertiser data-sharing relationship from which an opt-out would be necessary.

r845.riskReason: Learn.Genetics is a no-account, open-access university educational site that collects only standard anonymous server logs and voluntary feedback, with no evidence of advertising, third-party tracking, or student PII collection.
r845.parentSummary: Learn.Genetics collects no personal information from visitors unless they voluntarily submit feedback; it automatically logs only anonymous technical data such as IP address, browser type, and visit timestamps to measure site usage. No account is required to access content, no advertising is displayed, and the privacy policy makes no mention of selling or sharing data with third parties. The main concern for parents is that the policy is dated 2016 and does not explicitly address COPPA, FERPA, cookies, data retention, or security measures.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy is dated February 8, 2016, with no stated process for notifying users of changes or maintaining a revision history.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists automatically collected technical data (IP, domain, timestamp, browser, OS, referring URL) and voluntary feedback data, but does not address cookies or analytics tools that may also collect data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected automatically on visit and voluntarily via the feedback page, but does not specify the technical mechanisms (e.g., server logs, analytics scripts) used.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly state who owns the collected data; it is silent on data ownership rights of the user versus the institution.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The privacy policy provides no mechanism or process for users to request deletion of any data collected about them.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not mention any data retention period for automatically collected technical information or feedback submissions.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy contains no description of security measures, safeguards, or protocols used to protect collected data.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site is served over HTTPS providing transport-layer encryption, but the privacy policy itself does not mention encryption of stored data.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: No account or password is required to use the platform, so password enforcement is not applicable; this criterion is effectively met by design.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No account creation is required to access the platform, eliminating the need for MFA; the criterion is met by design.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy makes no mention of cookies, cookie types, or cookie purposes, leaving cookie usage practices entirely undisclosed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy does not name or disclose any third-party service providers, analytics tools, or other data recipients.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Because no third parties are named or acknowledged in the policy, there is no disclosure of what data (if any) is shared with each party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: The policy provides no opt-out mechanism for any form of data sharing, as third-party sharing is neither acknowledged nor addressed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: There is no mention of vendor agreements, data processing agreements, or third-party compliance obligations in the policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy contains no commitment to notify users if third-party data-sharing arrangements are introduced or changed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The site is an ad-free, open-access university educational resource with no advertising of any kind evident on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: There is no evidence of targeted advertising or behavioral profiling on the site; the policy does not reference any advertising activities.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No third-party advertising trackers or ad networks are disclosed or apparent, and the site does not reference any such tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy does not reference web beacons, pixel tags, or other ad-tracking technologies, and none are disclosed as being in use.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Because no advertising or data sharing with advertisers is present or disclosed, no opt-out is needed and this criterion is met by default.

dataCollected: Student first name and pronouns (for evaluations)
dataSharedWith: Third-party service providers (hosting, IT, email, payment processing)
r846.riskReason: While LilyAssist claims FERPA adherence and encryption, the parent Thriving Students Collective privacy policy references sharing data with advertisers and does not clearly exclude student data from such sharing, and no dedicated COPPA compliance or minimum age is stated for the platform itself.
r846.parentSummary: LilyAssist is an AI report-writing tool used by school psychologists that collects minimal student information — only a first name and pronouns are required, and full student PII is not needed. The platform claims all stored data is encrypted, can be deleted upon request, and is not shared with third parties outside the AI model used to generate report content. However, the overarching Thriving Students Collective privacy policy (which governs the platform) does reference potential data sharing with advertisers and service providers, and does not explicitly address COPPA compliance or minimum age requirements for users.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Software Terms of Service state that the form and nature of services may change without prior notice, and the general Terms and Conditions do not describe a clear advance notification or revision history process for policy changes.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The FAQ and tutorials pages describe some data collected (first name, pronouns, score report PDFs, interview forms), but the formal privacy policy does not enumerate all data types collected specifically for LilyAssist users in one consolidated list.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The platform generally describes that data is entered by users or uploaded as PDFs, but the privacy policy does not specifically detail all collection methods (e.g., automatic logging, cookies, analytics) in a comprehensive way.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The Software Terms of Service state that student education records remain under the control of the educational institution per FERPA, but data ownership for educator/user-generated content and account data is not clearly assigned to the user in the privacy policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The tutorials and software terms explicitly state that users and school districts can request access or deletion of any stored data at any time, meeting the full deletion requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy does not state a specific retention period; it only vaguely implies data is retained as needed for services, without a defined timeframe or post-service deletion schedule.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The platform claims data is encrypted and access is limited to designated technical personnel under strict data protection agreements, but does not enumerate specific security frameworks, certifications, or technical controls in the formal privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The tutorials and FAQ explicitly state that all stored data is encrypted and that no unauthorized personnel have access, meeting the encryption requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Neither the privacy policy nor the terms of service mention password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration is found in the publicly available policies or documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: No cookie policy or list of cookies with purposes is provided in either the privacy policy or terms of service; cookies are not addressed at all in the LilyAssist-specific documentation.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy references service providers such as hosting, IT, email, and payment processors in general categories but does not name specific third-party vendors used by LilyAssist.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy policy groups data shared with service providers broadly without specifying which data types are shared with each individual third party, including the unnamed AI model.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in the privacy policy or terms of service.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states service providers are subject to confidentiality obligations, but does not require named third parties to adhere to a specific vendor data protection agreement equivalent to the platform's own standards.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: Neither the privacy policy nor the terms of service include any provision for notifying users when third-party data processors or subprocessors change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The Thriving Students Collective privacy policy references sending advertisements and special offers from advertisers or third parties, creating ambiguity about whether ads may appear within the LilyAssist platform itself.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The privacy policy references measuring ad effectiveness and using data for internal business purposes related to advertising, but does not clearly confirm or deny targeted advertising to educators or within the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No opt-out for third-party tracking related to advertising is provided, and the presence of ad-effectiveness measurement language in the privacy policy raises concern about third-party tracking tools being active.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy does not address web beacons, pixels, or other tracking technologies, leaving the scope of tracking methods unspecified.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described anywhere in the privacy policy or terms of service.

dataSharedWith: Teachers (student quiz scores and usernames within class)
r847.riskReason: Lizard Point takes meaningful steps to protect child privacy—such as offering teacher-generated Child Student accounts with no email required for under-13 users—but the privacy policy lacks explicit statements on COPPA compliance, data sale prohibition, third-party advertiser restrictions, specific cookie disclosures, and security measures, leaving gaps that are significant for K-12 deployment.
r847.parentSummary: Lizard Point collects minimal personal information for student users, especially for children under 13 who can use teacher-generated numbered accounts that require no email address. Quiz activity and scores are stored and visible to the assigned teacher. The site uses cookies and third-party services such as Google Analytics, but the privacy policy does not clearly specify whether advertising cookies or behavioral tracking are applied to child users, nor does it explicitly state that student data is never sold.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy includes a 'Last updated: June 25, 2024' date, indicating some revision tracking, but there is no stated process for notifying users of future changes in advance.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy references automatically collected information and account data but visible snippets do not enumerate a complete list of all data types collected (e.g., cookies, IP addresses, quiz scores are implied but not fully itemized).
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected automatically when using the site and via account registration, but does not specifically describe all collection mechanisms such as cookies, web beacons, or third-party SDKs.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not contain a clear statement that users own their data; ownership and licensing terms are not explicitly addressed in the accessible portions of the policy.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: The account profile page explicitly provides a password-confirmed account deletion option, indicating users can delete their accounts and associated data.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy references data retention generally in the context of the last-updated date and account deletion, but does not specify explicit retention periods for different data categories.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: No specific security measures (e.g., encryption at rest, access controls, audit logs) are described in the accessible privacy policy text.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The site uses HTTPS (confirmed by URL structure), but the privacy policy does not explicitly mention encryption of data in transit or at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: Child Student accounts are teacher-generated with shared class passwords, which is a simplified model; the site recommends teachers not use full student names but does not enforce strong password policies for student accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication or SSO/LTI integration for student or teacher accounts is found in the accessible policy or help documentation.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy does not include a dedicated cookie section listing specific cookies used, their purposes, or durations, despite the site's use of Google Analytics and likely advertising cookies.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: PayPal is identified as a payment processor in the FAQ, and Google is implied through analytics/advertising technologies, but the privacy policy does not explicitly name all third-party vendors receiving user data.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy does not specify which data categories are shared with each named or unnamed third party (e.g., what PayPal receives vs. what Google Analytics receives).
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: No opt-out mechanism for third-party data sharing is described in the accessible portions of the privacy policy or on the website.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: There is no statement in the accessible policy requiring third-party vendors to adhere to data protection standards or a supplier/DPA agreement framework.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not state that users will be notified if third-party data sharing arrangements change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The site's use of third-party technologies (Google Analytics with advertising features implied) suggests advertising cookies may be present, but the policy does not clearly disclose whether ads are shown to students or restricted.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: No explicit statement prohibits targeted advertising toward student users, and the presence of advertising-related third-party technologies creates uncertainty about whether behavioral targeting occurs.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No disclosure or opt-out for third-party ad tracking (e.g., Google advertising cookies) is provided in the privacy policy for student users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy does not address web beacons, pixel trackers, or other non-cookie tracking methods, and their presence or absence on the site is not disclosed.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear opt-out process for data sharing with advertisers is described anywhere in the accessible privacy policy or site documentation.

dataCollected: Payment details, tax IDs, billing address (via Stripe)
Usage and analytics data (pages visited, session data)
dataSharedWith: Google (Google Analytics, Google SSO) – analytics and authentication
r849.riskReason: Marker.io is a professional bug-reporting and website feedback tool not designed for K-12 use; it explicitly prohibits users under 16, collects session replays and screenshots that may capture sensitive screen content, uses LinkedIn Ads and Google Analytics for marketing analytics, and lacks any COPPA or FERPA compliance commitments.
r849.parentSummary: Marker.io is a website feedback and bug-reporting tool designed for web development teams and businesses — it is not a K-12 educational platform and explicitly states it does not knowingly collect data from users under 16. The platform collects names, email addresses, screenshots, session recordings, device data, and billing information, and shares data with third parties including Google Analytics and LinkedIn Ads for marketing purposes. There are no COPPA or FERPA compliance provisions, making this tool inappropriate for use by K-12 students.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states material changes will be notified via email or in-service notice and the 'Last Updated' date is revised, but the Terms of Service state that continued use constitutes acceptance without guaranteed advance notice to all users.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy provides a detailed enumerated list of all data collected including contact data, account credentials, billing data, user-generated content, communications, and automatically collected technical/usage data.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy clearly explains that data is collected in three ways: directly from the user, automatically via cookies and tracking technologies, and from third parties.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy positions Marker.io as a Data Processor (not owner) for widget-collected data, with the customer as Data Controller, but for account and marketing data Marker.io acts as Data Controller, creating split ownership that is partially unclear for end users.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can delete their account and workspace data directly within the app, or contact privacy@marker.io; deleted data is permanently removed from backups within 90 days.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: Specific retention periods are stated: account data retained for subscription duration plus 30 days, billing records for 7 years, support tickets up to 3 years, and marketing data until consent is withdrawn.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The security page lists specific measures including AWS SOC2/ISO-27001 hosting in Ireland, 24×7 monitoring, biometric scanning, need-to-know access controls, regular SSH key rotation, and employee security training.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The GDPR help page explicitly states that all data is encrypted both in transit and at rest.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The Terms of Service require each Authorized User to have a unique login credential with no sharing permitted, and SSO via Google, GitHub, and Slack is supported.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Two-factor authentication is enforced for internal staff access; SSO options (Google, GitHub, Slack) are available for customer accounts, meeting this standard.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: A cookie policy page exists at marker.io/cookie-policy and categorizes cookies (necessary, performance, third-party), but does not provide a fully itemized list of every cookie with its specific purpose and duration.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: Specific named sub-processors are listed including AWS, Intercom, HubSpot, Stripe, Google Analytics, and LinkedIn Ads, with a full sub-processor list available at marker.io/subprocessors.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy policy groups data shared by sub-processor category (hosting, analytics, CRM, support, payments) with some named examples, but does not specify precisely which data fields are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications at any time and exercise GDPR/CCPA rights via privacy@marker.io, but there is no clear opt-out mechanism from analytics or advertising partner sharing (Google Analytics, LinkedIn Ads) beyond browser-level cookie controls.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: All sub-processors are required to sign data processing agreements consistent with GDPR Article 28, and Marker.io states it remains responsible for sub-processor acts and omissions.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The sub-processor list page notes it is subject to change as business needs change, but the policy does not commit to proactively notifying users in advance of specific third-party additions or changes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly lists LinkedIn Ads as an advertising partner used to understand website traffic and campaign effectiveness, meaning advertising-related tracking is active on the platform.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: LinkedIn Ads and Google Analytics are used for campaign effectiveness and targeting purposes, indicating third-party user tracking that could support targeted advertising.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Third-party tracking via Google Analytics and LinkedIn Ads is confirmed with no clear opt-out mechanism provided within the platform beyond general cookie consent or browser settings.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The cookie policy confirms use of Google Analytics (transmitting IP addresses to Google) and acknowledges third-party cookies are used for performance and marketing without fully enumerating all tracking methods.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No clear in-platform opt-out process for advertising data sharing is described; users are directed to browser settings or cookie consent tools, which do not constitute a clear opt-out process as required.

dataSharedWith: Law enforcement or as required by law
r850.riskReason: The privacy policy (embedded in the Terms of Use on the parent Demme Learning site) explicitly reserves the right to update without prior notice, lacks any COPPA or FERPA language despite serving K-12 students, makes only vague security claims, names no specific third parties, provides no data retention period, and permits promotional use of personal data.
r850.parentSummary: Math-U-See, published by Demme Learning, collects personal information including your name, address, email, IP address, and browsing behavior when you create an account or visit the site. The company states it will not sell your data but may use it for promotional communications and reserves the right to change its privacy policy at any time without notifying users. There is no mention of COPPA or FERPA compliance, no specific security measures, and no dedicated children's privacy protections despite the platform serving K-12 students.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Terms of Use explicitly state that Demme Learning reserves the right to revise the Terms and Privacy Policy at any time with or without notice, and revisions are effective immediately upon posting — no advance notification process exists.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists some data collected (name, address, email, IP address, usage/navigation data) but does not address student-specific data, learning records, or digital tool usage data from the Math-U-See platform.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy states data is collected when users voluntarily provide it and that IP/usage information is automatically tracked, but does not specifically describe collection methods such as cookies, forms, or account registration flows.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The policy does not explicitly address data ownership; users are not granted ownership rights and the company's right to use data for improving products and contacting users implies de facto company control over submitted data.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users may contact the Website Administrator to change information, but there is no clearly defined full deletion right, process, or timeline — only a correction/update pathway is mentioned.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: No data retention period is stated anywhere in the Terms of Use or the embedded Privacy Policy; there is no mention of how long personal data is kept or under what conditions it is deleted.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy states that 'suitable physical, electronic and managerial procedures' are in place to safeguard data, but provides no specifics about what those measures are.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: No mention of encryption is made in the Terms of Use or Privacy Policy; in fact, the policy explicitly states that internet security is imperfect and users transmit data at their own risk.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: There is no mention of password strength requirements, enforcement policies, or any account security standards anywhere in the available policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: No mention of multi-factor authentication, SSO, or LTI is made in any of the available policy documents.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The Demme Learning store privacy policy references a list of cookies and notes persistent cookies expire between 30 minutes and two years, but the main mathusee.com/demmelearning.com Terms of Use does not provide a comprehensive or itemized cookie disclosure.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: No specific third-party companies or service providers are named in the privacy policy; there is only a general statement about linked third-party sites not being controlled by Demme Learning.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: No breakdown of what specific data is shared with any particular third party is provided; the policy only broadly disclaims responsibility for linked sites.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of direct marketing by contacting the company via email, but there is no structured opt-out from third-party data sharing or a clearly described process for doing so.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy does not state that third parties or linked sites are contractually required to honor Demme Learning's privacy standards; it explicitly disclaims control over and responsibility for third-party sites.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy does not mention any obligation to notify users when third-party relationships or data-sharing practices change; revisions take effect immediately upon posting without notice.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The policy states data may be used to send 'promotional information about third parties,' which implies potential third-party advertising exposure, and no explicit statement that no ads are served to users is made.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy does not explicitly confirm targeted advertising, but the language permitting use of personal data for promotional purposes and the lack of any advertising restriction leaves the door open for targeting.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: No mention of third-party tracking pixels, ad networks, or opt-out mechanisms for tracking-based advertising is present in the policy.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies and usage tracking are acknowledged generally, but no specific disclosure of web beacons, tracking pixels, or their advertising purposes is made.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: No opt-out mechanism specifically for data sharing with advertisers is described; only a general opt-out from direct marketing emails via contacting the company is mentioned.

dataCollected: Class code and teacher-student linkage data
r851.riskReason: Mathigon, operated by Amplify Education, explicitly commits to COPPA and FERPA compliance, does not sell or use student data for advertising, encrypts data at rest and in transit, and positions schools as data controllers with district-executed Data Privacy Agreements available.
r851.parentSummary: Mathigon, now part of Amplify Education, collects student data such as name, email, and learning progress only for educational purposes, and most content can be used without an account at all. Student data is owned and controlled by the school, is not sold or used for advertising, and is protected with AES-256 encryption at rest and SSL/TLS in transit with SOC 2 Type 2 certification. Children under 13 may only create accounts with verifiable parental consent or through school authorization, and parents can request data review, deletion, or cessation of collection by contacting Amplify directly.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The Amplify Customer Privacy Policy states its last update date (July 6, 2023 for Mathigon-specific policies) and commits to notifying users of material changes via email or on-site notification, with revision history indicated by update dates.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The Amplify privacy policy enumerates categories of data collected including name, email, progress data, usage/device data, and account credentials, providing a reasonably comprehensive data inventory.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically describes data collection methods including direct user input at account creation, cookies, automatic collection during product use, and school roster provisioning.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Student Data is explicitly stated to be owned and controlled by the School, with Amplify acting only as a processor/service provider on behalf of the school, not claiming ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Parents, guardians, and users can request deletion of personal data via account settings or by contacting help@amplify.com, with Amplify committing to fulfill such requests subject to legal retention requirements.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states data is retained 'for as long as reasonably necessary' for disclosed purposes but does not specify exact retention periods (e.g., number of days/months), making this only a general retention statement.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: Amplify explicitly lists specific security measures including AES-256 encryption at rest, SSL/TLS in transit, SOC 2 Type 2 certification, ISO 27002 standards, penetration testing, brute-force prevention, and role-based access controls.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy and security documentation confirm full encryption of student data both at rest (AES-256) and in transit (industry-standard SSL/TLS), meeting this requirement comprehensively.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The platform supports login via Google and Microsoft SSO accounts for educators, and student accounts are provisioned through school systems or class codes, indicating SSO-based authentication rather than manual password creation.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: SSO via Google and Microsoft is available for educator accounts, providing a form of federated authentication, but explicit MFA for all account types is not confirmed in the reviewed policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy mentions the use of cookies and automatically collected information generally, and describes their purposes (personalization, analytics, session management), but does not provide a granular named-cookie inventory.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references categories of third-party service providers and research partners but does not enumerate specific named third-party vendors (beyond AWS as cloud host) in the publicly reviewed policy sections.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: Data shared with third parties is described at a category level (e.g., de-identified data to research partners, operational data to service providers) but specific data fields shared per named vendor are not detailed.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Student data is explicitly not sold or shared for advertising; schools control data sharing, and parents can request cessation of data collection, constituting an effective opt-out mechanism.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy states that third-party contractors with access to student data are contractually bound to maintain security and privacy, and the AUP holds schools and Amplify mutually accountable under FERPA, COPPA, and PPRA.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states material changes will be communicated via email or on-site notice, but does not specifically guarantee advance notification of changes to third-party data sharing arrangements, only general policy change notification.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: Amplify explicitly states it does not use Student Data for marketing or advertising purposes, and no advertisements are displayed within the Mathigon educational product.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy confirms that behavioral or targeted advertising is not conducted using student data, consistent with the Common Sense Privacy evaluation findings and Amplify's stated commitments.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: Student data is not used for third-party ad targeting; while third-party analytics tools may be used operationally, the policy prohibits use of student data for advertising tracking purposes.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: Cookies and automatically collected information are referenced for purposes such as personalization and analytics, but the full scope of tracking technologies (e.g., web beacons, pixels) is not explicitly enumerated, leaving some ambiguity.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since no advertising or data sharing with advertisers occurs for student accounts, there is effectively no need for an opt-out, and the policy's prohibition on advertising use of student data constitutes a complete protection.

dataCollected: School name and role (teacher, student, parent)
dataSharedWith: Email campaign and marketing automation providers
Social media advertisement providers (on Matific's behalf)
r852.riskReason: Matific does not sell student data and requires parental or school consent for users under 13, but third-party tracking for advertising purposes and ambiguous COPPA safe harbor status introduce meaningful privacy risks for K-12 deployments.
r852.parentSummary: Matific collects personal information such as names, email addresses, usage data, and student game progress, which is only visible to the associated parent, teacher, or school administrator. The platform states it does not sell student data and requires verifiable parental or school consent for children under 13, and parents or teachers can request deletion of student data. However, third-party advertising tracking services do collect data and personal information may be used to customize targeted advertisements on other sites, which is a notable concern for K-12 use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy states significant changes will be communicated via a prominent login notice and email, but no formal revision history or changelog is publicly maintained.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The privacy policy lists several categories of data collected (name, email, usage, IP, device, behavioral, payment token) but acknowledges some specific data types collected are not fully enumerated and the cookie policy page did not return detailed content.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The privacy policy specifically identifies three collection methods: directly from users via forms, through platform UI from school customers, and via third-party cookies and web beacons.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: The privacy policy does not explicitly state that users own their data, and ownership is ambiguous; the DPA indicates data is processed per school instructions but the public policy is silent on user data ownership.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Users can request deletion by contacting the DPO at DPO@slatescience.com, and schools, parents, and teachers can delete student data through the platform, satisfying full deletion rights.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The privacy policy states data is retained as long as needed to provide access or manage accounts and is deleted when accounts lapse, but no specific numeric retention period (e.g., 90 days, 1 year) is provided.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The privacy policy mentions industry-standard practices, encryption, and annual independent audits, but does not enumerate specific security controls (e.g., SOC 2, penetration testing schedules) in the public policy.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The privacy policy explicitly states that data kept on secure cloud servers is encrypted using leading industry-standard encryption tools.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The privacy policy and terms of service make no mention of password strength requirements or enforcement of strong passwords for user accounts.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: The platform supports social/federated login (SSO) options, which partially satisfies this criterion, but dedicated MFA is not explicitly described or confirmed in the public policies.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The privacy policy references a separate Cookies Notice and acknowledges use of cookies and web beacons including third-party ones, but the cookies policy page did not render detailed cookie listings during this review.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The privacy policy lists broad categories of third-party recipients (analytics, CRM, billing, marketing automation, cloud, support) but does not name specific third-party companies by name.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The privacy policy groups data sharing by third-party category rather than specifying exactly which data types are shared with each individual third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Users can opt out of marketing communications and request deletion of their data, but the policy does not provide a clear, easy opt-out mechanism specifically for third-party data sharing beyond contact with the DPO.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The privacy policy states that agents/service providers may not use personal information beyond what is necessary for the platform's services, but explicit contractual obligations binding third parties are detailed only in the DPA, not the public privacy policy.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The privacy policy states it may change from time to time and promises notice for significant changes, but does not specifically commit to notifying users when third-party service providers change.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy and terms explicitly state that the site and platform do not display any advertising to users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: While the platform itself displays no ads, Common Sense Media's evaluation found that personal information may be used to customize targeted advertisements to users on other third-party sites or services.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The privacy policy acknowledges use of third-party tracking cookies and web beacons and states Matific does not honor Do Not Track signals, with no clear opt-out from third-party tracking for advertising on other sites.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The privacy policy confirms use of third-party cookies and web beacons for tracking, and the platform does not respond to Do Not Track browser signals, indicating tracking methods are active with no functional opt-out.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Users can opt out of marketing communications, and the policy mentions data subject rights including objection to direct marketing, but the opt-out process for third-party advertising data sharing is not clearly described and requires contacting the DPO.

dataCollected: Payment / credit card information (for paid subscriptions)
dataSharedWith: Trusted service partners (statistical analysis, email, customer support)
Credit reference agencies (fraud prevention for paid orders)
GDPR-certified third-party service providers (listed on Help & Support site)
r853.riskReason: Mote explicitly states it does not sell user data or show ads, is a signatory to the Student Privacy Pledge, self-certifies COPPA and FERPA compliance, restricts student data sharing, and stores data on AWS with SSL encryption, though specific named third-party vendors and detailed cookie disclosures are not fully enumerated in the public policy.
r853.parentSummary: Mote collects voice recordings, account information (name and email), and basic technical data (IP address, browser info) to operate its voice-note service; it explicitly states it does not sell user data or show advertisements, and its subscription-based business model means student data is not monetized. For users identified as students, Mote further restricts data sharing by removing email addresses and device-level IPs from third-party data, disables most email communications, and deletes user-generated content after one year. Mote self-certifies as COPPA and FERPA compliant, is a signatory to the 2020 Student Privacy Pledge, and stores data securely on AWS with SSL encryption, making it a relatively low-risk tool for K-12 use.

complianceNotes.GENQ1: The privacy policy documents amendment dates (April 2022, February 2024, September 2025) and Mote states it will notify users of material changes, satisfying advance notification and revision history requirements.
complianceNotes.DCQ1: The policy lists several data types (voice recordings, email, IP address, browser info, payment data, cookies) but does not provide an exhaustive, structured list of every data field collected, leaving some gaps.
complianceNotes.DCQ2: The policy specifically explains how data is collected — directly from users (account creation, voice recording), automatically (IP, browser, cookies, server logs), and through payment processing — meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.DCQ3: Mote explicitly states it does not claim ownership of user-submitted content and that users retain ownership of their data, meeting the user-owns-data standard.
complianceNotes.DCQ4: Mote provides a documented account deletion process via in-app settings or by emailing support, and the privacy policy confirms users can correct, update, or remove personal information at any time.
complianceNotes.DCQ5: The policy states student-generated content is deleted after one year and dormant accounts are deleted after 12 months, but does not state a specific retention period for all other data categories, making this partially met.
complianceNotes.SECQ1: The policy specifically identifies Amazon Web Services as the cloud storage provider, SSL protocol, and password protection of all data storage systems as security measures.
complianceNotes.SECQ2: The policy explicitly states SSL/TLS encryption is used for data in transit, including for payment information, and data is stored on AWS with encryption measures in place.
complianceNotes.SECQ3: The policy requires account creation (Google SSO is supported) but does not explicitly state that strong passwords are enforced for non-SSO logins; SSO availability partially satisfies this requirement.
complianceNotes.SECQ4: Mote supports SSO (Single Sign-On) login as a login option, which satisfies this requirement for school deployments using Google or other SSO providers.
complianceNotes.SECQ5: The policy mentions use of cookies, pixel tags, local storage, and server logs generally, and references allaboutcookies.org, but does not provide a full cookie inventory with individual purposes listed for each cookie.
complianceNotes.SHRQ1: The policy references sharing with 'trusted partners' and names Amazon Web Services as the cloud storage provider, and notes a list of third-party providers exists on the Help & Support site, but does not name all third parties directly in the privacy policy itself.
complianceNotes.SHRQ2: The policy groups third-party sharing broadly (statistical analysis, email, customer support, fraud prevention) without specifying exactly which data fields are shared with each individual named third party.
complianceNotes.SHRQ3: Mote states it does not share user data with parties intending to advertise, does not sell data, and students can request data deletion; there is effectively no third-party ad sharing to opt out of, meeting this requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ4: The policy explicitly states all third parties are prohibited from using personal information except to provide services to Mote, are required to maintain confidentiality, and must be GDPR-certified, satisfying this requirement.
complianceNotes.SHRQ5: The policy states Mote will notify users of material changes and has a documented amendment history, but does not specifically call out a process for notifying users when individual third-party vendors change, making this partially met.
complianceNotes.ADVQ1: The privacy policy explicitly states 'We'll never show you an ad' and Mote's business model is subscription-only, fully meeting the no-ads standard.
complianceNotes.ADVQ2: The policy explicitly states Mote does not engage in behavioral targeting of advertising to minors and does not use user data for advertising targeting of any users.
complianceNotes.ADVQ3: The policy states Mote will never hand over user information to anyone who intends to advertise, and student data has email and device IP removed before any third-party sharing, effectively eliminating ad tracking.
complianceNotes.ADVQ4: The policy discloses use of cookies, pixel tags, and local storage for operational and service quality purposes, but does not provide a fully itemized tracking technology inventory, leaving some ambiguity about all tracking methods used.
complianceNotes.ADVQ5: Since Mote explicitly states it does not share data with advertisers and does not display ads, there is no advertising data sharing to opt out of, meeting this requirement by absence of the practice.

dataSharedWith: Third-party ad networks and advertising partners
